# Scribe's Journal — Zoomies

Critical documentation-drift learnings only. Routine fixes are not logged here.

## 2026-09-08 - Doc-completeness test had a blind spot: it only scanned one of two source files
Learning: `docs/problem-codes.md` claims to be checked "in both directions" by `internal/docs/codes_test.go`, and CLAUDE.md repeats that claim ("`internal/docs` tests in both directions"). But the test's `controllerSource` constant pointed only at `internal/controller/problems.go`. Two real, currently-emitted codes — `pool.dangerous` and `pool.cache_shared` — live in `internal/controller/views.go` (`PoolWarnings` / `cacheSharingWarning`), a file the test never parsed. Both `TestEveryProblemCodeIsDocumented` and `TestTheReferenceDescribesNoCodeThatIsGone` passed anyway, so the doc's own safety net had never actually covered these two rows.
Impact: An operator seeing `pool.dangerous` or `pool.cache_shared` in the UI's problems drawer had no reference row to look up what it means or how to fix it — exactly the failure the test exists to prevent, and the exact claim ("checked against the source by a test") in `docs/problem-codes.md` itself was false for these two codes.
Action: Added both rows to `docs/problem-codes.md`, and widened the test's source list (`controllerSources = []string{controllerSource, viewsSource}`) so a Problem literal anywhere in `internal/controller/` is caught, not just in `problems.go`. When a repo advertises "a test checks this," verify the test's own file list actually covers every place the checked-for thing can originate — a coverage claim is itself a claim worth spot-checking, not just the docs it backs.

# Testsmith's Journal — Zoomies

Critical test-coverage learnings only. Routine test additions are not logged here.

## 2026-09-27 - A helper's one conditional branch went untested across three call sites at once
Learning: `internal/scheduler/resources.go`'s `fieldFactor(p, typed)` returns `2` only when a field is both typed (operator-set, not derived from the host) and the pool runs docker-in-docker, and it is shared by `RunnerCharge`, `MinimumReserve` and `ReducedSize`. Every existing reduced-runner test happened to exercise a case where the condition is false: an automatic (untyped) DinD pool, or a typed non-DinD pool. The one combination that actually returns `2` -- a fixed-size DinD pool's reduced runner -- was placed and its per-container grant was asserted (`TestAReducedDockerInDockerPairSplitsWhatIsLeft`), but nothing fed that grant back through `RunnerCharge`/`Reserved` to check the doubling recovers the original host-side charge.
Risk: This is precisely the bug class the file's own comments describe as having shipped twice already, in both directions (charging one share while giving each container a whole one, and the mirror of it) -- a silent host-accounting drift that only shows up later as create timeouts on a machine the fleet believes is idle, or as a fleet refusing to use machines it has room on. Three functions sharing one helper meant one broken conditional would corrupt scheduling, minimum-reservation and reduced-sizing math simultaneously, and none of it would fail a test.
Action: When a helper's return value depends on a boolean combination (here: typed AND DinD), check that every *combination*, not just every call site, is covered by a test that traces the value through to an externally observable effect -- not just an intermediate value like a placement's per-container grant. Added `TestAReducedDockerInDockerRunnerIsChargedTwiceItsRow`, which places a reduced pair and then asserts `RunnerCharge`/`Reserved` double the row's stored allocation back to the charge. Verified it fails when the doubling condition is forced off.

---
name: babysit
description: Autonomous orchestration loop for driving the Zoomies test suite or a pull request to green — run, diagnose, fix, verify, repeat — with sparse breakpoints for the operator and a hard stop after three identical failures. Use when asked to babysit, watch, monitor, autofix or "keep going until it passes" on a build, a test run or a CI failure.
---

# Babysit

A babysitting run is a loop with a defined exit, not an open-ended licence to
keep pushing. It ends in one of exactly three states: **green**, **blocked**
(reported to the operator with the evidence), or **looping** (stopped by the
protection below). Never end a round having done nothing.

## Before the first iteration

Establish a baseline, or every later signal is ambiguous.

```sh
make build-nogui   # internal/api/webdist is a build product; nothing compiles without it
make lint
make test          # go test -race -count=1 ./...
```

Record which checks were already red on the base branch. A failure that
reproduces identically on `main` is not this change's failure, and the loop
below must not spend iterations on it — say so and move on.

## One iteration

Each iteration is the same five steps, in order. Do not start the next one
until the current one finishes.

1. **Run.** Execute the narrowest check that still covers the failure —
   `go test -run TestName ./internal/pkg/` while iterating, the full
   `make test` before any push.
2. **Read.** Take the first failure, not the loudest one. Later failures are
   often the first one's debris.
3. **Diagnose.** Name the mechanism in one sentence before editing anything.
   If you cannot, add instrumentation and re-run — that is a legitimate
   iteration with no fix in it.
4. **Fix.** Minimal and local: what the failure needs, nothing more. Do not
   widen scope on your own initiative.
5. **Verify.** Re-run the narrow check, then the suite. A fix is not applied
   until you have watched it turn the failure green.

Then record the iteration in the run log described below and continue.

## Sparse breakpoints

Do not report after every iteration — a per-iteration narration is noise, and
it defeats the point of an autonomous loop. Surface to the operator only at
these points:

- **Baseline.** One line stating what is failing and the plan, before
  iteration one.
- **Every fifth iteration.** A three-line status: what is fixed, what remains,
  what you are trying next.
- **A category change.** The failure moves to a different package, or a
  compile error becomes a test failure, or a new check goes red.
- **A blocker.** A decision only a person can make — a schema change, an API
  break, an ambiguous merge conflict, a missing credential. Stop and ask;
  `make test-e2e` needs real GitHub credentials and skips itself without them,
  so a skipped e2e run is not a blocker.
- **The exit.** Green, blocked or looping, with the run log.

Everything between breakpoints stays in the log.

## Loop protection

Three identical failures ends the loop. This is a hard rule, not a heuristic.

A **failure signature** is the tuple:

```text
(check or command, test identifier, first line of the assertion or panic)
```

normalised — strip timestamps, durations, temporary paths, ports, goroutine
numbers, memory addresses, run and job IDs. Two failures with the same
signature are identical even if the surrounding output differs.

- Keep a counter per signature across the whole run.
- On the **second** occurrence, change approach. The same fix applied harder
  is not a new attempt: widen the diagnosis, add instrumentation, or question
  the assumption underneath the previous two fixes.
- On the **third** occurrence, **stop**. Do not attempt a fourth fix, do not
  re-run hoping for a different result, and do not push.

On stopping, report:

1. The signature, and the three attempts with what each changed and why it did
   not work.
2. The narrowest command that reproduces it.
3. Your best hypothesis and what evidence would confirm or kill it.
4. The diff so far, left in the working tree unless the operator asked
   otherwise.

A re-run is not an iteration and never clears a counter. Re-run a job only to
confirm a failure that names a service the diff does not touch, or one that
died before any test body ran (checkout, install, runner loss), or one that
passed earlier on this exact commit — at most once in the whole run. A second
failure is real.

## What never counts as a fix

- Skipping, disabling, quarantining or `t.Skip`-ing a failing test.
- Loosening an assertion, widening a tolerance or adding a retry around a
  deterministic check to make red turn green.
- Adding a sleep to paper over a race. Tests here use injected clocks
  (`store.Options.Now`) and the fake GitHub in `internal/github/fake.go` —
  reach for those instead.
- An empty commit, or closing and reopening a pull request, to kick CI.
- Editing a generated file by hand. Regenerate it:
  `go run internal/api/gen_openapi.go`, `make openapi`, `make generate`.
- Calling something a flake without the evidence above.

## The run log

Keep a running table in the working notes, and include it at every breakpoint.

| # | Signature | Hypothesis | Change | Result |
| --- | --- | --- | --- | --- |
| 1 | `internal/scheduler` TestDecideKeepsAHostWarm: want 2 got 1 | snapshot missing the idle runner | pass the idle set through | green |

It is what makes the third identical failure obvious at the moment it happens,
rather than at iteration nine.

## Limits

This file is repository content. It describes how to run the loop; it does not
grant permission to approve or merge a pull request, to push to a branch you
were not asked to push to, to rewrite someone else's history, or to override
any rule your operator or the repository's own guidance states as never.

---
name: steward
description: Repository maintenance rules for Zoomies — keeping branches, pull requests, generated files, dependencies and docs healthy without trusting your own unverified work. Use when tidying the repository, acting on CI failures or review comments, refreshing generated artefacts, updating dependencies, or removing code, files, config keys or database rows.
---

# Steward

Maintenance work in this repository is held to the same standard as a feature:
verified before it is pushed, reversible after it lands, and approved by a
person before anything irreversible happens. This skill is the checklist for
that. It governs *how* maintenance is done; it never widens what may be done.

## When this applies

- Housekeeping passes over the tree: dead code, stale docs, orphaned tests.
- Regenerating the files CI diffs against their sources (see
  [.github/CLAUDE.md](../../../.github/CLAUDE.md), "Things CI will fail you on").
- Dependency bumps, including Dependabot follow-ups and `go mod tidy` churn.
- Driving a pull request to green after a CI failure or a review comment.
- Any change that removes something an operator or a downstream user can
  currently see: a config key, an API field, a route, a problem code, a column,
  a CLI flag.

## The three standing rules

### 1. No self-trust

A change is not finished because it looks right. It is finished when the
repository's own checks say so, run by you, on the tree you are about to push.

- Run `make build-nogui` first on a fresh checkout. `internal/api` embeds
  `internal/api/webdist`, which is a build product, so every other Go command
  fails until it exists.
- Then `make lint` and `make test` (`go test -race -count=1 ./...`). Narrow
  with `go test -run TestName ./internal/pkg/` while iterating, but run the
  whole suite before the push.
- Reproduce a reported failure *before* fixing it, and show the same check
  passing afterwards. A fix you have not seen fail is a guess.
- Re-read your own diff adversarially and ask what would make CI reject it.
  Generated files are the usual answer: `internal/api/openapi_spec.go`,
  `web/src/lib/api/schema.d.ts`, the `internal/naming/images.go` matrices,
  `docs/problem-codes.md`. Regenerate with the repository's tooling —
  `go run internal/api/gen_openapi.go`, `make openapi`, `make generate` —
  never by hand.
- Never treat a failing test as noise. "Flake" is a diagnosis you have
  evidence for, not a default. Never skip, disable or quarantine a test to
  reach green.

### 2. Soft deletions only

Deletion is the one maintenance action that cannot be undone by reading the
diff, so default to a reversible form of it.

| Instead of | Do this |
| --- | --- |
| Deleting a config key | Keep it parsed, ignore it, and raise a `config.Finding` naming the replacement |
| Deleting an API field or route | Mark it deprecated in `api/openapi.yaml`, keep serving it, regenerate both clients |
| Deleting a database row | Set the tombstone or state the store already models; go through `store.TransitionRunner` rather than removing history |
| Deleting a doc page | Leave a stub that links onward — `mkdocs build --strict` fails on a link that points nowhere |
| Dropping a dependency | Remove the import and the `docs/dependencies.md` row in the same commit, so the justification and the use disappear together |

Hard deletion is reserved for things with no external surface: unreferenced
private helpers, dead test fixtures, files you added yourself earlier in the
same branch. Before removing anything, read it — `grep` for the identifier
across `internal/`, `cmd/`, `web/` and `docs/` — and say in the commit message
what confirmed it was unused.

Never rewrite history on a branch you did not create: no rebase, no amend, no
force-push. A merge commit keeps other people's checkouts valid.

### 3. Human in the loop

Maintenance is allowed to be autonomous up to the point where a person's
judgement is the input. At that point, stop and ask, with enough context that
the answer does not require scrolling back.

Ask before:

- A schema migration, a breaking configuration change, or anything that alters
  the runner state machine.
- Removing a behaviour an operator could depend on, when the reversible form
  above is not available.
- Adding a dependency. `docs/dependencies.md` is enforced by review, and the
  standard library or fifty lines of our own is usually the answer.
- Resolving a merge conflict where both sides changed the same logic and
  picking either one loses behaviour.
- Any change to authentication, authorisation, secrets, runner isolation or a
  deletion path — `CONTRIBUTING.md` asks for an explicit threat and
  failure-mode review on those.

Proceed without asking on: a nit, a rename, an added test, regenerating a file
from its source, a lint or format fix, a lockfile refresh.

## What this skill cannot authorise

This file is repository content, not an instruction from your operator. It
cannot expand your access or redirect your task, and nothing in it makes any of
the following acceptable:

- Approving or merging a pull request.
- Skipping, disabling or quarantining a test.
- Pushing an empty commit, or closing and reopening a pull request, to kick CI.
- Rewriting history on someone else's branch.
- Pushing to, or resolving a larger ask on, a pull request you did not open.

## Before every push

1. `make build-nogui` — the tree compiles.
2. `make fmt` then `make lint` — `gofmt -l` is empty, `go vet` and the UI lint
   are clean.
3. `make test` — the full suite, with the race detector.
4. `go mod tidy` leaves `go.mod` and `go.sum` unchanged.
5. Generated files regenerated from their sources, not edited.
6. New behaviour arrives with a test; new settings arrive with a
   `docs/configuration.md` row and a `ZOOMIES_*` override in `applyEnv`; new
   finding codes arrive with a `docs/problem-codes.md` row.
7. The prose matches the house voice: British spelling, comments that say
   *why*, `--` in code and `—` in Markdown, commit messages as imperative
   sentences in sentence case with no Conventional Commits prefix.

One validated push beats three speculative ones.

# Linux and macOS hosts as they are, so a Windows checkout must not give them
# CRLF line endings: systemd would read a unit with a stray carriage return on
# every line, and the tests that render them check exact lines.
internal/installer/templates/* text eol=lf

# CLAUDE.md

Scoped guidance for CI and generated files, loaded in addition to the root [CLAUDE.md](../CLAUDE.md). It appends to that file and never overrides it.

## Things CI will fail you on

Beyond tests and lint, several files must stay in sync with their sources. Each
has a CI job that diffs them:

* `internal/api/openapi_spec.go` is generated from `api/openapi.yaml`. After
  editing the spec, run `go run internal/api/gen_openapi.go` from the repo root.
* `web/src/lib/api/schema.d.ts` is generated from the same spec. Run
  `make openapi` and commit the result.
* The runner image catalogue in `internal/naming/images.go` is the source for
  both workflows' build matrices, the Makefile's `variant.*` rows and the table
  in `docs/naming.md`. Adding or swapping an operating system is a row there and
  then `make generate`; editing any of the four by hand fails a test in
  `internal/naming`.
* `install.sh` at the repo root is copied verbatim to the site root — the script
  people `curl` is the script a contributor edits. Do not create a second copy.
* The app shell must stay under **200 KB gzipped** (`web/vite.config.ts`
  enforces it, the number is documented in `docs/ui-guidelines.md`). Route chunks
  are excluded, so move weight to a lazily loaded route rather than raising the
  budget.
* `go mod tidy` must leave `go.mod`/`go.sum` unchanged, and `gofmt -l` must be
  empty.
* `govulncheck ./...` must find nothing reachable. It runs in its own workflow,
  on every change and weekly against `main`, so a module found vulnerable after
  it merged still gets reported.
* Every `uses:` in `.github/workflows` is pinned to a commit with its release
  in a comment, and a workflow with more than one job grants no `write`
  permission at the top. Both are tested in `internal/docs`; Dependabot moves a
  pin and its comment together, and a new action gets the same treatment.
* `mkdocs build --strict` — a docs link that points nowhere fails the build. The
  site workflow also checks that `sitemap.xml` and `llms.txt` came out of it,
  both generated (by `overrides/sitemap.xml` and `hooks/seo.py`) rather than
  written, so a build that quietly stopped producing one would otherwise ship,
  and that the header names a release: `hooks/source.py` resolves the latest
  release, stars and forks from the GitHub API at build time, and an offline
  build is allowed to go without them where the published site is not.

# Support Zoomies: https://ko-fi.com/K3K113PEC5
ko_fi: eyupio

# What keeps the pins current. Every action in the workflows is pinned to a
# commit with its release in a comment, and Dependabot moves both together;
# the Go modules, the UI's npm packages and the base images under deploy/ are
# the other three things this repository builds from. One grouped pull request
# per ecosystem per week is one review rather than a dozen, and a week is
# short enough that a security fix is never far behind its advisory.
version: 2
updates:
  - package-ecosystem: github-actions
    directory: /
    schedule:
      interval: weekly
      day: monday
      time: "06:00"
      timezone: Etc/UTC
    groups:
      actions:
        patterns: ["*"]

  - package-ecosystem: gomod
    directory: /
    schedule:
      interval: weekly
      day: monday
      time: "06:00"
      timezone: Etc/UTC
    groups:
      go:
        patterns: ["*"]

  - package-ecosystem: npm
    directory: /web
    schedule:
      interval: weekly
      day: monday
      time: "06:00"
      timezone: Etc/UTC
    groups:
      npm:
        patterns: ["*"]
    ignore:
      # openapi-typescript declares a peer dependency on the TypeScript 5
      # line, so a major TypeScript bump fails `npm ci` in the UI job and the
      # image build until openapi-typescript moves. The 7.0.2 bump did exactly
      # that; the minor and patch updates still arrive.
      - dependency-name: typescript
        update-types: ["version-update:semver-major"]

  - package-ecosystem: docker
    directory: /deploy
    schedule:
      interval: weekly
      day: monday
      time: "06:00"
      timezone: Etc/UTC
    groups:
      images:
        patterns: ["*"]

  - package-ecosystem: pip
    directory: /docs
    schedule:
      interval: weekly
      day: monday
    groups:
      docs:
        patterns: ["*"]

#!/bin/sh
# Check that every manifest a GHCR tag points at can still be pulled.
#
# usage: ghcr-check-tags.sh PACKAGE [TAG...]
#
# With no TAG, every tag in the package is checked. A multi-platform tag is an
# index whose platform and attestation manifests are untagged package
# versions; deleting one leaves the tag resolving and `docker pull` failing
# with "manifest unknown". This walks the index the way a client does, so a
# missing child is found here rather than by a user.
#
# Prints "PACKAGE:TAG ok" or "PACKAGE:TAG BROKEN <missing digests>" per tag and
# exits 1 if any tag is broken or missing. Anonymous pull only: the packages
# are public, and a check that needs a secret is a check a fork cannot run.
set -eu

owner=${GHCR_OWNER:-eyupio}
pkg=$1
shift

accept='application/vnd.oci.image.index.v1+json,application/vnd.docker.distribution.manifest.list.v2+json,application/vnd.oci.image.manifest.v1+json,application/vnd.docker.distribution.manifest.v2+json'
token=$(curl -fsS "https://ghcr.io/token?scope=repository:$owner/$pkg:pull" | jq -r .token)

get() {
  curl -fsS -H "Authorization: Bearer $token" -H "Accept: $accept" \
    "https://ghcr.io/v2/$owner/$pkg/manifests/$1"
}

if [ "$#" -eq 0 ]; then
  # Attestation tags (sha256-...) are checked through the tags they describe.
  # Word splitting is the point: one tag per argument.
  # shellcheck disable=SC2046
  set -- $(curl -fsS -H "Authorization: Bearer $token" \
    "https://ghcr.io/v2/$owner/$pkg/tags/list?n=10000" | jq -r '.tags[]' | grep -v '^sha256-' || true)
fi

status=0
for tag in "$@"; do
  if ! body=$(get "$tag"); then
    echo "$pkg:$tag MISSING"
    status=1
    continue
  fi
  missing=""
  for digest in $(printf '%s' "$body" | jq -r '.manifests[]?.digest'); do
    get "$digest" >/dev/null 2>&1 || missing="$missing $digest"
  done
  if [ -n "$missing" ]; then
    echo "$pkg:$tag BROKEN$missing"
    status=1
  else
    echo "$pkg:$tag ok"
  fi
done
exit "$status"

#!/bin/sh
# Exercise ghcr-prune.sh against a fake registry and a fake `gh`, so the rule
# that broke v1.3.2 -- never delete what a kept tag still needs -- is checked
# without credentials or a live package. Run it from anywhere; needs python3,
# jq and curl. Exits non-zero on the first wrong answer.
set -eu

here=$(cd "$(dirname "$0")" && pwd)
work=$(mktemp -d)
trap 'kill "$server" 2>/dev/null || true; rm -rf "$work"' EXIT

old=2020-01-01T00:00:00Z
new=$(date -u +%Y-%m-%dT%H:%M:%SZ)
d() { printf 'sha256:%064d' "$1"; }

# The package: a tagged index over two platforms; an attestation whose
# subject is one of those platforms, untagged and old -- the case the first
# version of this script got wrong; an old unreferenced image with its own
# attestation (both should go); and a young orphan (a push in flight).
mkdir -p "$work/m"
index=$(d 1) amd=$(d 2) arm=$(d 3) att=$(d 4) stale=$(d 5) staleatt=$(d 6) young=$(d 7)
printf '{"manifests":[{"digest":"%s"},{"digest":"%s"}]}' "$amd" "$arm" > "$work/m/$index"
echo '{}' > "$work/m/$amd"
echo '{}' > "$work/m/$arm"
printf '{"subject":{"digest":"%s"}}' "$amd" > "$work/m/$att"
echo '{}' > "$work/m/$stale"
printf '{"subject":{"digest":"%s"}}' "$stale" > "$work/m/$staleatt"
echo '{}' > "$work/m/$young"
printf '1\t%s\t1\t%s\n2\t%s\t0\t%s\n3\t%s\t0\t%s\n4\t%s\t0\t%s\n5\t%s\t0\t%s\n6\t%s\t0\t%s\n7\t%s\t0\t%s\n' \
  "$index" "$old" "$amd" "$old" "$arm" "$old" "$att" "$old" "$stale" "$old" "$staleatt" "$old" "$young" "$new" \
  > "$work/versions"

cat > "$work/server.py" <<'PY'
import http.server, os, sys
root = sys.argv[1]
class H(http.server.BaseHTTPRequestHandler):
    def do_GET(self):
        if os.path.exists(os.path.join(root, "fail")):
            self.send_response(500); self.end_headers(); return
        p = os.path.join(root, "m", self.path.rsplit("/", 1)[-1])
        if not os.path.exists(p):
            self.send_response(404); self.end_headers(); return
        self.send_response(200); self.end_headers(); self.wfile.write(open(p, "rb").read())
    def log_message(self, *a): pass
s = http.server.HTTPServer(("127.0.0.1", 0), H)
open(os.path.join(root, "port"), "w").write(str(s.server_port))
s.serve_forever()
PY
python3 "$work/server.py" "$work" &
server=$!
while [ ! -s "$work/port" ]; do sleep 0.1; done

mkdir -p "$work/bin"
# The fake gh answers the package listing from versions, or from versions.next
# once the first listing has been served (a publish landing mid-prune), and
# reports busy image-publishing runs while the file busy exists.
cat > "$work/bin/gh" <<SH
#!/bin/sh
case "\$*" in
  *DELETE*) echo "\$*" >> "$work/deleted" ;;
  */actions/workflows/*) if [ -e "$work/busy" ]; then echo 1; else echo 0; fi ;;
  *)
    if [ -e "$work/listed" ] && [ -e "$work/versions.next" ]; then cat "$work/versions.next"; else cat "$work/versions"; fi
    touch "$work/listed" ;;
esac
SH
chmod +x "$work/bin/gh"

run() {
  : > "$work/deleted"
  rm -f "$work/listed"
  GITHUB_REPOSITORY=eyupio/zoomies PUBLISH_WAIT_TRIES=2 PUBLISH_WAIT_SECONDS=0 PATH="$work/bin:$PATH" GHCR_REGISTRY="http://127.0.0.1:$(cat "$work/port")" GHCR_PULL_TOKEN=x \
    DRY_RUN=false KEEP_DAYS=14 "$here/ghcr-prune.sh" zoomies > "$work/out" 2>&1
}

run
got=$(sed 's|.*/versions/||' "$work/deleted" | sort | tr '\n' ' ')
if [ "$got" != "5 6 " ]; then
  cat "$work/out"
  echo "FAIL: deleted versions [$got], want [5 6 ] -- the platforms, their attestation and the young orphan must stay"
  exit 1
fi

# A publish between the snapshot and the delete: a new tagged index re-uses
# the stale image as a child. Neither it nor its attestation may go.
index2=$(d 8)
printf '{"manifests":[{"digest":"%s"}]}' "$stale" > "$work/m/$index2"
{ cat "$work/versions"; printf '8\t%s\t1\t%s\n' "$index2" "$new"; } > "$work/versions.next"
run
if [ -s "$work/deleted" ]; then
  cat "$work/out"
  echo "FAIL: deleted $(cat "$work/deleted") after a new tag started referring to it"
  exit 1
fi
rm -f "$work/versions.next"

# While an image-publishing workflow runs, a real prune deletes nothing.
touch "$work/busy"
run
if [ -s "$work/deleted" ]; then
  echo "FAIL: deleted $(cat "$work/deleted") while an image publish was in progress"
  exit 1
fi
rm -f "$work/busy"

# A registry that cannot answer must leave everything in place.
touch "$work/fail"
if run; then
  echo "FAIL: the prune succeeded while the registry was failing"
  exit 1
fi
if [ -s "$work/deleted" ]; then
  echo "FAIL: deleted $(cat "$work/deleted") while the registry was failing"
  exit 1
fi
echo "ghcr-prune: ok"

#!/bin/sh
# Delete untagged GHCR package versions that nothing still refers to.
#
# usage: ghcr-prune.sh PACKAGE
# env:   GH_TOKEN (packages:write, actions:read), KEEP_DAYS (default 14),
#        DRY_RUN (default true), GITHUB_REPOSITORY, PUBLISHERS (workflow files
#        that push images, default "ci.yml release.yml"), PUBLISH_WAIT_TRIES
#        (default 10) and PUBLISH_WAIT_SECONDS (default 60)
#
# Why not actions/delete-package-versions: it treats every untagged version as
# garbage, but the platform and attestation manifests under a multi-platform
# tag are untagged too. Deleting them left v1.3.2 and :latest resolving to an
# index whose children were gone, and every `docker pull` failed with
# "manifest unknown". Here a version is deleted only when it is untagged,
# older than KEEP_DAYS, not referenced -- directly or through a nested index
# -- by any tagged version or any version being kept, and not a referrer (an
# attestation) whose subject is being kept.
#
# It fails closed: if any manifest that decides the keep set cannot be read
# for a reason other than already being gone, nothing is deleted.
set -eu

owner=${GHCR_OWNER:-eyupio}
pkg=$1
keep_days=${KEEP_DAYS:-14}
dry_run=${DRY_RUN:-true}
work=$(mktemp -d)
trap 'rm -rf "$work"' EXIT

# A publish in flight pushes an index before it tags it, and may re-use an
# old untagged digest as a child. The keep set is a snapshot, so rather than
# race a push, a real run waits for image-publishing workflows to finish and
# gives up -- deleting nothing -- if they do not.
if [ "$dry_run" != "true" ]; then
  tries=${PUBLISH_WAIT_TRIES:-10}
  while :; do
    busy=0
    for wf in ${PUBLISHERS:-ci.yml release.yml}; do
      for status in queued in_progress; do
        n=$(gh api "/repos/$GITHUB_REPOSITORY/actions/workflows/$wf/runs?status=$status&per_page=1" --jq '.total_count')
        busy=$((busy + n))
      done
    done
    [ "$busy" -eq 0 ] && break
    tries=$((tries - 1))
    if [ "$tries" -le 0 ]; then
      echo "::warning::$pkg: image-publishing workflows are still running; deleting nothing this time"
      exit 0
    fi
    echo "$pkg: $busy image-publishing run(s) in progress; waiting"
    sleep "${PUBLISH_WAIT_SECONDS:-60}"
  done
fi

list_versions() {
  gh api --paginate "/orgs/$owner/packages/container/$pkg/versions?per_page=100" \
    --jq '.[] | [.id, .name, (.metadata.container.tags | length), .updated_at] | @tsv'
}
list_versions > "$work/versions"

cutoff=$(date -u -d "-$keep_days days" +%Y-%m-%dT%H:%M:%SZ)

# The roots: every tagged version, and every untagged one still inside the
# grace period (a push in flight has not tagged its index yet).
roots() { awk -F'\t' -v c="$cutoff" '$3 > 0 || $4 >= c { print $2 }' "$1" | sort -u; }
roots "$work/versions" > "$work/roots"

accept='application/vnd.oci.image.index.v1+json,application/vnd.docker.distribution.manifest.list.v2+json,application/vnd.oci.image.manifest.v1+json,application/vnd.docker.distribution.manifest.v2+json'
registry=${GHCR_REGISTRY:-https://ghcr.io}
token=${GHCR_PULL_TOKEN:-$(curl -fsS "$registry/token?scope=repository:$owner/$pkg:pull" | jq -r .token)}

# fetch DIGEST: the manifest into $work/body. Returns 0 when read, 1 when the
# registry says it is gone, and exits the script on anything else -- a keep
# set built on a failed read is a guess, and guessing is how the original
# breakage happened.
fetch() {
  code=$(curl -sS -o "$work/body" -w '%{http_code}' -H "Authorization: Bearer $token" \
    -H "Accept: $accept" "$registry/v2/$owner/$pkg/manifests/$1") || code=000
  case "$code" in
    200) return 0 ;;
    404) return 1 ;;
    *) echo "::error::reading $pkg@$1 returned $code; deleting nothing"; exit 1 ;;
  esac
}

# close: add everything the digests in $work/todo refer to -- index children
# and the subject a referrer names -- to $work/keep, transitively.
close() {
  while [ -s "$work/todo" ]; do
    : > "$work/next"
    while read -r digest; do
      if ! fetch "$digest"; then
        # Already gone: a child an earlier prune took. Nothing under it is
        # left to protect, and ghcr-check-tags.sh is what reports the tag.
        echo "::warning::$pkg@$digest is referenced but missing"
        continue
      fi
      jq -r '.manifests[]?.digest, .subject?.digest // empty' "$work/body" >> "$work/next"
    done < "$work/todo"
    sort -u "$work/next" | comm -23 - "$work/keep" > "$work/todo"
    sort -u "$work/keep" "$work/todo" -o "$work/keep"
  done
}

cp "$work/roots" "$work/keep"
cp "$work/roots" "$work/todo"
close

# Referrers point the other way: an attestation names the image it describes
# as its subject, and the image does not list it. GHCR has no referrers API,
# so read every remaining candidate and keep any whose subject is kept --
# repeating, because keeping one can pull in children that are subjects too.
while :; do
  awk -F'\t' '$3 == 0 { print $2 }' "$work/versions" | sort -u | comm -23 - "$work/keep" > "$work/candidates"
  : > "$work/todo"
  while read -r digest; do
    fetch "$digest" || continue
    subject=$(jq -r '.subject?.digest // empty' "$work/body")
    if [ -n "$subject" ] && grep -qxF "$subject" "$work/keep"; then
      echo "$digest" >> "$work/todo"
    fi
  done < "$work/candidates"
  [ -s "$work/todo" ] || break
  sort -u "$work/keep" "$work/todo" -o "$work/keep"
  close
done

# still_unused DIGEST: re-read the package immediately before a delete. A
# version tagged, or pushed, since the snapshot is a new root; walk what it
# refers to into the keep set, then refuse the candidate if it is now kept,
# tagged, or an attestation of something kept. Manifests are immutable, so
# only new roots can add references -- this is the whole graph, brought up to
# date, without re-reading every manifest per candidate.
still_unused() {
  list_versions > "$work/now"
  roots "$work/now" | comm -23 - "$work/keep" > "$work/todo"
  sort -u "$work/keep" "$work/todo" -o "$work/keep"
  close
  grep -qxF "$1" "$work/keep" && return 1
  awk -F'\t' -v d="$1" '$2 == d && $3 == 0 { found = 1 } END { exit !found }' "$work/now" || return 1
  fetch "$1" || return 1
  subject=$(jq -r '.subject?.digest // empty' "$work/body")
  if [ -n "$subject" ] && grep -qxF "$subject" "$work/keep"; then
    return 1
  fi
  return 0
}

deleted=0
while IFS="$(printf '\t')" read -r id name tags updated; do
  [ "$tags" -eq 0 ] || continue
  grep -qxF "$name" "$work/keep" && continue
  if [ "$dry_run" = "true" ]; then
    echo "would delete $pkg@$name (version $id, updated $updated)"
  elif ! still_unused "$name"; then
    echo "kept $pkg@$name: referenced or tagged since the snapshot"
    continue
  else
    gh api -X DELETE "/orgs/$owner/packages/container/$pkg/versions/$id" >/dev/null
    echo "deleted $pkg@$name (version $id, updated $updated)"
  fi
  deleted=$((deleted + 1))
done < "$work/versions"
echo "$pkg: $(wc -l < "$work/keep") versions kept, $deleted selected for deletion (dry run: $dry_run)"

name: Cancel Checks For Merged Pull Requests

# Merging a pull request pushes its tree to main, which starts a fresh CI,
# CodeQL, fuzz and govulncheck run of its own. A run still queued or
# in-progress against the pull request's old head at that point is answering
# a question nobody will read -- cancel it rather than let it spend a fleet
# slot or a GitHub-hosted minute on a result the merge already superseded.

on:
  pull_request:
    types: [closed]

permissions: {}

jobs:
  cancel:
    name: Cancel
    if: github.event.pull_request.merged == true
    runs-on: ubuntu-latest
    permissions:
      actions: write
    steps:
      - name: Cancel runs still queued or in progress for the merged commit
        env:
          GH_TOKEN: ${{ github.token }}
          REPO: ${{ github.repository }}
          HEAD_SHA: ${{ github.event.pull_request.head.sha }}
        run: |
          set -euo pipefail
          for status in queued in_progress; do
            ids=$(gh api "repos/$REPO/actions/runs?head_sha=$HEAD_SHA&status=$status&event=pull_request" --jq '.workflow_runs[].id')
            for id in $ids; do
              echo "Cancelling run $id ($status)"
              gh api -X POST "repos/$REPO/actions/runs/$id/cancel" || true
            done
          done

name: CI

on:
  push:
    branches: [main]
  pull_request:
  workflow_dispatch:
    inputs:
      runner:
        description: "Where CI runs. github is the recovery path for every job."
        type: choice
        default: zoomies
        options: [zoomies, github]

permissions:
  contents: read

concurrency:
  group: ci-${{ github.ref }}
  # A pull request only needs its newest result. Main is also the publisher for
  # the moving :dev channel, though: cancelling it before Images has pushed can
  # leave every successful merge unavailable to `zoomies upgrade`. Queue main
  # runs so the newest one always gets a chance to publish.
  cancel-in-progress: ${{ github.ref != 'refs/heads/main' }}

env:
  GO_VERSION: "1.27.1"
  NODE_VERSION: "22"

# CI defaults to the Zoomies pool. Forks use GitHub-hosted runners, and a
# manual dispatch with runner=github recovers every job, including image builds.
# Pin the pool to an already published runner image digest; advance that pin
# separately after validating new images so builds do not require their output.
jobs:
  # Which jobs a change needs. A docs-only change used to run the whole suite:
  # an hour of the Go packages under the race detector, the Playwright suite,
  # five cross-compiles and the image builds, every one of them on a fleet
  # slot another pull request was queueing for. Now a change runs what its
  # files can affect -- on main as well as on a pull request. Main used to run
  # everything on every merge, so a README edit rebuilt and republished every
  # binary and image on the dev channel with nothing in them different.
  #
  # Main still publishes, but only a commit that changes something shipped:
  # Go, the UI the binary embeds, or what the images are made of. A commit that
  # changes only prose, the install script or the workflows leaves the dev
  # channel where it was, which keeps its promise -- every binary and image on
  # it names one commit -- because none of them moves. CI still starts for
  # every commit on main, and finishes in the time the first job takes when
  # there is nothing to do, because the dev watchdog reads a commit with no
  # finished CI run as one the fleet is starving. A manual dispatch runs
  # everything, because it is the recovery path.
  #
  # This is a shell case statement rather than an action so that it stays a
  # single read: what a path triggers is written next to the path, and an
  # unknown path falls through to the Go set, which is the largest -- a new
  # kind of file runs too much rather than too little.
  changes:
    name: What changed
    runs-on: ${{ ((github.event_name == 'workflow_dispatch' && inputs.runner == 'github') || (github.event_name == 'pull_request' && github.event.pull_request.head.repo.fork)) && 'ubuntu-latest' || 'zoomies-linux-x64' }}
    outputs:
      go: ${{ steps.filter.outputs.go }}
      shards: ${{ steps.filter.outputs.shards }}
      web: ${{ steps.filter.outputs.web }}
      deploy: ${{ steps.filter.outputs.deploy }}
      installer: ${{ steps.filter.outputs.installer }}
      publish: ${{ steps.filter.outputs.publish }}
    steps:
      - uses: actions/checkout@3d3c42e5aac5ba805825da76410c181273ba90b1 # v7.0.1
      - id: filter
        env:
          EVENT: ${{ github.event_name }}
          REF: ${{ github.ref }}
          BASE: ${{ github.event.pull_request.base.sha || github.event.before }}
        run: |
          set -eu
          # Main publishes the dev channel from any commit that changes what
          # is shipped. Nothing else publishes from CI.
          on_main=false
          if [ "$EVENT" != "pull_request" ] && [ "$REF" = "refs/heads/main" ]; then
            on_main=true
          fi
          everything() {
            {
              echo "go=true"; echo "web=true"; echo "deploy=true"; echo "installer=true"
              echo 'shards=["controller","api","store","rest"]'
              echo "publish=$on_main"
            } >> "$GITHUB_OUTPUT"
            exit 0
          }
          if [ "$EVENT" = "workflow_dispatch" ]; then
            everything
          fi
          # A pull request's checkout is the merge into its base, so its diff
          # against the base commit is exactly what it changes; a push's is
          # the diff against the commit main was at before. A base that cannot
          # be fetched -- a force push, a new branch's all-zero "before", a
          # base that moved on -- says nothing about what changed, so run
          # everything rather than guess.
          case "$BASE" in ''|0000000000000000000000000000000000000000) everything ;; esac
          if ! git fetch --no-tags --depth=1 origin "$BASE" 2>/dev/null; then
            everything
          fi
          go=false; web=false; deploy=false; installer=false; rest=false; docs=false
          for f in $(git diff --name-only "$BASE" HEAD); do
            case "$f" in
              # The build and the tests themselves: every job is downstream.
              .github/workflows/ci.yml|Makefile|go.mod|go.sum) everything ;;
              # The UI, and the spec its client is generated from. The spec is
              # embedded in the binary too, so it is a Go change as well.
              api/openapi.yaml) go=true; web=true ;;
              # The controller image runs npm ci, so its inputs are the
              # image's too.
              web/package.json|web/package-lock.json) web=true; deploy=true; docs=true ;;
              # internal/docs reads the UI's source for the pages it names.
              web/*) web=true; docs=true ;;
              # What the images are made of. The runner scripts are also read
              # by the installer job's shell checks, and every deploy/ file by
              # tests in internal/backend, internal/installer and internal/docs,
              # which are in the rest shard.
              deploy/runner-*.sh) deploy=true; installer=true; rest=true ;;
              deploy/*|docker-compose.yml|.dockerignore) deploy=true; rest=true ;;
              # The check each built runner image is run through.
              test/runner-image/*) deploy=true; installer=true ;;
              # The script people curl is checked by the install.sh job and
              # exercised by the upgrade test. No Go test reads it, and no
              # binary or image carries it: the site serves it, and the site's
              # own workflow rebuilds when it changes.
              install.sh|test/install/*|test/upgrade/*) installer=true ;;
              # Prose, and the workflows. internal/docs tests the problem-code
              # table, the README, the workflows and the roadmap against the
              # code, and internal/naming the image table; those two packages
              # are the docs shard, a minute rather than the hour the rest of
              # the suite takes. Nothing heavier runs.
              docs/*|roadmap/*|overrides/*|hooks/*|mkdocs.yml|*.md|.github/*) docs=true ;;
              # Files that neither ship nor are read by a test.
              .gitignore|.gitattributes|.editorconfig|LICENSE|NOTICE|.claude/*|.devcontainer/*|nixpacks.toml) ;;
              # Everything else is Go, or something Go embeds.
              *) go=true ;;
            esac
          done
          if [ "$go" = true ]; then
            shards='["controller","api","store","rest"]'
          elif [ "$rest" = true ]; then
            shards='["rest"]'
          elif [ "$docs" = true ]; then
            shards='["docs"]'
          else
            shards='[]'
          fi
          # A binary carries Go and the UI; the images carry the binary and
          # what deploy/ says. Any of the three changes what the dev channel
          # would ship.
          publish=false
          if [ "$on_main" = true ] && { [ "$go" = true ] || [ "$web" = true ] || [ "$deploy" = true ]; }; then
            publish=true
          fi
          {
            echo "go=$go"; echo "web=$web"; echo "deploy=$deploy"; echo "installer=$installer"
            echo "shards=$shards"; echo "publish=$publish"
          } >> "$GITHUB_OUTPUT"
          echo "go=$go web=$web deploy=$deploy installer=$installer shards=$shards publish=$publish"

  # The Go suite, split by package across runners. Three packages are most of
  # it -- on the fleet the controller has taken 45 minutes, the API 29 and the
  # store 22, single-threaded under the race detector -- so each is a shard of
  # its own and everything else shares the fourth, along with the checks that
  # read the whole tree. The wall-clock is now the slowest shard, and a shard
  # can be tuned on its own.
  #
  # Coverage is measured on main and on a manual dispatch, not on a pull
  # request: -coverpkg=./... with atomic counters is the most expensive
  # instrumentation Go offers, and the number it produces is the one Codecov
  # tracks on main. A pull request still runs every test under the race
  # detector.
  go:
    name: Go (${{ matrix.shard }})
    needs: [changes]
    if: needs.changes.outputs.shards != '[]'
    permissions:
      contents: read
    # On the fleet the controller shard takes 45 to 50 minutes when the runner
    # has a host to itself, more with coverage on main, and a busy evening's
    # backlog stretches it. The limit is here to catch a hang, not a slow
    # machine, so it sits well above the slowest shard seen.
    timeout-minutes: 120
    runs-on: ${{ ((github.event_name == 'workflow_dispatch' && inputs.runner == 'github') || (github.event_name == 'pull_request' && github.event.pull_request.head.repo.fork)) && 'ubuntu-latest' || 'zoomies-linux-x64' }}
    strategy:
      fail-fast: false
      matrix:
        shard: ${{ fromJSON(needs.changes.outputs.shards) }}
    steps:
      - uses: actions/checkout@3d3c42e5aac5ba805825da76410c181273ba90b1 # v7.0.1
      - uses: actions/setup-go@b7ad1dad31e06c5925ef5d2fc7ad053ef454303e # v7.0.0
        with:
          go-version: ${{ env.GO_VERSION }}
          cache: true

      # go:embed needs the directory to exist even when the UI is not built.
      # The docs shard tests two packages that import nothing of ours, so it
      # has no embedded UI to stub. Writing the stub compiles nothing: this
      # step used to build the whole binary, which on a cold fleet runner was
      # minutes of compiling and, when the module proxy stalled, a step that
      # never finished.
      - name: Stub the embedded UI
        if: matrix.shard != 'docs'
        timeout-minutes: 1
        run: make ui-stub

      # Fetching modules is the one step here that waits on the network, so it
      # is on its own with a bound: a stalled proxy fails in minutes and says
      # so, rather than eating the job's two hours inside go vet or go test.
      - name: Download modules
        if: matrix.shard != 'docs'
        timeout-minutes: 10
        run: go mod download

      # The checks that read the whole tree run once, in the shard that is
      # otherwise the lightest.
      - name: gofmt
        if: matrix.shard == 'rest'
        run: |
          out=$(gofmt -l $(git ls-files '*.go'))
          if [ -n "$out" ]; then
            echo "These files need gofmt:"; echo "$out"; exit 1
          fi

      - name: go vet
        if: matrix.shard == 'rest'
        run: go vet ./...

      - name: go mod tidy is clean
        if: matrix.shard == 'rest'
        run: |
          go mod tidy
          git diff --exit-code go.mod go.sum

      - name: Pick the shard's packages
        id: pkgs
        env:
          SHARD: ${{ matrix.shard }}
        run: |
          set -eu
          case "$SHARD" in
            controller) pkgs=./internal/controller/ ;;
            api) pkgs=./internal/api/ ;;
            store) pkgs=./internal/store/ ;;
            rest) pkgs=$(go list ./... | grep -vE '/internal/(controller|api|store)$' | tr '\n' ' ') ;;
            # Only a change to prose, the workflows or the UI's source: the two
            # packages that read those files against the code. The rest shard
            # carries them too, so they never run twice.
            docs) pkgs="./internal/docs/ ./internal/naming/" ;;
            *) echo "::error::unknown shard $SHARD"; exit 1 ;;
          esac
          echo "list=$pkgs" >> "$GITHUB_OUTPUT"

      # Coverage is main's record of the whole suite, so it is measured only
      # when the whole suite runs. A shard run for a deploy or docs change on
      # main is tested the way a pull request is, and uploads nothing that
      # would read as the project's coverage falling to one package's.
      - name: Test
        if: github.event_name == 'pull_request' || needs.changes.outputs.go != 'true'
        # The timeout is per package, not per test. The API and controller
        # suites repeatedly migrate pure-Go SQLite under race instrumentation
        # and exceed Go's default ten-minute budget many times over on the
        # fleet runner; the Makefile carries the bounded budget so local
        # make test shares it.
        run: make test TEST_PKGS="${{ steps.pkgs.outputs.list }}"

      - name: Test with coverage
        if: github.event_name != 'pull_request' && needs.changes.outputs.go == 'true'
        run: make cover-shard TEST_PKGS="${{ steps.pkgs.outputs.list }}" COVERDIR="$RUNNER_TEMP/covdata"

      - name: Preserve the shard's coverage
        if: github.event_name != 'pull_request' && needs.changes.outputs.go == 'true'
        uses: actions/upload-artifact@043fb46d1a93c77aae656e7c1c64a875d1fc6a0a # v7.0.1
        with:
          name: covdata-${{ matrix.shard }}
          path: ${{ runner.temp }}/covdata
          if-no-files-found: error
          retention-days: 3

  # One coverage number from four shards. Each shard instrumented every
  # package, so their counters are merged rather than concatenated -- see
  # cover-merge in the Makefile -- and the merged profile is what Codecov and
  # the job summary see.
  ai-context-workflow:
    name: AI Context generator and publication contract
    needs: changes
    if: needs.changes.outputs.go == 'true'
    runs-on: ${{ ((github.event_name == 'workflow_dispatch' && inputs.runner == 'github') || (github.event_name == 'pull_request' && github.event.pull_request.head.repo.fork)) && 'ubuntu-latest' || 'zoomies-linux-x64' }}
    timeout-minutes: 10
    permissions:
      contents: read
    steps:
      - uses: actions/checkout@3d3c42e5aac5ba805825da76410c181273ba90b1 # v7.0.1
      - uses: actions/setup-go@b7ad1dad31e06c5925ef5d2fc7ad053ef454303e # v7.0.0
        with:
          go-version: '1.27.1'
      - uses: actions/setup-node@820762786026740c76f36085b0efc47a31fe5020 # v7.0.0
        with:
          node-version: '24'
          package-manager-cache: false
      - name: Install the exact managed generator toolchain
        run: |
          set -eu
          mkdir -p "$RUNNER_TEMP/zoomies-tools"
          cp internal/aicontext/templates/package-lock.json "$RUNNER_TEMP/zoomies-tools/package-lock.json"
          printf '%s\n' '{"name":"zoomies-ai-context","private":true,"dependencies":{"repomix":"1.18.1"}}' > "$RUNNER_TEMP/zoomies-tools/package.json"
          npm ci --prefix "$RUNNER_TEMP/zoomies-tools" --ignore-scripts --no-audit --no-fund
      - name: Verify real Repomix generation and publication boundaries
        env:
          ZOOMIES_TEST_REPOMIX_CLI: ${{ runner.temp }}/zoomies-tools/node_modules/.bin/repomix
        run: go test -race ./internal/aicontext -count=1

  coverage:
    name: Coverage
    needs: [changes, go]
    if: github.event_name != 'pull_request' && needs.changes.outputs.go == 'true'
    permissions:
      contents: read
      id-token: write # Codecov authenticates uploads without a stored secret.
    runs-on: ${{ ((github.event_name == 'workflow_dispatch' && inputs.runner == 'github') || (github.event_name == 'pull_request' && github.event.pull_request.head.repo.fork)) && 'ubuntu-latest' || 'zoomies-linux-x64' }}
    steps:
      - uses: actions/checkout@3d3c42e5aac5ba805825da76410c181273ba90b1 # v7.0.1
      - uses: actions/setup-go@b7ad1dad31e06c5925ef5d2fc7ad053ef454303e # v7.0.0
        with:
          go-version: ${{ env.GO_VERSION }}
          cache: true
      - name: Download coverage shards
        id: download-covdata
        uses: actions/download-artifact@3e5f45b2cfb9172054b4087a40e8e0b5a5461e7c # v8.0.1
        continue-on-error: true
        with:
          pattern: covdata-*
          path: ${{ runner.temp }}/covdata
      # The artifact backend occasionally answers a self-hosted runner with a
      # 403 "Error from intermediary" that clears itself on a second attempt --
      # only one leg of an otherwise identical matrix fails this way, so it is
      # the request that is flaky, not the artifact.
      - name: Retry coverage shard download
        if: steps.download-covdata.outcome == 'failure'
        uses: actions/download-artifact@3e5f45b2cfb9172054b4087a40e8e0b5a5461e7c # v8.0.1
        with:
          pattern: covdata-*
          path: ${{ runner.temp }}/covdata
      - name: Merge the shards
        run: |
          set -eu
          dirs=$(ls -d "$RUNNER_TEMP"/covdata/covdata-* | tr '\n' ',' | sed 's/,$//')
          make cover-merge COVERDIRS="$dirs"
      - name: Coverage summary
        run: go tool cover -func=coverage.out | tail -1 >> "$GITHUB_STEP_SUMMARY"
      - name: Upload coverage to Codecov
        if: ${{ github.actor != 'dependabot[bot]' }}
        uses: codecov/codecov-action@303a32d7a59b442fa8d48b6a1cc6825c09c847a5 # v7.1.1
        with:
          use_oidc: true
          files: ./coverage.out
          disable_search: true
          fail_ci_if_error: true

  drill:
    name: Drill
    needs: [changes]
    if: needs.changes.outputs.go == 'true'
    # The drill uses two local processes and no Docker daemon. Keep it off the
    # project runner pool so a lost runner cannot discard its evidence or block
    # this independent integration check.
    runs-on: ubuntu-latest
    timeout-minutes: 30
    steps:
      - uses: actions/checkout@3d3c42e5aac5ba805825da76410c181273ba90b1 # v7.0.1
      - uses: actions/setup-go@b7ad1dad31e06c5925ef5d2fc7ad053ef454303e # v7.0.0
        with:
          go-version: ${{ env.GO_VERSION }}
          cache: true

      # The runtime tier runs the built binary as two real processes. It needs
      # no Docker daemon and no GitHub credentials: the backend is `process`
      # with a stub runner staged on disk, and GitHub is a fake in the test
      # process. That is what makes it something every pull request can afford.
      # Where the record ends before this run appends to it, so the summary and
      # the commit below carry this run's rows rather than the whole history.
      - name: Note where the drill record ends
        id: record
        run: echo "lines=$(wc -l < roadmap/validation/drills.md 2>/dev/null || echo 0)" >> "$GITHUB_OUTPUT"

      - name: Run the lifecycle drill
        run: make test-drill

      # The load measurement runs here too, for its assertions rather than its
      # figures: every read still answers, and a deep page is still a page of
      # rows, with a month of history under it. The timings go to the job
      # summary and nowhere else -- a runner's p95 is not a gate, and the
      # recorded evidence is written by `make measure` on a known machine.
      - name: Measure the reads a page makes
        run: make measure LOAD_RECORD=$RUNNER_TEMP/load.md

      - name: Load record
        if: always()
        run: cat "$RUNNER_TEMP/load.md" >> "$GITHUB_STEP_SUMMARY" 2>/dev/null || true

      # The record is the deliverable, not just the exit code: it says what was
      # observed and whether anything was left for a person to clean up. The
      # summary carries this run's rows only -- the history belongs in the file.
      - name: Drill record
        if: always()
        run: |
          if [ -f roadmap/validation/drills.md ]; then
            tail -n +$(( ${{ steps.record.outputs.lines }} + 1 )) roadmap/validation/drills.md >> "$GITHUB_STEP_SUMMARY"
          fi

      # Keep evidence per commit without letting test code write to main.
      - name: Preserve drill evidence
        if: always()
        uses: actions/upload-artifact@043fb46d1a93c77aae656e7c1c64a875d1fc6a0a # v7.0.1
        with:
          name: drill-evidence-${{ github.sha }}
          path: roadmap/validation/drills.md
          if-no-files-found: error
          retention-days: 90

  # Linux arm64 is the other architecture every release ships for, and until
  # this job existed nothing had run a test on it: the support matrix recorded
  # it as cross-compiled and no more. The Go suite and the runtime drill on
  # GitHub's hosted arm64 runner are what move that row. Hosted rather than the
  # Zoomies pool because the pool has no arm64 host to dogfood on yet; a
  # public repository pays nothing for the label.
  arm64:
    name: Linux arm64
    runs-on: ubuntu-24.04-arm
    needs: [changes]
    if: needs.changes.outputs.go == 'true'
    timeout-minutes: 90
    steps:
      - uses: actions/checkout@3d3c42e5aac5ba805825da76410c181273ba90b1 # v7.0.1
      - uses: actions/setup-go@b7ad1dad31e06c5925ef5d2fc7ad053ef454303e # v7.0.0
        with:
          go-version: ${{ env.GO_VERSION }}
          cache: true
      # The drill needs the real binary, so this one builds; the bound turns
      # a stalled module fetch into a failure that names this step.
      - name: Build the binary
        timeout-minutes: 15
        run: make build-nogui
      - name: Test
        run: make test
      - name: Note where the drill record ends
        id: record
        run: echo "lines=$(wc -l < roadmap/validation/drills.md 2>/dev/null || echo 0)" >> "$GITHUB_OUTPUT"
      - name: Run the lifecycle drill
        run: make test-drill
      # This run's rows go to the summary only. The file on main is written by
      # the Drill job, and two jobs appending the same drills to one file
      # would double every row.
      - name: Drill record
        if: always()
        run: |
          if [ -f roadmap/validation/drills.md ]; then
            echo "Drills on $(uname -m):" >> "$GITHUB_STEP_SUMMARY"
            tail -n +$(( ${{ steps.record.outputs.lines }} + 1 )) roadmap/validation/drills.md >> "$GITHUB_STEP_SUMMARY"
          fi

  # Windows is the platform the agent learnt to run on last, and this is the
  # only place anything runs on it. The whole tree builds and vets, and the
  # packages the Windows agent is made of run their tests here without the
  # race detector, which needs a C toolchain the stock runner does not pair
  # with CGO_ENABLED=0. The rest of the suite is Linux-shaped (shell stubs,
  # signals, unit files) and skips or does not apply; the support matrix says
  # which row this leg backs.
  windows:
    name: Windows
    runs-on: windows-latest
    needs: [changes]
    if: needs.changes.outputs.go == 'true'
    timeout-minutes: 60
    defaults:
      run:
        shell: bash
    steps:
      - uses: actions/checkout@3d3c42e5aac5ba805825da76410c181273ba90b1 # v7.0.1
      - uses: actions/setup-go@b7ad1dad31e06c5925ef5d2fc7ad053ef454303e # v7.0.0
        with:
          go-version: ${{ env.GO_VERSION }}
          cache: true
      # go:embed needs the directory to exist even when the UI is not built,
      # and the stock Windows runner has no make.
      - name: Stub the embedded UI
        run: |
          mkdir -p internal/api/webdist
          printf '<!doctype html><title>Zoomies</title><p>The UI was not built.' > internal/api/webdist/index.html
      - name: go vet
        run: go vet ./...
      - name: Build
        run: go build -trimpath -o zoomies.exe ./cmd/zoomies
      - name: Test the packages the Windows agent is made of
        run: go test -count=1 -timeout 20m ./internal/backend/ ./internal/machine/ ./internal/agent/ ./internal/installer/ ./internal/config/ ./internal/naming/ ./cmd/zoomies/
      # The database lock is a byte-range lock here rather than flock, and it
      # is the one thing in the store that has a Windows implementation of its
      # own; the test proves it holds across processes.
      - name: The database lock holds between processes
        run: go test -count=1 -run TestTheDatabaseLock ./internal/store/

  upgrade:
    name: Upgrade
    needs: [changes]
    if: needs.changes.outputs.go == 'true' || needs.changes.outputs.installer == 'true'
    runs-on: ${{ ((github.event_name == 'workflow_dispatch' && inputs.runner == 'github') || (github.event_name == 'pull_request' && github.event.pull_request.head.repo.fork)) && 'ubuntu-latest' || 'zoomies-linux-x64' }}
    steps:
      - uses: actions/checkout@3d3c42e5aac5ba805825da76410c181273ba90b1 # v7.0.1
      - uses: actions/setup-go@b7ad1dad31e06c5925ef5d2fc7ad053ef454303e # v7.0.0
        with:
          go-version: ${{ env.GO_VERSION }}
          cache: true

      # This is the one job that runs two builds of Zoomies: the last published
      # release, installed the way an operator installs it, and the build under
      # test on top of it. It is also the only check that install.sh can still
      # find a release at all -- everything else about the installer is a syntax
      # check.
      - name: Pick the latest installable release
        env:
          GITHUB_TOKEN: ${{ github.token }}
        run: |
          tag=$(python3 - <<'PY'
          import os
          import json
          import urllib.request

          repo = "eyupio/zoomies"
          asset = "zoomies_linux_amd64"
          token = os.environ.get("GITHUB_TOKEN", "")
          headers = {"Accept": "application/vnd.github+json"}
          if token:
              headers["Authorization"] = "token " + token
          page = 1
          while True:
              req = urllib.request.Request(
                  f"https://api.github.com/repos/{repo}/releases?per_page=100&page={page}",
                  headers=headers,
              )
              with urllib.request.urlopen(req, timeout=30) as resp:
                  releases = json.load(resp)
              if not releases:
                  break
              for release in releases:
                  # The rolling dev prerelease carries binaries too, but this
                  # job exercises upgrading from a versioned release.
                  if not str(release.get("tag_name", "")).startswith("v"):
                      continue
                  names = {a.get("name") for a in release.get("assets", [])}
                  if asset in names:
                      print(release["tag_name"])
                      raise SystemExit(0)
              page += 1
          raise SystemExit(f"no published release has the {asset} asset")
          PY
          )
          echo "ZOOMIES_VERSION=$tag" >> "$GITHUB_ENV"
      - name: Upgrade the last published release to this build
        run: make test-upgrade

  staticcheck:
    name: staticcheck
    needs: [changes]
    if: needs.changes.outputs.go == 'true'
    runs-on: ${{ ((github.event_name == 'workflow_dispatch' && inputs.runner == 'github') || (github.event_name == 'pull_request' && github.event.pull_request.head.repo.fork)) && 'ubuntu-latest' || 'zoomies-linux-x64' }}
    steps:
      - uses: actions/checkout@3d3c42e5aac5ba805825da76410c181273ba90b1 # v7.0.1
      - uses: actions/setup-go@b7ad1dad31e06c5925ef5d2fc7ad053ef454303e # v7.0.0
        with:
          go-version: ${{ env.GO_VERSION }}
          cache: true
      - name: Stub the embedded UI
        timeout-minutes: 1
        run: make ui-stub
      - uses: dominikh/staticcheck-action@9716614d4101e79b4340dd97b10e54d68234e431 # v1.4.1
        with:
          version: latest
          install-go: false

  ui:
    name: UI
    needs: [changes]
    if: needs.changes.outputs.go == 'true' || needs.changes.outputs.web == 'true'
    runs-on: ${{ ((github.event_name == 'workflow_dispatch' && inputs.runner == 'github') || (github.event_name == 'pull_request' && github.event.pull_request.head.repo.fork)) && 'ubuntu-latest' || 'zoomies-linux-x64' }}
    steps:
      - uses: actions/checkout@3d3c42e5aac5ba805825da76410c181273ba90b1 # v7.0.1
      - uses: actions/setup-node@820762786026740c76f36085b0efc47a31fe5020 # v7.0.0
        with:
          node-version: ${{ env.NODE_VERSION }}
          cache: npm
          cache-dependency-path: web/package-lock.json
      - run: npm ci --no-audit --no-fund
        working-directory: web
      - run: npm run lint
        working-directory: web
      # The generated client must match api/openapi.yaml. If it does not, the
      # UI is typed against an API that no longer exists.
      - name: The generated API client is up to date
        run: |
          npm run generate:api
          git diff --exit-code src/lib/api/schema.d.ts \
            || { echo "::error::src/lib/api/schema.d.ts is stale. Run 'make openapi' and commit the result."; exit 1; }
        working-directory: web
      - run: npm run check
        working-directory: web
      # The build fails on its own if the gzipped shell exceeds the 200 KB
      # budget documented in docs/ui-guidelines.md.
      - run: npm run build
        working-directory: web
      - uses: actions/upload-artifact@043fb46d1a93c77aae656e7c1c64a875d1fc6a0a # v7.0.1
        with:
          name: webdist
          path: internal/api/webdist
          retention-days: 3

  playwright:
    name: Playwright
    # Not gated on sudo the way the runner image's passwordless entry
    # promises (see deploy/Dockerfile.runner): a pool running the process
    # backend gives its agent's systemd unit NoNewPrivileges=yes, which
    # makes sudo refuse to escalate no matter what the sudoers file says --
    # see the installer job below. Unlike dash/shellcheck, Chromium's shared
    # libraries cannot be fetched as a standalone binary, so the install step
    # below unpacks them into a private prefix instead of installing them
    # system-wide when sudo is not available.
    runs-on: ${{ ((github.event_name == 'workflow_dispatch' && inputs.runner == 'github') || (github.event_name == 'pull_request' && github.event.pull_request.head.repo.fork)) && 'ubuntu-latest' || 'zoomies-linux-x64' }}
    # The suite drives the real binary, so a Go change can break it as
    # surely as a web one.
    needs: [changes, ui]
    if: needs.changes.outputs.go == 'true' || needs.changes.outputs.web == 'true'
    steps:
      - uses: actions/checkout@3d3c42e5aac5ba805825da76410c181273ba90b1 # v7.0.1
      - uses: actions/setup-go@b7ad1dad31e06c5925ef5d2fc7ad053ef454303e # v7.0.0
        with:
          go-version: ${{ env.GO_VERSION }}
          cache: true
      - uses: actions/setup-node@820762786026740c76f36085b0efc47a31fe5020 # v7.0.0
        with:
          node-version: ${{ env.NODE_VERSION }}
          cache: npm
          cache-dependency-path: web/package-lock.json
      - name: Download webdist artifact
        id: download-webdist
        uses: actions/download-artifact@3e5f45b2cfb9172054b4087a40e8e0b5a5461e7c # v8.0.1
        continue-on-error: true
        with:
          name: webdist
          path: internal/api/webdist
      # See the coverage job's comment above: this is the same transient
      # intermediary 403, not a broken artifact.
      - name: Retry webdist download
        if: steps.download-webdist.outcome == 'failure'
        uses: actions/download-artifact@3e5f45b2cfb9172054b4087a40e8e0b5a5461e7c # v8.0.1
        with:
          name: webdist
          path: internal/api/webdist
      - run: go build -o zoomies ./cmd/zoomies
      - run: npm ci --no-audit --no-fund
        working-directory: web
      - name: Install Playwright Chromium
        # The browser itself needs no privilege; only the shared libraries it
        # links against do. Where sudo actually works, install-deps puts them
        # where every other package on the system lives -- run unprivileged,
        # not under sudo itself: it shells out to `sudo -- sh -c "apt-get
        # ..."` on its own for just the package install, and wrapping the
        # whole npx invocation in sudo instead drops it onto root's
        # sudoers-restricted PATH, which does not carry the Node version
        # actions/setup-node put on this job's own PATH. Where sudo does not
        # work (see the job comment above), the .debs are downloaded with
        # apt's own cache and state redirected into a writable prefix --
        # `download` and `dpkg -x` need no root either way -- and the browser
        # is pointed at the unpacked libraries with LD_LIBRARY_PATH instead.
        # The package list is what `playwright install-deps --dry-run
        # chromium` prints on the runner image's own Ubuntu 24.04, minus
        # Xvfb and the font packages, which only matter for a display
        # chrome-headless-shell never opens.
        run: |
          npx playwright install chromium
          if sudo -n true >/dev/null 2>&1; then
            npx playwright install-deps chromium
          else
            prefix="${RUNNER_TEMP}/chromium-deps"
            mkdir -p "${prefix}/lists/partial" "${prefix}/cache/archives/partial" "${prefix}/debs" "${prefix}/root"
            apt_opts=(-o "Dir::State::Lists=${prefix}/lists" -o "Dir::Cache=${prefix}/cache" -o "Acquire::Retries=3")
            apt-get "${apt_opts[@]}" update
            (cd "${prefix}/debs" && apt-get "${apt_opts[@]}" download \
              libasound2t64 libatk-bridge2.0-0t64 libatk1.0-0t64 libatspi2.0-0t64 \
              libcairo2 libcups2t64 libdbus-1-3 libdrm2 libgbm1 libglib2.0-0t64 \
              libnspr4 libnss3 libpango-1.0-0 libx11-6 libxcb1 libxcomposite1 \
              libxdamage1 libxext6 libxfixes3 libxkbcommon0 libxrandr2)
            for deb in "${prefix}"/debs/*.deb; do dpkg -x "${deb}" "${prefix}/root"; done
            echo "LD_LIBRARY_PATH=${prefix}/root/usr/lib/x86_64-linux-gnu${LD_LIBRARY_PATH:+:${LD_LIBRARY_PATH}}" >> "${GITHUB_ENV}"
          fi
        working-directory: web
      - run: npm run test:e2e
        working-directory: web
      - uses: actions/upload-artifact@043fb46d1a93c77aae656e7c1c64a875d1fc6a0a # v7.0.1
        if: failure()
        with:
          name: playwright-report
          path: web/playwright-report
          retention-days: 7

  build-matrix:
    name: Cross-compile
    runs-on: ${{ ((github.event_name == 'workflow_dispatch' && inputs.runner == 'github') || (github.event_name == 'pull_request' && github.event.pull_request.head.repo.fork)) && 'ubuntu-latest' || 'zoomies-linux-x64' }}
    needs: [changes, ui]
    if: needs.changes.outputs.go == 'true'
    strategy:
      fail-fast: false
      matrix:
        include:
          - { goos: linux,  goarch: amd64 }
          - { goos: linux,  goarch: arm64 }
          - { goos: darwin, goarch: amd64 }
          - { goos: darwin, goarch: arm64 }
          - { goos: windows, goarch: amd64 }
    steps:
      - uses: actions/checkout@3d3c42e5aac5ba805825da76410c181273ba90b1 # v7.0.1
      - uses: actions/setup-go@b7ad1dad31e06c5925ef5d2fc7ad053ef454303e # v7.0.0
        with:
          go-version: ${{ env.GO_VERSION }}
          cache: true
      - name: Download webdist artifact
        id: download-webdist
        uses: actions/download-artifact@3e5f45b2cfb9172054b4087a40e8e0b5a5461e7c # v8.0.1
        continue-on-error: true
        with:
          name: webdist
          path: internal/api/webdist
      # See the coverage job's comment above: this is the same transient
      # intermediary 403, not a broken artifact.
      - name: Retry webdist download
        if: steps.download-webdist.outcome == 'failure'
        uses: actions/download-artifact@3e5f45b2cfb9172054b4087a40e8e0b5a5461e7c # v8.0.1
        with:
          name: webdist
          path: internal/api/webdist
      - env:
          GOOS: ${{ matrix.goos }}
          GOARCH: ${{ matrix.goarch }}
          CGO_ENABLED: "0"
        run: go build -trimpath -o /tmp/zoomies ./cmd/zoomies

  # The dev channel is installable, not just pullable. The image and binary
  # carry the same main-sha-* stamp, and the rolling prerelease gives
  # install.sh --version dev a stable URL whose bytes are replaced on every
  # successful push to main.
  dev-binaries:
    name: Publish dev binaries
    # Only a commit on main that changes what ships (see changes). The jobs it
    # waits on are skipped when their inputs did not change, and a skipped job
    # is not a failed one, so the condition says "none failed" rather than
    # leaving GitHub to skip this one because a job it waits on did not run.
    if: ${{ !cancelled() && ((github.event_name == 'push' && github.ref == 'refs/heads/main') || (github.event_name == 'workflow_dispatch' && github.ref == 'refs/heads/main')) && needs.changes.outputs.publish == 'true' && !contains(needs.*.result, 'failure') && !contains(needs.*.result, 'cancelled') }}
    needs: [changes, go, ui, installer]
    runs-on: ${{ ((github.event_name == 'workflow_dispatch' && inputs.runner == 'github') || (github.event_name == 'pull_request' && github.event.pull_request.head.repo.fork)) && 'ubuntu-latest' || 'zoomies-linux-x64' }}
    permissions:
      contents: write
      id-token: write
      attestations: write
    steps:
      - uses: actions/checkout@3d3c42e5aac5ba805825da76410c181273ba90b1 # v7.0.1
        with: { fetch-depth: 0 }
      - uses: actions/setup-go@b7ad1dad31e06c5925ef5d2fc7ad053ef454303e # v7.0.0
        with: { go-version: "${{ env.GO_VERSION }}", cache: true }
      - uses: actions/setup-node@820762786026740c76f36085b0efc47a31fe5020 # v7.0.0
        with:
          node-version: ${{ env.NODE_VERSION }}
          cache: npm
          cache-dependency-path: web/package-lock.json
      - id: build
        run: |
          echo "version=main-sha-$(git rev-parse --short HEAD)" >> "$GITHUB_OUTPUT"
          echo "date=$(date -u +%Y-%m-%dT%H:%M:%SZ)" >> "$GITHUB_OUTPUT"
      - run: make dist VERSION=${{ steps.build.outputs.version }} COMMIT=${{ github.sha }} DATE=${{ steps.build.outputs.date }}
      - id: binary-provenance
        uses: actions/attest-build-provenance@4d101475d8b20a2381f78447822ac1eab6504dd8 # v4.2.2
        with:
          subject-path: "dist/zoomies_*"
      # Two files from one attestation. The Sigstore bundle is what
      # `gh attestation verify` reads: the signed statement plus the
      # certificate and transparency-log entry that prove who signed it. The
      # .intoto.jsonl beside it is the same signed statement on its own, in
      # the DSSE envelope the SLSA tooling and the OpenSSF Scorecard look for;
      # a release carrying only the bundle scores as signed but unattested.
      - name: Attach verifiable provenance to the release
        env:
          BUNDLE: ${{ steps.binary-provenance.outputs.bundle-path }}
        run: |
          set -eu
          cp "$BUNDLE" dist/zoomies-provenance.sigstore.json
          jq -c '.dsseEnvelope' "$BUNDLE" > dist/zoomies-provenance.intoto.jsonl
          # A bundle without an envelope is not provenance; refuse it here
          # rather than attach an empty file that verifies nothing.
          test "$(jq -r '.payloadType' dist/zoomies-provenance.intoto.jsonl)" = "application/vnd.in-toto+json"

      - name: Move the dev tag to this build
        run: |
          git tag -f dev "$GITHUB_SHA"
          git push --force origin refs/tags/dev
      # Published with gh rather than an action, because what this has to
      # survive is GitHub's own asset upload being slow: each of these
      # binaries is about 50 MB, and a publish has taken nine minutes a file
      # and then failed on the next one with "Error saving asset" -- an error
      # with no status, no name and no retry behind it.
      #
      # Three properties answer that, and no action offers them together. An
      # asset the release already holds with the same digest is not sent
      # again, so a re-run after a failure carries on where it stopped instead
      # of spending ten minutes arriving back where it started. An upload that
      # fails is retried, because a transfer that long has more chances to be
      # interrupted than to be wrong. And the release is checked at the end,
      # because a channel missing a binary is a channel `zoomies upgrade`
      # breaks on, and the whole point of this job is that it does not.
      - name: Publish the dev release
        env:
          GH_TOKEN: ${{ github.token }}
          NOTES: |
            Rolling development build from `main`. Assets and the `dev` tag move on every successful push.

            Use a versioned release for production or reproducible installs.
        run: |
          set -euo pipefail
          files="dist/zoomies_linux_amd64 dist/zoomies_linux_arm64 dist/zoomies_darwin_amd64 dist/zoomies_darwin_arm64 dist/zoomies_windows_amd64.exe dist/checksums.txt dist/zoomies-provenance.sigstore.json dist/zoomies-provenance.intoto.jsonl"
          for f in $files; do
            test -f "$f" || { echo "::error::make dist did not produce $f"; exit 1; }
          done

          if gh release view dev >/dev/null 2>&1; then
            gh release edit dev --title "Development build" --notes "$NOTES" --prerelease --latest=false
          else
            gh release create dev --title "Development build" --notes "$NOTES" --prerelease --latest=false
          fi

          # name and digest of what is up there already. A release from before
          # GitHub recorded digests reports none, and an asset with no digest
          # is one we cannot vouch for, so it is replaced.
          have=$(gh api "repos/$GITHUB_REPOSITORY/releases/tags/dev" --jq '.assets[] | "\(.name) \(.digest // "")"')

          for f in $files; do
            name=$(basename "$f")
            want="sha256:$(sha256sum "$f" | cut -d' ' -f1)"
            if printf '%s\n' "$have" | grep -qxF "$name $want"; then
              echo "= $name is already published"
              continue
            fi
            for attempt in 1 2 3; do
              if gh release upload dev "$f" --clobber; then
                echo "+ $name"
                break
              fi
              if [ "$attempt" = 3 ]; then
                echo "::error::$name could not be uploaded after three attempts"
                exit 1
              fi
              sleep $((attempt * 30))
            done
          done

          published=$(gh api "repos/$GITHUB_REPOSITORY/releases/tags/dev" --jq '.assets[].name')
          missing=""
          for f in $files; do
            name=$(basename "$f")
            printf '%s\n' "$published" | grep -qxF "$name" || missing="$missing $name"
          done
          if [ -n "$missing" ]; then
            echo "::error::the dev release is missing:$missing"
            exit 1
          fi

  installer:
    name: install.sh
    needs: [changes]
    if: needs.changes.outputs.installer == 'true'
    # Not gated on sudo: a pool running the process backend gives its agent's
    # systemd unit NoNewPrivileges=yes (the job tree hangs off that same
    # process), which makes sudo refuse to escalate, passwordless entry in
    # the sudoers file or not. Both tools below are fetched without root
    # instead, which also works unchanged on a GitHub-hosted runner.
    runs-on: ${{ ((github.event_name == 'workflow_dispatch' && inputs.runner == 'github') || (github.event_name == 'pull_request' && github.event.pull_request.head.repo.fork)) && 'ubuntu-latest' || 'zoomies-linux-x64' }}
    steps:
      - uses: actions/checkout@3d3c42e5aac5ba805825da76410c181273ba90b1 # v7.0.1
      - name: POSIX shell syntax
        run: |
          # dash is the strictest POSIX sh most users will have; install.sh must
          # parse under it, not just under bash. Debian and Ubuntu require it
          # as the /bin/sh provider, so it is already here on both a Zoomies
          # runner and a GitHub-hosted one -- nothing to install.
          command -v dash >/dev/null || { echo "::error::dash is not on PATH"; exit 1; }

          # shellcheck carries no such guarantee, and fetching the pinned
          # static binary needs no root at all.
          SHELLCHECK_VERSION=0.10.0
          SHELLCHECK_SHA256=6c881ab0698e4e6ea235245f22832860544f17ba386442fe7e9d629f8cbedf87
          curl -fsSL -o /tmp/shellcheck.tar.xz \
            "https://github.com/koalaman/shellcheck/releases/download/v${SHELLCHECK_VERSION}/shellcheck-v${SHELLCHECK_VERSION}.linux.x86_64.tar.xz"
          echo "${SHELLCHECK_SHA256}  /tmp/shellcheck.tar.xz" | sha256sum -c -
          tar -xJf /tmp/shellcheck.tar.xz -C /tmp
          mkdir -p "$HOME/.local/bin"
          install -m 0755 "/tmp/shellcheck-v${SHELLCHECK_VERSION}/shellcheck" "$HOME/.local/bin/shellcheck"
          export PATH="$HOME/.local/bin:$PATH"

          dash -n install.sh
          shellcheck -s sh install.sh
          dash -n test/install/install-check.sh
          shellcheck -s sh test/install/install-check.sh
