          shellcheck deploy/runner-entrypoint.sh
          dash -n test/upgrade/upgrade-check.sh
          shellcheck -s sh test/upgrade/upgrade-check.sh
          dash -n test/runner-image/check.sh
          shellcheck -s sh test/runner-image/check.sh
          dash -n test/runner-image/dnf-check.sh
          shellcheck -s sh test/runner-image/dnf-check.sh
          # Both image workflows and make invoke this directly. Shell syntax
          # checks alone accepted mode 0644 and every release leg then failed.
          test -x test/runner-image/check.sh || { echo "::error::test/runner-image/check.sh must be executable"; exit 1; }
          # The runner image's own scripts run under whatever /bin/sh the base
          # image has, which on Debian is not bash. Globbed rather than listed,
          # so a new one is covered by existing.
          for f in deploy/runner-*.sh; do
            # The entrypoint is bash and is checked as bash, above.
            case "$f" in deploy/runner-entrypoint.sh) continue ;; esac
            dash -n "$f"
            shellcheck -s sh "$f"
          done

      - name: RPM package install recovery
        run: dash test/runner-image/dnf-check.sh

      - name: What install.sh does on a host that already has the binary
        run: |
          # Syntax checking is not behaviour checking, and the difference is why
          # a re-run of the controller's own join command used to drop the join.
          # Run under dash as well as sh, since that is what most hosts have.
          TEST_SH=dash test/install/install-check.sh install.sh

  images:
    name: Images
    runs-on: ${{ ((github.event_name == 'workflow_dispatch' && inputs.runner == 'github') || (github.event_name == 'pull_request' && github.event.pull_request.head.repo.fork)) && 'ubuntu-latest' || 'zoomies-linux-x64' }}
    needs: [changes, dev-binaries]
    # Main pushes and manual recovery publish matching binaries before images.
    # Pull requests and checks on other branches do not publish dev binaries,
    # and only build the images when something that goes into them changed:
    # the binary and the UI inside are built and tested by their own jobs.
    # A pull request builds the images when their inputs change. Main builds
    # them whenever it publishes binaries, whatever changed: a Go-only commit
    # still changes the binary inside the controller image, and the dev
    # channel's binaries and images must name the same commit.
    if: ${{ !cancelled() && (github.event_name == 'pull_request' || github.ref != 'refs/heads/main' || needs.dev-binaries.result == 'success') && (needs.changes.outputs.deploy == 'true' || needs.changes.outputs.publish == 'true') }}
    # Publishing needs to write packages; everything else here only reads.
    permissions:
      contents: read
      packages: write
    env:
      CONTROLLER_IMAGE: ghcr.io/eyupio/zoomies
      AGENT_IMAGE: ghcr.io/eyupio/zoomies-agent
      RUNNER_IMAGE: ghcr.io/eyupio/zoomies-runner
      RUNNER_DOCKER_IMAGE: ghcr.io/eyupio/zoomies-runner-docker
    # The runner-images job below repeats none of these decisions; it reads them
    # from here, so a change to what publishes only has to be made once.
    outputs:
      publish: ${{ steps.publish.outputs.value }}
      runner: ${{ steps.changed.outputs.runner }}
      sha: ${{ steps.tags.outputs.sha }}
      version: ${{ steps.tags.outputs.version }}
      date: ${{ steps.tags.outputs.date }}
    steps:
      # Full history: the "what changed" step below diffs against a base commit
      # that a shallow clone does not contain.
      - uses: actions/checkout@3d3c42e5aac5ba805825da76410c181273ba90b1 # v7.0.1
        with: { fetch-depth: 0 }

      # Whether this run publishes anything. Only main does. A pull request --
      # from a fork especially -- is untrusted code carrying a read-only token,
      # and has no business writing to the registry: it builds the images to
      # prove the Dockerfiles still work, and pushes nothing.
      - id: publish
        name: Decide whether to publish
        run: |
          set -eu
          if [ "${{ github.event_name }}" != "pull_request" ] \
             && [ "${{ github.ref }}" = "refs/heads/main" ]; then
            echo "value=true" >> "$GITHUB_OUTPUT"
          else
            echo "value=false" >> "$GITHUB_OUTPUT"
          fi

      # main publishes :dev, :main and :sha-<commit>.
      #
      # Not :latest. That tag is the release workflow's, and while both wrote it
      # the last one to run won: a merge to main overwrote the :latest a release
      # had just published, so an operator who pulled it got an unreleased build
      # and a controller stamped main-sha-abc1234 -- which no installer can
      # match a host to, because agents are installed from release assets.
      #
      # :dev says what it is. Someone who wants main asks for main; :latest
      # means the newest release, which is what everyone else expects it to
      # mean.
      - id: tags
        name: Work out the tags
        run: |
          short=$(git rev-parse --short HEAD)
          echo "sha=sha-$short" >> "$GITHUB_OUTPUT"
          echo "version=main-sha-$short" >> "$GITHUB_OUTPUT"
          echo "date=$(date -u +%Y-%m-%dT%H:%M:%SZ)" >> "$GITHUB_OUTPUT"

      - if: steps.publish.outputs.value == 'true'
        uses: docker/login-action@dbcb813823bdd20940b903addbd779551569679f # v4.6.0
        with:
          registry: ghcr.io
          username: ${{ github.actor }}
          # github.token rather than secrets.GITHUB_TOKEN: the same value, but
          # GitHub reserves the GITHUB_ prefix for secret names, so referring to
          # it this way keeps the workflow clear of that namespace entirely.
          password: ${{ github.token }}

      # Pull requests build amd64; main publishes both architectures. The
      # controller and agent cross-compile natively, so neither needs an arm64
      # machine; the runner images, which install packages, build each
      # architecture on its own kind of machine in runner-images below.
      - id: platforms
        name: Decide the platforms
        run: |
          if [ "${{ github.event_name }}" = "pull_request" ]; then
            echo "list=linux/amd64" >> "$GITHUB_OUTPUT"
          else
            echo "list=linux/amd64,linux/arm64" >> "$GITHUB_OUTPUT"
          fi

      - name: Set up Docker Buildx
        uses: docker/setup-buildx-action@f87e5991a6d7451dcb8d9637bfbc97413f497069 # v4.4.1

      # Pull requests only need to prove a changed runner Dockerfile still
      # builds. Every push to main rebuilds every runner variant even when its
      # inputs did not change, because :dev is a build channel: its labels and
      # embedded build stamp must identify the same commit as the controller,
      # agent image and binary.
      #
      # Runs after the builder is set up, because deciding needs a registry
      # lookup.
      - id: changed
        name: Work out what changed
        env:
          BASE: ${{ github.event.pull_request.base.sha || github.event.before }}
          PUBLISH: ${{ steps.publish.outputs.value }}
        run: |
          set -eu
          build_it() { echo "runner=true" >> "$GITHUB_OUTPUT"; exit 0; }

          if [ "$PUBLISH" = "true" ]; then
            build_it
          fi

          if [ "${{ github.event_name }}" = "workflow_dispatch" ]; then
            build_it
          fi

          # A base we cannot resolve -- a force push, a branch's first commit --
          # tells us nothing about what changed, so assume the worst.
          if [ -z "${BASE:-}" ] || ! git cat-file -e "${BASE}^{commit}" 2>/dev/null; then
            build_it
          fi

          if git diff --name-only "$BASE" HEAD |
             grep -qE '^(deploy/(Dockerfile\.runner|runner-entrypoint\.sh|runner-[a-z-]+\.sh)|test/runner-image/.*)$'; then
            echo "runner=true" >> "$GITHUB_OUTPUT"
          else
            echo "runner=false" >> "$GITHUB_OUTPUT"
          fi

      - name: Build the controller image
        uses: docker/build-push-action@c3c9e263c25d99ce0380d002d59b67737d91b0dc # v7.4.0
        with:
          context: .
          file: deploy/Dockerfile
          target: controller
          platforms: ${{ steps.platforms.outputs.list }}
          push: ${{ steps.publish.outputs.value }}
          # Export intermediate layers for the next ephemeral builder. Each
          # target has its own scope; cache export is optional and bounded.
          cache-from: type=gha,version=2,scope=ci-controller
          cache-to: type=gha,version=2,scope=ci-controller,mode=max,timeout=5m,ignore-error=true
          # Without these, `zoomies version` inside a published image reports
          # the Dockerfile's "dev" default, and nothing in the image says which
          # commit it came from.
          build-args: |
            RUNNER_IMAGE_TAG=dev
            VERSION=${{ steps.tags.outputs.version }}
            COMMIT=${{ github.sha }}
            DATE=${{ steps.tags.outputs.date }}
          tags: |
            ${{ env.CONTROLLER_IMAGE }}:dev
            ${{ env.CONTROLLER_IMAGE }}:main
            ${{ env.CONTROLLER_IMAGE }}:${{ steps.tags.outputs.sha }}

      # The agent image, which nothing built until now.
      #
      # deploy/Dockerfile has carried an `agent` target all along and no
      # workflow named it, so the only way to run an agent in a container was to
      # run the controller image and override its command. An agent host that
      # wants a container now has one that says what it is.
      - name: Build the agent image
        uses: docker/build-push-action@c3c9e263c25d99ce0380d002d59b67737d91b0dc # v7.4.0
        with:
          context: .
          file: deploy/Dockerfile
          target: agent
          platforms: ${{ steps.platforms.outputs.list }}
          push: ${{ steps.publish.outputs.value }}
          cache-from: type=gha,version=2,scope=ci-agent
          cache-to: type=gha,version=2,scope=ci-agent,mode=max,timeout=5m,ignore-error=true
          build-args: |
            RUNNER_IMAGE_TAG=dev
            VERSION=${{ steps.tags.outputs.version }}
            COMMIT=${{ github.sha }}
            DATE=${{ steps.tags.outputs.date }}
          tags: |
            ${{ env.AGENT_IMAGE }}:dev
            ${{ env.AGENT_IMAGE }}:main
            ${{ env.AGENT_IMAGE }}:${{ steps.tags.outputs.sha }}

      - name: Say what happened
        env:
          PUBLISH: ${{ steps.publish.outputs.value }}
          RUNNER_BUILT: ${{ steps.changed.outputs.runner }}
          SHA_TAG: ${{ steps.tags.outputs.sha }}
        run: |
          set -eu
          {
            if [ "$RUNNER_BUILT" != "true" ]; then
              echo "The runner images were not rebuilt: nothing under deploy/ that goes into them changed."
              echo
            fi
            if [ "$PUBLISH" != "true" ]; then
              echo "Nothing was published: images are pushed from main only."
            else
              echo "Published:"
              echo
              echo "- \`$CONTROLLER_IMAGE:dev\`, \`:main\`, \`:$SHA_TAG\`"
              echo "- \`$AGENT_IMAGE:dev\`, \`:main\`, \`:$SHA_TAG\`"
              if [ "$RUNNER_BUILT" = "true" ]; then
                echo "- \`$RUNNER_IMAGE:dev\`, \`:main\`, \`:$SHA_TAG\`"
                echo "- \`$RUNNER_DOCKER_IMAGE:dev\`, \`:main\`, \`:$SHA_TAG\`"
              else
                echo "- The runner images were checked but not published."
              fi
            fi
          } >> "$GITHUB_STEP_SUMMARY"

  # One build per operating system in internal/naming's catalogue and per
  # architecture, each building both of deploy/Dockerfile.runner's targets.
  #
  # It is a separate job from `images` because it is the expensive half -- five
  # variants, each downloading the ~200 MB actions/runner archive and a build
  # toolchain. Pull requests run it only for relevant changes; main runs it for
  # every published dev build so all artifacts carry one commit stamp.
  #
  # Each architecture builds on a machine of its own kind: amd64 on the x64
  # pool, arm64 on GitHub's hosted arm64 runner, as the arm64 test job does.
  # They used to share an x64 builder with QEMU emulating arm64, which was slow
  # and could not build Ubuntu 22.04 at all -- the emulator segfaulted inside
  # ldconfig. A leg pushes its image by digest only, and runner-manifests below
  # joins the legs into the tags a pool pulls. A pull request builds both
  # architectures, because the arm64 leg is the half an emulator used to hide,
  # and publishes nothing.
  #
  # TestWorkflowMatricesCoverTheCatalogue keeps this list and internal/naming's
  # catalogue in step, so a new operating system cannot be half-added.
  runner-images:
    name: Runner image (${{ matrix.tag }}, ${{ matrix.arch }})
    runs-on: ${{ matrix.arch == 'arm64' && 'ubuntu-24.04-arm' || (((github.event_name == 'workflow_dispatch' && inputs.runner == 'github') || (github.event_name == 'pull_request' && github.event.pull_request.head.repo.fork)) && 'ubuntu-latest' || 'zoomies-linux-x64') }}
    needs: [images]
    if: needs.images.outputs.runner == 'true'
    permissions:
      contents: read
      packages: write
    env:
      RUNNER_IMAGE: ghcr.io/eyupio/zoomies-runner
      RUNNER_DOCKER_IMAGE: ghcr.io/eyupio/zoomies-runner-docker
      RUNNER_FULL_IMAGE: ghcr.io/eyupio/zoomies-runner-full
      PUBLISH: ${{ needs.images.outputs.publish }}
    strategy:
      fail-fast: false
      matrix:
        # Generated from internal/naming's catalogue by `make generate`. Adding
        # or swapping an operating system is a row there, not here.
        # zoomies:catalogue-begin
        include:
          - { tag: ubuntu-2404, arch: amd64, base: "ubuntu:24.04@sha256:224a1869083a311ef3f13648a154ba79832fbef6364d31493642ca03082da254",            family: apt, os: ubuntu, version: "24.04", platforms: "linux/amd64,linux/arm64", default: true, full: true }
          - { tag: ubuntu-2404, arch: arm64, base: "ubuntu:24.04@sha256:224a1869083a311ef3f13648a154ba79832fbef6364d31493642ca03082da254",            family: apt, os: ubuntu, version: "24.04", platforms: "linux/amd64,linux/arm64", default: true, full: true }
          - { tag: ubuntu-2604, arch: amd64, base: "ubuntu:26.04@sha256:da6fc2be547864451aa253836dd926da33623312df4a9a243e35dc877c378a78",            family: apt, os: ubuntu, version: "26.04", platforms: "linux/amd64,linux/arm64", full: true }
          - { tag: ubuntu-2604, arch: arm64, base: "ubuntu:26.04@sha256:da6fc2be547864451aa253836dd926da33623312df4a9a243e35dc877c378a78",            family: apt, os: ubuntu, version: "26.04", platforms: "linux/amd64,linux/arm64", full: true }
          - { tag: ubuntu-2204, arch: amd64, base: "ubuntu:22.04@sha256:829f6df217bcbae2b371026e81711d1a787c61b2967ad09d015063663ebafbf7",            family: apt, os: ubuntu, version: "22.04", platforms: "linux/amd64,linux/arm64", full: true }
          - { tag: ubuntu-2204, arch: arm64, base: "ubuntu:22.04@sha256:829f6df217bcbae2b371026e81711d1a787c61b2967ad09d015063663ebafbf7",            family: apt, os: ubuntu, version: "22.04", platforms: "linux/amd64,linux/arm64", full: true }
          - { tag: debian-13,   arch: amd64, base: "debian:13-slim@sha256:a99cfc517144bc59b1978475ec53b46ecabec7e43635402ee5b77cc54cd1b20a",          family: apt, os: debian, version: "13",    platforms: "linux/amd64,linux/arm64" }
          - { tag: debian-13,   arch: arm64, base: "debian:13-slim@sha256:a99cfc517144bc59b1978475ec53b46ecabec7e43635402ee5b77cc54cd1b20a",          family: apt, os: debian, version: "13",    platforms: "linux/amd64,linux/arm64" }
          - { tag: debian-12,   arch: amd64, base: "debian:12-slim@sha256:88200866dfff7ea7f5cbcb6ec7c8a701889efe6fe859fe64d6990e4b07ea4171",          family: apt, os: debian, version: "12",    platforms: "linux/amd64,linux/arm64" }
          - { tag: debian-12,   arch: arm64, base: "debian:12-slim@sha256:88200866dfff7ea7f5cbcb6ec7c8a701889efe6fe859fe64d6990e4b07ea4171",          family: apt, os: debian, version: "12",    platforms: "linux/amd64,linux/arm64" }
          - { tag: fedora-42,   arch: amd64, base: "fedora:42@sha256:99e203b80b1c3d8f7e161ec10a68fd02b081ef83a3963553e513c82846b97814",               family: dnf, os: fedora, version: "42",    platforms: "linux/amd64,linux/arm64" }
          - { tag: fedora-42,   arch: arm64, base: "fedora:42@sha256:99e203b80b1c3d8f7e161ec10a68fd02b081ef83a3963553e513c82846b97814",               family: dnf, os: fedora, version: "42",    platforms: "linux/amd64,linux/arm64" }
          - { tag: rocky-9,     arch: amd64, base: "rockylinux/rockylinux:9@sha256:8101994123cf3d0a8fee517bee7f39e555c7d92bd2d9eb3303cc988a0eeed00f", family: dnf, os: rocky,  version: "9",     platforms: "linux/amd64,linux/arm64" }
          - { tag: rocky-9,     arch: arm64, base: "rockylinux/rockylinux:9@sha256:8101994123cf3d0a8fee517bee7f39e555c7d92bd2d9eb3303cc988a0eeed00f", family: dnf, os: rocky,  version: "9",     platforms: "linux/amd64,linux/arm64" }
        # zoomies:catalogue-end
    steps:
      - uses: actions/checkout@3d3c42e5aac5ba805825da76410c181273ba90b1 # v7.0.1

      - if: needs.images.outputs.publish == 'true'
        uses: docker/login-action@dbcb813823bdd20940b903addbd779551569679f # v4.6.0
        with:
          registry: ghcr.io
          username: ${{ github.actor }}
          password: ${{ github.token }}

      - name: Set up Docker Buildx
        id: buildx
        uses: docker/setup-buildx-action@f87e5991a6d7451dcb8d9637bfbc97413f497069 # v4.4.1

      # Only the default variant carries the unqualified tags. Anything else
      # would mean a pool that named no operating system got whichever variant
      # this matrix happened to finish last.
      #
      # Written to a file rather than applied here: this leg holds one
      # architecture, and a tag pointing at it alone would hand the other
      # architecture's hosts an image they cannot run. runner-manifests applies
      # them once every leg has pushed.
      - id: tags
        name: Work out the tags
        env:
          IS_DEFAULT: ${{ matrix.default && 'true' || 'false' }}
          IS_FULL: ${{ matrix.full && 'true' || 'false' }}
          TAG: ${{ matrix.tag }}
          ARCH: ${{ matrix.arch }}
          PLATFORMS: ${{ matrix.platforms }}
          SHA_TAG: ${{ needs.images.outputs.sha }}
        run: |
          set -eu
          out="$RUNNER_TEMP/digests/$TAG"
          mkdir -p "$out"
          echo "$PLATFORMS" > "$out/platforms"
          images="$RUNNER_IMAGE $RUNNER_DOCKER_IMAGE"
          # runner-full exists for the catalogue's Full rows only; the marker
          # is how runner-manifests knows to publish it for this variant.
          if [ "$IS_FULL" = "true" ]; then
            images="$images $RUNNER_FULL_IMAGE"
            touch "$out/full"
          fi
          for image in $images; do
            key="${image##*/}"
            {
              echo "$image:$TAG-dev"
              echo "$image:$TAG-main"
              echo "$image:$TAG-$SHA_TAG"
              if [ "$IS_DEFAULT" = "true" ]; then
                echo "$image:dev"
                echo "$image:main"
                echo "$image:$SHA_TAG"
              fi
            } > "$out/$ARCH-$key.tags"
          done

      - id: runner
        uses: docker/build-push-action@c3c9e263c25d99ce0380d002d59b67737d91b0dc # v7.4.0
        with:
          context: .
          file: deploy/Dockerfile.runner
          target: runner
          platforms: linux/${{ matrix.arch }}
          # Pushed by digest and named by nothing yet; see the tags step.
          outputs: ${{ env.PUBLISH == 'true' && format('type=image,name={0},push-by-digest=true,name-canonical=true,push=true', env.RUNNER_IMAGE) || 'type=cacheonly' }}
          # Separate variants, architectures and targets so matrix jobs cannot
          # replace one another's cache. GitHub also isolates PR caches from main.
          cache-from: type=gha,version=2,scope=ci-runner-${{ matrix.tag }}-${{ matrix.arch }}
          cache-to: type=gha,version=2,scope=ci-runner-${{ matrix.tag }}-${{ matrix.arch }},mode=max,timeout=5m,ignore-error=true
          build-args: |
            BASE=${{ matrix.base }}
            OS_FAMILY=${{ matrix.family }}
            OS_ID=${{ matrix.os }}
            OS_VERSION=${{ matrix.version }}
            VERSION=${{ needs.images.outputs.version }}
            COMMIT=${{ github.sha }}
            DATE=${{ needs.images.outputs.date }}

      # The variant with a Docker CLI, for pools whose docker_mode gives jobs a
      # daemon. Everything below the client is a layer the step above just
      # built, so this costs one package install rather than another image.
      - id: runner-docker
        uses: docker/build-push-action@c3c9e263c25d99ce0380d002d59b67737d91b0dc # v7.4.0
        with:
          context: .
          file: deploy/Dockerfile.runner
          target: runner-docker
          platforms: linux/${{ matrix.arch }}
          outputs: ${{ env.PUBLISH == 'true' && format('type=image,name={0},push-by-digest=true,name-canonical=true,push=true', env.RUNNER_DOCKER_IMAGE) || 'type=cacheonly' }}
          cache-from: type=gha,version=2,scope=ci-runner-docker-${{ matrix.tag }}-${{ matrix.arch }}
          cache-to: type=gha,version=2,scope=ci-runner-docker-${{ matrix.tag }}-${{ matrix.arch }},mode=max,timeout=5m,ignore-error=true
          build-args: |
            BASE=${{ matrix.base }}
            OS_FAMILY=${{ matrix.family }}
            OS_ID=${{ matrix.os }}
            OS_VERSION=${{ matrix.version }}
            VERSION=${{ needs.images.outputs.version }}
            COMMIT=${{ github.sha }}
            DATE=${{ needs.images.outputs.date }}

      # The language toolchains on top of runner-docker, for the Ubuntu rows.
      # Its layers are several gigabytes of downloads, so they are not written
      # to the Actions cache, whose limit they would fill by themselves and
      # push everything else out of; everything beneath them is the
      # runner-docker build above, from the same builder.
      - id: runner-full
        if: matrix.full
        uses: docker/build-push-action@c3c9e263c25d99ce0380d002d59b67737d91b0dc # v7.4.0
        with:
          context: .
          file: deploy/Dockerfile.runner
          target: runner-full
          platforms: linux/${{ matrix.arch }}
          outputs: ${{ env.PUBLISH == 'true' && format('type=image,name={0},push-by-digest=true,name-canonical=true,push=true', env.RUNNER_FULL_IMAGE) || 'type=cacheonly' }}
          cache-from: type=gha,version=2,scope=ci-runner-docker-${{ matrix.tag }}-${{ matrix.arch }}
          build-args: |
            BASE=${{ matrix.base }}
            OS_FAMILY=${{ matrix.family }}
            OS_ID=${{ matrix.os }}
            OS_VERSION=${{ matrix.version }}
            VERSION=${{ needs.images.outputs.version }}
            COMMIT=${{ github.sha }}
            DATE=${{ needs.images.outputs.date }}

      # Check each finished image holds what the rest of Zoomies assumes of it:
      # the runner user's uid, the files the entrypoint execs, the pinned
      # actions/runner release, the tools workflows expect, the Docker client
      # on exactly one of the two targets, and an operating system that is the
      # one this catalogue row names. test/runner-image/check.sh says where
      # each expectation comes from.
      #
      # The same build arguments, platform and cache scope as the build above,
      # so each load is a cache hit rather than a rebuild -- and each leg checks
      # the image of its own architecture, natively. These steps once named
      # linux/amd64 outright, from when every leg shared an x64 builder; once
      # the arm64 legs moved to arm64 runners that meant rebuilding the amd64
      # image under emulation there, where git-lfs's installer crashes, and
      # then failing to run it at all (exec format error).
      - name: Load the runner image to check it
        uses: docker/build-push-action@c3c9e263c25d99ce0380d002d59b67737d91b0dc # v7.4.0
        with:
          context: .
          file: deploy/Dockerfile.runner
          target: runner
          platforms: linux/${{ matrix.arch }}
          push: false
          load: true
          cache-from: type=gha,version=2,scope=ci-runner-${{ matrix.tag }}-${{ matrix.arch }}
          build-args: |
            BASE=${{ matrix.base }}
            OS_FAMILY=${{ matrix.family }}
            OS_ID=${{ matrix.os }}
            OS_VERSION=${{ matrix.version }}
            VERSION=${{ needs.images.outputs.version }}
            COMMIT=${{ github.sha }}
            DATE=${{ needs.images.outputs.date }}
          tags: zoomies-runner-check:${{ matrix.tag }}

      - name: The runner image has what Zoomies relies on
        run: test/runner-image/check.sh "zoomies-runner-check:${{ matrix.tag }}" "${{ matrix.os }}" "${{ matrix.version }}" runner

      - name: Load the runner-docker image to check it
        uses: docker/build-push-action@c3c9e263c25d99ce0380d002d59b67737d91b0dc # v7.4.0
        with:
          context: .
          file: deploy/Dockerfile.runner
          target: runner-docker
          platforms: linux/${{ matrix.arch }}
          push: false
          load: true
          cache-from: type=gha,version=2,scope=ci-runner-docker-${{ matrix.tag }}-${{ matrix.arch }}
          build-args: |
            BASE=${{ matrix.base }}
            OS_FAMILY=${{ matrix.family }}
            OS_ID=${{ matrix.os }}
            OS_VERSION=${{ matrix.version }}
            VERSION=${{ needs.images.outputs.version }}
            COMMIT=${{ github.sha }}
            DATE=${{ needs.images.outputs.date }}
          tags: zoomies-runner-docker-check:${{ matrix.tag }}

      - name: The runner-docker image has what Zoomies relies on
        run: test/runner-image/check.sh "zoomies-runner-docker-check:${{ matrix.tag }}" "${{ matrix.os }}" "${{ matrix.version }}" runner-docker

      # EXTRA_PACKAGES is a documented way to bake a fleet's own toolchain into
      # a variant without forking the Dockerfile, and nothing above exercises
      # it: it could stop reaching the image entirely and every build in this
      # workflow would still pass. So each variant is built once more with it
      # set, and the result is run.
      #
      # That is cheap because deploy/runner-extra.sh is the image's last layer:
      # everything beneath it is a cache hit from the build above. Doing it on
      # every row rather than one covers both package families, which is the
      # only thing that script branches on, and both architectures, now that
      # each leg's machine can run what it built.
      - name: Build the variant with an extra package
        uses: docker/build-push-action@c3c9e263c25d99ce0380d002d59b67737d91b0dc # v7.4.0
        with:
          context: .
          file: deploy/Dockerfile.runner
          target: runner
          platforms: linux/${{ matrix.arch }}
          push: false
          load: true
          # Reuse the base, but do not replace its cache with this temporary
          # image.
          cache-from: type=gha,version=2,scope=ci-runner-${{ matrix.tag }}-${{ matrix.arch }}
          build-args: |
            BASE=${{ matrix.base }}
            OS_FAMILY=${{ matrix.family }}
            OS_ID=${{ matrix.os }}
            OS_VERSION=${{ matrix.version }}
            EXTRA_PACKAGES=tree
          tags: zoomies-runner-extra-packages:${{ matrix.tag }}

      - name: The extra package is in the image
        env:
          IMAGE: zoomies-runner-extra-packages:${{ matrix.tag }}
        run: |
          set -eu
          # `tree` is in no variant's own package list, so finding it on PATH
          # can only mean the build argument arrived.
          docker run --rm --entrypoint tree "$IMAGE" --version

      # The pushed full image is durable even after its builder cache is gone.
      # Loading it through Buildx keeps another copy of the multi-gigabyte
      # toolchains beside the checked image, exhausting the DinD runner's disk.
      # Finish all other builds first, then validate the exact digest that will
      # receive the published tag. PRs have no pushed digest, so keep their
      # local Buildx load and do not discard the cache it depends on.
      - name: Make room to check the published runner-full image
        if: matrix.full && matrix.arch == 'amd64' && env.PUBLISH == 'true'
        env:
          BUILDER: ${{ steps.buildx.outputs.name }}
          DIGEST: ${{ steps.runner-full.outputs.digest }}
          TAG: ${{ matrix.tag }}
        run: |
          set -eu
          test -n "$DIGEST"
          docker image rm "zoomies-runner-check:$TAG" "zoomies-runner-docker-check:$TAG" "zoomies-runner-extra-packages:$TAG"
          docker buildx prune --builder "$BUILDER" --all --force
          ref="$RUNNER_FULL_IMAGE@$DIGEST"
          docker pull --platform linux/amd64 "$ref"
          docker tag "$ref" "zoomies-runner-full-check:$TAG"

      # On its own architecture only: under an emulator this would be
      # gigabytes of toolchains unpacked and run through QEMU. The arm64 leg's
      # build above already runs every toolchain's own version check.
      - name: Load the runner-full image to check it
        if: matrix.full && matrix.arch == 'amd64' && env.PUBLISH != 'true'
        uses: docker/build-push-action@c3c9e263c25d99ce0380d002d59b67737d91b0dc # v7.4.0
        with:
          context: .
          file: deploy/Dockerfile.runner
          target: runner-full
          platforms: linux/amd64
          push: false
          load: true
          cache-from: type=gha,version=2,scope=ci-runner-docker-${{ matrix.tag }}-${{ matrix.arch }}
          build-args: |
            BASE=${{ matrix.base }}
            OS_FAMILY=${{ matrix.family }}
            OS_ID=${{ matrix.os }}
            OS_VERSION=${{ matrix.version }}
            VERSION=${{ needs.images.outputs.version }}
            COMMIT=${{ github.sha }}
            DATE=${{ needs.images.outputs.date }}
          tags: zoomies-runner-full-check:${{ matrix.tag }}

      - name: The runner-full image has what Zoomies relies on
        if: matrix.full && matrix.arch == 'amd64'
        run: test/runner-image/check.sh "zoomies-runner-full-check:${{ matrix.tag }}" "${{ matrix.os }}" "${{ matrix.version }}" runner-full

      # Only a matrix leg that passed every image check may hand its pushed
      # digests to the manifest publisher. A failed validation must not move a
      # user-facing image tag.
      - if: needs.images.outputs.publish == 'true'
        name: Record the digests
        env:
          TAG: ${{ matrix.tag }}
          ARCH: ${{ matrix.arch }}
          IS_FULL: ${{ matrix.full && 'true' || 'false' }}
          RUNNER_DIGEST: ${{ steps.runner.outputs.digest }}
          RUNNER_DOCKER_DIGEST: ${{ steps.runner-docker.outputs.digest }}
          RUNNER_FULL_DIGEST: ${{ steps.runner-full.outputs.digest }}
        run: |
          set -eu
          test -n "$RUNNER_DIGEST" && test -n "$RUNNER_DOCKER_DIGEST"
          echo "$RUNNER_DIGEST" > "$RUNNER_TEMP/digests/$TAG/$ARCH-zoomies-runner.digest"
          echo "$RUNNER_DOCKER_DIGEST" > "$RUNNER_TEMP/digests/$TAG/$ARCH-zoomies-runner-docker.digest"
          if [ "$IS_FULL" = "true" ]; then
            test -n "$RUNNER_FULL_DIGEST"
            echo "$RUNNER_FULL_DIGEST" > "$RUNNER_TEMP/digests/$TAG/$ARCH-zoomies-runner-full.digest"
          fi

      - if: needs.images.outputs.publish == 'true'
        uses: actions/upload-artifact@043fb46d1a93c77aae656e7c1c64a875d1fc6a0a # v7.0.1
        with:
          name: runner-digests-${{ matrix.tag }}-${{ matrix.arch }}
          path: ${{ runner.temp }}/digests
          if-no-files-found: error
          retention-days: 1

  # Joins each variant's per-architecture digests into the tags a pool pulls.
  # A variant goes out only when every architecture it is published for
  # pushed: a tag missing one would be a runner that cannot start on that
  # architecture's hosts, which is worse than the previous tag it would have
  # replaced. One variant failing leaves the others to publish, as it did when
  # a matrix row built both architectures itself.
  runner-manifests:
    name: Runner image manifests
    runs-on: ${{ ((github.event_name == 'workflow_dispatch' && inputs.runner == 'github') || (github.event_name == 'pull_request' && github.event.pull_request.head.repo.fork)) && 'ubuntu-latest' || 'zoomies-linux-x64' }}
    needs: [images, runner-images]
    if: ${{ !cancelled() && needs.images.outputs.publish == 'true' && needs.images.outputs.runner == 'true' && needs.runner-images.result != 'skipped' }}
    permissions:
      contents: read
      packages: write
    steps:
      - uses: actions/download-artifact@3e5f45b2cfb9172054b4087a40e8e0b5a5461e7c # v8.0.1
        with:
          pattern: runner-digests-*
          path: ${{ runner.temp }}/digests
          merge-multiple: true

      - uses: docker/login-action@dbcb813823bdd20940b903addbd779551569679f # v4.6.0
        with:
          registry: ghcr.io
          username: ${{ github.actor }}
          password: ${{ github.token }}

      - name: Set up Docker Buildx
        uses: docker/setup-buildx-action@f87e5991a6d7451dcb8d9637bfbc97413f497069 # v4.4.1

      - name: Publish the tags
        env:
          DIGESTS: ${{ runner.temp }}/digests
        run: |
          set -eu
          shopt -s nullglob
          dirs=("$DIGESTS"/*/)
          if [ "${#dirs[@]}" -eq 0 ]; then
            echo "::error::Runner images were expected, but no validated digest artifacts were produced."
            exit 1
          fi
          failed=0
          for dir in "${dirs[@]}"; do
            variant=$(basename "$dir")
            images="zoomies-runner zoomies-runner-docker"
            [ -f "$dir/full" ] && images="$images zoomies-runner-full"
            for image in $images; do
              refs="" missing=""
              for platform in $(tr ',' ' ' < "$dir/platforms"); do
                arch="${platform#linux/}"
                if [ -s "$dir/$arch-$image.digest" ]; then
                  refs="$refs ghcr.io/eyupio/$image@$(cat "$dir/$arch-$image.digest")"
                else
                  missing="$missing $arch"
                fi
              done
              if [ -n "$missing" ]; then
                echo "::error::$image for $variant was not published: nothing was built for$missing"
                failed=1
                continue
              fi
              tags=$(sort -u "$dir"/*-"$image".tags | sed 's/^/-t /' | tr '\n' ' ')
              # Both lists are split into words on purpose.
              # shellcheck disable=SC2086
              docker buildx imagetools create $tags $refs
            done
          done
          exit "$failed"

name: Cleanup Old Container Images

# CI and release workflows publish five GHCR package families. Moving tags such
# as dev, main and latest are updated in place, and cache layers and replaced
# indexes leave untagged package versions behind.
#
# "Untagged" is not "unused". The platform and attestation manifests under a
# multi-platform tag are untagged package versions too, and the daily run of
# actions/delete-package-versions (untagged only, newest ten kept) deleted
# them: v1.3.2 and :latest went on resolving to an index whose children were
# gone, and every `docker pull` failed with "manifest unknown".
#
# .github/scripts/ghcr-prune.sh deletes an untagged version only when no
# tagged or recent version refers to it and it is not an attestation of one
# being kept, and deletes nothing when it cannot tell.
#
# The dry run was read against the live packages on 2026-09-27 (run
# 36340551046): zoomies, zoomies-agent, zoomies-runner, zoomies-runner-docker
# and zoomies-runner-full each had 0 versions it would delete, so none of them
# was referenced by a current tag or an attestation of one. The daily run
# therefore deletes for real, keeping anything younger than 14 days; a manual
# run is still a dry run unless asked otherwise. Image health runs when this
# finishes, so anything it breaks goes red the same night.

on:
  schedule:
    - cron: "47 2 * * *" # daily at 02:47 UTC, a real run
  workflow_dispatch:
    inputs:
      dry_run:
        description: "List what would be deleted without deleting it."
        type: boolean
        default: true
      keep_days:
        description: "Never delete an untagged version younger than this many days."
        type: string
        default: "14"

permissions: {}

concurrency:
  group: cleanup-packages
  cancel-in-progress: false

jobs:
  cleanup:
    permissions:
      actions: read
      contents: read
      packages: write
    name: Cleanup ${{ matrix.package }}
    runs-on: ubuntu-latest
    strategy:
      fail-fast: false
      matrix:
        package:
          - zoomies
          - zoomies-agent
          - zoomies-runner
          - zoomies-runner-docker
          - zoomies-runner-full
    steps:
      - uses: actions/checkout@3d3c42e5aac5ba805825da76410c181273ba90b1 # v7.0.1
      # The rule it enforces, checked against a fake registry before it is
      # trusted with the real one.
      - name: Test the prune
        run: .github/scripts/ghcr-prune-test.sh
      - name: Delete unreferenced untagged versions
        env:
          GH_TOKEN: ${{ github.token }}
          DRY_RUN: ${{ github.event_name == 'schedule' && 'false' || inputs.dry_run }}
          KEEP_DAYS: ${{ inputs.keep_days || '14' }}
        run: .github/scripts/ghcr-prune.sh "${{ matrix.package }}"
      - name: Check that every tag still pulls
        if: ${{ github.event_name == 'schedule' || !inputs.dry_run }}
        run: .github/scripts/ghcr-check-tags.sh "${{ matrix.package }}" dev latest

name: CodeQL

# Only a change to code either analysis reads: Go for one, the UI and any other
# JavaScript, TypeScript or HTML for the other. A change to prose or to the
# install script gave CodeQL nothing new to find and held a fleet slot for
# twenty minutes finding it. The weekly run still covers main in full, which is
# what catches a query that learnt something new about unchanged code.
on:
  push:
    branches: [main]
    paths:
      - "**.go"
      - "go.mod"
      - "go.sum"
      - "web/**"
      - "**.js"
      - "**.mjs"
      - "**.ts"
      - "**.html"
      - ".github/workflows/codeql.yml"
  pull_request:
    paths:
      - "**.go"
      - "go.mod"
      - "go.sum"
      - "web/**"
      - "**.js"
      - "**.mjs"
      - "**.ts"
      - "**.html"
      - ".github/workflows/codeql.yml"
  schedule:
    - cron: "11 5 * * 2"
  workflow_dispatch:

permissions:
  contents: read

jobs:
  analyze:
    name: CodeQL (${{ matrix.language }})
    # GitHub's runner, not the fleet's. A fleet slot is a 2-core, 4 GB runner
    # whose cgroup gives CodeQL under 2 GB, and both analyses outgrew it: the
    # JavaScript queries stop with "CodeQL is out of memory" and the traced Go
    # build is killed with exit 137, on changes that touch neither. The rest of
    # CI stays on the fleet it is testing; this one job needs the memory more
    # than the dogfooding, and on a public repository it costs nothing.
    runs-on: ubuntu-latest
    timeout-minutes: 90
    permissions:
      contents: read
      security-events: write
    strategy:
      fail-fast: false
      matrix:
        language: [go, javascript-typescript]
    steps:
      - uses: actions/checkout@3d3c42e5aac5ba805825da76410c181273ba90b1 # v7.0.1
        with:
          persist-credentials: false
      - uses: actions/setup-go@b7ad1dad31e06c5925ef5d2fc7ad053ef454303e # v7.0.0
        if: matrix.language == 'go'
        with:
          go-version-file: go.mod
      - uses: github/codeql-action/init@2892aa5e19bbd11bc0cff5427e3b750a04d9e3c2 # v4.38.2
        with:
          languages: ${{ matrix.language }}
          build-mode: ${{ matrix.language == 'go' && 'manual' || 'none' }}
      - name: Build Go for analysis
        if: matrix.language == 'go'
        run: make build-nogui
      - uses: github/codeql-action/analyze@2892aa5e19bbd11bc0cff5427e3b750a04d9e3c2 # v4.38.2
        with:
          category: /language:${{ matrix.language }}

name: Dev Channel Watchdog

# The :dev channel is published by CI's run on main, and that run dogfoods the
# fleet: its jobs run on zoomies-linux-x64, the pool this repository's own
# Zoomies deployment serves. That is the right default and it is tested. It
# also means the release that carries a fix to the fleet runs on the fleet,
# so a fault that starves the fleet starves the release that would cure it.
#
# That happened. A host's only slot was left unusable by a scheduler bug, the
# fleet fell behind, and one main run held CI's concurrency slot for six hours
# waiting for runners. Five merges landed behind it. GitHub keeps one running
# and one pending run per concurrency group, and a new run always takes the
# pending place -- cancel-in-progress only decides the fate of the running
# one -- so each of the five was cancelled by the next before a single job
# started. Nothing reached :dev, and the fleet never got the fix for the bug
# that was starving it.
#
# CI already has the way out: dispatched with runner=github, every job runs on
# GitHub's machines instead. This workflow is the part that notices. It runs
# where the fleet cannot starve it, and when the newest commit on main has
# gone too long without its CI finishing, it starts that recovery run.
#
# Starting it is not enough on its own. The recovery run joins the same
# concurrency group, so it waits behind whatever holds the running slot --
# which is the very run that is stuck. So once the recovery run is in place,
# the watchdog cancels main's push runs that are still queued or running.
# That is safe for the reason the group is serialised in the first place:
# whichever main run publishes last owns :dev, and the recovery run is built
# from the newest commit, so it publishes everything a cancelled run would
# have and more. It is never done the other way round -- nothing is
# cancelled until the recovery run has been seen -- because cancelling the
# only publisher with no replacement is the failure this guards against.
#
# What it does not do:
#
# It does not retry a failure. A commit whose CI finished red is a commit with
# a problem, and running it again elsewhere would only hide it. The watchdog
# acts on CI that never got to an answer, not on an answer nobody liked.
#
# It does not touch pull requests or recovery runs. It cancels push runs on
# main and nothing else; a dispatched run is somebody's recovery, possibly
# this workflow's, and is left to finish.
#
# It does not end dogfooding. Every pull request's CI still runs on the fleet
# -- that is where dogfooding is proven, and a test holds it there -- so by
# the time a commit reaches main its code has already been through CI on the
# fleet. Main's own run exists to publish. Handing it to GitHub's machines on
# a day the fleet is behind trades little coverage for a :dev that is hours
# closer to what was merged.
#
# The limit is DEV_WATCHDOG_MINUTES, a repository variable, and 120 without
# one. It is measured from the moment the commit's CI was first queued. Main
# runs on this fleet have taken two to five hours on a busy day, so the
# default will take over on most busy days, which is the intent; raise the
# variable to give the fleet longer. Run the workflow by hand with dry_run to
# see what it would decide without it doing anything.

on:
  # The trigger that does the work. When main's CI is asked for, a job on
  # GitHub's machines starts at once and watches that commit's run. A clock
  # cannot do this here: this repository's scheduled runs start five to six
  # and a half hours after their cron says, longer than the limit the watchdog
  # enforces, so a tick arrives after the harm is done.
  workflow_run:
    workflows: [CI]
    types: [requested]
    branches: [main]
  # The backstop, for a commit whose CI was never requested at all.
  schedule:
    # Off the hour and the half-hour on purpose. GitHub runs scheduled
    # workflows on a best-effort basis and says the start of every hour is when
    # its load is highest, when a run may be delayed or dropped; the first tick
    # of this workflow, due at 18:00, never ran. A watchdog whose ticks are
    # dropped at the moment everybody else's are is not watching.
    - cron: "17,47 * * * *"
  workflow_dispatch:
    inputs:
      dry_run:
        description: "Say what the watchdog would do, and do nothing"
        type: boolean
        default: false

permissions: {}

jobs:
  # Started by main's CI being requested: waits, on GitHub's machines, until
  # that commit's CI finishes, a newer commit supersedes it, or the limit
  # passes -- and only the last of those hands over to Watch.
  wait:
    name: Wait
    # A push only. A dispatched run is a recovery, possibly this workflow's
    # own, and a watchdog waiting on it would recover the recovery.
    if: github.event_name == 'workflow_run' && github.event.workflow_run.event == 'push'
    runs-on: ubuntu-latest
    # GitHub's ceiling for a hosted job. A limit longer than this cannot be
    # waited out here; the schedule is what covers it.
    timeout-minutes: 360
    permissions:
      actions: read
    # A newer commit's wait replaces an older one's: main's head is the only
    # commit whose CI publishes, and one waiter holding the group for hours
    # would otherwise leave the newest commit queued behind it.
    concurrency:
      group: dev-channel-watchdog-wait
      cancel-in-progress: true
    outputs:
      act: ${{ steps.wait.outputs.act }}
    steps:
      - name: Wait for this commit's CI, or the limit
        id: wait
        env:
          GH_TOKEN: ${{ github.token }}
          REPO: ${{ github.repository }}
          SHA: ${{ github.event.workflow_run.head_sha }}
          LIMIT_MINUTES: ${{ vars.DEV_WATCHDOG_MINUTES || '120' }}
        run: |
          set -euo pipefail

          case "$LIMIT_MINUTES" in
            ''|*[!0-9]*)
              echo "::error::DEV_WATCHDOG_MINUTES is '$LIMIT_MINUTES'; it must be a whole number of minutes, such as 120."
              exit 1 ;;
          esac

          short=${SHA:0:7}
          while true; do
            head=$(gh api "repos/$REPO/commits/main" --jq .sha)
            if [ "$head" != "$SHA" ]; then
              echo "main has moved on from $short; the newer commit's watchdog has it."
              echo "act=false" >> "$GITHUB_OUTPUT"
              exit 0
            fi
            runs=$(gh api "repos/$REPO/actions/workflows/ci.yml/runs?head_sha=$SHA&per_page=100")
            finished=$(jq '[.workflow_runs[] | select(.status == "completed" and .conclusion != "cancelled")] | length' <<<"$runs")
            if [ "$finished" -gt 0 ]; then
              echo "CI for $short has finished; nothing to do."
              echo "act=false" >> "$GITHUB_OUTPUT"
              exit 0
            fi
            since=$(jq -r '[.workflow_runs[].created_at] | min // empty' <<<"$runs")
            if [ -n "$since" ]; then
              waited=$(( ( $(date -u +%s) - $(date -u -d "$since" +%s) ) / 60 ))
              if [ "$waited" -ge "$LIMIT_MINUTES" ]; then
                echo "CI for $short has not finished after ${waited}m; handing over."
                echo "act=true" >> "$GITHUB_OUTPUT"
                exit 0
              fi
              echo "CI for $short has been going for ${waited}m of ${LIMIT_MINUTES}m."
            fi
            sleep 300
          done

  watch:
    name: Watch
    needs: wait
    # Straight away on a tick or by hand; after a wait, only when it ran out the
    # limit. Keyed on the event, not on Wait being skipped: Wait is skipped for
    # a CI run that was not a push too, and that is a reason to do nothing, not
    # to act at once. A wait cancelled by a newer commit's is not a reason to
    # act either.
    if: ${{ !cancelled() && (github.event_name != 'workflow_run' || needs.wait.outputs.act == 'true') }}
    # GitHub's machines, never the fleet's: this is the job that has to run
    # when the fleet cannot.
    runs-on: ubuntu-latest
    timeout-minutes: 10
    # Two watchdogs deciding at once could each start a recovery run. Queue
    # them; the second finds the first's recovery under way and leaves it.
    # On this job, not the workflow: a Wait holding the group for hours would
    # otherwise queue every tick behind it.
    concurrency:
      group: dev-channel-watchdog
      cancel-in-progress: false
    permissions:
      actions: write
    steps:
      - name: Recover main if its CI is stuck
        env:
          GH_TOKEN: ${{ github.token }}
          REPO: ${{ github.repository }}
          LIMIT_MINUTES: ${{ vars.DEV_WATCHDOG_MINUTES || '120' }}
          DRY_RUN: ${{ inputs.dry_run || 'false' }}
        run: |
          set -euo pipefail

          case "$LIMIT_MINUTES" in
            ''|*[!0-9]*)
              echo "::error::DEV_WATCHDOG_MINUTES is '$LIMIT_MINUTES'; it must be a whole number of minutes, such as 120."
              exit 1 ;;
          esac

          say() { echo "$1"; echo "$1" >> "$GITHUB_STEP_SUMMARY"; }

          head=$(gh api "repos/$REPO/commits/main" --jq .sha)
          short=${head:0:7}
          runs=$(gh api "repos/$REPO/actions/workflows/ci.yml/runs?head_sha=$head&per_page=100")

          # CI reached a verdict for this commit. A red one is a real failure
          # and is not ours to hide by running it somewhere else.
          finished=$(jq '[.workflow_runs[] | select(.status == "completed" and .conclusion != "cancelled")] | length' <<<"$runs")
          if [ "$finished" -gt 0 ]; then
            say "main is at $short and its CI has finished; nothing to do."
            exit 0
          fi

          # A recovery run for this commit is already going, ours or somebody's.
          recovering=$(jq '[.workflow_runs[] | select(.event == "workflow_dispatch" and .status != "completed")] | length' <<<"$runs")
          if [ "$recovering" -gt 0 ]; then
            say "main is at $short and a recovery run is already under way; leaving it."
            exit 0
          fi

          # How long this commit has been waiting: from its first CI run, or,
          # if no run was ever created, from the commit itself.
          since=$(jq -r '[.workflow_runs[].created_at] | min // empty' <<<"$runs")
          if [ -z "$since" ]; then
            since=$(gh api "repos/$REPO/commits/$head" --jq .commit.committer.date)
          fi
          waited=$(( ( $(date -u +%s) - $(date -u -d "$since" +%s) ) / 60 ))
          if [ "$waited" -lt "$LIMIT_MINUTES" ]; then
            say "main is at $short and its CI has been going for ${waited}m, inside the ${LIMIT_MINUTES}m limit; leaving the fleet to it."
            exit 0
          fi

          # What is holding CI's slot on main: push runs past the concurrency
          # gate. A pending run is not in this list -- the recovery run takes
          # its place on its own.
          blockers=$(gh api "repos/$REPO/actions/workflows/ci.yml/runs?branch=main&event=push&per_page=100" \
            --jq '[.workflow_runs[] | select(.status == "queued" or .status == "in_progress") | .id] | join(" ")')

          say "main is at $short and its CI has not finished after ${waited}m, past the ${LIMIT_MINUTES}m limit."
          say "Holding CI's slot on main: ${blockers:-nothing}."

          if [ "$DRY_RUN" = "true" ]; then
            say "Dry run: would start CI on main with runner=github, then cancel the runs above."
            exit 0
          fi

          # A minute's grace for the runner's clock and GitHub's to disagree:
          # a recovery run stamped a second before this one's idea of now
          # would otherwise never be seen, and the watchdog would stop.
          started=$(date -u -d '-1 minute' +%Y-%m-%dT%H:%M:%SZ)
          gh workflow run ci.yml --repo "$REPO" --ref main -f runner=github

          # Wait to see the recovery run before cancelling anything. Cancelling
          # the only run that would publish, with nothing to replace it, is
          # the failure this workflow exists to prevent.
          seen=""
          for _ in $(seq 1 12); do
            sleep 5
            seen=$(gh api "repos/$REPO/actions/workflows/ci.yml/runs?event=workflow_dispatch&branch=main&per_page=10" \
              --jq "[.workflow_runs[] | select(.created_at >= \"$started\") | .id] | first // empty")
            [ -n "$seen" ] && break
          done
          if [ -z "$seen" ]; then
            echo "::error::Asked GitHub for a recovery run and none appeared within a minute, so nothing was cancelled. Check the Actions tab, and dispatch CI on main with runner=github by hand."
            exit 1
          fi
          say "Started recovery run $seen on GitHub's machines."

          for id in $blockers; do
            if gh api -X POST "repos/$REPO/actions/runs/$id/cancel" >/dev/null; then
              say "Cancelled run $id, which was holding the slot the recovery run needs."
            else
              echo "::warning::Could not cancel run $id; the recovery run will wait until it finishes."
            fi
          done

          echo "::notice::main's CI was stuck for ${waited}m; started recovery run $seen on GitHub's machines."

name: Website

# Publishes zoomies.sh from the docs that live in docs/, so the site cannot
# drift from the repository, and serves install.sh from the site root -- copied
# from the one in the repository root, so the script people curl and the script
# a contributor edits are the same file.

on:
  push:
    branches: [main]
    paths:
      - "docs/**"
      - "overrides/**"
      - "hooks/**"
      - "mkdocs.yml"
      - "install.sh"
      - ".github/workflows/docs.yml"
  pull_request:
    paths:
      - "docs/**"
      - "overrides/**"
      - "hooks/**"
      - "mkdocs.yml"
      - "install.sh"
      - ".github/workflows/docs.yml"
  # The header names the latest release, resolved when the site is built
  # (hooks/source.py). A release that did not rebuild the site would leave it
  # naming the one before until the daily build below caught up.
  release:
    types: [published]
  # A failed publish takes the whole site with it: pushes only build this
  # workflow when something under docs/ changed, so the last good deploy stays
  # up -- missing whatever the failed one carried -- until somebody happens to
  # edit the documentation again. The build is a couple of minutes and produces
  # the same site when nothing changed, so rebuild it daily: a runner having a
  # bad day then costs the site a day, not a fortnight.
  schedule:
    - cron: "29 4 * * *" # daily at 04:29 UTC
  workflow_dispatch:
    inputs:
      runner:
        description: "Where to build. github is the escape hatch from a single vendor."
        type: choice
        default: blacksmith
        options: [blacksmith, github]

permissions:
  contents: read

concurrency:
  group: pages
  cancel-in-progress: false

jobs:
  refresh-release:
    name: Refresh the website from main
    # A release run belongs to its tag even if checkout selects main. Pages
    # rejects that tag before the deploy job starts, so request a new run whose
    # ref really is main. workflow_dispatch can be triggered by GITHUB_TOKEN.
    if: github.event_name == 'release' && github.event.repository.has_pages
    runs-on: ubuntu-latest
    permissions:
      actions: write
    steps:
      - name: Start the website workflow on main
        env:
          GH_TOKEN: ${{ github.token }}
          REPO: ${{ github.repository }}
        run: gh workflow run docs.yml --repo "$REPO" --ref main

  build:
    name: Build
    # The main-branch run requested above owns both the build and deployment.
    if: github.event_name != 'release'
    outputs:
      # The pages this build changed, as an IndexNow payload (hooks/indexnow.py),
      # for the deploy job to submit once they are actually live. Empty when
      # nothing changed.
      indexnow: ${{ steps.indexnow.outputs.payload }}
    env:
      # The IndexNow key. Not a secret: the protocol proves ownership by this
      # key being served as docs/<key>.txt at the site root, where anyone can
      # read it. See hooks/indexnow.py.
      INDEXNOW_KEY: d849cbc8f4ab6dbef799f56bd99d1475
    # The site is a mkdocs build with no vendor-specific step in it, so the
    # escape hatch here is one expression: publishing documentation must not be
    # impossible because a runner vendor is having a bad day.
    runs-on: ${{ inputs.runner == 'github' && 'ubuntu-latest' || 'blacksmith-4vcpu-ubuntu-2404' }}
    steps:
      - uses: actions/checkout@3d3c42e5aac5ba805825da76410c181273ba90b1 # v7.0.1
        with:
          # The sitemap stamps each URL with the date its page was last edited,
          # which is in the history. A shallow checkout has none, and every page
          # would claim to have changed on the day of the build.
          fetch-depth: 0

      - uses: actions/setup-python@5fda3b95a4ea91299a34e894583c3862153e4b97 # v7.0.0
        with:
          python-version: "3.12"
          cache: pip
          cache-dependency-path: docs/requirements.txt

      - run: pip install --require-hashes -r docs/requirements.txt

      # --strict, so a link that points nowhere fails the build rather than
      # shipping. The docs cross-reference each other heavily.
      - name: Build
        env:
          # hooks/source.py asks the GitHub API for the latest release and the
          # repository's counts. Anonymous requests share one rate limit per
          # address, which a shared runner's address can already have spent.
          GITHUB_TOKEN: ${{ github.token }}
        run: mkdocs build --strict

      # The two files a crawler and an assistant look for first. Both are
      # generated, so a build that quietly stopped producing one would
      # otherwise ship a site nothing can index.
      - name: The sitemap and llms.txt were produced
        run: |
          set -eu
          grep -q "https://zoomies.sh/quickstart/" site/sitemap.xml
          grep -q "https://zoomies.sh/faq/" site/llms.txt

      # The header's release, stars and forks are resolved at build time, and a
      # build that cannot reach the API still succeeds -- for a developer
      # offline, not for the site. A header that names no release is the thing
      # this exists to prevent, so it does not ship.
      - name: The header names the latest release
        run: grep -q "md-source__fact--version" site/index.html

      # The badge is linked from READMEs the migration wizard has edited, out
      # in other people's repositories, and nothing in the docs build looks at
      # it: no page links to it, so --strict would not notice it going missing.
      # A broken image on somebody's front page is ours to prevent.
      - name: The CI has the Zoomies badge is published at the site root
        run: |
          set -eu
          test -s site/badge.svg

      - name: Publish install.sh at the site root
        run: |
          set -eu
          # One source of truth. `curl -fsSL https://zoomies.sh/install.sh | sh`
          # gets exactly the file in this repository's root.
          cp install.sh site/install.sh
          # A courtesy alias, because people type both.
          cp install.sh site/install
          # The custom domain. Without this file Pages serves the repo path.
          echo "zoomies.sh" > site/CNAME
          # Pages would otherwise run the output through Jekyll, which ignores
          # files and directories beginning with an underscore.
          touch site/.nojekyll

      # IndexNow tells Bing and the other participating engines which pages
      # changed, rather than waiting for them to recrawl. The protocol trusts a
      # submission only if the key file is served at the site root, so a build
      # that stopped publishing it would have every submission ignored.
      - name: The IndexNow key file is published at the site root
        run: |
          set -eu
          test "$(cat "site/${INDEXNOW_KEY}.txt")" = "${INDEXNOW_KEY}"

      # Compared against the sitemap that is live now, before this build
      # replaces it: only new pages and pages whose last-edited date moved are
      # submitted. It never fails the build.
      - name: Work out which pages changed, for IndexNow
        id: indexnow
        run: python hooks/indexnow.py site/sitemap.xml https://zoomies.sh/sitemap.xml "${INDEXNOW_KEY}"

      - name: The published install.sh is byte-identical to the repository's
        run: cmp install.sh site/install.sh

      - name: It is still valid POSIX sh after publishing
        run: dash -n site/install.sh

      - uses: actions/upload-pages-artifact@fc324d3547104276b827a68afc52ff2a11cc49c9 # v5.0.0
        with:
          path: site

  deploy:
    name: Deploy
    # Only from main, and only when Pages is enabled. Release events request a
    # main-branch run above; tags and pull requests never enter the environment.
    if: github.event.repository.has_pages && github.ref == 'refs/heads/main' && github.event_name != 'pull_request'
    needs: build
    runs-on: ${{ inputs.runner == 'github' && 'ubuntu-latest' || 'blacksmith-4vcpu-ubuntu-2404' }}
    permissions:
      pages: write
      id-token: write
    environment:
      name: github-pages
      url: ${{ steps.deploy.outputs.page_url }}
    steps:
      - id: deploy
        uses: actions/deploy-pages@368f82528645a54fb793d4d04e342629a3f51346 # v5.0.1

      # After the deploy, not before: an engine told about a page fetches it
      # straight away, and it has to find the new one. A failed submission is
      # reported and does not fail the deploy -- the site is up, and the
      # sitemap will get the pages found regardless.
      - name: Tell IndexNow which pages changed
        if: needs.build.outputs.indexnow != ''
        env:
          PAYLOAD: ${{ needs.build.outputs.indexnow }}
        run: |
          set -u
          status=$(curl -sS -o /dev/null -w '%{http_code}' -X POST \
            -H 'Content-Type: application/json; charset=utf-8' \
            --data "$PAYLOAD" https://api.indexnow.org/indexnow) || status=unreachable
          case "$status" in
            200|202) echo "IndexNow accepted the submission ($status)" ;;
            *) echo "::warning::IndexNow did not accept the submission ($status)" ;;
          esac

name: Fuzz

# The fuzz targets are the encryption boundaries in internal/cryptox, so only a
# change there, or to the toolchain it is built with, can find anything new.
# The weekly run keeps fuzzing main regardless.
on:
  push:
    branches: [main]
    paths:
      - "internal/cryptox/**"
      - "go.mod"
      - "go.sum"
      - ".github/workflows/fuzz.yml"
  pull_request:
    paths:
      - "internal/cryptox/**"
      - "go.mod"
      - "go.sum"
      - ".github/workflows/fuzz.yml"
  schedule:
    - cron: "31 5 * * 2"
  workflow_dispatch:

permissions:
  contents: read

jobs:
  fuzz:
    runs-on: zoomies-linux-x64
    timeout-minutes: 30
    strategy:
      fail-fast: false
      matrix:
        target: [FuzzParseKey, FuzzSealOpen]
    steps:
      - uses: actions/checkout@3d3c42e5aac5ba805825da76410c181273ba90b1 # v7.0.1
        with:
          persist-credentials: false
      - uses: actions/setup-go@b7ad1dad31e06c5925ef5d2fc7ad053ef454303e # v7.0.0
        with:
          go-version-file: go.mod
      - name: Fuzz encryption boundaries
        env:
          TARGET: ${{ matrix.target }}
          DURATION: ${{ github.event_name == 'schedule' && '5m' || '30s' }}
        run: go test ./internal/cryptox -run '^$' -fuzz "^${TARGET}$" -fuzztime "$DURATION" -parallel 2
      - name: Preserve failing inputs
        if: failure()
        uses: actions/upload-artifact@043fb46d1a93c77aae656e7c1c64a875d1fc6a0a # v7.0.1
        with:
          name: fuzz-corpus-${{ matrix.target }}
          path: internal/cryptox/testdata/fuzz/
          if-no-files-found: ignore

name: govulncheck

# A module that was clean when it was merged can be found vulnerable later,
# and nothing in CI would run again to say so. This scans the Go modules on
# every change to Go or its modules and once a week against main, and it lives outside ci.yml so
# the weekly run is this one job rather than the whole pipeline. govulncheck
# reports a vulnerability only when the code can reach it, which is what makes
# it quiet enough to block a pull request on.

on:
  push:
    branches: [main]
    paths:
      - "**.go"
      - "go.mod"
      - "go.sum"
      - ".github/workflows/govulncheck.yml"
  pull_request:
    paths:
      - "**.go"
      - "go.mod"
      - "go.sum"
      - ".github/workflows/govulncheck.yml"
  schedule:
    - cron: "37 6 * * 1"
  workflow_dispatch:
    inputs:
      runner:
        description: "Where to scan. github is the recovery path."
        type: choice
        default: zoomies
        options: [zoomies, github]

permissions:
  contents: read

env:
  GO_VERSION: "1.27.1"

jobs:
  govulncheck:
    name: govulncheck
    # Fork code never reaches the self-hosted fleet. A manual dispatch can use
    # GitHub-hosted capacity if the Zoomies pool is unavailable.
    runs-on: ${{ ((github.event_name == 'workflow_dispatch' && inputs.runner == 'github') || (github.event_name == 'pull_request' && github.event.pull_request.head.repo.fork)) && 'ubuntu-latest' || 'zoomies-linux-x64' }}
    steps:
      - uses: actions/checkout@3d3c42e5aac5ba805825da76410c181273ba90b1 # v7.0.1
      - uses: actions/setup-go@b7ad1dad31e06c5925ef5d2fc7ad053ef454303e # v7.0.0
        with:
          go-version: ${{ env.GO_VERSION }}
          cache: true

      # go:embed needs the directory to exist even when the UI is not built.
      - name: Stub the embedded UI
        timeout-minutes: 1
        run: make ui-stub

      # The scanner is a dependency too, so it is pinned like the actions are.
      - run: go run golang.org/x/vuln/cmd/govulncheck@v1.7.0 ./...

name: Image health

# A tag that resolves is not a tag that pulls. A multi-platform tag is an
# index, and if one of the manifests it lists is deleted the registry still
# answers for the tag while `docker pull` fails with "manifest unknown" -- which
# is how v1.3.2 and :latest broke without anything going red. This walks the
# tags people actually pull, every day and after every release, and fails
# loudly when a child manifest is missing.

on:
  schedule:
    - cron: "17 6 * * *" # daily at 06:17 UTC
  release:
    types: [published]
  # Straight after the nightly package cleanup, so a deletion that breaks a
  # tag is caught the same night rather than at 06:17.
  workflow_run:
    workflows: [Cleanup Old Container Images]
    types: [completed]
  workflow_dispatch:

permissions: {}

jobs:
  check:
    permissions:
      contents: read
    name: Check ${{ matrix.package }}
    # GitHub-hosted on purpose: whether the images pull must not depend on the
    # fleet those images run.
    runs-on: ubuntu-latest
    strategy:
      fail-fast: false
      matrix:
        package:
          - zoomies
          - zoomies-agent
          - zoomies-runner
          - zoomies-runner-docker
          - zoomies-runner-full
    steps:
      - uses: actions/checkout@3d3c42e5aac5ba805825da76410c181273ba90b1 # v7.0.1
      - name: Check latest, dev and the release in question
        env:
          GH_TOKEN: ${{ github.token }}
          PACKAGE: ${{ matrix.package }}
          # The release that triggered this run, prerelease or not. Looking up
          # "the newest full release" instead would check an older tag and
          # pass while the new one is broken.
          RELEASE_TAG: ${{ github.event.release.tag_name }}
        run: |
          set -eu
          if [ "$GITHUB_EVENT_NAME" = "release" ]; then
            # The image jobs push after the release is published; give them time.
            sleep 1800
            tag=$RELEASE_TAG
          else
            tag=$(gh release list --repo "$GITHUB_REPOSITORY" --exclude-drafts --exclude-pre-releases \
              --limit 1 --json tagName --jq '.[0].tagName')
          fi
          if ! .github/scripts/ghcr-check-tags.sh "$PACKAGE" latest dev "$tag"; then
            echo "::error::ghcr.io/eyupio/$PACKAGE has a tag that no longer pulls. See docs/development/image-recovery.md."
            exit 1
          fi

---
name: OpenCode
on:
  issue_comment:
    types: [created]
  pull_request_review_comment:
    types: [created]
permissions:
  contents: write
  issues: write
  pull-requests: write
  id-token: write
jobs:
  opencode:
    if: contains(github.event.comment.body, '/oc') || contains(github.event.comment.body, '/opencode')
    runs-on: ubuntu-latest
    steps:
      - name: Checkout repository
        uses: actions/checkout@3d3c42e5aac5ba805825da76410c181273ba90b1  # v7.0.1
        with:
          persist-credentials: false
      - name: Run OpenCode
        uses: dceoy/opencode-action@0ff64486494c3134c46df6ce0e51eda4a64e349f  # v0.7.3
        env:
          OPENCODE_API_KEY: ${{ secrets.OPENCODE_API_KEY }}
          GITHUB_TOKEN: ${{ github.token }}
        with:
          model: opencode-go/kimi-k3

name: Release

on:
  # A GitHub release is the thing users consume, so it is the source of truth.
  # Listening for a tag push misses releases created from an existing tag and,
  # when the release creates the tag, races the published release below.
  release:
    types: [published]
  # The manual path exists for the day the usual one cannot be taken: a tag
  # whose run was cancelled, or a runner vendor that is down. It takes the tag
  # rather than assuming the ref, because a dispatch runs from a branch.
  workflow_dispatch:
    inputs:
      tag:
        description: "The tag to release, e.g. v1.2.3. It has to exist already."
        required: true
        type: string
      runner:
        description: "Where to build. github is the escape hatch from a single vendor."
        type: choice
        default: blacksmith
        options: [blacksmith, github]

# Nothing by default. Each job asks for what it needs and no more: only the
# binaries job writes a release, and only the image jobs write packages, so
# granting both to both -- which this used to -- gave the image builds the
# ability to publish a release they have no business touching.
permissions:
  contents: read

env:
  GO_VERSION: "1.27.1"
  NODE_VERSION: "22"

jobs:
  # One place decides what is being released and where it is built, so no two
  # jobs can disagree about the version they stamp into a binary and an image.
  setup:
    # The rolling dev prerelease is maintained by CI. A published dev release
    # therefore produces a cleanly skipped release run rather than trying to
    # turn a moving channel into a versioned release. That is the only tag
    # skipped here: every other one reaches the check below, which refuses a
    # tag that is not a release tag out loud. This used to match `v*`, and so
    # `V1.1.0` matched nothing, built nothing, and was published as a full
    # release with no assets while every job showed as skipped.
    if: github.event_name == 'workflow_dispatch' || github.event.release.tag_name != 'dev'
    runs-on: zoomies-linux-x64
    outputs:
      tag: ${{ steps.release.outputs.tag }}
      version: ${{ steps.release.outputs.version }}
      prerelease: ${{ steps.release.outputs.prerelease }}
      runs-on: ${{ steps.release.outputs.runs-on }}
    steps:
      - id: release
        env:
          # The published release's tag, or the explicit recovery tag when this
          # workflow is dispatched by hand.
          TAG: ${{ github.event.release.tag_name || inputs.tag }}
          RUNNER: ${{ inputs.runner || 'blacksmith' }}
        run: |
          set -eu
          case "$TAG" in
            v*) ;;
            *) echo "::error::$TAG is not a release tag; they begin with a lower-case v" && exit 1 ;;
          esac
          echo "tag=$TAG" >> "$GITHUB_OUTPUT"
          # The tag is v1.2.3 and the version a binary reports is 1.2.3.
          echo "version=${TAG#v}" >> "$GITHUB_OUTPUT"
          # A hyphen is what this project's own tags use to say "not finished":
          # v0.1-alpha, v1.0-rc1. Publishing one as a full release is how an
          # installer's "latest" points at something nobody meant to ship.
          case "$TAG" in
            *-*) echo "prerelease=true" >> "$GITHUB_OUTPUT" ;;
            *)   echo "prerelease=false" >> "$GITHUB_OUTPUT" ;;
          esac
          if [ "$RUNNER" = "github" ]; then
            echo "runs-on=ubuntu-latest" >> "$GITHUB_OUTPUT"
          else
            echo "runs-on=blacksmith-4vcpu-ubuntu-2404" >> "$GITHUB_OUTPUT"
          fi

      # A published release event has to be allowed to attach the generated
      # assets: GitHub publishes the release before it delivers that event. A
      # later manual dispatch is different. Rebuilding a full release by hand
      # would replace bytes people have already downloaded behind the same tag.
      # Drafts and prereleases are still explicitly unfinished and recoverable.
      - name: Refuse to rebuild a published release
        env:
          GH_TOKEN: ${{ github.token }}
          TAG: ${{ steps.release.outputs.tag }}
          PRERELEASE: ${{ steps.release.outputs.prerelease }}
          EVENT: ${{ github.event_name }}
        run: |
          set -eu
          state=$(gh release view "$TAG" --repo "$GITHUB_REPOSITORY" --json isDraft,isPrerelease \
            --jq 'if .isDraft then "draft" elif .isPrerelease then "prerelease" else "published" end' \
            2>/dev/null || echo "none")
          case "$state" in
            published)
              if [ "$EVENT" = "release" ]; then
                echo "$TAG is the newly published release that triggered this run; generated assets will be attached."
              elif [ "$PRERELEASE" = "true" ]; then
                echo "$TAG is published as a full release, but the tag marks it as a prerelease; it will be replaced as a prerelease."
              else
                echo "::error::$TAG is already published. A released tag is a promise; " \
                     "cut a new tag rather than replacing what people have already downloaded."
                exit 1
              fi ;;
            prerelease) echo "$TAG is already published as a prerelease; it will be replaced." ;;
            draft) echo "$TAG has an unpublished draft; it will be replaced." ;;
            none)  echo "$TAG has no release yet." ;;
          esac

  binaries:
    needs: setup
    runs-on: ${{ needs.setup.outputs.runs-on }}
    permissions:
      contents: write
      # What signs the provenance: an attestation says these bytes came from
      # this workflow at this commit, which is the claim install.sh's checksum
      # alone cannot make.
      id-token: write
      attestations: write
    steps:
      - uses: actions/checkout@3d3c42e5aac5ba805825da76410c181273ba90b1 # v7.0.1
        with: { fetch-depth: 0, ref: "${{ needs.setup.outputs.tag }}" }
      - uses: actions/setup-go@b7ad1dad31e06c5925ef5d2fc7ad053ef454303e # v7.0.0
        with: { go-version: "${{ env.GO_VERSION }}", cache: true }
      - uses: actions/setup-node@820762786026740c76f36085b0efc47a31fe5020 # v7.0.0
        with:
          node-version: ${{ env.NODE_VERSION }}
          cache: npm
          cache-dependency-path: web/package-lock.json
      - run: make dist VERSION=${{ needs.setup.outputs.version }}

      # What the checksum file cannot say. install.sh verifies that the bytes
      # it downloaded are the bytes this release names; an attestation says
      # those bytes were built by this workflow, from this commit, and nowhere
      # else. `gh attestation verify` checks it against the release.
      - id: binary-provenance
        uses: actions/attest-build-provenance@4d101475d8b20a2381f78447822ac1eab6504dd8 # v4.2.2
        with:
          subject-path: "dist/zoomies_*"
      # Two files from one attestation. The Sigstore bundle is what
      # `gh attestation verify` reads: the signed statement plus the
      # certificate and transparency-log entry that prove who signed it. The
      # .intoto.jsonl beside it is the same signed statement on its own, in
      # the DSSE envelope the SLSA tooling and the OpenSSF Scorecard look for;
      # a release carrying only the bundle scores as signed but unattested.
      - name: Attach verifiable provenance to the release
        env:
          BUNDLE: ${{ steps.binary-provenance.outputs.bundle-path }}
        run: |
          set -eu
          cp "$BUNDLE" dist/zoomies-provenance.sigstore.json
          jq -c '.dsseEnvelope' "$BUNDLE" > dist/zoomies-provenance.intoto.jsonl
          # A bundle without an envelope is not provenance; refuse it here
          # rather than attach an empty file that verifies nothing.
          test "$(jq -r '.payloadType' dist/zoomies-provenance.intoto.jsonl)" = "application/vnd.in-toto+json"

      - uses: softprops/action-gh-release@efb35369e0ad2afab669f228072c1b0d510eae64 # v3.0.3
        with:
          tag_name: ${{ needs.setup.outputs.tag }}
          files: |
            dist/zoomies_*
            dist/checksums.txt
            dist/zoomies-provenance.sigstore.json
            dist/zoomies-provenance.intoto.jsonl
          generate_release_notes: true
          # A release event points at an existing published release. A manual
          # recovery keeps the previous draft-first behaviour.
          draft: ${{ github.event_name == 'workflow_dispatch' }}
          # A tag with a hyphen -- v0.1-alpha, v1.0-rc1 -- is this project
          # saying the release is not finished. Marked as a prerelease, GitHub
          # keeps it out of "latest", which is what install.sh asks for.
          prerelease: ${{ needs.setup.outputs.prerelease == 'true' }}
          # One upload at a time, for the reason the dev channel above carries:
          # a release whose binaries were uploaded all at once is a release that
          # fails on the transfer rather than on anything about the build.
          preserve_order: true

  images:
    needs: setup
    runs-on: ${{ needs.setup.outputs.runs-on }}
    permissions:
      contents: read
      packages: write
      id-token: write
      attestations: write
    env:
      BLACKSMITH: ${{ needs.setup.outputs.runs-on != 'ubuntu-latest' }}
    steps:
      - uses: actions/checkout@3d3c42e5aac5ba805825da76410c181273ba90b1 # v7.0.1
        with: { ref: "${{ needs.setup.outputs.tag }}" }

      # Two builders, one of which runs. The vendor's is the fast path and the
      # standard one is the escape hatch: a release must not be impossible
      # because a runner vendor is having a bad day. Only the setup differs --
      # both leave a buildx builder that the same build step drives.
      - name: Set up the builder (Blacksmith)
        if: env.BLACKSMITH == 'true'
        uses: useblacksmith/setup-docker-builder@19215110ab936351210feebdfa5b440b4493e184 # v2.2.0
        with:
          # The same key as ci.yml's controller image on purpose: a tagged build
          # should reuse the layers main has already built rather than start cold.
          cache-key: deploy/Dockerfile
          nofallback: true
      - name: Set up the builder (GitHub-hosted)
        if: env.BLACKSMITH != 'true'
        uses: docker/setup-buildx-action@f87e5991a6d7451dcb8d9637bfbc97413f497069 # v4.4.1

      - uses: docker/login-action@dbcb813823bdd20940b903addbd779551569679f # v4.6.0
        with:
          registry: ghcr.io
          username: ${{ github.actor }}
          # github.token rather than secrets.GITHUB_TOKEN: the same value, but
