      x-zoomies-role: viewer
      requestBody:
        required: true
        content:
          application/json:
            schema: { $ref: "#/components/schemas/UserPreferences" }
      responses:
        "200":
          description: Saved
          content:
            application/json:
              schema: { $ref: "#/components/schemas/UserPreferences" }
        "401": { $ref: "#/components/responses/Unauthorized" }
        "403": { $ref: "#/components/responses/Forbidden" }
        "422": { $ref: "#/components/responses/Unprocessable" }

  /auth/password:
    post:
      operationId: changeOwnPassword
      tags: [auth]
      summary: Change your own password
      description: >-
        Invalidates every other session belonging to this account, and ends every MCP
        connection it holds (audited as `mcp_connection.revoke_all`).
      x-zoomies-role: viewer
      requestBody:
        required: true
        content:
          application/json:
            schema:
              type: object
              required: [new_password]
              properties:
                old_password: { type: string, format: password }
                new_password: { type: string, minLength: 12, format: password }
      responses:
        "204": { description: Changed }
        "401": { $ref: "#/components/responses/Unauthorized" }
        "422": { $ref: "#/components/responses/Unprocessable" }
        "429": { $ref: "#/components/responses/RateLimited" }

  /auth/oidc/start:
    get:
      operationId: oidcStart
      tags: [auth]
      summary: Begin single sign-on
      description: >-
        Sends the browser to the identity provider. A browser navigation, not an API call:
        the answer is a redirect, and the handshake state travels in a short-lived cookie.
      security: []
      responses:
        "302": { description: Redirected to the identity provider. }
        "503": { description: Single sign-on is not enabled on this instance. }

  /auth/oidc/callback:
    get:
      operationId: oidcCallback
      tags: [auth]
      summary: Finish single sign-on
      description: >-
        Where the identity provider sends the browser back. On success the session cookie is
        set and the browser is redirected into the app; on any failure it is redirected to
        the login page with the reason in the query string, because whoever is here is a
        person trying to sign in and that is where they can try again.
      security: []
      parameters:
        - { name: code, in: query, schema: { type: string } }
        - { name: state, in: query, schema: { type: string } }
        - { name: error, in: query, schema: { type: string } }
        - { name: error_description, in: query, schema: { type: string } }
      responses:
        "302": { description: Redirected into the app, or to the login page with a message. }
        "503": { description: Single sign-on is not enabled on this instance. }

  # ==========================================================================
  # Overview
  # ==========================================================================
  /stats:
    get:
      operationId: getStats
      tags: [overview]
      summary: Fleet statistics
      x-zoomies-role: viewer
      parameters:
        - name: window
          in: query
          description: Rolling window for the completed/failed counts and queue-wait percentiles.
          schema: { type: string, default: "1h", examples: ["1h", "24h"] }
      responses:
        "200":
          description: OK
          content:
            application/json:
              schema: { $ref: "#/components/schemas/Stats" }

  /samples:
    get:
      operationId: listSamples
      tags: [overview]
      summary: Fleet samples for the sparklines
      x-zoomies-role: viewer
      parameters:
        - name: window
          in: query
          schema: { type: string, default: "1h" }
      responses:
        "200":
          description: OK
          content:
            application/json:
              schema:
                type: object
                properties:
                  items:
                    type: array
                    items: { $ref: "#/components/schemas/FleetSample" }

  /problems:
    get:
      operationId: listProblems
      tags: [overview]
      summary: Everything currently wrong, and every dangerous setting in effect
      description: |
        The Overview's problems panel. Includes unhealthy hosts, failed
        registrations, webhook delivery failures, queued jobs no pool claims,
        and every warning the configuration validator produced.

        `ok` is true and `items` is empty when there is nothing to say, which is
        the common case and is rendered as a single quiet line rather than an
        empty box.
      x-zoomies-role: viewer
      responses:
        "200":
          description: OK
          content:
            application/json:
              schema:
                type: object
                required: [ok, items]
                properties:
                  ok: { type: boolean }
                  items:
                    type: array
                    items: { $ref: "#/components/schemas/Problem" }

  /scaling-events:
    get:
      operationId: listScalingEvents
      tags: [overview]
      summary: Recent scaling decisions, with the reason in words
      x-zoomies-role: viewer
      parameters:
        - name: pool_id
          in: query
          schema: { type: string }
        - $ref: "#/components/parameters/Limit"
      responses:
        "200":
          description: OK
          content:
            application/json:
              schema:
                type: object
                properties:
                  items:
                    type: array
                    items: { $ref: "#/components/schemas/ScalingEvent" }

  /events:
    get:
      operationId: streamEvents
      tags: [overview]
      summary: Live event stream (Server-Sent Events)
      description: |
        `text/event-stream`. Every state change the operator would want to see.
        Honours `Last-Event-ID` on reconnect and replays what the server still
        holds. Event ids are `<epoch>.<sequence>`, where the epoch names one
        run of the controller; when the events since the client's last id
        cannot all be replayed -- the buffer has moved on, or the controller
        restarted -- the first frame is a `resync` event telling the client
        to fetch the resources again. A `heartbeat` event every 20 seconds
        keeps proxies from closing an idle connection.
      x-zoomies-role: viewer
      parameters:
        - name: kinds
          in: query
          description: Comma-separated event kinds to receive. Omit for all.
          schema: { type: string, examples: ["runner.updated,scaling"] }
        - name: topic
          in: query
          description: Topic prefix filter, e.g. `runner:run_k3f9qz2m`.
          schema: { type: string }
      responses:
        "200":
          description: The stream
          content:
            text/event-stream:
              schema: { type: string }
        "409": { $ref: "#/components/responses/LimitReached" }

  # ==========================================================================
  # Installations
  # ==========================================================================
  /installations:
    get:
      operationId: listInstallations
      tags: [installations]
      summary: List GitHub App installations
      x-zoomies-role: viewer
      responses:
        "200":
          description: OK
          content:
            application/json:
              schema:
                type: object
                properties:
                  items:
                    type: array
                    items: { $ref: "#/components/schemas/Installation" }
    post:
      operationId: createInstallation
      tags: [installations]
      summary: Connect a GitHub App installation
      description: The private key is sealed with the instance encryption key before it reaches the database, and is never returned.
      x-zoomies-role: admin
      requestBody:
        required: true
        content:
          application/json:
            schema: { $ref: "#/components/schemas/InstallationCreate" }
      responses:
        "201":
          description: Created
          content:
            application/json:
              schema: { $ref: "#/components/schemas/Installation" }
        "409": { $ref: "#/components/responses/Conflict" }
        "422": { $ref: "#/components/responses/Unprocessable" }

  /installations/{id}:
    parameters: [{ $ref: "#/components/parameters/PathID" }]
    get:
      operationId: getInstallation
      tags: [installations]
      summary: Get an installation
      x-zoomies-role: viewer
      responses:
        "200":
          description: OK
          content:
            application/json:
              schema: { $ref: "#/components/schemas/Installation" }
        "404": { $ref: "#/components/responses/NotFound" }
    patch:
      operationId: updateInstallation
      tags: [installations]
      summary: Update an installation
      x-zoomies-role: admin
      requestBody:
        required: true
        content:
          application/json:
            schema: { $ref: "#/components/schemas/InstallationUpdate" }
      responses:
        "200":
          description: OK
          content:
            application/json:
              schema: { $ref: "#/components/schemas/Installation" }
        "404": { $ref: "#/components/responses/NotFound" }
    delete:
      operationId: deleteInstallation
      tags: [installations]
      summary: Remove an installation
      description: >-
        Cascades to its pools, and removes their runners now, interrupting any job they are
        running: a runner has to be deregistered from GitHub while the installation's
        credentials still exist, which is before the row goes, so there is no drain here.
        Drain the pools first with `DELETE /pools/{id}` if the running jobs matter. The
        response says how many pools and runners went with it. Jobs, deliveries, scaling
        events and usage are left behind unless `purge=true`, which removes the same set
        `POST /installations/{id}/export` writes -- and only that set, never another
        installation's rows -- and wants `confirm` set to the installation's target.
      x-zoomies-role: admin
      parameters:
        - { name: purge, in: query, schema: { type: boolean, default: false } }
        - { name: confirm, in: query, description: "The installation's target, typed, when purge is true.", schema: { type: string } }
      responses:
        "200":
          description: Removed
          content:
            application/json:
              schema:
                type: object
                properties:
                  pools_deleted: { type: integer }
                  runners_affected: { type: integer }
                  purged: { type: boolean }
        "404": { $ref: "#/components/responses/NotFound" }
        "422": { $ref: "#/components/responses/Unprocessable" }

  /installations/{id}/export:
    parameters: [{ $ref: "#/components/parameters/PathID" }]
    post:
      operationId: exportInstallation
      tags: [installations]
      summary: Everything about one installation, as one archive
      description: >-
        Its pools, runners, jobs and their events, deliveries, scaling events, runner
        sessions, usage days and capacity samples, and the audit rows that name any of
        them. The App's private key and webhook secret leave only when a passphrase is
        given, sealed under it (argon2id and AES-256-GCM), so the archive can be imported
        on another instance without this one's key. Audited.
      x-zoomies-role: admin
      requestBody:
        required: false
        content:
          application/json:
            schema:
              type: object
              additionalProperties: false
              properties:
                passphrase: { type: string }
      responses:
        "200":
          description: The archive
          content:
            application/json:
              schema: { $ref: "#/components/schemas/InstallationArchive" }
        "404": { $ref: "#/components/responses/NotFound" }

  /installations/import:
    post:
      operationId: importInstallation
      tags: [installations]
      summary: Write an exported installation onto this instance
      description: >-
        All of it or none. Rows keep their IDs; runner rows and pre-pull records are left
        out, because they name hosts only the exporting instance has, and the runners'
        history arrives as their sessions. The credentials are opened with the passphrase
        and sealed under this instance's key. A 409 means a row in the archive is already
        here. Audited.
      x-zoomies-role: admin
      requestBody:
        required: true
        content:
          application/json:
            schema:
              type: object
              additionalProperties: false
              required: [archive]
              properties:
                archive: { $ref: "#/components/schemas/InstallationArchive" }
                passphrase: { type: string }
      responses:
        "201":
          description: Imported
          content:
            application/json:
              schema:
                type: object
                required: [installation, rows, skipped]
                properties:
                  installation: { $ref: "#/components/schemas/Installation" }
                  rows: { type: object, additionalProperties: { type: integer } }
                  skipped: { type: object, additionalProperties: { type: integer } }
        "409": { $ref: "#/components/responses/Conflict" }
        "422": { $ref: "#/components/responses/Unprocessable" }

  /installations/{id}/verify:
    parameters: [{ $ref: "#/components/parameters/PathID" }]
    post:
      operationId: verifyInstallation
      tags: [installations]
      summary: Check the credentials and permissions
      description: On a 403 from GitHub, the message names the permission that is probably missing rather than echoing the status code.
      x-zoomies-role: operator
      responses:
        "200":
          description: The result of the probe
          content:
            application/json:
              schema: { $ref: "#/components/schemas/InstallationHealth" }
        "404": { $ref: "#/components/responses/NotFound" }

  /installations/{id}/runner-groups:
    parameters: [{ $ref: "#/components/parameters/PathID" }]
    get:
      operationId: listRunnerGroups
      tags: [installations]
      summary: The target's runner groups
      x-zoomies-role: viewer
      responses:
        "200":
          description: OK
          content:
            application/json:
              schema:
                type: object
                properties:
                  items:
                    type: array
                    items:
                      type: object
                      properties:
                        id: { type: integer, format: int64 }
                        name: { type: string }

  /installations/{id}/rate-limit:
    parameters: [{ $ref: "#/components/parameters/PathID" }]
    get:
      operationId: getRateLimit
      tags: [installations]
      summary: Remaining GitHub API quota
      x-zoomies-role: viewer
      responses:
        "200":
          description: OK
          content:
            application/json:
              schema:
                type: object
                properties:
                  limit: { type: integer }
                  remaining: { type: integer }
                  reset_at: { type: string, format: date-time }

  /installations/{id}/report:
    parameters: [{ $ref: "#/components/parameters/PathID" }]
    get:
      operationId: getInstallationReport
      tags: [installations]
      summary: How the fleet served one installation over a window
      description: |
        The counts and exact timings of the per-installation report, each
        defined in docs/metrics.md under "Per-installation report". The
        window is moved back to the UTC midnight it begins in, so every day
        the daily roll-up answers is whole. Days past the row retention are
        counted from the roll-up; the timings are read from runner sessions
        only, and `unavailable` says where either stops. The body names no
        repository, and the installation's target only to a caller who may
        read it.
      x-zoomies-role: viewer
      parameters:
        - name: window
          in: query
          description: How far back the report reaches from now, as a duration. At most 8784h.
          schema: { type: string, default: "720h", examples: ["720h", "168h"] }
      responses:
        "200":
          description: OK
          content: { application/json: { schema: { $ref: "#/components/schemas/InstallationReport" } } }
        "404": { $ref: "#/components/responses/NotFound" }

  /installations/manifest:
    post:
      operationId: createAppManifest
      tags: [installations]
      summary: Build a GitHub App manifest
      description: |
        Returns the manifest JSON, GitHub destination and handshake state. The
        browser POSTs the manifest to `manifest/handoff?state=...` on this
        instance, which redirects the POST to GitHub. The operator confirms
        there, and GitHub redirects back with a code that `manifest/exchange`
        turns into App credentials.

        The manifest asks for the permissions the fleet needs to run runners and
        nothing else: runner administration for the target, read access to
        Actions and the metadata read GitHub requires of every App. The three
        repository permissions the migration wizard needs (`contents`,
        `pull_requests` and `workflows`, all write) are added only when
        `migration` is true, because nothing else in Zoomies writes to a
        repository.
      x-zoomies-role: admin
      requestBody:
        required: true
        content:
          application/json:
            schema:
              type: object
              required: [target, target_type]
              properties:
                name: { type: string, examples: ["Zoomies (acme)"] }
                target: { type: string, examples: [acme] }
                target_type: { $ref: "#/components/schemas/TargetType" }
                api_base_url: { type: string, examples: ["https://api.github.com"] }
                migration:
                  type: boolean
                  default: false
                  description: |
                    Also request the three write permissions the migration wizard
                    needs to open pull requests. Leave it off for a fleet that
                    will not migrate workflows. Adding them to an existing App
                    later is possible, but GitHub holds the change until the
                    account's owner accepts it on the installation.
      responses:
        "200":
          description: OK
          content:
            application/json:
              schema:
                type: object
                properties:
                  post_url: { type: string, description: GitHub destination reached through the controller's manifest handoff. }
                  manifest: { type: string, description: The manifest JSON, to be sent as a form field named `manifest`. }
                  state: { type: string, description: Single-use value echoed back on the callback. }

  /installations/manifest/handoff:
    post:
      operationId: handoffAppManifest
      tags: [installations]
      summary: Hand the browser's manifest POST to GitHub
      description: |
        Submit a same-tab HTML form to Zoomies with the exact manifest
        and state returned by `createAppManifest`. After validating the pending
        handshake, manifest and allowed destination, the controller responds
        with a 307 redirect to GitHub or the configured GitHub Enterprise Server.
        The browser must preserve the POST method and form body on that redirect.

        This is a browser navigation endpoint, not a JSON fetch. The state is
        also included in the destination URL for GitHub to echo on the callback.
        Handoff does not consume the state; the code exchange completes it.
      x-zoomies-role: admin
      parameters:
        - name: state
          in: query
          required: true
          description: Pending handshake state returned by `createAppManifest`.
          schema: { type: string }
      requestBody:
        required: true
        content:
          application/x-www-form-urlencoded:
            schema:
              type: object
              required: [manifest]
              properties:
                manifest:
                  type: string
                  description: Exact manifest JSON returned by `createAppManifest`.
      responses:
        "307":
          description: Continue the same POST to GitHub, preserving the form body.
          headers:
            Location:
              required: true
              description: Validated GitHub manifest URL including the handshake state.
              schema: { type: string, format: uri }
        "400":
          description: Unreadable or altered manifest, or an invalid or disallowed destination.
          content:
            text/plain:
              schema: { type: string }
        "401": { $ref: "#/components/responses/Unauthorized" }
        "403": { $ref: "#/components/responses/Forbidden" }
        "410":
          description: Missing, unknown, expired or already consumed handshake state; restart setup.
          content:
            text/plain:
              schema: { type: string }

  /installations/manifest/exchange:
    post:
      operationId: exchangeAppManifest
      tags: [installations]
      summary: Exchange a manifest code for App credentials
      x-zoomies-role: admin
      requestBody:
        required: true
        content:
          application/json:
            schema:
              type: object
              required: [code]
              properties:
                code: { type: string }
                state: { type: string }
                api_base_url: { type: string }
      responses:
        "200":
          description: The App was created; finish by installing it.
          content:
            application/json:
              schema:
                type: object
                properties:
                  app_id: { type: integer, format: int64 }
                  slug: { type: string }
                  name: { type: string }
                  html_url: { type: string }
                  install_url: { type: string, description: Send the operator here to install the App on their organisation. }
                  settings_url:
                    type: string
                    description: >-
                      The App's own settings page. A manifest cannot set an App's logo -- GitHub
                      takes an avatar as an upload and has no manifest field for it -- so this is
                      where the operator is sent to give the App the Zoomies mark.
                  target: { type: string, description: The organisation or repository the App was created for. }
                  target_type: { $ref: "#/components/schemas/TargetType" }
        "422": { $ref: "#/components/responses/Unprocessable" }

  /webhook-deliveries:
    get:
      operationId: listWebhookDeliveries
      tags: [installations]
      summary: Recent webhook deliveries
      x-zoomies-role: viewer
      parameters:
        - name: status
          in: query
          schema: { type: string, enum: [accepted, rejected, error] }
        - $ref: "#/components/parameters/Limit"
      responses:
        "200":
          description: OK
          content:
            application/json:
              schema:
                type: object
                properties:
                  items:
                    type: array
                    items: { $ref: "#/components/schemas/WebhookDelivery" }
                  last_received_at:
                    type: [string, "null"]
                    format: date-time
                    description: Null when nothing has ever arrived, which distinguishes "quiet" from "broken".

  /webhook-test:
    post:
      operationId: testWebhookReachability
      tags: [installations]
      summary: Check whether GitHub can reach Zoomies
      description: |
        Reports plainly whether the configured external URL is reachable from
        outside, and when it is not, gives the specific fix -- open a port, use
        a tunnel, configure the reverse proxy -- along with the option of
        falling back to polling.
      x-zoomies-role: operator
      responses:
        "200":
          description: The result
          content:
            application/json:
              schema: { $ref: "#/components/schemas/WebhookCheck" }

  # ==========================================================================
  # Pools
  # ==========================================================================
  /pools:
    get:
      operationId: listPools
      tags: [pools]
      summary: List pools
      description: Each pool carries live per-state runner counts and its current utilisation.
      x-zoomies-role: viewer
      responses:
        "200":
          description: OK
          content:
            application/json:
              schema:
                type: object
                properties:
                  items:
                    type: array
                    items: { $ref: "#/components/schemas/Pool" }
    post:
      operationId: createPool
      tags: [pools]
      summary: Create a pool
      x-zoomies-role: operator
      requestBody:
        required: true
        content:
          application/json:
            schema: { $ref: "#/components/schemas/PoolCreate" }
      responses:
        "201":
          description: Created
          content:
            application/json:
              schema: { $ref: "#/components/schemas/Pool" }
        "409":
          description: >-
            The request conflicts with the current state, or `limits.pools` has been reached --
            the code is then `limit_reached` and `field` names the setting.
          content:
            application/json:
              schema: { $ref: "#/components/schemas/ErrorEnvelope" }
        "422": { $ref: "#/components/responses/Unprocessable" }

  /pools/platforms:
    get:
      operationId: listPoolPlatforms
      tags: [pools]
      summary: The platforms a pool may ask for
      description: |
        The runner image catalogue: every operating system and release Zoomies
        publishes a zoomies-runner image for, and the architectures each is
        built for. It is served rather than hard-coded in a client so that a
        pool cannot be offered an operating system no image exists for.
      x-zoomies-role: viewer
      responses:
        "200":
          description: The catalogue
          content:
            application/json:
              schema:
                type: object
                required: [items]
                properties:
                  items:
                    type: array
                    items: { $ref: "#/components/schemas/PoolPlatform" }

  /pools/defaults:
    get:
      operationId: getPoolDefaults
      tags: [pools]
      summary: What a pool that says nothing is
      description: |
        What a new pool starts as, and separately what a size slider should
        open on. `resources` is the first: empty, because a new pool leaves
        its runners' size to the host they land on. `suggested_resources` is
        the second -- the fleet's own figures (`runners.default_cpus`,
        `runners.default_memory_mb`) -- for a form offering to set a fixed
        size instead, so it does not open on a constant of its own. The same
        figures are what a host's recommended capacity is worked out from
        before any pool exists.
      x-zoomies-role: viewer
      responses:
        "200":
          description: The defaults
          content:
            application/json:
              schema:
                type: object
                required: [resources, suggested_resources]
                properties:
                  resources: { $ref: "#/components/schemas/Resources" }
                  suggested_resources:
                    allOf: [{ $ref: "#/components/schemas/Resources" }]
                    description: Where a fixed-size form opens, never what an unspecified pool becomes.
                  min_runners: { type: integer }
                  max_runners: { type: integer }
                  idle_timeout: { type: string, examples: ["5m0s"] }
                  runner_settings:
                    type: object
                    description: >-
                      The fleet's own runner timings, so a form offering to override one
                      can say what it is overriding. They are here rather than on
                      `/settings` because creating a pool is an operator action and
                      reading the settings page is an administrator's.
                    required: [provision_timeout, drain_timeout, max_runner_lifetime, scale_up_delay, docker_wait]
                    properties:
                      provision_timeout: { type: string, examples: ["20m0s"] }
                      drain_timeout: { type: string, examples: ["5m0s"] }
                      max_runner_lifetime: { type: string, examples: ["24h0m0s"] }
                      scale_up_delay: { type: string, examples: ["0s"] }
                      docker_wait:
                        type: string
                        description: The wait that actually happens rather than the one configured — zero in the setting means the runner image chooses, and the image waits two minutes.
                        examples: ["2m0s"]

  /pools/export:
    get:
      operationId: exportPools
      tags: [pools]
      summary: Every pool, as a file another instance can import
      description: >-
        Every pool's own settings -- platform, labels, limits, runner settings --
        and nothing the instance made up about it: no id, no counts, no
        timestamps. The installation is named by the organisation or repository
        it covers rather than by its id, so the document imports on another
        instance with the same GitHub App installed. No environment value is
        ever in it; `env_keys` names the variables to set by hand. `format=json`
        wraps the list with when it was taken and where from; `format=yaml` is
        the same list with those facts as a comment. Audited.
      x-zoomies-role: viewer
      parameters:
        - { name: format, in: query, schema: { type: string, enum: [json, yaml], default: json } }
      responses:
        "200":
          description: The export
          content:
            application/json:
              schema: { $ref: "#/components/schemas/PoolsExport" }
            application/yaml:
              schema: { type: string }

  /pools/import:
    post:
      operationId: importPools
      tags: [pools]
      summary: Read a pools export back, previewing first
      description: >-
        Every pool in the document is matched by name and planned through the
        checks a create or an edit makes, and reported as `create`, `change`,
        `unchanged` or `refused`, with the current and incoming value of every
        setting that would move and the reason for a refusal. An edit that
        would leave a pool with no host that could run it is refused, as a
        PATCH is; a new pool no host could run yet is created with a warning,
        as the wizard allows. A dry run reports and writes nothing. A real run
        refuses the whole document with 422 while any pool is refused, so an
        import is one change or none; `skip` names the pools to leave out. A
        pool the document does not name is left alone, and a setting a pool
        entry leaves out keeps its current value. New pools count against
        `limits.pools` together: a document that would leave the instance over
        it is refused with 409, dry run or not, and nothing is written.
      x-zoomies-role: operator
      requestBody:
        required: true
        content:
          application/json:
            schema: { $ref: "#/components/schemas/PoolsImportRequest" }
      responses:
        "200":
          description: The preview, or the result
          content:
            application/json:
              schema: { $ref: "#/components/schemas/PoolsImport" }
        "409": { $ref: "#/components/responses/LimitReached" }
        "422": { $ref: "#/components/responses/Unprocessable" }

  /pools/validate:
    post:
      operationId: validatePool
      tags: [pools]
      summary: Dry-run a pool definition
      description: |
        Returns the field errors and the dangerous-setting warnings the pool
        would produce, without creating anything. The creation wizard's review
        step calls this, so the warnings an operator sees before confirming are
        the same ones the server would raise afterwards.
      x-zoomies-role: operator
      parameters:
        - name: id
          in: query
          required: false
          schema: { type: string }
          description: |
            The pool this would be an edit to. Its own name is then not treated
            as a clash -- without this, editing anything about a pool is refused
            because a pool with that name already exists, namely itself.
      requestBody:
        required: true
        content:
          application/json:
            schema: { $ref: "#/components/schemas/PoolCreate" }
      responses:
        "200":
          description: The verdict
          content:
            application/json:
              schema:
                type: object
                required: [valid]
                properties:
                  valid: { type: boolean }
                  errors:
                    type: array
                    items: { $ref: "#/components/schemas/FieldError" }
                  warnings:
                    type: array
                    items: { $ref: "#/components/schemas/Problem" }
                  matching_hosts:
                    type: integer
                    description: How many hosts could actually run this pool. Zero is worth saying out loud before the pool is created.
                  selected_hosts:
                    type: integer
                    description: How many hosts this pool's host selector reaches, whatever became of them afterwards. The wizard's placement step counts by the selector alone, so this is the number it shows and matching_hosts is the number its review step shows.
                  excluded_hosts:
                    type: array
                    description: Every host the selector reaches that the fleet could not run this pool on, with the reason. It is what turns "2 hosts match" followed by "1 host can run this pool" from a contradiction into an explanation.
                    items: { $ref: "#/components/schemas/HostExclusion" }
                  reduced_hosts:
                    type: array
                    description: Hosts that can run this pool, and are counted in matching_hosts, but give its runners less than a larger machine would — the pool's minimum at work, with code `reduced` and a sentence saying how much. Information, not a warning.
                    items: { $ref: "#/components/schemas/HostExclusion" }
                  image:
                    type: string
                    description: The image the pool would actually run, which for a pool that gives its jobs a daemon is the stock image's Docker variant rather than the image the request named. Empty for a pool that names no image, where nothing is stored — `effective_image` is the answer there.
                  effective_image:
                    type: string
                    description: The image a pool that names none would boot — the variant its platform picks, or the fleet's default, with the Docker swap applied. It is what the wizard's automatic path shows on its review step, where the pool being described has no image of its own.
                  resources:
                    allOf: [{ $ref: "#/components/schemas/Resources" }]
                    description: The size the pool would run at on every host. Empty for a pool that leaves the size to its host, where the per-host share is in `room.hosts[].charge_cpus` and `charge_memory_mb` instead.
                  sizing:
                    type: string
                    enum: [automatic, fixed]
                    description: Which of the two this pool is doing, so a reader need not infer "the host decides" from an absent number.
                  room:
                    allOf: [{ $ref: "#/components/schemas/PoolRoom" }]
                    description: How many runners of this size the hosts it can land on have room for, host by host. It is what a maximum is worth comparing against.

  /pools/{id}:
    parameters: [{ $ref: "#/components/parameters/PathID" }]
    get:
      operationId: getPool
      tags: [pools]
      summary: Get a pool
      x-zoomies-role: viewer
      responses:
        "200":
          description: OK
          content:
            application/json:
              schema: { $ref: "#/components/schemas/Pool" }
        "404": { $ref: "#/components/responses/NotFound" }
    patch:
      operationId: updatePool
      tags: [pools]
      summary: Update a pool
      description: >-
        Refused with 409 when the change would leave this pool with no host in the
        fleet that could ever run it, while a host can run it as it stands. The
        message names the machine it no longer fits and by how much; confirm=true
        saves it anyway, which is right for a pool whose hosts have not joined yet.
      x-zoomies-role: operator
      parameters:
        - name: confirm
          in: query
          description: Accept leaving this pool with nowhere to run.
          schema: { type: boolean, default: false }
      requestBody:
        required: true
        content:
          application/json:
            schema: { $ref: "#/components/schemas/PoolUpdate" }
      responses:
        "200":
          description: OK
          content:
            application/json:
              schema: { $ref: "#/components/schemas/Pool" }
        "404": { $ref: "#/components/responses/NotFound" }
        "409": { $ref: "#/components/responses/Conflict" }
        "422": { $ref: "#/components/responses/Unprocessable" }
    delete:
      operationId: deletePool
      tags: [pools]
      summary: Delete a pool
      description: >-
        Deleting a pool deletes its runners' records with it, so it is refused
        with 409 while any of them is still finishing a job. The refusal still
        asks them to stop, so the call that follows it is the short one: delete
        the pool again once they have gone. A pool whose runners are idle is
        deleted in one call, because an idle runner is removed outright rather
        than drained.
      x-zoomies-role: operator
      parameters:
        - name: drain
          in: query
          description: Let running jobs finish first. The default, and the only safe choice while work is in flight.
          schema: { type: boolean, default: true }
        - name: force
          in: query
          description: >-
            Destroy runners immediately, interrupting any job they are running.
            Deletes the pool in one call, because nothing is left to wait for.
          schema: { type: boolean, default: false }
      responses:
        "200":
          description: Deleted
          content:
            application/json:
              schema:
                type: object
                properties:
                  runners_affected: { type: integer }
        "404": { $ref: "#/components/responses/NotFound" }
        "409": { $ref: "#/components/responses/Conflict" }

  /pools/{id}/prewarm:
    post:
      operationId: prewarmPool
      tags: [pools]
      summary: Prewarm the pool image on every matching host
      x-zoomies-role: operator
      parameters:
        - $ref: "#/components/parameters/PathID"
      responses:
        "202":
          description: Tasks queued; hosts contains per-host pending or prior state.
          content:
            application/json:
              schema:
                type: object
                properties:
                  queued: { type: integer }
                  hosts: { type: array, items: { $ref: "#/components/schemas/PoolPrewarm" } }
        "422": { $ref: "#/components/responses/Unprocessable" }

  /pools/{id}/enable:
    parameters: [{ $ref: "#/components/parameters/PathID" }]
    post:
      operationId: enablePool
      tags: [pools]
      summary: Enable a pool
      x-zoomies-role: operator
      responses:
        "200":
          description: OK
          content:
            application/json:
              schema: { $ref: "#/components/schemas/Pool" }

  /pools/{id}/disable:
    parameters: [{ $ref: "#/components/parameters/PathID" }]
    post:
      operationId: disablePool
      tags: [pools]
      summary: Disable a pool
      description: Existing runners drain as they become idle; no new ones are created. Running jobs are not interrupted.
      x-zoomies-role: operator
      responses:
        "200":
          description: OK
          content:
            application/json:
              schema: { $ref: "#/components/schemas/Pool" }

  # ==========================================================================
  # Runners
  # ==========================================================================
  /toolchains:
    get:
      operationId: getToolchains
      tags: [pools]
      summary: What each pool's jobs install, read from their workflows
      description: >-
        The latest workflow scan: for each pool, every setup-python,
        setup-node, setup-go, setup-java and setup-dotnet version its jobs ask
        for, with how many jobs and which repositories. A job is counted
        against the pool the scheduler would give it. A version the workflows
        do not state -- read from a file in the repository, or chosen by an
        expression -- is listed with the reason rather than guessed. Empty
        until the first scan finishes.
      x-zoomies-role: viewer
      responses:
        "200":
          description: OK
          content:
            application/json:
              schema: { $ref: "#/components/schemas/ToolchainScan" }

  /toolchains/scan:
    post:
      operationId: scanToolchains
      tags: [pools]
      summary: Scan every installation's workflows for the toolchains they install
      description: >-
        Starts a scan in the background and answers at once; GET /toolchains
        says when it has finished. A scan reads every workflow file every
        installation can see, which spends the GitHub quota the scheduler
        shares. When it finishes, every pool that keeps a tool cache is filled
        with the versions it found, on each host that can run the pool;
        GET /toolchains reports each fill under `fills`.
      x-zoomies-role: operator
      responses:
        "202":
          description: The scan has started.
          content:
            application/json:
              schema: { $ref: "#/components/schemas/ToolchainScan" }
        "409": { $ref: "#/components/responses/Conflict" }

  /runners:
    get:
      operationId: listRunners
      tags: [runners]
      summary: List runners
      x-zoomies-role: viewer
      parameters:
        - { name: pool_id, in: query, schema: { type: array, items: { type: string } }, style: form, explode: true }
        - { name: host_id, in: query, schema: { type: array, items: { type: string } }, style: form, explode: true }
        - name: state
          in: query
          schema: { type: array, items: { $ref: "#/components/schemas/RunnerState" } }
          style: form
          explode: true
        - { name: q, in: query, description: Substring match on name, ID or container ID., schema: { type: string } }
        - name: include_removed
          in: query
          description: Terminal runners are hidden by default, because a busy fleet accumulates thousands of them.
          schema: { type: boolean, default: false }
        - $ref: "#/components/parameters/Limit"
        - $ref: "#/components/parameters/Offset"
        - $ref: "#/components/parameters/Sort"
        - $ref: "#/components/parameters/Order"
      responses:
        "200":
          description: OK
          content:
            application/json:
              schema:
                allOf:
                  - $ref: "#/components/schemas/Page"
                  - type: object
                    properties:
                      items:
                        type: array
                        items: { $ref: "#/components/schemas/Runner" }

  /runners/{id}:
    parameters: [{ $ref: "#/components/parameters/PathID" }]
    get:
      operationId: getRunner
      tags: [runners]
      summary: Get a runner
      x-zoomies-role: viewer
      responses:
        "200":
          description: OK
          content:
            application/json:
              schema: { $ref: "#/components/schemas/RunnerDetail" }
        "404": { $ref: "#/components/responses/NotFound" }
    delete:
      operationId: deleteRunner
      tags: [runners]
      summary: Delete a runner
      description: Without `force` this drains first, which still ends a running job after five minutes, so an unforced delete of a busy runner needs `confirm=true`. The registration is removed from GitHub either way.
      x-zoomies-role: operator
      parameters:
        - name: force
          in: query
          schema: { type: boolean, default: false }
        - name: confirm
          in: query
          description: >-
            Accept that a job running on this runner will be ended. Needed only
            for an unforced delete of a busy runner, which drains it; `force`
            already says the same thing more loudly.
          schema: { type: boolean, default: false }
      responses:
        "202": { description: Accepted }
        "404": { $ref: "#/components/responses/NotFound" }
        "409":
          description: The runner is running a job and neither `force` nor `confirm` was set.
          content:
            application/json:
              schema: { $ref: "#/components/schemas/ErrorEnvelope" }

  /runners/{id}/drain:
    parameters: [{ $ref: "#/components/parameters/PathID" }]
    post:
      operationId: drainRunner
      tags: [runners]
      summary: Drain a runner
      description: >-
        Stop taking new jobs, finish the current one, then exit. The runner is
        given five minutes to finish and is then stopped, so draining a runner
        that is busy ends its job and GitHub marks it failed. That is refused
        with 409 unless `confirm=true` says the caller accepts it; a runner that
        is not busy has nothing to lose and drains without it.
      x-zoomies-role: operator
      parameters:
        - name: confirm
          in: query
          description: >-
            Accept that a job running on this runner will be ended. Required
            only when the runner is busy.
          schema: { type: boolean, default: false }
      responses:
        "202":
          description: Accepted
          content:
            application/json:
              schema: { $ref: "#/components/schemas/Runner" }
        "404": { $ref: "#/components/responses/NotFound" }
        "409":
          description: The runner is already terminal, or it is running a job and `confirm` was not set.
          content:
            application/json:
              schema: { $ref: "#/components/schemas/ErrorEnvelope" }

  /runners/{id}/timeline:
    parameters: [{ $ref: "#/components/parameters/PathID" }]
    get:
      operationId: getRunnerTimeline
      tags: [runners]
      summary: A runner's state history
      x-zoomies-role: viewer
      responses:
        "200":
          description: OK
          content:
            application/json:
              schema:
                type: object
                properties:
                  items:
                    type: array
                    items: { $ref: "#/components/schemas/TimelineEntry" }

  /runners/bulk:
    post:
      operationId: bulkRunnerAction
      tags: [runners]
      summary: Drain or delete several runners
      description: Returns a per-ID result, so a partial failure is visible rather than hidden behind one status code.
      x-zoomies-role: operator
      requestBody:
        required: true
        content:
          application/json:
            schema:
              type: object
              required: [action, ids]
              properties:
                action: { type: string, enum: [drain, delete] }
                ids: { type: array, items: { type: string }, minItems: 1, maxItems: 500 }
                force: { type: boolean, default: false }
                confirm:
                  type: boolean
                  default: false
                  description: >-
                    Accept that any runner in this batch which is running a job
                    will lose it. Without it a busy runner comes back as its own
                    failed row rather than failing the batch.
      responses:
        "200":
          description: Per-ID outcomes
          content:
            application/json:
              schema:
                type: object
                properties:
                  results:
                    type: array
                    items:
                      type: object
                      properties:
                        id: { type: string }
                        ok: { type: boolean }
                        error: { type: string }

  /runners/{id}/logs:
    parameters: [{ $ref: "#/components/parameters/PathID" }]
    get:
      operationId: streamRunnerLogs
      tags: [runners]
      summary: Live log tail (Server-Sent Events)
      description: |
        `text/event-stream`. The controller asks the runner's agent to open an
        outbound relay and fans the output out here. Nothing dials the agent.
      x-zoomies-role: viewer
      parameters:
        - { name: tail, in: query, description: Lines of backlog before following. 0 means everything., schema: { type: integer, default: 1000 } }
        - { name: follow, in: query, schema: { type: boolean, default: true } }
      responses:
        "200":
          description: The stream
          content:
            text/event-stream:
              schema: { type: string }
        "404": { $ref: "#/components/responses/NotFound" }

  /runners/{id}/logs/download:
    parameters: [{ $ref: "#/components/parameters/PathID" }]
    get:
      operationId: downloadRunnerLogs
      tags: [runners]
      summary: Download a runner's logs
      description: |
        A snapshot of the runner's output, read until the relay goes quiet. With `tail` it
        is only the last lines, which is what a caller after the end of a long build wants
        rather than reading the whole log and keeping what fits.
      x-zoomies-role: viewer
      parameters:
        - { name: tail, in: query, description: Lines from the end of the log to return. Absent or 0 means everything., schema: { type: integer, minimum: 0, default: 0 } }
      responses:
        "200":
          description: A snapshot
          headers:
            Content-Disposition:
              schema: { type: string, examples: ['attachment; filename="zoomies-linux-x64-k3f9.log"'] }
          content:
            text/plain:
              schema: { type: string }

  # ==========================================================================
  # Jobs
  # ==========================================================================
  /provisioning:
    get:
      operationId: listProvisioning
      tags: [jobs]
      summary: Queued provisioning demand
      description: Always restricted to queued jobs belonging to this fleet. Counts respect all filters except provisioning status.
      x-zoomies-role: viewer
      parameters:
        - { name: branch, in: query, schema: { type: array, items: { type: string } }, style: form, explode: true }
        - { name: provisioning, in: query, schema: { type: array, items: { type: string, enum: [ready, expedited, paused, deleted] } }, style: form, explode: true }
        - { name: repo, in: query, schema: { type: array, items: { type: string } }, style: form, explode: true }
        - { name: workflow, in: query, schema: { type: array, items: { type: string } }, style: form, explode: true }
        - { name: pool_id, in: query, schema: { type: array, items: { type: string } }, style: form, explode: true }
        - { name: runner_id, in: query, schema: { type: array, items: { type: string } }, style: form, explode: true }
        - { name: state, in: query, schema: { type: array, items: { $ref: "#/components/schemas/JobState" } }, style: form, explode: true }
        - { name: conclusion, in: query, schema: { type: array, items: { type: string } }, style: form, explode: true }
        - { name: label, in: query, schema: { type: array, items: { type: string } }, style: form, explode: true }
        - { name: q, in: query, schema: { type: string } }
        - { name: since, in: query, schema: { type: string, format: date-time } }
        - { name: until, in: query, schema: { type: string, format: date-time } }
        - name: unmatched
          in: query
          description: >-
            Only jobs that are still queued and that no enabled pool claims. A job that
            already started or finished was run by something else, so it is not included
            however its labels read, and neither is one whose labels all name GitHub's own
            runners or a hosted-runner vendor's: those run where their labels say.
          schema: { type: boolean }
        - name: managed
          in: query
          description: >-
            Only jobs Zoomies has a hand in: one an enabled pool claims, one that
            ran on a runner this fleet started, and queued jobs no pool claims -- which
            nothing ran, so they belong here too, unless their labels all name somebody
            else's runners. Leave it off to see every job GitHub has reported, including
            those run on hosted runners this fleet does not own.
          schema: { type: boolean }
        - name: failed
          in: query
          description: >-
            Only jobs that went wrong, on either side: a conclusion GitHub counts as a
            failure (failure, timed_out, startup_failure), or a runner of this fleet that
            stopped under the job -- including one GitHub still believes is running.
          schema: { type: boolean }
        - $ref: "#/components/parameters/Limit"
        - $ref: "#/components/parameters/Offset"
        - $ref: "#/components/parameters/Sort"
        - $ref: "#/components/parameters/Order"
      responses:
        "200":
          description: OK
          content:
            application/json:
              schema:
                allOf:
                  - $ref: "#/components/schemas/Page"
                  - type: object
                    properties:
                      counts:
                        type: object
                        additionalProperties: { type: integer }
                      items:
                        type: array
                        items: { $ref: "#/components/schemas/Job" }

  /provisioning/selection:
    get:
      operationId: selectProvisioning
      tags: [jobs]
      summary: Snapshot all matching queued item IDs, capped at 5000
      x-zoomies-role: viewer
      parameters:
        - { name: branch, in: query, schema: { type: array, items: { type: string } }, style: form, explode: true }
        - { name: provisioning, in: query, schema: { type: array, items: { type: string, enum: [ready, expedited, paused, deleted] } }, style: form, explode: true }
        - { name: repo, in: query, schema: { type: array, items: { type: string } }, style: form, explode: true }
        - { name: workflow, in: query, schema: { type: array, items: { type: string } }, style: form, explode: true }

  /jobs:

        - { name: provisioning, in: query, schema: { type: array, items: { type: string, enum: [ready, expedited, paused, deleted] } }, style: form, explode: true }
        - { name: repo, in: query, schema: { type: array, items: { type: string } }, style: form, explode: true }
        - { name: workflow, in: query, schema: { type: array, items: { type: string } }, style: form, explode: true }
        - { name: pool_id, in: query, schema: { type: array, items: { type: string } }, style: form, explode: true }
        - { name: runner_id, in: query, schema: { type: array, items: { type: string } }, style: form, explode: true }
        - name: run_id
          in: query
          description: >-
            Only the jobs of these workflow runs, by GitHub's run ID -- how the Workflows
            page opens a run to the jobs inside it. Send `repo` with it: a run ID keys a
            run only within its repository.
          schema: { type: array, items: { type: integer, format: int64 } }
          style: form
          explode: true
        - { name: state, in: query, schema: { type: array, items: { $ref: "#/components/schemas/JobState" } }, style: form, explode: true }
        - { name: conclusion, in: query, schema: { type: array, items: { type: string } }, style: form, explode: true }
        - { name: label, in: query, schema: { type: array, items: { type: string } }, style: form, explode: true }
        - { name: q, in: query, schema: { type: string } }
        - name: since
          in: query
          description: Only jobs queued at or after this instant. The start is included.
          schema: { type: string, format: date-time }
        - name: until
          in: query
          description: >-
            Only jobs queued before this instant. The end is not included, so a window cut
            at one instant -- the last 30 days and the 30 before them -- counts every job
            once.
          schema: { type: string, format: date-time }
        - name: controller_version
          in: query
          description: >-
            Only jobs stamped with one of these controller versions, as `controller_version`
            shows it. `unknown` matches the jobs that were never stamped: recorded before
            the field existed, or never claimed by a pool here.
          schema: { type: array, items: { type: string } }
          style: form
          explode: true
        - name: host_id
          in: query
          description: Only jobs that ran on one of these hosts, as stamped when a runner took the job.
          schema: { type: array, items: { type: string } }
          style: form
          explode: true
        - name: job_name
          in: query
          description: >-
            Only jobs with exactly this name, unlike `q`, which matches a substring. Repeat
            the parameter for several; commas are not separators, because a matrix job's
            name contains them.
          schema: { type: array, items: { type: string } }
          style: form
          explode: false
        - name: hosted
          in: query
          description: >-
            `true` keeps only jobs whose labels all name somebody else's runners -- GitHub's
            own or a hosted-runner vendor's -- and `false` keeps the rest. Anything else is
            a 400.
          schema: { type: boolean }
        - name: before
          in: query
          description: >-
            A cursor: the `next` of the previous page, passed back unchanged. The page starts
            after the last job that one returned, in the default order (newest queued first,
            then by id), so a job queued while a client is paging cannot move a row from one
            page to the next, as it can with `offset`. Cannot be combined with `offset`,
            `sort` or `order`. An unrecognised value is a 400.
          schema: { type: string }
        - name: include_steps
          in: query
          description: >-
            `true` (the default) returns every job as a full `Job`, steps included.
            `false` returns `JobSummary` items instead: the columns a comparison reads,
            without the step list that is most of a job's size.
          schema: { type: boolean, default: true }
        - name: unmatched
          in: query
          description: >-
            Only jobs that are still queued and that no enabled pool claims. A job that
            already started or finished was run by something else, so it is not included
            however its labels read, and neither is one whose labels all name GitHub's own
            runners or a hosted-runner vendor's: those run where their labels say.
          schema: { type: boolean }
        - name: managed
          in: query
          description: >-
            Only jobs Zoomies has a hand in: one an enabled pool claims, one that
            ran on a runner this fleet started, and queued jobs no pool claims -- which
            nothing ran, so they belong here too, unless their labels all name somebody
            else's runners. Leave it off to see every job GitHub has reported, including
            those run on hosted runners this fleet does not own.
          schema: { type: boolean }
        - name: failed
          in: query
          description: >-
            Only jobs that went wrong, on either side: a conclusion GitHub counts as a
            failure (failure, timed_out, startup_failure), or a runner of this fleet that
            stopped under the job -- including one GitHub still believes is running.
          schema: { type: boolean }
        - name: faulted
          in: query
          description: >-
            Only the failures this fleet caused: the `failed` list narrowed to the jobs
            whose runner never started or stopped under them. This is the list to open
            when somebody says CI is flaky, because it is the half nobody else can fix.
          schema: { type: boolean }
        - name: workflow_failed
          in: query
          description: >-
            The other half: jobs GitHub failed with nothing wrong on this side. Sending
            this and `faulted` together is a 400, because they ask for opposite halves of
            one list.
          schema: { type: boolean }
        - name: cancelling
          in: query
          description: >-
            Narrow by whether a cancellation has been asked of GitHub and not yet
            confirmed. Leaving it off is every job, which is what a history wants;
            `cancelling=false` is what a list of work still in hand wants, because a
            cancelled job is neither waiting for a runner nor running on one. The Jobs
            page sends it with its Running and Queued views for that reason.
          schema: { type: boolean }
        - name: fault
          in: query
          description: >-
            Narrow a fleet failure to particular categories; repeatable. A category this
            build does not know is a 400 rather than a filter that quietly matches
            everything, which would read as a fleet in better shape than it is.
          schema:
            type: array
            items: { $ref: "#/components/schemas/FaultKind" }
        - $ref: "#/components/parameters/Limit"
        - $ref: "#/components/parameters/Offset"
        - $ref: "#/components/parameters/Sort"
        - $ref: "#/components/parameters/Order"
      responses:
        "200":
          description: OK
          content:
            application/json:
              schema:

                  - $ref: "#/components/schemas/Page"
                  - type: object
                    properties:
                      items:
                        type: array
                        items:
                          oneOf:
                            - { $ref: "#/components/schemas/Job" }
                            - { $ref: "#/components/schemas/JobSummary" }
                      next:
                        type: string
                        description: >-
                          Pass as `before` to read the page after this one. Absent when this
                          is the last page, and when the listing was sorted other than newest
                          queued first, which a cursor cannot continue.

  /jobs/stats:
    get:
      operationId: getJobStats
      tags: [jobs]
      summary: Job statistics
      x-zoomies-role: viewer
      description: >-
        Completed jobs counted and timed, grouped by up to two keys, computed from the job
        rows on each request. Selected by when a job was queued, over `[since, until)`;
        `until` defaults to now and `since` to a week before it. A window longer than
        `limits.job_stats_window` (90 days unless set) is a 400 naming the setting.

        Duration percentiles leave out cancelled and skipped jobs, and the response says
        so in `duration_excludes`. Queue wait keeps them. Startup is the runner's container
        start less its creation, so it exists only while the runner's own record is kept.
        Jobs with no stamped release fall into the group `unknown`.

        Jobs live for `retention.jobs` (30 days unless set), so a window reaching further
        back than that describes only what is left.

        - { name: since, in: query, description: Start of the window, included. Defaults to a week before `until`., schema: { type: string, format: date-time } }
        - { name: until, in: query, description: End of the window, not included. Defaults to now., schema: { type: string, format: date-time } }
        - name: group_by
          in: query
          description: >-
            What to group by, at most two, each named once. `controller_version` groups
            releases in the order they were first seen, `day` is the UTC day the job was
            queued, `host` and `pool` are IDs, and the values are what the listing's
            `controller_version`, `host_id`, `pool_id` and `job_name` filters take back.

            maxItems: 2

        - { name: pool_id, in: query, schema: { type: array, items: { type: string } }, style: form, explode: true }
        - { name: host_id, in: query, schema: { type: array, items: { type: string } }, style: form, explode: true }
        - { name: controller_version, in: query, schema: { type: array, items: { type: string } }, style: form, explode: true }
        - name: job_name
          in: query
          description: Only jobs with exactly this name. Commas are not separators.
          schema: { type: array, items: { type: string } }
          style: form
          explode: false
        - { name: hosted, in: query, description: "`true` keeps only jobs on somebody else's hosted runners, `false` only the rest.", schema: { type: boolean } }
      responses:
        "200":
          description: OK
          content:
            application/json:
              schema: { $ref: "#/components/schemas/JobStats" }

        request is asynchronous; Zoomies keeps the job pending until a webhook
        or the fallback poller confirms its terminal state. Requires the opt-in

  /jobs/{id}/rerun:
    parameters: [{ $ref: "#/components/parameters/PathID" }]
    post:
      operationId: rerunJobWorkflow
      tags: [jobs]
      summary: Ask GitHub to run this run's failed jobs again
      description: >-
        The remedy for a job the fleet broke. A job whose runner died did not fail on
        its merits, and running it again is the ordinary fix; this saves finding the run
        on GitHub to press the button there.

        GitHub has no job-level rerun, so this re-runs **every failed job in the run**,
        not only this one. The request is asynchronous and nothing local is changed: the
        rerun arrives as new deliveries with a higher `run_attempt`, through the same
        webhook path as everything else.

        It refuses a job that has not finished and a job that did not fail, and it does
        not check whose fault the failure was -- an operator who has looked at one and
        decided to run it again is entitled to. The `fault_domain` on the job is what
        decides where the action is offered, not whether it is allowed. Needs the GitHub
        App's Actions write permission.

          description: GitHub accepted the re-run request

                properties:
                  accepted: { type: boolean }
                  run_id: { type: integer, format: int64 }
                  fault_domain:
                    type: string
                    enum: [fleet, workflow]
                    description: Whose the failure being re-run was, echoed back for a script's log.
        "403": { $ref: "#/components/responses/Forbidden" }
        "404": { $ref: "#/components/responses/NotFound" }
        "409": { $ref: "#/components/responses/Conflict" }

        - { name: q, in: query, schema: { type: string } }
        - { name: since, in: query, schema: { type: string, format: date-time } }

      description: >-

      requestBody:
        required: true
        content:
          application/json:
            schema:
              type: object
              required: [repo, run_id, action]
              properties:
                repo: { type: string, description: "The repository, as owner/name." }
                run_id: { type: integer, format: int64, description: GitHub's own ID for the run. }
                action: { type: string, enum: [pause, resume, run_now] }
      responses:
        "200":
          description: A result per queued job of the run the action reached
          content:
            application/json:
              schema:
                type: object
                required: [results, repo, run_id]
                properties:
                  repo: { type: string }
                  run_id: { type: integer, format: int64 }
                  results:
                    type: array
                    items:
                      type: object
                      required: [id, ok]
                      properties:
                        id: { type: string }
                        ok: { type: boolean }
                        error: { type: string }
        "403": { $ref: "#/components/responses/Forbidden" }
        "404": { $ref: "#/components/responses/NotFound" }
        "409": { $ref: "#/components/responses/Conflict" }

  # ==========================================================================
  # Hosts
  # ==========================================================================
  /hosts:
    get:
      operationId: listHosts
      tags: [hosts]
      summary: List hosts
      x-zoomies-role: viewer
      responses:
        "200":
          description: OK
          content:
            application/json:
              schema:
                type: object
                properties:
                  items:
                    type: array
                    items: { $ref: "#/components/schemas/Host" }

  /hosts/samples:
    get:
      operationId: listHostSamples
      tags: [hosts]
      summary: Per-host minute samples for the capacity map
      description: >-
        One row per host per minute: its slots, what its agent measured (CPU,
        the one-minute load average, available memory), what the scheduler had
        promised away on it, and its disk. A measurement the host had not made,
        or one older than 90 seconds when the minute was sampled, is absent
        rather than zero, so a host that stopped reporting draws a gap rather
        than a flat line. Kept for `retention.samples`, like the fleet samples.
      x-zoomies-role: viewer
      parameters:
        - name: window
          in: query
          schema: { type: string, default: "1h" }
        - name: since
          in: query
          description: An exact instant to resume from. Wins over `window` when both are given.
          schema: { type: string, format: date-time }
        - name: host_id
          in: query
          description: One host's samples only. Left out, every host's.
          schema: { type: string }
      responses:
        "200":
          description: OK
          content:
            application/json:
              schema:
                type: object
                properties:
                  items:
                    type: array
                    items: { $ref: "#/components/schemas/HostSample" }

  /hosts/{id}:
    parameters: [{ $ref: "#/components/parameters/PathID" }]
    get:
      operationId: getHost
      tags: [hosts]
      summary: Get a host
      x-zoomies-role: viewer
      responses:
        "200":
          description: OK
          content:
            application/json:
              schema: { $ref: "#/components/schemas/Host" }
        "404": { $ref: "#/components/responses/NotFound" }
    patch:
      operationId: updateHost
      tags: [hosts]
      summary: Update a host's capacity, labels or reserve
      description: >-
        Refused with 409 when the reserve or the labels described would leave a pool
        that runs here today with no host in the fleet that could ever run it. The
        message names the pool and the shortfall; confirm=true saves it anyway, which
        is right when the pool is on its way out.
      x-zoomies-role: operator
      parameters:
        - name: confirm
          in: query
          description: Accept leaving a pool with nowhere to run.
          schema: { type: boolean, default: false }
      requestBody:
        required: true
        content:
          application/json:
            schema:
              type: object
              description: >-
                Every field is optional and independent; what is not named is left alone.
                The reserve is what this machine keeps for itself, in the units the host
                reports its own figures in. A reserve on a figure the host has never
                reported, or one that would leave nothing to place on, is refused rather
                than clamped.
              properties:
                capacity: { type: integer, minimum: 0 }
                labels: { type: object, additionalProperties: { type: string } }
                reserve_cpus: { type: integer, minimum: 0 }
                reserve_memory_mb: { type: integer, format: int64, minimum: 0 }
                reserve_disk_mb: { type: integer, format: int64, minimum: 0 }
      responses:
        "200":
          description: OK
          content:
            application/json:
              schema: { $ref: "#/components/schemas/Host" }
        "409": { $ref: "#/components/responses/Conflict" }
        "422": { $ref: "#/components/responses/Unprocessable" }
    delete:
      operationId: deleteHost
      tags: [hosts]
      summary: Remove a host
      description: Refused while the host still has live runners, unless forced.
      x-zoomies-role: admin
      parameters:
        - { name: force, in: query, schema: { type: boolean, default: false } }
      responses:
        "204": { description: Removed }
        "409": { $ref: "#/components/responses/Conflict" }

  /hosts/{id}/cordon:
    parameters: [{ $ref: "#/components/parameters/PathID" }]
    post:
      operationId: cordonHost
      tags: [hosts]
      summary: Cordon or uncordon a host
      description: A cordoned host keeps its existing runners and accepts no new ones.
      x-zoomies-role: operator
      requestBody:
        required: true
        content:
          application/json:
            schema:
              type: object
              required: [cordoned]
              properties:
                cordoned: { type: boolean }
      responses:
        "200":
          description: OK
          content:
            application/json:
              schema: { $ref: "#/components/schemas/Host" }

  /hosts/{id}/throttle/clear:
    parameters: [{ $ref: "#/components/parameters/PathID" }]
    post:
      operationId: clearHostThrottle
      tags: [hosts]
      summary: Lift a host's throttle
      description: |
        Lifts the throttle the controller has this host on, whatever rung it is on:
        the host takes its configured capacity again on the next scheduling pass and
        every runner here with a CPU limit is restored to its full quota on the agent's
        next heartbeat. Nothing pins it the other way -- if the pressure is still there,
        the next heartbeat steps it back up -- so this is for a host whose cause is
        known and fixed, not a way to switch throttling off. A host on no rung is
        returned unchanged. Audited as `host.throttle_clear` under the caller's identity.
      x-zoomies-role: operator
      responses:
        "200":
          description: OK
          content:
            application/json:
              schema: { $ref: "#/components/schemas/Host" }
        "404": { $ref: "#/components/responses/NotFound" }

  /join-tokens:
    get:
      operationId: listJoinTokens
      tags: [hosts]
      summary: List join tokens
      description: The secret itself is never returned; only its prefix, for identification.
      x-zoomies-role: admin
      responses:
        "200":
          description: OK
          content:
            application/json:
              schema:
                type: object
                properties:
                  items:
                    type: array
                    items: { $ref: "#/components/schemas/JoinToken" }
    post:
      operationId: createJoinToken
      tags: [hosts]
      summary: Mint a join token
      description: |
        Returns the plaintext token **once**, along with a ready-to-paste
        command for the new host. Single-use, and short-lived by default.
      x-zoomies-role: admin
      requestBody:
        required: true
        content:
          application/json:
            schema:
              type: object
              properties:
                ttl: { type: string, default: "15m", examples: ["15m", "1h"] }
                capacity:
                  type: integer
                  default: 2
                  minimum: 0
                  description: 0 lets the agent decide from the host's CPU count.
                labels: { type: object, additionalProperties: { type: string } }
                connection:
                  type: string
                  enum: [direct, tailcat]
                  default: direct
                  description: Tailcat creates a private encrypted agent connection and supplies its address in the returned commands.
                controller_url:
                  type: string
                  format: uri
                  description: |
                    The address the new host should join on, used in the
                    returned command in place of `server.external_url`. The
                    UI sends the address the browser reached Zoomies
                    on, which is the one a machine beside it can usually reach
                    too. Must be an absolute http or https URL.
                  examples: ["https://zoomies.example.com"]
