      responses:
        "201":
          description: Created
          content:
            application/json:
              schema:
                allOf:
                  - $ref: "#/components/schemas/JoinToken"
                  - type: object
                    properties:
                      token:
                        type: string
                        description: Shown once. Only its hash is stored.
                      join_command:
                        type: string
                        description: Command for an existing binary. Contains credentials; shown only in this response.
                      command:
                        type: string
                        description: The one-liner to run on the new host.
                        examples: ["curl -fsSL https://zoomies.sh/install.sh | sh -s -- --mode agent --controller https://zoomies.example.com --join-token zoojoin_... --version v1.0.0"]
                      controller_version:
                        type: string
                        description: The concrete controller build the command was generated by.
                        examples: ["main-sha-abc1234 (abc1234)"]
                      install_tag:
                        type: string
                        description: The binary and image channel selected for the new host.
                        examples: ["dev"]
                      version_note:
                        type: string
                        description: >-
                          Why the command could not be pinned to this instance's build, or
                          absent when it was. Main builds use the rolling dev asset; only local
                          or otherwise unpublished builds have no matching install tag.
        "409": { $ref: "#/components/responses/LimitReached" }
        "422": { $ref: "#/components/responses/Unprocessable" }

  /join-tokens/{id}:
    parameters: [{ $ref: "#/components/parameters/PathID" }]
    get:
      operationId: getJoinToken
      tags: [hosts]
      summary: Get a join token
      description: |
        The token's state, never its secret. Once a host has redeemed it,
        `used_by_id` is that host's id -- which is how the Add-a-host page
        knows the machine it is waiting for has arrived.
      x-zoomies-role: admin
      responses:
        "200":
          description: OK
          content:
            application/json:
              schema: { $ref: "#/components/schemas/JoinToken" }
        "404": { $ref: "#/components/responses/NotFound" }
    delete:
      operationId: deleteJoinToken
      tags: [hosts]
      summary: Revoke an unused join token
      x-zoomies-role: admin
      responses:
        "204": { description: Revoked }
        "404": { $ref: "#/components/responses/NotFound" }

  # ==========================================================================
  # Providers and machines
  # ==========================================================================
  /providers:
    get:
      operationId: listProviders
      tags: [providers]
      summary: List infrastructure providers
      description: >-
        A provider is one place machines can be rented from. The credential is never in
        the response and has no field it could be in: `credentials_configured` says
        whether one is sealed in the row, which is all a form needs to know.
      x-zoomies-role: viewer
      responses:
        "200":
          description: OK
          content:
            application/json:
              schema:
                type: object
                properties:
                  items:
                    type: array
                    items: { $ref: "#/components/schemas/Provider" }
    post:
      operationId: createProvider
      tags: [providers]
      summary: Configure a provider
      description: >-
        The credential is sealed with the instance key before the row is written. A
        provider is created renting nothing - `max_machines` defaults to zero - so that
        nothing starts spending money on the strength of a connection test.
      x-zoomies-role: admin
      requestBody:
        required: true
        content:
          application/json:
            schema: { $ref: "#/components/schemas/ProviderInput" }
      responses:
        "201":
          description: Created
          content:
            application/json:
              schema: { $ref: "#/components/schemas/Provider" }
        "409": { $ref: "#/components/responses/Conflict" }
        "422": { $ref: "#/components/responses/Unprocessable" }

  /providers/validate:
    post:
      operationId: validateProvider
      tags: [providers]
      summary: Check a draft provider without saving it
      description: >-
        A dry run over a draft, for the wizard's review step. It writes nothing and dials
        nothing - a driver's own validator is offline by contract - so it can be run as
        somebody types. It always answers 200: whether the draft is valid is in the body.
        Pass `?id=` when the draft is an edit to an existing provider, so the name check
        does not refuse it about itself. `POST /providers/{id}/check` is the call that
        talks to the hypervisor.
      x-zoomies-role: admin
      parameters:
        - { name: id, in: query, schema: { type: string }, description: The provider this is a dry run of an edit to. }
      requestBody:
        required: true
        content:
          application/json:
            schema: { $ref: "#/components/schemas/ProviderInput" }
      responses:
        "200":
          description: OK
          content:
            application/json:
              schema: { $ref: "#/components/schemas/ProviderValidation" }

  /providers/discover:
    post:
      operationId: discoverProviderDraft
      tags: [providers]
      summary: Ask a draft provider what its credential can see
      description: >-
        The same lists as `GET /providers/{id}/discovery`, for a provider that has not been
        saved yet, so the wizard can offer nodes, storages, bridges and templates as a
        menu before there is a row. The draft is checked exactly as a create would check
        it and refused with the same field errors, so nothing is asked about a body that
        could not be saved. A hypervisor that does not answer or refuses the token is
        200 with empty lists and the reason in `unavailable`: halfway through a wizard
        that is the expected state, and the form asks for identifiers instead.
      x-zoomies-role: admin
      requestBody:
        required: true
        content:
          application/json:
            schema: { $ref: "#/components/schemas/ProviderInput" }
      responses:
        "200":
          description: OK
          content:
            application/json:
              schema: { $ref: "#/components/schemas/ProviderDiscovery" }
        "409": { $ref: "#/components/responses/Conflict" }
        "422": { $ref: "#/components/responses/Unprocessable" }

  /providers/kinds:
    get:
      operationId: listProviderKinds
      tags: [providers]
      summary: What this build can rent machines from
      description: >-
        Every driver this build ships, its capabilities, and the questions its
        configuration form has to ask. The wizard renders its form from this, so a setting
        a driver gained cannot be missing from the form that collects it.
      x-zoomies-role: viewer
      responses:
        "200":
          description: OK
          content:
            application/json:
              schema:
                type: object
                properties:
                  items:
                    type: array
                    items: { $ref: "#/components/schemas/ProviderKind" }

  /providers/{id}:
    parameters: [{ $ref: "#/components/parameters/PathID" }]
    get:
      operationId: getProvider
      tags: [providers]
      summary: Get a provider
      x-zoomies-role: viewer
      responses:
        "200":
          description: OK
          content:
            application/json:
              schema: { $ref: "#/components/schemas/Provider" }
        "404": { $ref: "#/components/responses/NotFound" }
    patch:
      operationId: updateProvider
      tags: [providers]
      summary: Change a provider's settings, shape or ceilings
      description: >-
        Every field is optional and independent; what is not named is left alone. A
        credential of `""` leaves the stored one alone, so a form with a blank password
        box does not erase it. A provider's kind cannot be changed: the machines it
        already owns are that kind.
      x-zoomies-role: admin
      requestBody:
        required: true
        content:
          application/json:
            schema: { $ref: "#/components/schemas/ProviderInput" }
      responses:
        "200":
          description: OK
          content:
            application/json:
              schema: { $ref: "#/components/schemas/Provider" }
        "404": { $ref: "#/components/responses/NotFound" }
        "422": { $ref: "#/components/responses/Unprocessable" }
    delete:
      operationId: deleteProvider
      tags: [providers]
      summary: Remove a provider
      description: >-
        Refused while any of its machines still believes it holds a resource, naming how
        many. The rows are the only record of what was rented, so the machines go first.
      x-zoomies-role: admin
      responses:
        "204": { description: Removed }
        "404": { $ref: "#/components/responses/NotFound" }
        "409": { $ref: "#/components/responses/Conflict" }

  /providers/{id}/check:
    parameters: [{ $ref: "#/components/parameters/PathID" }]
    post:
      operationId: checkProvider
      tags: [providers]
      summary: Run the live preflight
      description: >-
        Asks the provider what it would refuse, changing nothing there. The result is
        recorded on the row as well as returned, so a check run in a terminal quiets the
        warning the UI is showing. Audited, because it uses the credential.
      x-zoomies-role: operator
      responses:
        "200":
          description: OK
          content:
            application/json:
              schema: { $ref: "#/components/schemas/ProviderCheck" }
        "404": { $ref: "#/components/responses/NotFound" }
        "409": { $ref: "#/components/responses/Conflict" }

  /providers/{id}/discovery:
    parameters: [{ $ref: "#/components/parameters/PathID" }]
    get:
      operationId: getProviderDiscovery
      tags: [providers]
      summary: What this credential can actually see
      description: >-
        The nodes, storages, bridges and templates a provider offers, so the form presents
        a menu rather than asking somebody to go and look an identifier up. A driver that
        cannot list them answers 409 and the form asks for the identifiers instead.
      x-zoomies-role: operator
      responses:
        "200":
          description: OK
          content:
            application/json:
              schema: { $ref: "#/components/schemas/ProviderDiscovery" }
        "404": { $ref: "#/components/responses/NotFound" }
        "409": { $ref: "#/components/responses/Conflict" }

  /providers/{id}/orphans:
    parameters: [{ $ref: "#/components/parameters/PathID" }]
    get:
      operationId: getProviderOrphans
      tags: [providers]
      summary: Rows and resources that disagree
      description: >-
        The three ways a machine row and a real resource can fail to agree: a resource
        wearing this fleet's naming that no row accounts for, a row that holds nothing,
        and a machine whose ownership nothing has been able to confirm. Nothing here is
        ever acted on automatically.
      x-zoomies-role: admin
      responses:
        "200":
          description: OK
          content:
            application/json:
              schema: { $ref: "#/components/schemas/ProviderOrphans" }
        "404": { $ref: "#/components/responses/NotFound" }

  /providers/{id}/pause:
    parameters: [{ $ref: "#/components/parameters/PathID" }]
    post:
      operationId: pauseProvider
      tags: [providers]
      summary: Stop this provider buying new machines
      description: >-
        The kill switch. It blocks new machines only: draining, deleting, recovering and
        verifying ownership all continue, because a switch that stopped those would strand
        running machines nobody is watching. Pressing it twice is not an error.
      x-zoomies-role: operator
      requestBody:
        required: false
        content:
          application/json:
            schema:
              type: object
              properties:
                reason: { type: string, description: Why, for the card and the audit row. }
      responses:
        "200":
          description: OK
          content:
            application/json:
              schema: { $ref: "#/components/schemas/Provider" }
        "404": { $ref: "#/components/responses/NotFound" }

  /providers/{id}/resume:
    parameters: [{ $ref: "#/components/parameters/PathID" }]
    post:
      operationId: resumeProvider
      tags: [providers]
      summary: Let this provider buy machines again
      description: Pressing it twice is not an error.
      x-zoomies-role: operator
      responses:
        "200":
          description: OK
          content:
            application/json:
              schema: { $ref: "#/components/schemas/Provider" }
        "404": { $ref: "#/components/responses/NotFound" }

  /machines:
    get:
      operationId: listMachines
      tags: [providers]
      summary: List rented machines
      description: >-
        There is deliberately no POST. A machine exists because demand asked for one: one
        creation path means one accounting path, and a machine made by hand would be
        supply the reconciler would then decide to delete.
      x-zoomies-role: viewer
      parameters:
        - { $ref: "#/components/parameters/Limit" }
        - { $ref: "#/components/parameters/Offset" }
        - { $ref: "#/components/parameters/Sort" }
        - { $ref: "#/components/parameters/Order" }
        - { name: provider, in: query, schema: { type: string }, description: Repeatable, or comma-separated. }
        - { name: pool, in: query, schema: { type: string } }
        - { name: host, in: query, schema: { type: string } }
        - { name: state, in: query, schema: { $ref: "#/components/schemas/MachineState" } }
        - { name: q, in: query, schema: { type: string } }
        - { name: include_deleted, in: query, schema: { type: boolean, default: false }, description: Keep machines whose resource is confirmed gone. }
      responses:
        "200":
          description: OK
          content:
            application/json:
              schema:
                allOf:
                  - $ref: "#/components/schemas/Page"
                  - type: object
                    properties:
                      items:
                        type: array
                        items: { $ref: "#/components/schemas/Machine" }

  /machines/{id}:
    parameters: [{ $ref: "#/components/parameters/PathID" }]
    get:
      operationId: getMachine
      tags: [providers]
      summary: Get a machine, with the phases it has reached
      x-zoomies-role: viewer
      responses:
        "200":
          description: OK
          content:
            application/json:
              schema: { $ref: "#/components/schemas/Machine" }
        "404": { $ref: "#/components/responses/NotFound" }
    delete:
      operationId: deleteMachine
      tags: [providers]
      summary: Destroy a machine and the resource behind it
      description: >-
        Records the intent and answers with the machine in `deleting`: a delete is
        finished when the resource can no longer be found, not when the provider returns.
        Refused while runners are still going unless forced. A quarantined machine is
        never deletable, forced or not - its resource may belong to somebody else - and
        the escape hatch there is release.
      x-zoomies-role: admin
      parameters:
        - { name: force, in: query, schema: { type: boolean, default: false } }
      responses:
        "200":
          description: OK
          content:
            application/json:
              schema: { $ref: "#/components/schemas/Machine" }
        "404": { $ref: "#/components/responses/NotFound" }
        "409": { $ref: "#/components/responses/Conflict" }

  /machines/{id}/drain:
    parameters: [{ $ref: "#/components/parameters/PathID" }]
    post:
      operationId: drainMachine
      tags: [providers]
      summary: Cordon a machine and let its runners finish
      description: >-
        Reversible right up until the delete starts: demand coming back takes a draining
        machine to ready again rather than paying for a new one.
      x-zoomies-role: operator
      responses:
        "200":
          description: OK
          content:
            application/json:
              schema: { $ref: "#/components/schemas/Machine" }
        "404": { $ref: "#/components/responses/NotFound" }
        "409": { $ref: "#/components/responses/Conflict" }

  /machines/{id}/release:
    parameters: [{ $ref: "#/components/parameters/PathID" }]
    post:
      operationId: releaseMachine
      tags: [providers]
      summary: Forget a machine without touching its resource
      description: >-
        For the machine nobody can safely delete: a quarantined one whose resource turned
        out to be somebody else's, or a row for a resource that was removed by hand. The
        machine's name must be in the body to confirm. If the resource does still exist it
        goes on running, so the audit row keeps the provider's identifiers for it after
        the database has stopped holding them.
      x-zoomies-role: admin
      requestBody:
        required: true
        content:
          application/json:
            schema:
              type: object
              required: [name]
              properties:
                name: { type: string, description: The machine's name, typed to confirm. }
      responses:
        "204": { description: Forgotten }
        "404": { $ref: "#/components/responses/NotFound" }
        "422": { $ref: "#/components/responses/Unprocessable" }

  # ==========================================================================
  # Migrations
  # ==========================================================================
  /migrations/plan:
    post:
      operationId: planMigration
      tags: [migrations]
      summary: What moving these repositories onto Zoomies would change
      description: |
        Reads the workflow files in the repositories a GitHub App installation
        can see, and reports the `runs-on` lines it would rewrite, the ones it
        would leave alone and why, and a unified diff of each change.

        It writes nothing. Everything it returns is a proposal for the operator
        to edit before `POST /migrations/pull-requests` acts on it.

        With no `mapping`, the server proposes one from the pools that exist,
        matching each GitHub-hosted label against the pool that promises the
        same operating system and architecture. A label with no plausible pool
        is left unmapped rather than mapped approximately, and appears in
        `unmapped`.

        `mapping` is one answer per label for every repository, which is what
        most fleets want. `overrides` are the exceptions to it: each names one
        job in one workflow file in one repository and sends it somewhere else,
        or -- with an empty `to` -- leaves that one job on GitHub's runners.
      x-zoomies-role: operator
      requestBody:
        required: true
        content:
          application/json:
            schema:
              type: object
              required: [installation_id]
              properties:
                installation_id: { type: string }
                repos:
                  type: array
                  items: { type: string }
                  description: Limits the plan to these repositories. Empty means every repository the installation can see, up to the server's limit.
                mapping:
                  type: object
                  additionalProperties: { type: string }
                  description: >-
                    Hosted label to the runs-on value that replaces it, e.g.
                    {"ubuntu-latest": "zoomies-linux-x64"}. Empty asks the server to propose one.
                overrides:
                  type: array
                  items: { $ref: "#/components/schemas/MigrationOverride" }
                  description: >-
                    Exceptions to `mapping`, each naming one job in one workflow file in one
                    repository. Empty is the common case: most fleets want one answer per
                    hosted-runner label everywhere.
                cursor:
                  type: string
                  description: >-
                    The page of repositories to read: the `next_cursor` a previous plan
                    returned, which is the full name of the last repository it listed.
                    Empty starts at the first page. Ignored when `repos` names repositories.
      responses:
        "200":
          description: The plan
          content:
            application/json:
              schema: { $ref: "#/components/schemas/MigrationPlan" }
        "422": { $ref: "#/components/responses/Unprocessable" }

  /migrations/pull-requests:
    post:
      operationId: openMigrationPullRequests
      tags: [migrations]
      summary: Open the pull requests a plan described
      description: |
        Opens one pull request per repository, each on its own branch, changing
        only the workflow files whose `runs-on` the mapping covers.

        The plan is recomputed here from the repositories' current contents
        rather than taken from the client: the workflows may have changed since
        the review step, and accepting file contents from a browser would make
        this a way to write arbitrary files into any repository the App can
        reach. Every file is committed against the blob SHA it was read at, so a
        push that lands in between is a conflict rather than a silent revert.

        The App needs three permissions the rest of Zoomies does not:
        Contents (write), Pull requests (write) and Workflows (write). The plan
        endpoint reports which are missing before anything is attempted.
      x-zoomies-role: operator
      requestBody:
        required: true
        content:
          application/json:
            schema:
              type: object
              required: [installation_id, repos]
              properties:
                installation_id: { type: string }
                repos:
                  type: array
                  items: { type: string }
                  description: The repositories to open pull requests on. Required; this endpoint never defaults to every repository an App can see.
                mapping:
                  type: object
                  additionalProperties: { type: string }
                overrides:
                  type: array
                  items: { $ref: "#/components/schemas/MigrationOverride" }
                  description: >-
                    Exceptions to `mapping`. A request with no mapped label is accepted when at
                    least one override carries a `to`, because pointing three jobs at a pool by
                    name is a migration too.
                workflows:
                  type: object
                  additionalProperties:
                    type: array
                    items: { type: string }
                  description: >-
                    Narrows a repository to these workflow files, keyed by repository, e.g.
                    {"acme/widgets": [".github/workflows/ci.yml"]}. A repository left out of
                    the map gets every file the mapping would change. A path that is not
                    directly under .github/workflows is rejected.
                title: { type: string, description: Overrides the default pull request title. }
                body: { type: string, description: Overrides the generated body, which lists what moved and what was left alone. }
                commit_message: { type: string, description: Overrides the default commit message. }
                badge:
                  type: boolean
                  default: true
                  description: >-
                    Whether each pull request also adds the "CI has the Zoomies" badge to the
                    repository's README, at the end of the row of badges it already has or on
                    its own line under the title. On unless you say otherwise; a README that is
                    missing, not Markdown, or already carries the badge is left alone and the
                    result says so. The badge never stops a pull request being opened.
      responses:
        "200":
          description: What happened to each repository
          content:
            application/json:
              schema: { $ref: "#/components/schemas/MigrationOutcome" }
        "422": { $ref: "#/components/responses/Unprocessable" }

  # ==========================================================================
  # Audit
  # ==========================================================================
  /audit:
    get:
      operationId: listAudit
      tags: [audit]
      summary: The audit log
      x-zoomies-role: viewer
      parameters:
        - { name: actor_id, in: query, schema: { type: array, items: { type: string } }, style: form, explode: true }
        - { name: action, in: query, schema: { type: array, items: { type: string } }, style: form, explode: true }
        - { name: target_kind, in: query, schema: { type: array, items: { type: string } }, style: form, explode: true }
        - { name: target_id, in: query, schema: { type: string } }
        - { name: q, in: query, schema: { type: string } }
        - { name: since, in: query, schema: { type: string, format: date-time } }
        - { name: until, in: query, schema: { type: string, format: date-time } }
        - $ref: "#/components/parameters/Limit"
        - $ref: "#/components/parameters/Offset"
        - $ref: "#/components/parameters/Sort"
        - $ref: "#/components/parameters/Order"
      responses:
        "200":
          description: OK
          content:
            application/json:
              schema:
                allOf:
                  - $ref: "#/components/schemas/Page"
                  - type: object
                    properties:
                      items:
                        type: array
                        items: { $ref: "#/components/schemas/AuditEvent" }

  /audit/actions:
    get:
      operationId: listAuditActions
      tags: [audit]
      summary: Distinct action names, for the filter menu
      x-zoomies-role: viewer
      responses:
        "200":
          description: OK
          content:
            application/json:
              schema:
                type: object
                properties:
                  items: { type: array, items: { type: string } }

  # ==========================================================================
  # Administration
  # ==========================================================================
  /users:
    get:
      operationId: listUsers
      tags: [admin]
      summary: List users
      x-zoomies-role: admin
      responses:
        "200":
          description: OK
          content:
            application/json:
              schema:
                type: object
                properties:
                  items: { type: array, items: { $ref: "#/components/schemas/User" } }
    post:
      operationId: createUser
      tags: [admin]
      summary: Create a user
      x-zoomies-role: admin
      requestBody:
        required: true
        content:
          application/json:
            schema:
              type: object
              required: [username, role]
              properties:
                username: { type: string, minLength: 1, maxLength: 64 }
                password: { type: string, minLength: 12, format: password, description: Omit for an account that will sign in through OIDC. }
                email: { type: string, format: email }
                display_name: { type: string }
                role: { $ref: "#/components/schemas/Role" }
      responses:
        "201":
          description: Created
          content:
            application/json:
              schema: { $ref: "#/components/schemas/User" }
        "409": { $ref: "#/components/responses/Conflict" }

  /users/{id}:
    parameters: [{ $ref: "#/components/parameters/PathID" }]
    get:
      operationId: getUser
      tags: [admin]
      summary: Get a user
      x-zoomies-role: admin
      responses:
        "200":
          description: OK
          content:
            application/json:
              schema: { $ref: "#/components/schemas/User" }
        "404": { $ref: "#/components/responses/NotFound" }
    patch:
      operationId: updateUser
      tags: [admin]
      summary: Update a user
      description: Refused if it would leave the instance with no enabled administrator.
      x-zoomies-role: admin
      requestBody:
        required: true
        content:
          application/json:
            schema:
              type: object
              properties:
                email: { type: string, format: email }
                display_name: { type: string }
                role: { $ref: "#/components/schemas/Role" }
                disabled: { type: boolean }
      responses:
        "200":
          description: OK
          content:
            application/json:
              schema: { $ref: "#/components/schemas/User" }
        "409": { $ref: "#/components/responses/Conflict" }
    delete:
      operationId: deleteUser
      tags: [admin]
      summary: Delete a user
      description: Refused if it would leave the instance with no enabled administrator.
      x-zoomies-role: admin
      responses:
        "204": { description: Deleted }
        "409": { $ref: "#/components/responses/Conflict" }

  /users/{id}/password:
    parameters: [{ $ref: "#/components/parameters/PathID" }]
    post:
      operationId: resetUserPassword
      tags: [admin]
      summary: Reset a user's password
      description: Sets `must_change_password`, so the user picks their own on next sign-in.
      x-zoomies-role: admin
      requestBody:
        required: true
        content:
          application/json:
            schema:
              type: object
              required: [new_password]
              properties:
                new_password: { type: string, minLength: 12, format: password }
      responses:
        "204": { description: Reset }

  /users/{id}/two-step:
    parameters: [{ $ref: "#/components/parameters/PathID" }]
    delete:
      operationId: resetUserTwoStep
      tags: [admin]
      summary: Reset a user's two-step verification
      description: >-
        For somebody who has lost their authenticator and their recovery codes. Removes the
        key and the codes and ends the account's sessions; audited as `user.two_step_reset`.
      x-zoomies-role: admin
      responses:
        "204": { description: Reset }
        "404": { $ref: "#/components/responses/NotFound" }

  /tokens:
    get:
      operationId: listTokens
      tags: [admin]
      summary: List API tokens
      description: >-
        Metadata only. The token value exists in plaintext exactly once, at creation.
        Your own tokens; everybody's with `tokens:read`, which is the administrator role.
      x-zoomies-role: viewer
      responses:
        "200":
          description: OK
          content:
            application/json:
              schema:
                type: object
                properties:
                  items: { type: array, items: { $ref: "#/components/schemas/APIToken" } }
    post:
      operationId: createToken
      tags: [admin]
      summary: Create an API token
      description: |
        A token carries no more than the caller that made it: the role may not
        exceed the caller's, and a caller narrowed by scopes may only mint a
        token narrowed at least as far. The token is attributed to the account
        behind the caller -- the signed-in user, or the owner of the token in
        use -- so disabling or deleting that account ends it too. A token with
        no owner cannot mint tokens; anything wider than the caller is a 422.
        Anybody signed in may mint their own, never above their own role.
        Audited as `token.create`.
      x-zoomies-role: viewer
      requestBody:
        required: true
        content:
          application/json:
            schema:
              type: object
              required: [name, role]
              properties:
                name: { type: string, examples: ["prometheus"] }
                role: { $ref: "#/components/schemas/Role" }
                scopes:
                  type: array
                  items: { type: string, examples: ["pools:read", "runners:write"] }
                  description: Optional narrowing within the role. Empty means whatever the role allows.
                expires_in: { type: string, examples: ["2160h"], description: Omit for a token that never expires, which is worth avoiding. }
      responses:
        "201":
          description: Created
          content:
            application/json:
              schema:
                allOf:
                  - $ref: "#/components/schemas/APIToken"
                  - type: object
                    properties:
                      token: { type: string, description: Shown once. }

  /tokens/purge:
    post:
      operationId: purgeTokens
      tags: [admin]
      summary: Delete every revoked or expired API token
      description: |
        Removes spent tokens for good: the caller's own by default, one
        account's with `user_id`, or every one the caller can see with `all`.
        A token that still works is never touched, so this is safe to run
        without reading the list first. Each deletion is audited as
        `token.delete`, naming the token's prefix and never its value.
        Giving both `user_id` and `all` is ambiguous and answered with a 422.
        Below administrator only your own may be purged; `user_id` naming
        somebody else, or `all`, is a 403.
      x-zoomies-role: viewer
      requestBody:
        required: false
        content:
          application/json:
            schema:
              type: object
              properties:
                user_id: { type: string, description: Purge this account's spent tokens rather than the caller's. }
                all: { type: boolean, description: Purge every spent token the caller can see. }
      responses:
        "200":
          description: The tokens that were deleted
          content:
            application/json:
              schema:
                type: object
                required: [deleted]
                properties:
                  deleted: { type: array, items: { $ref: "#/components/schemas/APIToken" } }
        "422": { $ref: "#/components/responses/Unprocessable" }

  /tokens/{id}:
    parameters: [{ $ref: "#/components/parameters/PathID" }]
    delete:
      operationId: revokeToken
      tags: [admin]
      summary: Revoke an API token, or delete a spent one
      description: |
        Without `purge`, revokes: the token stops working at once and its row
        stays, marked `revoked`. With `purge=true`, removes a token that is
        already revoked or expired; one that still works is a 409, because
        deleting is tidying up after a revocation and never a quieter way to
        do one. Both are audited (`token.revoke`, `token.delete`) by prefix.
        Below administrator only your own; anybody else's is a 404, as if it
        were not there.
      x-zoomies-role: viewer
      parameters:
        - name: purge
          in: query
          required: false
          schema: { type: boolean }
          description: Delete a revoked or expired token instead of revoking it.
      responses:
        "204": { description: Revoked, or deleted }
        "404": { $ref: "#/components/responses/NotFound" }
        "409": { $ref: "#/components/responses/Conflict" }

  /mcp-clients:
    get:
      operationId: listMCPClients
      tags: [admin]
      summary: List MCP clients
      description: >-
        Every OAuth client that may ask for an MCP connection: those an administrator created, those
        that registered themselves, and those named by a client ID metadata document. Secrets are
        never returned after creation.
      x-zoomies-role: admin
      responses:
        "200":
          description: OK
          content:
            application/json:
              schema:
                type: object
                properties:
                  items: { type: array, items: { $ref: "#/components/schemas/MCPClient" } }
    post:
      operationId: createMCPClient
      tags: [admin]
      summary: Create an MCP client
      description: >-
        A client ID -- and, when `confidential`, a secret shown once -- to type into an MCP client's
        OAuth settings, such as Claude's custom connector form. Redirect URIs default to Claude's,
        `https://claude.ai/api/mcp/auth_callback`; each must be https or http to loopback. A
        confidential client proves its secret at the token endpoint and still uses PKCE.
      x-zoomies-role: admin
      requestBody:
        required: true
        content:
          application/json:
            schema:
              type: object
              required: [name]
              properties:
                name: { type: string, examples: ["Claude"] }
                redirect_uris:
                  type: array
                  items: { type: string, examples: ["https://claude.ai/api/mcp/auth_callback"] }
                confidential: { type: boolean, default: false }
      responses:
        "201":
          description: Created
          content:
            application/json:
              schema: { $ref: "#/components/schemas/MCPClient" }
        "422": { $ref: "#/components/responses/Unprocessable" }

  /mcp-clients/{id}/secret:
    parameters: [{ $ref: "#/components/parameters/PathID" }]
    post:
      operationId: rotateMCPClientSecret
      tags: [admin]
      summary: Rotate a confidential MCP client's secret
      description: The old secret stops working at once; the new one is in this response and nowhere else.
      x-zoomies-role: admin
      responses:
        "200":
          description: Rotated
          content:
            application/json:
              schema: { $ref: "#/components/schemas/MCPClient" }
        "404": { $ref: "#/components/responses/NotFound" }
        "422": { $ref: "#/components/responses/Unprocessable" }

  /mcp-clients/{id}:
    parameters: [{ $ref: "#/components/parameters/PathID" }]
    delete:
      operationId: revokeMCPClient
      tags: [admin]
      summary: Revoke an MCP client
      description: The client can no longer ask, and every connection it holds ends. Audited as `mcp_client.revoke`.
      x-zoomies-role: admin
      responses:
        "204": { description: Revoked }
        "404": { $ref: "#/components/responses/NotFound" }
        "409": { $ref: "#/components/responses/Conflict" }

  /mcp-connections:
    get:
      operationId: listMCPConnections
      tags: [admin]
      summary: Everybody's MCP connections
      x-zoomies-role: admin
      responses:
        "200":
          description: OK
          content:
            application/json:
              schema:
                type: object
                properties:
                  items: { type: array, items: { $ref: "#/components/schemas/MCPConnection" } }

  /mcp-connections/{id}:
    parameters: [{ $ref: "#/components/parameters/PathID" }]
    delete:
      operationId: revokeMCPConnection
      tags: [admin]
      summary: End somebody's MCP connection
      x-zoomies-role: admin
      responses:
        "204": { description: Revoked }
        "404": { $ref: "#/components/responses/NotFound" }
        "409": { $ref: "#/components/responses/Conflict" }

  /recovery:
    get:
      operationId: getRecovery
      tags: [recovery]
      summary: Whether this fleet is held for recovery
      description: >-
        A restored database is marked for recovery, and a controller that reads that mark
        decides as normal and applies none of it: no runner is created, drained or
        removed, nothing is reaped from GitHub, and the fallback poller does not sweep.
        The plan is still computed and published, so an operator can see exactly what
        would happen the moment the fence is lifted -- and can tell "nothing to do" from
        "not allowed to". A fenced instance answers `/readyz` with 503; liveness is
        unaffected, so its container runtime does not restart it.
      x-zoomies-role: viewer
      responses:
        "200":
          description: OK
          content:
            application/json:
              schema: { $ref: "#/components/schemas/Recovery" }

  /recovery/unfence:
    post:
      operationId: unfence
      tags: [recovery]
      summary: Lift the recovery fence
      description: >-
        A person saying that a recovered fleet has been checked and may act on the world
        again. It is audited under its own action, because the audit log is where somebody
        later asks who decided that and when. Lifting an unfenced instance succeeds and
        changes nothing: two operators recovering one fleet will both press it.
      x-zoomies-role: admin
      responses:
        "200":
          description: OK
          content:
            application/json:
              schema: { $ref: "#/components/schemas/Recovery" }

  # ==========================================================================
  # Backups
  # ==========================================================================
  # Every route here is admin, and a backup is the whole database: every
  # account's password hash and every sealed credential. The upload is bounded
  # by its own handler rather than the API's ordinary body limit.
  /backups:
    get:
      operationId: listBackups
      tags: [backups]
      summary: Every backup, and the state of the schedule
      description: >-
        The backups in `backup.directory` and the copies the store took before
        migrating, newest first, each with what its manifest says and whether a
        restore of it would be refused; the schedule and its last outcome; the
        restore waiting for a restart, if any; and what became of the last one.
      x-zoomies-role: admin
      responses:
        "200":
          description: OK
          content:
            application/json:
              schema: { $ref: "#/components/schemas/Backups" }
    post:
      operationId: takeBackup
      tags: [backups]
      summary: Take a backup now
      description: >-
        A consistent copy of the live database, taken with `VACUUM INTO`, checked
        with `PRAGMA integrity_check`, and written with its manifest into
        `backup.directory`. Retention (`backup.keep`) runs afterwards. Refused with
        409 while another backup is being taken.
      x-zoomies-role: admin
      responses:
        "201":
          description: Taken
          content:
            application/json:
              schema: { $ref: "#/components/schemas/Backup" }
        "409": { $ref: "#/components/responses/Conflict" }

  /backups/upload:
    post:
      operationId: uploadBackup
      tags: [backups]
      summary: Bring a backup here
      description: >-
        A `multipart/form-data` form with the archive in `file` -- a `.tar.gz` a
        download produced, or the `.tar.gz.enc` an encrypted download produced with
        its `passphrase` in a second part. The archive is unpacked into a staging
        directory, verified as a restore would verify it, and then listed under the
        name its manifest gives it, with its source recorded as uploaded. An upload
        is never counted or removed by retention.
      x-zoomies-role: admin
      requestBody:
        required: true
        content:
          multipart/form-data:
            schema:
              type: object
              required: [file]
              properties:
                file: { type: string, format: binary }
                passphrase: { type: string, format: password }
      responses:
        "201":
          description: Unpacked and verified
          content:
            application/json:
              schema: { $ref: "#/components/schemas/Backup" }
        "413": { description: The upload is over the limit. }
        "422": { $ref: "#/components/responses/Unprocessable" }

  /backups/restore:
    delete:
      operationId: cancelRestore
      tags: [backups]
      summary: Cancel the staged restore
      description: Forgets the restore waiting for a restart. Cancelling when none is staged succeeds.
      x-zoomies-role: admin
      responses:
        "204": { description: Cancelled }

  /backups/restore/apply:
    post:
      operationId: applyRestore
      tags: [backups]
      summary: Restart the controller to apply the staged restore
      description: >-
        Stops Zoomies so that its service manager starts the next one,
        which applies the staged restore before it opens the database. The response
        is written before the process stops. Refused with 409 when nothing is
        staged, because a restart with nothing to apply is an outage. Whether the
        process comes back is up to whatever started it; a systemd unit and a
        container with a restart policy both bring it back, and a controller run
        by hand needs starting by hand.
      x-zoomies-role: admin
      responses:
        "202":
          description: Stopping
          content:
            application/json:
              schema: { $ref: "#/components/schemas/Restarting" }
        "409": { $ref: "#/components/responses/Conflict" }

  /backups/restore/outcome:
    delete:
      operationId: dismissRestoreOutcome
      tags: [backups]
      summary: Dismiss what became of the last restore
      x-zoomies-role: admin
      responses:
        "204": { description: Dismissed }

  /backups/offsite:
    post:
      operationId: shipBackups
      tags: [backups]
      summary: Copy the backups to every remote now
      description: >-
        Makes each enabled destination under `backup.remotes` hold what the backup
        directory holds: the remote is listed, whatever it is missing is sent oldest
        first, and its own retention is applied afterwards. It is the pass the
        controller runs by itself after every backup and once an hour; this is the
        way to run it now, which is what an operator who has just fixed a credential
        wants. A destination that refuses is reported in `error` while the others
        still go. Refused with 409 while a pass is already running.
      x-zoomies-role: admin
      responses:
        "200":
          description: The pass ran
          content:
            application/json:
              schema: { $ref: "#/components/schemas/BackupShipment" }
        "409": { $ref: "#/components/responses/Conflict" }

  /backups/prune:
    post:
      operationId: pruneBackups
      tags: [backups]
      summary: Apply retention now
      description: >-
        Deletes the copies beyond `backup.keep` from the backup directory, and the
        ones beyond each destination's own `keep` from its bucket. Retention
        otherwise runs as part of taking a backup, which leaves a fleet that has
        just lowered `backup.keep` holding the old number until the next one —
        and on a fleet with `backup.interval` off, holding it forever. A copy that
        was uploaded here or fetched back out of a bucket is never counted and
        never removed. The answer lists what went, per destination, and a bucket
        that refused is reported against its own name while the others are still
        pruned. Refused with 409 while a backup or an offsite pass is running.
      x-zoomies-role: admin
      responses:
        "200":
          description: Retention was applied
          content:
            application/json:
              schema: { $ref: "#/components/schemas/BackupPruning" }
        "409": { $ref: "#/components/responses/Conflict" }

  /backups/remotes:
    post:
      operationId: createBackupRemote
      tags: [backups]
      summary: Add a backup remote
      description: >-
        Stores an S3-compatible destination this fleet copies every backup to.
        The secret key and the passphrase are sealed with the instance encryption
        key before anything else happens to them, and no response ever carries
        them back — the page is told whether each is set, which is the only thing
        it can act on. A destination `backup.remotes` in `zoomies.yaml` already
        names is refused: the file has the last word, and two rows that disagree
        would be worse than one that cannot be added.
      x-zoomies-role: admin
      requestBody:
        required: true
        content:
          application/json:
            schema: { $ref: "#/components/schemas/BackupRemoteInput" }
      responses:
        "201":
          description: Added
          content:
            application/json:
              schema: { $ref: "#/components/schemas/BackupRemote" }
        "422": { $ref: "#/components/responses/Unprocessable" }

  /backups/remotes/check:
    post:
      operationId: checkDraftBackupRemote
      tags: [backups]
      summary: Test a backup remote before it is saved
      description: >-
        Lists one key under the destination described in the body, so that a
        secret key is proved before it is stored rather than after. A body with
        no `secret_access_key` falls back to the one stored under that name,
        which is how a saved destination is re-tested after its bucket or prefix
        is changed. A destination that refuses is a `200` with `ok: false` and
        the service's own words.
      x-zoomies-role: admin
      requestBody:
        required: true
        content:
          application/json:
            schema: { $ref: "#/components/schemas/BackupRemoteInput" }
      responses:
        "200":
          description: The check ran
          content:
            application/json:
              schema: { $ref: "#/components/schemas/RemoteBackupCheck" }
        "422": { $ref: "#/components/responses/Unprocessable" }

  /backups/remotes/{name}:
    parameters:
      - name: name
        in: path
        required: true
        schema: { type: string }
        description: The remote's name, e.g. `offsite`.
    patch:
      operationId: updateBackupRemote
      tags: [backups]
      summary: Change a stored backup remote
      description: >-
        Only the fields the body carries are changed. The two secrets follow the
        credential convention: absent leaves what is stored, a value replaces it,
        and an explicit empty string clears it — which is how a passphrase is
        removed from a destination that should send the plain archive. A
        destination described in `zoomies.yaml` answers `409`: it is changed in
        the file.
      x-zoomies-role: admin
      requestBody:
        required: true
        content:
          application/json:
            schema: { $ref: "#/components/schemas/BackupRemoteInput" }
      responses:
        "200":
          description: Changed
          content:
            application/json:
              schema: { $ref: "#/components/schemas/BackupRemote" }
        "404": { $ref: "#/components/responses/NotFound" }
        "409": { $ref: "#/components/responses/Conflict" }
        "422": { $ref: "#/components/responses/Unprocessable" }
    delete:
      operationId: deleteBackupRemote
      tags: [backups]
      summary: Remove a stored backup remote
      description: >-
        Forgets the destination. What its bucket holds is left alone: forgetting
        where the copies are is not the same as deciding they should not exist,
        and each one can be deleted from the listing first.
      x-zoomies-role: admin
      responses:
        "204": { description: Removed }
        "404": { $ref: "#/components/responses/NotFound" }
        "409": { $ref: "#/components/responses/Conflict" }

  /backups/remotes/{name}/copies:
    parameters:
      - name: name
        in: path
        required: true
        schema: { type: string }
        description: The remote's name, as `backup.remotes` gives it, e.g. `offsite`.
    get:
      operationId: listRemoteBackups
      tags: [backups]
      summary: What one backup remote holds
      description: >-
        The archives in the remote's bucket and prefix, newest first, read live
        rather than from anything the controller remembers -- the question this
        answers is whether the offsite copy is actually there, and a remembered
        yes is worth nothing. Anything under the prefix that this fleet did not
        write is ignored: a bucket may be shared.
      x-zoomies-role: admin
      responses:
        "200":
          description: OK
          content:
            application/json:
              schema: { $ref: "#/components/schemas/RemoteBackupCopies" }
        "404": { $ref: "#/components/responses/NotFound" }
        "422": { $ref: "#/components/responses/Unprocessable" }

  /backups/remotes/{name}/check:
    parameters:
      - name: name
        in: path
        required: true
        schema: { type: string }
    post:
      operationId: checkBackupRemote
      tags: [backups]
      summary: Test that a backup remote can be reached
      description: >-
        Lists one key under the remote's prefix, which is the whole of what has to
        work for a backup to reach it: the endpoint resolves, TLS agrees, the
        signature is accepted, the bucket exists and the policy allows reading it.
        A remote that refuses is a 200 with `ok: false` and the service's own
        refusal in `error` -- the check ran, and what it found is the result.
      x-zoomies-role: admin
      responses:
        "200":
          description: The check ran
          content:
            application/json:
              schema: { $ref: "#/components/schemas/RemoteBackupCheck" }
        "404": { $ref: "#/components/responses/NotFound" }

  /backups/remotes/{name}/copies/{id}:
    parameters:
      - name: name
        in: path
        required: true
        schema: { type: string }
      - name: id
        in: path
        required: true
        schema: { type: string }
        description: The backup's id, e.g. `zoomies-20260916-120000`.
    delete:
      operationId: deleteRemoteBackup
      tags: [backups]
      summary: Remove one copy from a backup remote
      description: >-
        Deletes the archive from the bucket. Audited like deleting a local backup,
        and for a stronger reason: the offsite copy is the one that exists because
        the local ones might not.
      x-zoomies-role: admin
      responses:
        "204": { description: Removed }
        "404": { $ref: "#/components/responses/NotFound" }
        "422": { $ref: "#/components/responses/Unprocessable" }

  /backups/remotes/{name}/copies/{id}/fetch:
    parameters:
      - name: name
        in: path
        required: true
        schema: { type: string }
      - name: id
        in: path
        required: true
        schema: { type: string }
    post:
      operationId: fetchRemoteBackup
      tags: [backups]
      summary: Bring one copy back from a backup remote
      description: >-
        Downloads the archive, decrypts it with the remote's passphrase -- or the
        one in the body, for an archive sealed with a passphrase this configuration
        no longer carries -- and unpacks it into the backup directory, verified
        exactly as an upload is. It is then an ordinary backup, restorable through
        the same staging as any other. There is deliberately no "restore from the
        bucket": a restore swaps the database this fleet runs on, and the copy it
        swaps in should be one somebody has seen land and verified first.
      x-zoomies-role: admin
      requestBody:
        required: false
        content:
          application/json:
            schema:
              type: object
              properties:
                passphrase: { type: string, format: password }
      responses:
        "201":
          description: Fetched and verified
          content:
            application/json:
              schema: { $ref: "#/components/schemas/Backup" }
        "404": { $ref: "#/components/responses/NotFound" }
        "422": { $ref: "#/components/responses/Unprocessable" }

  /backups/{id}:
    parameters:
      - name: id
        in: path
        required: true
        schema: { type: string }
        description: The backup's directory name, e.g. `zoomies-20260916-120000`.
    get:
      operationId: getBackup
      tags: [backups]
      summary: One backup
      x-zoomies-role: admin
      responses:
        "200":
          description: OK
          content:
            application/json:
              schema: { $ref: "#/components/schemas/Backup" }
        "404": { $ref: "#/components/responses/NotFound" }
    delete:
      operationId: deleteBackup
      tags: [backups]
      summary: Delete a backup
      description: Refused with 409 while the backup is staged to be restored.
      x-zoomies-role: admin
      responses:
        "204": { description: Deleted }
        "404": { $ref: "#/components/responses/NotFound" }
        "409": { $ref: "#/components/responses/Conflict" }

  /backups/{id}/verify:
    parameters:
      - name: id
        in: path
        required: true
        schema: { type: string }
    post:
      operationId: verifyBackup
      tags: [backups]
      summary: Re-read a backup and check it
      description: >-
        Compares the database's digest with the one the manifest recorded, opens it,
        runs `PRAGMA integrity_check`, and says whether this build could restore it.
        A POST because it reads the whole file.
      x-zoomies-role: admin
      responses:
        "200":
          description: OK
          content:
            application/json:
              schema: { $ref: "#/components/schemas/BackupVerification" }
        "404": { $ref: "#/components/responses/NotFound" }

  /backups/{id}/download:
    parameters:
      - name: id
        in: path
        required: true
        schema: { type: string }
    get:
      operationId: downloadBackup
      tags: [backups]
      summary: Download a backup as a gzipped tar
      description: >-
        The backup's directory -- manifest, database and, only when it was taken
        with it, the encryption key -- as `<id>.tar.gz`. Audited: it is the whole
        database leaving the machine.
      x-zoomies-role: admin
      responses:
        "200": { description: The archive, content: { application/octet-stream: { schema: { type: string, format: binary } } } }
        "404": { $ref: "#/components/responses/NotFound" }
    post:
      operationId: downloadBackupEncrypted
      tags: [backups]
      summary: Download a backup encrypted with a passphrase
      description: >-
        The same archive, encrypted as `<id>.tar.gz.enc`: the passphrase is run
        through argon2id and the archive through AES-256-GCM in chunks, so a file
        cut short or altered does not open as a shorter backup. The upload route
        takes the same passphrase to bring it back.
      x-zoomies-role: admin
      requestBody:
        required: true
        content:
          application/json:
            schema:
              type: object
              required: [passphrase]
              properties:
                passphrase: { type: string, format: password, minLength: 8 }
      responses:
        "200": { description: The encrypted archive, content: { application/octet-stream: { schema: { type: string, format: binary } } } }
        "404": { $ref: "#/components/responses/NotFound" }
        "422": { $ref: "#/components/responses/Unprocessable" }

  /backups/{id}/restore:
    parameters:
      - name: id
        in: path
        required: true
        schema: { type: string }
    post:
      operationId: stageRestore
      tags: [backups]
      summary: Stage a restore of this backup for the next restart
      description: >-
        Nothing is restored by this call. The controller cannot swap the database it
        is running on, so every check a restore makes is made now -- the copy is
        sound, this build can read it, and this host's encryption key is the one that
        sealed it -- and the restore is written down beside the database for the next
        controller to apply before it opens anything. `POST /backups/restore/apply`
        is the restart that does it. The restored fleet comes back fenced, with
        every session ended and every unredeemed join token removed; the two options
        go further, as `zoomies restore`'s flags do.
      x-zoomies-role: admin
      requestBody:
        content:
          application/json:
            schema:
              type: object
              properties:
                revoke_api_tokens: { type: boolean, description: Revoke every API token as well. }
                reset_agent_tokens: { type: boolean, description: Forget every host's agent credential, so each agent joins again. }
      responses:
        "202":
          description: Staged
          content:
            application/json:
              schema: { $ref: "#/components/schemas/StagedRestore" }
        "404": { $ref: "#/components/responses/NotFound" }
        "409": { $ref: "#/components/responses/Conflict" }
        "422": { $ref: "#/components/responses/Unprocessable" }

  /diagnostics/bundle:
    get:
      operationId: getSupportBundle
      tags: [diagnostics]
      summary: A support bundle for this instance
      description: >-
        Everything a bug report needs about this instance in one JSON document: the
        build and the process, the effective configuration and its findings, the current
        problems, the fleet's installations, pools, hosts and runners, the work in flight
        with the controller's own explanation for each of it, and the recent scheduler
        decisions. It is assembled from the same renderings the other routes serve, so a
        section that is secret-free on its own route is secret-free here.


        It never carries workflow log bodies. There is no redaction pass for them and
        there cannot be a reliable one, so the bundle carries runner ids and the download
        route instead and an operator attaches logs deliberately.


        Assembly is section by section: a section that fails costs its own contents and
        lands in `errors` rather than failing the whole document, because the moment a
        bundle is taken is the moment a query is most likely to fail. Sections are capped
        by row count and the whole document by bytes; anything shortened says so in
        `truncated`.
      x-zoomies-role: admin
      responses:
        "200":
          description: OK
          content:
            application/json:
              schema: { $ref: "#/components/schemas/SupportBundle" }

  /settings:
    get:
      operationId: getSettings
      tags: [admin]
      summary: The effective configuration, key by key
      description: >-
        Every key with its value, its kind, the layer it came from and whether it
        can be changed here, plus the same configuration as a nested object. No
        secret's value is ever sent. The validator's findings are included so the
        UI can show each one next to the setting it concerns.
      x-zoomies-role: admin
      responses:
        "200":
          description: OK
          content:
            application/json:
              schema: { $ref: "#/components/schemas/Settings" }
    patch:
      operationId: updateSettings
      tags: [admin]
      summary: Change this fleet's settings
      description: |
        Keys may be sent nested (`{"retention":{"jobs":"720h"}}`) or dotted
        (`{"retention.jobs":"720h"}`). A `null` value clears the stored setting,
        so the key goes back to whatever the configuration file or the built-in
        default says.

        Every key is checked before any is written, and the whole request is
        refused if one fails — including when the result would be a controller
        that will not start, which the validator is asked about before anything
        is stored.

        An accepted change is always kept. One the running process can apply
        does so at once; one it cannot — rebinding the listener, rebuilding the
        backends — is stored and named in `pending_restart`.

        Refused: a key that is read before the database opens, one that belongs
        to a standalone agent's own host, and one an environment variable is
        pinning. Each refusal says which it is and what to do instead.
      x-zoomies-role: admin
      requestBody:
        required: true
        content:
          application/json:
            schema:
              type: object
              additionalProperties: true
      responses:
        "200":
          description: OK
          content:
            application/json:
              schema: { $ref: "#/components/schemas/Settings" }
        "422": { $ref: "#/components/responses/Unprocessable" }

  /settings/export:
    get:
      operationId: exportSettings
      tags: [admin]
      summary: Every setting somebody has set, as a file
      description: >-
        Stored here, set in the configuration file, or pinned by the environment;
        never a default, because those are computed on the host that reads them,
        and never a secret's value. `format=json` wraps the tree with when it was
        taken, where from, and which secrets were configured but not exported;
        `format=yaml` is the tree alone, in the shape zoomies.yaml takes, so the
        download can be started from. Audited.
      x-zoomies-role: admin
      parameters:
        - { name: format, in: query, schema: { type: string, enum: [json, yaml], default: json } }
      responses:
        "200":
          description: The export
          content:
            application/json:
              schema: { $ref: "#/components/schemas/SettingsExport" }
            application/yaml:
              schema: { type: string }

  /settings/import:
    post:
      operationId: importSettings
      tags: [admin]
      summary: Read an export or a zoomies.yaml back, previewing first
      description: >-
        Every key in the document is planned through the checks a PATCH makes and
        reported as `change`, `unchanged`, `unset` or `refused` with the reason. A
        dry run reports and writes nothing. A real run refuses the whole document
        with 422 while any key is refused, so an import is one change or none;
        `skip` names the keys to leave out. Applying returns the settings page too.
      x-zoomies-role: admin
      requestBody:
        required: true
        content:
          application/json:
            schema: { $ref: "#/components/schemas/SettingsImportRequest" }
      responses:
        "200":
          description: The preview, or the result
          content:
            application/json:
              schema: { $ref: "#/components/schemas/SettingsImport" }
        "422": { $ref: "#/components/responses/Unprocessable" }

  # ==========================================================================
  # Agent routes
  # ==========================================================================
  # The half of the API agents talk to. These carry an agent token, never a
  # user session, and an agent can reach nothing else. They are here so that
  # this document is the whole surface it says it is, and marked x-internal
  # because no general client should call them: the wire types are owned by
  # internal/agent/protocol.go, and a client generator should skip them.
  /agent/join:
    post:
      operationId: agentJoin
      tags: [agent]
      x-internal: true
      summary: Redeem a join token and enrol a host
      description: >-
        The one anonymous agent route, because it is the call that mints the credential every
        other one carries. The join token is single-use and short-lived; the agent token in
        the response is shown exactly once, and the controller keeps only its hash.
      security: []
      requestBody:
        required: true
        content:
          application/json:
            schema: { $ref: "#/components/schemas/AgentJoinRequest" }
      responses:
        "200":
          description: Enrolled
          content:
            application/json:
              schema: { $ref: "#/components/schemas/AgentJoinResponse" }
        "409": { $ref: "#/components/responses/LimitReached" }
        "422": { $ref: "#/components/responses/Unprocessable" }

  /agent/heartbeat:
    post:
      operationId: agentHeartbeat
      tags: [agent]
      x-internal: true
      summary: Report that the host is alive, and what its runners are doing
      security: [{ agentAuth: [] }]
      requestBody:
        required: true
        content:
          application/json:
            schema: { $ref: "#/components/schemas/AgentHeartbeatRequest" }
      responses:
        "200":
          description: Recorded
          content:
            application/json:
              schema: { $ref: "#/components/schemas/AgentHeartbeatResponse" }
        "401": { $ref: "#/components/responses/Unauthorized" }
        "404": { description: The host was deleted. No amount of retrying brings the row back; the agent re-joins. }
        "413": { description: The report carried more runners than any host runs (agent.MaxRunnersPerReport). The agent is misbehaving. }
        "429": { $ref: "#/components/responses/RateLimited" }

  /agent/tasks:
    get:
      operationId: agentPollTasks
      tags: [agent]
      x-internal: true
      summary: Long-poll for work
      description: Blocks until the host has work or the wait elapses, so a task reaches an agent the instant it is queued while an idle agent makes two or three requests a minute. A host holds one poll at a time; a second, while the first is held, is answered at once with an empty batch.
      security: [{ agentAuth: [] }]
      parameters:
        - name: wait
          in: query
          description: Seconds to wait for work before answering with an empty batch.
          schema: { type: integer, minimum: 1, default: 25 }
      responses:
        "200":
          description: The tasks queued for this host, possibly none.
          content:
            application/json:
              schema: { $ref: "#/components/schemas/AgentTaskBatch" }
        "401": { $ref: "#/components/responses/Unauthorized" }

  /agent/results:
    post:
      operationId: agentReportResult
      tags: [agent]
      x-internal: true
      summary: Report the outcome of one task
      security: [{ agentAuth: [] }]
      requestBody:
        required: true
        content:
          application/json:
            schema: { $ref: "#/components/schemas/AgentTaskResult" }
      responses:
        "204": { description: Applied }
        "401": { $ref: "#/components/responses/Unauthorized" }
        "404": { $ref: "#/components/responses/NotFound" }
        "429": { $ref: "#/components/responses/RateLimited" }

  /agent/report:
    post:
      operationId: agentReportRunners
      tags: [agent]
      x-internal: true
      summary: Report what the host's runners are doing, outside a heartbeat
      description: The body is a bare array of runner reports, because that is what the agent sends and the two halves of the protocol must agree.
      security: [{ agentAuth: [] }]
      requestBody:
        required: true
        content:
          application/json:
            schema:
              type: array
              items: { $ref: "#/components/schemas/RunnerReport" }
      responses:
        "204": { description: Applied }
        "401": { $ref: "#/components/responses/Unauthorized" }
        "413": { description: The report carried more runners than any host runs (agent.MaxRunnersPerReport). The agent is misbehaving. }
        "429": { $ref: "#/components/responses/RateLimited" }

  /agent/logs/{stream_id}:
    post:
      operationId: agentRelayLogs
      tags: [agent]
      x-internal: true
      summary: Relay a runner's output to a viewer
      description: >-
        The inverted half of log streaming. The controller never dials an agent, so a viewer's
        request makes it queue a stream_logs task, and the agent answers by opening this
        chunked POST, which stays open for as long as the runner produces output. Exempt from
        the body-size limit for that reason; instead each stream has a byte budget, and output
        over it is read and dropped rather than waited on.
      security: [{ agentAuth: [] }]
      parameters:
        - { name: stream_id, in: path, required: true, schema: { type: string }, description: The stream named by the stream_logs task. }
      requestBody:
        required: true
        content:
          application/octet-stream:
            schema: { type: string, format: binary }
      responses:
        "204": { description: The stream ended. }
        "401": { $ref: "#/components/responses/Unauthorized" }
        "404": { description: Nobody is watching this stream any more; the agent stops sending. }
components:
  securitySchemes:
    cookieAuth:
      type: apiKey
      in: cookie
      name: zoomies_session
      description: Set by `POST /auth/login`. HttpOnly, SameSite=Lax, and Secure when the external URL is https.
    bearerAuth:
      type: http
      scheme: bearer
      bearerFormat: zoo_<prefix>_<secret>
      description: An API token. Not subject to the same-origin check, because it is not vulnerable to CSRF.
    agentAuth:
      type: http
      scheme: bearer
      bearerFormat: zooagent_<secret>
      description: >-
        An agent's own token, minted by `POST /agent/join`. Accepted on `/agent/*` only: a
        user credential is refused there, and an agent token is refused everywhere else.

  parameters:
    PathID:
      name: id
      in: path
      required: true
      schema: { type: string }
      description: The resource ID, e.g. `pool_k3f9qz2m`.
    Limit:
      name: limit
      in: query
      schema: { type: integer, default: 50, minimum: 1, maximum: 500 }
    Offset:
      name: offset
      in: query
      schema: { type: integer, default: 0, minimum: 0 }
    Sort:
      name: sort
      in: query
      description: A column name. An unknown value falls back to the default rather than erroring, so a stale bookmark does not break the page.
      schema: { type: string }
    Order:
      name: order
      in: query
      schema: { type: string, enum: [asc, desc], default: desc }

  responses:
    Unauthorized:
      description: Not signed in, or the credential was rejected.
      content:
        application/json:
          schema: { $ref: "#/components/schemas/ErrorEnvelope" }
    Forbidden:
      description: Signed in, but the role is not sufficient. The message says which role is needed.
      content:
        application/json:
          schema: { $ref: "#/components/schemas/ErrorEnvelope" }
    NotFound:
      description: No such thing.
      content:
        application/json:
          schema: { $ref: "#/components/schemas/ErrorEnvelope" }
    Conflict:
      description: The request conflicts with the current state.
      content:
        application/json:
          schema: { $ref: "#/components/schemas/ErrorEnvelope" }
    LimitReached:
      description: >-
        One of the `limits.*` ceilings has been reached. The code is `limit_reached`, and the message and
        `field` name the setting. Nothing resent will succeed until a resource is removed or the setting is raised.
      content:
        application/json:
          schema: { $ref: "#/components/schemas/ErrorEnvelope" }
    Unprocessable:
      description: The request was understood but is not valid. `errors` names the fields.
      content:
        application/json:
          schema:
            allOf:
              - $ref: "#/components/schemas/ErrorEnvelope"
              - type: object
                properties:
                  errors: { type: array, items: { $ref: "#/components/schemas/FieldError" } }
    RateLimited:
      description: Too many attempts. Retry-After says how long to wait.
      headers:
        Retry-After:
          description: Seconds until the address is allowed another attempt.
          schema: { type: integer, minimum: 1 }
      content:
        application/json:
          schema: { $ref: "#/components/schemas/ErrorEnvelope" }

  schemas:
    AIContextMaintenanceRequest:
      type: object
      required: [mode, revision]
      properties:
        mode: { type: string, enum: [reinstall, amend, remove] }
        revision: { type: integer, format: int64 }
        plan_hash: { type: string, pattern: '^[a-f0-9]{64}$' }
        config: { $ref: "#/components/schemas/AIContextRepository/properties/config" }
    AIContextSetupPreview:
      type: object
      required: [revision, base_commit, branch, plan_hash, files]
      properties:
        mode: { type: string }
        config: { $ref: "#/components/schemas/AIContextRepository/properties/config" }
        previous_hash: { type: string }
        revision: { type: integer, format: int64 }
        base_commit: { type: string }
        branch: { type: string }
        plan_hash: { type: string }
        files:
          type: array
          items:
            type: object
            required: [path, mode, previous_sha, content]
            properties:
              path: { type: string }
              mode: { type: string, enum: ["100644", "100755"] }
              previous_sha: { type: string }
              content: { type: string }
              delete: { type: boolean }
        setup:
          type: object
          required: [repository_id, revision, plan_hash, state, pr_number, pr_url]
          properties:
            repository_id: { type: string }
            revision: { type: integer, format: int64 }
            plan_hash: { type: string }
            state: { type: string, enum: [pending, awaiting_merge] }
            pr_number: { type: integer }
            pr_url: { type: string }
    AIContextSourcePage:
      type: object
      required: [commit, snapshot]
      properties:
        commit: { type: string }
        snapshot: { type: string }
        total: { type: integer }
        next_offset: { type: integer }
        files:
          type: array
          items:
            type: object
            required: [path, bytes, lines]
            properties:
              path: { type: string }
              bytes: { type: integer }
              lines: { type: integer }
        excerpts:
          type: array
          items:
            type: object
            required: [path, text, offset, next_offset]
            properties:
              path: { type: string }
              text: { type: string }
