              offset: { type: integer }
              next_offset: { type: integer, nullable: true }
        matches:
          type: array
          items:
            type: object
            required: [path, line, text]
            properties:
              path: { type: string }
              line: { type: integer }
              text: { type: string }
    AIContextReaderPage:
      type: object
      required: [items, total, limit, offset]
      properties:
        items:
          type: array
          items:
            type: object
            required: [id, full_name, instructions, badge_markdown]
            properties:
              id: { type: string }
              full_name: { type: string }
              instructions: { type: string }
              badge_markdown: { type: string }
        total: { type: integer }
        limit: { type: integer }
        offset: { type: integer }
    AIContextInstallations:
      type: object
      required: [items]
      properties:
        items:
          type: array
          items:
            type: object
            required: [id, target, target_type]
            properties:
              id: { type: string }
              target: { type: string }
              target_type: { type: string, enum: [org, repo] }
    AIContextMembers:
      type: object
      required: [user_ids]
      properties:
        user_ids: { type: array, maxItems: 200, uniqueItems: true, items: { type: string } }
    AIContextConnectionSelection:
      type: object
      required: [items, total, limit, offset, selected_repository_ids]
      properties:
        items:
          type: array
          items:
            type: object
            required: [id, full_name]
            properties:
              id: { type: string }
              full_name: { type: string }
        total: { type: integer }
        limit: { type: integer }
        offset: { type: integer }
        selected_repository_ids: { type: array, maxItems: 100, items: { type: string } }
    AIContextRepository:
      type: object
      required: [id, repository, full_name, config, revision, available, created_at, updated_at]
      properties:
        id: { type: string }
        repository:
          type: object
          required: [github_host, installation_id, repository_id]
          properties:
            github_host: { type: string }
            installation_id: { type: string }
            repository_id: { type: integer, format: int64 }
        full_name: { type: string }
        instructions: { type: string }
        badge_markdown: { type: string }
        config:
          type: object
          required: [source_branch, destination, exclude, keep_snapshots]
          properties:
            source_branch: { type: string }
            destination: { type: string, enum: [repository, zoomies, both] }
            exclude: { type: array, items: { type: string } }
            keep_snapshots: { type: integer, minimum: 1, maximum: 100 }
            readme_badge: { type: boolean, deprecated: true, description: "Legacy field; the README badge is automatic." }
            setup_generation: { type: integer, format: int64 }
            disabled: { type: boolean }
            upload_url: { type: string, readOnly: true, description: "Set by the controller for Zoomies-only output: where the workflow uploads, and the audience of its OIDC token. Any value a client sends is replaced." }
        revision: { type: integer, format: int64 }
        freshness:
          type: object
          required: [state, desired_commit, published_commit, snapshot_id, checked_at]
          properties:
            state: { type: string, enum: [awaiting_merge, unavailable, stale, ready] }
            desired_commit: { type: string }
            published_commit: { type: string }
            snapshot_id: { type: string }
            checked_at: { type: string, format: date-time }
            failure: { type: string }
        setup_state: { type: string, enum: [pending, awaiting_merge] }
        setup_pr_url: { type: string }
        available: { type: boolean }
        created_at: { type: string, format: date-time }
        updated_at: { type: string, format: date-time }
    # --- primitives -------------------------------------------------------
    Role:
      type: string
      enum: [viewer, operator, admin, platform]
      description: >-
        What an identity may do. `platform` is above `admin` and belongs to
        whoever runs the process rather than the fleet; on an instance where
        one team does both, the account that installed it holds it.
    TargetType:
      type: string
      enum: [org, repo]
    BackendKind:
      type: string
      enum: [docker, podman, process]
    PullPolicy:
      type: string
      enum: [if-not-present, always, pinned-only]
      default: if-not-present
      description: pinned-only requires an image@sha256 digest and rejects mutable tags.

    DockerMode:
      type: string
      enum: [none, dind, host-socket]
      description: |
        How much Docker a job on this pool gets.
        `none` is the default and the only one that is not a warning.
        `dind` gives a private, privileged sidecar daemon.
        `host-socket` hands the job the host's daemon, and with it root on the host.
        Either of those switches a pool on the stock `ghcr.io/eyupio/zoomies-runner`
        image to `ghcr.io/eyupio/zoomies-runner-docker` under the same tag as it is
        saved, because the stock image has no client for the daemon. That covers
        every tag this build publishes: the channels, and the operating-system
        aliases. A digest, a tag from some other build, or an image of your own is
        left as given, and a pool left on one raises `pool.docker_client_missing`.
    RunnerState:
      type: string
      enum: [provisioning, registering, idle, busy, draining, removed, failed]
    JobState:
      type: string
      enum: [waiting, queued, in_progress, completed]
    Severity:
      type: string
      enum: [error, warning, info]
    Duration:
      type: string
      description: A Go duration string.
      examples: ["5m", "1h30s"]

    Page:
      type: object
      required: [total, limit, offset]
      properties:
        total: { type: integer, description: Rows matching the filter, not rows returned. }
        limit: { type: integer }
        offset: { type: integer }

    ErrorEnvelope:
      type: object
      required: [error]
      properties:
        error:
          type: object
          required: [code, message]
          properties:
            code:
              type: string
              enum: [bad_request, unauthorized, forbidden, not_found, conflict, unprocessable, too_large, rate_limited, limit_reached, internal]
            message: { type: string, description: Written for a person to read, and to act on. }
            field: { type: string, description: "The form field at fault, or on a `limit_reached` refusal the `limits.*` setting that refused." }
            detail: { type: string }

    FieldError:
      type: object
      required: [field, message]
      properties:
        field: { type: string, examples: [labels] }
        message: { type: string, examples: ["a pool needs at least one label your workflows can ask for"] }

    HostExclusion:
      type: object
      required: [host, code, reason]
      properties:
        host: { type: string, examples: [zoomies-12vcpu-31gb-debian-12] }
        code:
          type: string
          description: Which placement rule turned this host down.
          enum: [unavailable, backend, platform, size, reduced]
        reason:
          type: string
          description: A sentence about the host with its name left out, so a caller can put the name where its own layout wants it.
          examples: ["it has 12 CPU to place on, and one runner of this pool is charged 16, twice what it asks for, because a docker-in-docker runner is charged for its sidecar too"]

    SettingSource:
      type: string
      enum: [default, file, database, environment]
      description: >-
        Which layer set a value. They stack in that order -- the built-in defaults, then
        zoomies.yaml, then this fleet's database, then `ZOOMIES_*` in the environment --
        and each wins over the one before it.

        It is the answer to the question that makes a configuration problem hard: "I
        changed it and nothing happened". A value the environment is pinning cannot be
        changed from the file or from this API, and one stored in the database is not
        changed by editing the file.

    Problem:
      type: object
      required: [code, severity, title, audience]
      properties:
        code: { type: string, examples: [bind.public_no_tls] }
        severity: { $ref: "#/components/schemas/Severity" }
        audience:
          type: string
          enum: [platform, fleet, both]
          description: >-
            Whose problem this is. `platform` is the process's own -- its lease, its
            loops, its backups, the release it could be running -- and reaches only a
            caller at the `platform` role. `fleet` is what the fleet's own pools, hosts,
            runners and jobs are doing wrong, and reaches everyone who can read the list.
            `both` is for the ones genuinely both people's: a list that could not be
            fully gathered has to say so to whoever is reading it.


            On a single-team instance the one account holds `platform` and the list is
            undivided, which is what it was before the role existed.
          examples: [platform]
        setting: { type: string, examples: [server.bind] }
        source:
          $ref: "#/components/schemas/SettingSource"
        undo:
          type: string
          description: >-
            The command that takes this value back out of the layer that set it, when there
            is one. Empty for a value in the configuration file, which is edited where it
            is, and for a default.

            It exists for the case the settings page cannot help with: a value saved here
            that stops the controller starting is unreachable from a page the controller
            serves, so the way back has to be something an operator can type at a stopped
            one.
          examples: ["zoomies config unset server.bind"]
        title: { type: string, description: One line - what is true. }
        detail: { type: string, description: Why it matters, and the consequence. }
        fix:
          type: string
          description: >-
            What to change, concretely. Read it with `source`: an operator told to change a
            setting will edit the configuration file, and a value stored in this fleet's
            database or pinned by a ZOOMIES_* variable is one the file cannot change.
        target_kind: { type: string }
        target_id: { type: string }
        alternatives:
          type: array
          description: >-
            The choices the fix leaves open, when the fix is a choice. For a pool
            no host can run, these are the backends its hosts do offer, so the UI
            can put the change one click away.
          items: { $ref: "#/components/schemas/BackendKind" }
          examples: [[podman]]
        since: { type: string, format: date-time }

    # --- status -----------------------------------------------------------
    CountBand:
      type: string
      enum: [none, few, many, backed_up]
      description: >-
        A count said roughly: none, a few (up to five), many, or -- for the
        queue only -- backed up, meaning more jobs are waiting than the fleet
        has slots for.
    FleetStatus:
      type: object
      required: [state, since, version, queued, running, median_wait_minutes, p95_wait_minutes, reasons, explanations]
      properties:
        state:
          type: string
          enum: [healthy, degraded, blocked]
          description: >-
            blocked when the worst of the fleet's problems is an error,
            degraded when it is a warning, healthy otherwise.
        since:
          type: string
          format: date-time
          description: When this controller first saw the fleet in this state.
        version: { type: string }
        queued: { $ref: "#/components/schemas/CountBand" }
        running: { $ref: "#/components/schemas/CountBand" }
        median_wait_minutes: { type: integer, description: The median queue wait over the last hour, rounded to the minute. }
        p95_wait_minutes: { type: integer, description: The 95th-percentile queue wait over the last hour, rounded to the minute. }
        reasons:
          type: array
          description: The fleet's current problems, one per code, worst first.
          items: { $ref: "#/components/schemas/FleetStatusReason" }
        explanations:
          type: object
          description: The public sentence for each code in reasons, from docs/problem-codes.md.
          additionalProperties: { type: string }
    FleetStatusReason:
      type: object
      additionalProperties: false
      required: [code, severity]
      properties:
        code: { type: string, examples: [pool.no_capacity] }
        severity: { type: string, enum: [error, warning] }
        since: { type: string, format: date-time }

    # --- meta -------------------------------------------------------------
    Meta:
      type: object
      required: [version, bootstrap_required]
      properties:
        version: { type: string, examples: ["1.0.0 (abc1234)"] }
        version_channel: { type: string, examples: ["v1.0.0", "dev"], description: The published image and binary tag carrying this build. }
        commit: { type: string }
        bootstrap_required: { type: boolean, description: True when no user exists yet. `/readyz` carries the same field, so a provisioner can wait on one endpoint. }
        tailcat_available: { type: boolean, description: Whether private enrolment is enabled and the controller has its encryption key. Relay connectivity is checked at enrolment. }
        auth_disabled: { type: boolean, description: True when authentication has been switched off in the configuration. }
        oidc_enabled: { type: boolean }
        oidc_label: { type: string, examples: ["Sign in with Okta"], description: "`oidc.label`, or \"Sign in with\" and the issuer's host." }
        password_login_hidden:
          type: boolean
          description: >-
            The sign-in page offers single sign-on alone: `oidc.hide_password_login` is on and
            single sign-on is working. An administrator can still ask for the form with /login?password.
        external_url: { type: string }
        webhook_url: { type: string }
        polling_only: { type: boolean, description: True when no webhook has ever been received and the poller is doing the work. }
        poller_enabled: { type: boolean, description: True when the fallback poller is running. It is off only by configuration, never by failure. }
        workflow_cancellation_enabled: { type: boolean, description: True when operators may ask GitHub to cancel workflow runs. }
        providers_available:
          type: boolean
          description: >-
            True when this deployment can rent machines - the build ships at least one
            provider driver and provider.enabled is on - so the page that would otherwise
            offer to buy machines nothing would ever create knows not to.
        poller_last_poll_at: { type: string, format: date-time, nullable: true, description: When the fallback poller last completed a sweep, or absent if it has not completed one since Zoomies started. }
        capacity_map:
          type: object
          description: >-
            How the host capacity map opens on each page that carries it, from
            ui.capacity_map.* in the fleet's settings. An operator who picks the
            other layout on the page keeps that pick in their browser; this is
            what somebody who has never chosen sees.
          properties:
            overview_layout: { $ref: "#/components/schemas/CapacityMapLayout" }
            hosts_layout: { $ref: "#/components/schemas/CapacityMapLayout" }
        queue_warning_threshold:
          type: integer
          description: >-
            How many jobs must be queued before the queue tiles on the Overview,
            Jobs and Pools pages turn to their warning colour, from
            ui.queue_warning_threshold in the fleet's settings.
          examples: [1]
    CapacityMapLayout:
      type: string
      description: overlay draws every host on one chart; split draws a chart for each.
      enum: [overlay, split]

    # --- overview ---------------------------------------------------------
    Stats:
      type: object
      properties:
        window: { type: string, description: The window these counts cover, echoed back., examples: ["1h"] }
        queued_jobs:
          type: integer
          description: >-
            Jobs waiting for a runner right now, whatever the window says. Work an
            operator removed from the queue is not waiting and is not counted, so a
            fleet whose queue has been emptied reports zero; paused work is still
            waiting and is still counted. Nor is a job whose workflow run has been
            cancelled, from the moment GitHub accepts the cancellation rather than
            when its completion delivery arrives.
        running_jobs:
          type: integer
          description: >-
            Jobs a runner is working on right now. A job whose workflow run has been
            cancelled stops counting the moment GitHub accepts the cancellation --
            its runner has already been taken away -- rather than when GitHub's
            completion delivery finally arrives.
        completed: { type: integer, description: Within the requested window. The sum of the four below. }
        succeeded: { type: integer, description: GitHub reported success and the fleet had no fault in it. }
        failed: { type: integer, description: A failing conclusion, or a runner that stopped under the job. }
        fleet_failed:
          type: integer
          description: >-
            How many of `failed` this deployment caused rather than the workflows: a runner
            that never started, or one that stopped under the job. A subset rather than a
            fifth outcome, because GitHub's answer for such a job is still "failure" and a
            split that did not add up would be a worse lie than no split.
        faults:
          type: object
          additionalProperties: { type: integer }
          description: >-
            Those failures by category, keyed by FaultKind. Categories with no jobs are
            absent rather than zero. This is what turns "eleven failures this hour" into
            "eleven, nine of them out of memory", which is a different sentence and sends a
            different person to a different page.
        runner_start_faults:
          type: object
          additionalProperties: { type: integer }
          description: >-
            Runners that failed before they could take a job, by category. These appear in
            no job count anywhere, because the jobs they were meant for are still queued --
            which is exactly why a pool that cannot start a container reads, everywhere
            else, as a fleet that is merely busy.
        cancelled: { type: integer, description: Cancelled or skipped, with no fault of the fleet's. }
        unknown: { type: integer, description: None of the above, including a job GitHub stopped reporting. Never counted as a success. }
        median_wait_ms: { type: integer, format: int64 }
        p95_wait_ms: { type: integer, format: int64 }
        p50_startup_ms: { type: integer, format: int64, description: Median runner creation-to-container-start latency. }
        p95_startup_ms: { type: integer, format: int64 }
        p50_registration_ms: { type: integer, format: int64, description: Median container-start-to-registration latency. }
        p95_registration_ms: { type: integer, format: int64 }
        fleet:
          type: object
          description: >
            The same job figures narrowed to the jobs this fleet has a hand in:
            one an enabled pool claimed, one that ran on a runner started here,
            or one still queued that no pool claims. GitHub reports every job in
            an installed repository, so on an organisation that also uses hosted
            runners the figures above are mostly somebody else's. Both are
            carried in one payload because the same numbers arrive over the
            event stream, which is one frame for every viewer.
          properties:
            queued_jobs: { type: integer, description: "As above, and on the same terms about removed work." }
            running_jobs: { type: integer, description: "As above, and on the same terms about cancelled work." }
            completed: { type: integer }
            succeeded: { type: integer }
            failed: { type: integer }
            fleet_failed: { type: integer, description: How many of failed this fleet caused. }
            cancelled: { type: integer }
            unknown: { type: integer }
            median_wait_ms: { type: integer, format: int64 }
            p95_wait_ms: { type: integer, format: int64 }
        runners:
          type: object
          properties:
            provisioning: { type: integer }
            registering: { type: integer }
            idle: { type: integer }
            busy: { type: integer }
            draining: { type: integer }
            failed: { type: integer }
            total: { type: integer }
        hosts:
          type: object
          properties:
            total: { type: integer }
            healthy: { type: integer }
            cordoned: { type: integer }
            capacity: { type: integer }
            used: { type: integer }
        pools:
          type: array
          items:
            type: object
            properties:
              pool_id: { type: string }
              pool_name: { type: string }
              min: { type: integer }
              max: { type: integer }
              live: { type: integer }
              busy: { type: integer }
              idle: { type: integer }
              queued: { type: integer }
              utilisation: { type: number, format: double, minimum: 0, maximum: 1 }

    FleetSample:
      type: object
      properties:
        at: { type: string, format: date-time }
        queued_jobs: { type: integer }
        running_jobs: { type: integer }
        fleet_queued_jobs: { type: integer, description: The same minute narrowed to the jobs this fleet has a hand in. Zero on samples taken before this was recorded. }
        fleet_running_jobs: { type: integer, description: As above, for jobs in progress. }
        idle_runners: { type: integer }
        busy_runners: { type: integer }
        total_runners: { type: integer }

    ScalingEvent:
      type: object
      properties:
        id: { type: string }
        pool_id: { type: string }
        pool_name: { type: string }
        from: { type: integer }
        to: { type: integer }
        reason:
          type: string
          description: The scheduler's own words, shown verbatim in the UI.
          examples: ["scaled linux-x64 2 -> 4: 3 jobs queued > 30s"]
        created_at: { type: string, format: date-time }

    # --- installations ----------------------------------------------------
    InstallationArchive:
      type: object
      required: [kind, archive_version, exported_at, version, installation_id, target, tables]
      properties:
        kind: { type: string, enum: [zoomies-installation] }
        archive_version: { type: integer }
        exported_at: { type: string, format: date-time }
        exported_from: { type: string }
        version: { type: string }
        installation_id: { type: string }
        target: { type: string }
        secrets:
          type: object
          description: Passphrase-sealed, base64. Absent when the export had no passphrase.
          properties:
            private_key: { type: string, format: byte }
            webhook_secret: { type: string, format: byte }
        tables:
          type: array
          items:
            type: object
            required: [table, columns, rows]
            properties:
              table: { type: string }
              columns: { type: array, items: { type: string } }
              rows:
                type: array
                description: One array per row, in column order. A blob is an object with a base64 field.
                items: { type: array, items: {} }
    Installation:
      type: object
      properties:
        id: { type: string }
        app_id: { type: integer, format: int64 }
        installation_id: { type: integer, format: int64 }
        target: { type: string, examples: [acme, "acme/widgets"] }
        target_type: { $ref: "#/components/schemas/TargetType" }
        api_base_url: { type: string }
        app_slug: { type: string }
        web_url: { type: string }
        settings_url:
          type: string
          description: >-
            The App's own settings page on GitHub, which is the only place its
            avatar can be uploaded. Absent when the App's slug is unknown.
          examples: ["https://github.com/organizations/acme/settings/apps/zoomies-acme"]
        enterprise: { type: boolean }
        healthy: { type: boolean }
        last_error: { type: string }
        last_checked_at: { type: [string, "null"], format: date-time }
        pool_count: { type: integer }
        created_at: { type: string, format: date-time }
        updated_at: { type: string, format: date-time }

    InstallationCreate:
      type: object
      required: [app_id, installation_id, target, target_type, private_key]
      properties:
        app_id: { type: integer, format: int64 }
        installation_id: { type: integer, format: int64 }
        target: { type: string }
        target_type: { $ref: "#/components/schemas/TargetType" }
        api_base_url: { type: string, default: "https://api.github.com" }
        private_key: { type: string, format: password, description: The App's PEM private key. Sealed before storage and never returned. }
        webhook_secret: { type: string, format: password }

    InstallationUpdate:
      type: object
      properties:
        target: { type: string }
        api_base_url: { type: string }
        private_key: { type: string, format: password }
        webhook_secret: { type: string, format: password }

    InstallationHealth:
      type: object
      properties:
        ok: { type: boolean }
        app_slug: { type: string }
        app_name: { type: string }
        message: { type: string, description: On failure, names the missing permission where GitHub tells us. }
        permissions: { type: object, additionalProperties: { type: string } }
        events: { type: array, items: { type: string } }
        missing_permissions: { type: array, items: { type: string } }
        missing_events: { type: array, items: { type: string } }
        rate_limit_remaining: { type: integer }
        repository_selection:
          type: string
          enum: [all, selected]
          description: >-
            GitHub's own word for how much of the target this installation covers. An App
            with every permission correct, installed on "only select repositories" and not
            on the one somebody pushes to, is a fleet where nothing ever queues and no page
            says why -- so the verify answer names it.
        repository_count:
          type: integer
          description: How many repositories the installation can see, up to the scan's own cap.
        repositories:
          type: array
          items: { type: string }
          description: The first few by name, so an operator can look for the one they expected.
        repositories_capped:
          type: boolean
          description: True when there are more than the names listed.

    WebhookDelivery:
      type: object
      properties:
        id: { type: string }
        delivery_id: { type: string }
        event: { type: string }
        action: { type: string }
        repo: { type: string }
        status: { type: string, enum: [accepted, rejected, error] }
        error: { type: string }
        installation_id:
          type: string
          description: >-
            The installation whose webhook secret verified this delivery. It is not
            necessarily the one covering the repository: when none does, every configured
            secret is tried, and this says which one answered. Empty on a delivery that
            verified against none.
        received_at: { type: string, format: date-time }

    WebhookCheck:
      type: object
      properties:
        reachable: { type: boolean }
        url: { type: string }
        message: { type: string }
        fix: { type: string, description: The specific remedy - open a port, use a tunnel, configure the proxy. }
        polling_available: { type: boolean }
        last_delivery_at: { type: [string, "null"], format: date-time }

    # --- migrations -------------------------------------------------------
    MigrationOverride:
      type: object
      description: |
        One job sent somewhere other than the consolidated `mapping` says.

        It names exactly one place -- a job, in a workflow file, in a repository
        -- and nothing about it is a pattern: a pattern would match more than
        the operator read in the review step. A job the plan could not attribute
        to a name cannot be overridden, because there would be nothing stable to
        key on when the apply step re-reads the file.
      required: [repo, path, job]
      properties:
        repo: { type: string, examples: ["acme/widgets"], description: Compared case-insensitively, as GitHub does. }
        path: { type: string, examples: [".github/workflows/ci.yml"] }
        job: { type: string, examples: ["integration"] }
        to:
          type: string
          examples: ["zoomies-linux-arm64"]
          description: >-
            The runs-on value this job gets. Empty leaves this one job on the rented runner it
            names today - a decision, reported with its own reason rather than as an unmapped
            label.

    MigrationRewrite:
      type: object
      description: One runs-on value a migration would change.
      properties:
        line: { type: integer, description: The 1-based line in the file as it is today. }
        job: { type: string, description: The workflow job the line belongs to, where indentation could tell. }
        label:
          type: string
          examples: ["ubuntu-latest"]
          description: >-
            The hosted-runner label being replaced, set only where the value asks for exactly
            one. A line carrying both a job and a label is one an override can name.
        from: { type: string, examples: ["ubuntu-latest"] }
        to: { type: string, examples: ["zoomies-linux-x64"] }
        overridden: { type: boolean, description: True when `to` came from an override rather than from the consolidated mapping. }

    MigrationSkip:
      type: object
      description: |
        A runs-on the migration deliberately left alone, and why. A skip is not
        a failure: a matrix expression, a job already on a self-hosted runner
        and a hosted label nobody mapped are all things a person has to decide.
      properties:
        line: { type: integer }
        job: { type: string }
        label:
          type: string
          description: >-
            The hosted-runner label this job asks for, set only where the value asks for exactly
            one. A skip carrying both a job and a label is one an override can settle; a
            ${{ }} expression carries neither, because no override can decide it.
        value: { type: string }
        reason: { type: string }

    MigrationWorkflow:
      type: object
      properties:
        path: { type: string, examples: [".github/workflows/ci.yml"] }
        sha: { type: string, description: The blob SHA the plan was computed against. }
        rewrites: { type: array, items: { $ref: "#/components/schemas/MigrationRewrite" } }
        skips: { type: array, items: { $ref: "#/components/schemas/MigrationSkip" } }
        hosted_labels:
          type: array
          items: { type: string }
          description: The hosted-runner labels this file asks for, mapped or not.
        diff: { type: string, description: A unified diff of the change, empty when the file is untouched. }

    MigrationRepo:
      type: object
      properties:
        repo: { type: string, examples: ["acme/widgets"] }
        default_branch: { type: string }
        workflows: { type: array, items: { $ref: "#/components/schemas/MigrationWorkflow" } }
        hosted_labels:
          type: array
          items: { type: string }
          description: The hosted-runner labels this repository asks for - GitHub's own and the vendors' - mapped or not.
        error: { type: string, description: Set when this repository could not be read; the rest of the plan still stands. }
        archived:
          type: boolean
          description: >-
            The repository is archived and therefore read-only, so no pull request can be
            opened against it. Its workflows are not read, and it is never counted as
            something the migration would change.
        on_zoomies:
          type: boolean
          description: At least one job in this repository already runs on a pool of this fleet.

    MigrationPoolOption:
      type: object
      properties:
        id: { type: string }
        name: { type: string }
        labels: { type: array, items: { type: string } }
        runs_on: { type: string, description: What a workflow writes to reach this pool, and the value a mapping should hold. }
        enabled: { type: boolean }

    MigrationCounts:
      type: object
      properties:
        repos: { type: integer }
        workflows: { type: integer }
        jobs: { type: integer }
        skipped: { type: integer }

    MigrationPlan:
      type: object
      properties:
        installation_id: { type: string }
        target: { type: string }
        repositories: { type: array, items: { $ref: "#/components/schemas/MigrationRepo" } }
        hosted_labels: { type: array, items: { type: string } }
        mapping:
          type: object
          additionalProperties: { type: string }
          description: What was applied - the request's mapping, or the one the server proposed.
        overrides:
          type: array
          items: { $ref: "#/components/schemas/MigrationOverride" }
          description: >-
            The exceptions that were applied on top of the mapping, echoed back so a plan
            describes itself.
        unmapped:
          type: array
          items: { type: string }
          description: Hosted labels no pool was proposed for. Jobs on these are left where they are.
        pools: { type: array, items: { $ref: "#/components/schemas/MigrationPoolOption" } }
        counts: { $ref: "#/components/schemas/MigrationCounts" }
        truncated: { type: boolean, description: True when there are more repositories after this page. }
        next_cursor: { type: string, description: Send as `cursor` to read the next page of repositories. Absent on the last page. }
        total_repos: { type: integer, description: How many repositories the installation can see in total, of which this is one page. }
        missing_permissions:
          type: array
          items: { type: string }
          description: >-
            What the App still needs before pull requests can be opened. Reported here,
            in the step before, because discovering it halfway through leaves half the
            pull requests open.
        permission_hint: { type: string }
        settings_url: { type: string, description: The App's settings page, where the missing permissions are granted. }

    MigrationResult:
      type: object
      properties:
        repo: { type: string }
        status: { type: string, enum: [opened, skipped, failed] }
        pull_request_url: { type: string }
        pull_request_number: { type: integer }
        branch: { type: string }
        workflows: { type: integer }
        jobs: { type: integer }
        reason: { type: string, description: Why it was skipped, or how it failed. }
        badge:
          type: string
          enum: [added, present, no_readme, unread, off]
          description: >-
            What became of the README badge on a pull request that was opened. `present`
            means the README already carried it; `no_readme` that there was no Markdown
            README to put it in; `unread` that GitHub would not hand the README over; `off`
            that the request asked for none.
        badge_reason: { type: string, description: Which kind of nowhere a `no_readme` was, or what GitHub said for an `unread`. }

    MigrationOutcome:
      type: object
      properties:
        results: { type: array, items: { $ref: "#/components/schemas/MigrationResult" } }
        opened: { type: integer }
        skipped: { type: integer }
        failed: { type: integer }

    # --- pools ------------------------------------------------------------
    Resources:
      type: object
      description: >-
        What one runner of a pool may consume on its host. Leaving both `cpus`
        and `memory_mb` out is the pool's way of saying "the host decides":
        each runner is then given one slot's share of whichever machine it
        lands on, charged against that host and applied as a real cgroup limit
        (`scheduler.default_runner_limits`, on by default). That is the sizing
        most fleets want, because it keeps fitting when a larger machine
        joins; set the two figures only where a pool's jobs need a particular
        size on every host. `disk_gb` and `pids_limit` are independent of the
        choice, and zero in either means no limit.
      properties:
        cpus:
          type: number
          format: double
          minimum: 0.25
          examples: [2]
          description: Cores, fractions allowed. Omitted or zero leaves the size to the host, which gives each runner one slot's share of its machine; below a quarter of a core is refused, because the runner binary cannot keep up with its own job.
        memory_mb:
          type: integer
          format: int64
          examples: [4096]
          description: Megabytes. Omitted or zero leaves the size to the host, which gives each runner one slot's share of its machine; below 512 is refused, because the runner binary is killed before it takes a job.
        disk_gb: { type: integer, format: int64, description: Advisory, and charged against the host's free disk. Zero is no limit. }
        pids_limit: { type: integer, format: int64, description: The container's pids cgroup limit. Zero is no limit. }
        min_cpus:
          type: number
          format: double
          examples: [1.5]
          description: >-
            The least CPU a runner may be given when no host has room for its standard: `cpus`,
            or -- where `cpus` is left to the host -- a whole slot's share of it. A host a
            little short of the standard then runs the job with as much as it can spare, never
            less than this, instead of leaving it queued. The standard is still what the fleet
            places at wherever it can. Must be below `cpus` when `cpus` is set, and at least a
            quarter of a core. On a pool, zero follows the fleet's `runners.minimum_cpus`,
            read live; `effective_minimum` is the minimum in force.
        min_memory_mb:
          type: integer
          format: int64
          examples: [3072]
          description: >-
            The least memory, in megabytes, a runner may be given when no host has room for
            `memory_mb` or a whole slot's share, as `min_cpus` is for CPU. Must be below
            `memory_mb` when that is set, and is held to the same 512 MB floor. On a pool, zero
            follows the fleet's `runners.minimum_memory_mb`, read live; `effective_minimum` is
            the minimum in force.

    CPUBurstPolicy:
      type: object
      description: >-
        Whether an automatically-sized Docker or Podman pool only observes, or
        may use, CPU left over after every live runner's guaranteed host share
        and one imminent start have been protected. Memory never changes while
        a job runs. Existing pools default to off; new pools default to observe.
      properties:
        mode:
          type: string
          enum: [off, observe, automatic]
          default: off
          description: >-
            `off` makes no decisions; `observe` publishes the decision and
            metrics without changing quotas; `automatic` applies the target to
            capable agents. Host pressure throttling always takes precedence.
        max_cpus:
          type: number
          format: double
          minimum: 0
          description: >-
            Maximum CPU for one logical runner. Zero uses the host's allocatable
            CPU as the ceiling. For Docker-in-Docker this covers the runner and
            sidecar together.
        size_for_ceiling:
          type: boolean
          default: true
          description: >-
            With `automatic`, start each runner with `CARGO_BUILD_JOBS`,
            `DOTNET_PROCESSOR_COUNT` and `-XX:ActiveProcessorCount` in
            `JAVA_TOOL_OPTIONS` set to its CPU ceiling in whole cores, because
            those toolchains size their workers once, at start, and could not
            otherwise use CPU lent later. A variable the pool's or the fleet's
            env already sets is left alone. Absent is on; ignored unless the
            mode is `automatic`.

    RunnerSettings:
      type: object
      description: >-
        What one pool overrides of the fleet's own runner timings. Every field
        is optional and every one is nullable, and the three states are
        distinct: absent leaves whatever the pool already had, `null` clears
        the override and hands the setting back to the fleet, and a duration
        sets it. A pool that overrides nothing follows the fleet and keeps
        following it when the fleet's figure changes, which is why these are
        not copied onto the pool when it is created.

        Zero is a real answer in each, not "unset": a pool on a slow
        air-gapped registry means "never fail a runner for taking too long to
        register" by setting `provision_timeout` to `0`.

        These are the settings whose right answer belongs to the pool rather
        than the fleet. A pool pulling a twelve-gigabyte Windows image and a
        pool booting Alpine do not agree about how long registering should
        take, and a fleet that has to pick one picks the slower. `idle_timeout`
        is not here because it is already a field on the pool itself.
      properties:
        provision_timeout:
          allOf: [{ $ref: "#/components/schemas/Duration" }]
          nullable: true
          description: Fails a runner of this pool that never finishes registering. Overrides `scheduler.provision_timeout`.
          examples: ["20m"]
        drain_timeout:
          allOf: [{ $ref: "#/components/schemas/Duration" }]
          nullable: true
          description: Fails a runner of this pool that has been draining this long with no job left on it. Overrides `scheduler.drain_timeout`. A runner still finishing a job is never touched by it.
          examples: ["10m"]
        max_runner_lifetime:
          allOf: [{ $ref: "#/components/schemas/Duration" }]
          nullable: true
          description: Drains a runner of this pool that has lived this long, the next time it is not busy. Overrides `scheduler.max_runner_lifetime`. It never ends a job.
          examples: ["24h"]
        scale_up_delay:
          allOf: [{ $ref: "#/components/schemas/Duration" }]
          nullable: true
          description: How long a job for this pool must have been queued before it counts as demand. Overrides `scheduler.scale_up_delay`.
          examples: ["0s"]
        docker_wait:
          allOf: [{ $ref: "#/components/schemas/Duration" }]
          nullable: true
          description: How long a runner of this pool waits for the Docker daemon it was promised before refusing a job. Overrides `runners.docker_wait`, and means nothing on a pool whose `docker_mode` is `none`.
          examples: ["120s"]

    PoolHostRoom:
      type: object
      description: >-
        One host's room for a pool: what it promises, what the machine can back
        at that pool's size, and what one runner of it is charged there.
      properties:
        host_id: { type: string }
        host: { type: string }
        slots: { type: integer, description: The host's runner capacity, less any throttle in force. }
        fits: { type: integer, description: How many runners of this pool the machine has room for, ignoring the slot count. A host whose slots outrun its machine reads as free capacity and refuses every create for it. }
        room: { type: integer, description: The smaller of the two, which is what the pool can actually expect here. }
        limited_by:
          type: string
          enum: [slots, cpu, memory, disk]
          description: What ran out first. Absent on a host that has measured nothing, where only its slots bind.
        charge_cpus: { type: number, format: double, description: What one runner of this pool costs here, which is twice what the pool says for a docker-in-docker pool -- the sidecar gets the same limits. }
        charge_memory_mb: { type: integer, format: int64 }
        cpus: { type: number, format: double, description: The machine less its reserve, which is what the charge is taken from. }
        memory_mb: { type: integer, format: int64 }
        disk_mb: { type: integer, format: int64 }
        cpus_known: { type: boolean }
        memory_known: { type: boolean }
        disk_known: { type: boolean }
        elastic_cpu:
          type: boolean
          description: >-
            Whether this host's agent can move a live runner's CPU quota. An elastic pool is
            honoured only where it is true; a runner of one placed elsewhere is held at its share.

    PoolRoom:
      type: object
      description: >-
        How many runners of a pool the hosts that can run it have room for,
        counted on an empty fleet. What is running right now changes with every
        job; the question a size and a maximum are chosen against is how big the
        machines are, in runners of this pool.
      properties:
        runners: { type: integer, description: The room across every matching host. It is the number a maximum is worth comparing against. }
        slots: { type: integer, description: What those hosts' capacities add up to, whatever the size. }
        hosts:
          type: array
          items: { $ref: "#/components/schemas/PoolHostRoom" }
        smallest_disk_mb: { type: integer, format: int64, description: The least free disk on any matching host, which is what a cache size limit has to live inside. }
        smallest_disk_host: { type: string }
        disk_known: { type: boolean }

    PoolPlatform:
      type: object
      description: One row of the runner image catalogue.
      properties:
        os: { type: string, examples: [ubuntu] }
        os_version: { type: string, examples: ["24.04"] }
        label: { type: string, examples: ["Ubuntu 24.04"] }
        image: { type: string, examples: ["ghcr.io/eyupio/zoomies-runner:ubuntu-2404"] }
        arches: { type: array, items: { type: string }, examples: [[amd64, arm64]] }
        default: { type: boolean, description: True for the variant :latest points at. }

    Platform:
      type: object
      description: >-
        The machine a pool's runners need, or the machine a host is. Every field
        is optional; an empty field is a promise nobody made and matches
        anything. A pool's platform selects its runner image and restricts the
        hosts the scheduler may place its runners on.
      properties:
        os:
          type: string
          description: A distribution, not a kernel - "linux" cannot pick a runner image.
          enum: [ubuntu, debian, fedora, rocky, macos, windows]
          examples: [ubuntu]
        os_version: { type: string, examples: ["24.04"] }
        arch: { type: string, enum: [amd64, arm64], examples: [arm64] }
    ReportPercentiles:
      type: object
      description: Exact nearest-rank percentiles of one interval's stored samples.
      required: [samples, p50_seconds, p95_seconds]
      properties:
        samples: { type: integer, description: How many intervals had both ends recorded. }
        p50_seconds: { type: [number, "null"], description: Null when there are no samples. }
        p95_seconds: { type: [number, "null"], description: Null when there are no samples. }
    InstallationReport:
      type: object
      required: [installation, window, installation_id, from, to, counts, timings, counts_from, timings_from, unavailable]
      properties:
        installation:
          type: object
          required: [id]
          properties:
            id: { type: string }
            target: { type: string, description: Only to a caller who may read installations and, for a repository target, jobs. }
            target_type: { type: string, enum: [org, repo] }
        window: { type: string, description: The window asked for, echoed back. }
        installation_id: { type: string }
        from: { type: string, format: date-time, description: The start of the window, at UTC midnight. }
        to: { type: string, format: date-time }
        counts:
          type: object
          required: [observed, eligible, created_for, ran_here, ran_elsewhere, fleet_fault, cleanup_pending, cleanup_converged]
          properties:
            observed: { type: integer }
            eligible: { type: integer }
            created_for: { type: integer }
            ran_here: { type: integer }
            ran_elsewhere: { type: integer }
            fleet_fault: { type: integer }
            cleanup_pending: { type: integer }
            cleanup_converged: { type: integer }
        timings:
          type: object
          required: [scheduling, registration, cleanup]
          properties:
            scheduling: { $ref: "#/components/schemas/ReportPercentiles" }
            registration: { $ref: "#/components/schemas/ReportPercentiles" }
            cleanup: { $ref: "#/components/schemas/ReportPercentiles" }
        counts_from: { type: string, format: date-time, description: Where the counts are complete from; later than from when part of the window is unavailable. }
        timings_from: { type: string, format: date-time, description: Where the timings are complete from. }
        rolled_until: { type: string, format: date-time, description: Where the daily roll-up hands over to the rows, when any of the window came from it. }
        unavailable:
          type: array
          items: { type: string }
          description: Each part of the window a figure does not cover, and why, in words.
    UsageResponse:
      type: object
      required: [from, to, group_by, items, costs_are_estimates, allocation_attributable, history_from]
      properties:
        from: { type: string, format: date-time }
        to: { type: string, format: date-time }
        group_by: { type: string, enum: [installation, repository, workflow, pool, host] }
        costs_are_estimates: { type: boolean, const: true }
        allocation_attributable:
          type: boolean
          description: |
            Whether allocated runner lifetime, and therefore cost, can be
            attributed to this grouping at all. A runner idles on behalf of a
            pool, never on behalf of a repository or a workflow, so it is false
            for the repository and workflow groupings and every row's
            allocated_runner_seconds is null.
        history_from:
          type: object
          required: [jobs, runners]
          description: |
            Where the history each figure is computed from begins, given what
            retention has already pruned. Job counts, execution time and
            queue waits come from job rows. Allocated runner time and cost
            come from the usage ledger — a daily roll-up for the whole UTC
            days it covers, and runner rows and sessions for the rest — so
            `runners` is where the ledger begins rather than where
            retention.runners cuts the rows. A report whose `from` is earlier
            than one of these is complete only from that instant on. Null
            means that history is never pruned.
          properties:
            jobs: { type: string, format: date-time, nullable: true }
            runners: { type: string, format: date-time, nullable: true }
        items:
          type: array
          items:
            type: object
            required: [key, job_execution_seconds, allocated_runner_seconds, jobs, jobs_started, jobs_completed, average_queue_wait_seconds, peak_concurrency]
            properties:
              history:
                type: array
                items: { $ref: "#/components/schemas/UsageBucket" }
              succeeded: { type: integer }
              failed: { type: integer }
              cancelled: { type: integer }
              unknown: { type: integer }
              key: { type: string }
              job_execution_seconds: { type: number, description: Job execution time clipped to the reported interval. }
              allocated_runner_seconds:
                type: number
                nullable: true
                description: Runner lifetime clipped to the interval, or null when the grouping cannot attribute it. Null is not zero.
              jobs: { type: integer, description: "Jobs queued within the interval. Counts are additive: adjacent reports sum." }
              jobs_started: { type: integer, description: Jobs whose run began within the interval. }
              jobs_completed: { type: integer, description: Jobs that finished within the interval. }
              average_queue_wait_seconds:
                type: number
                nullable: true
                description: Mean wait of the jobs_started jobs, so the denominator is the population with an observed wait. Null when nothing started in the interval.
              peak_concurrency: { type: integer }
              estimated_cost: { type: number, description: Estimate from administrator-assigned pool rates; omitted when no rate exists. }

    UsageBucket:
      type: object
      required: [from, queued, started, succeeded, failed, cancelled, unknown, execution_seconds, allocated_seconds, capacity_samples, capacity_reached]
      properties:
        from: { type: string, format: date-time }
        queued: { type: integer }
        started: { type: integer }
        succeeded: { type: integer }
        failed: { type: integer }
        cancelled: { type: integer }
        unknown: { type: integer }
        execution_seconds: { type: number }
        allocated_seconds: { type: number }
        capacity_samples: { type: integer, description: Observed pool minutes; zero means no capacity telemetry. }
        capacity_reached: { type: integer, description: Observed pool minutes containing at least one capacity-blocked placement. Not incident count or exact duration. }

    ToolchainDemand:
      type: object
      required: [tool, jobs, repositories]
      properties:
        tool: { type: string, enum: [python, node, go, java, dotnet] }
        version: { type: string, description: "The version or range as the workflow writes it. Absent when unresolved is set." }
        distribution: { type: string, description: "setup-java's distribution; absent for other tools." }
        unresolved: { type: string, description: "Why the version is not known from the workflow file." }
        jobs: { type: integer, description: "Workflow jobs asking for it, each matrix combination counted once." }
        repositories: { type: array, items: { type: string } }

    ToolchainScanInstallation:
      type: object
      required: [installation_id, target, repositories, workflows]
      properties:
        installation_id: { type: string }
        target: { type: string }
        repositories: { type: integer }
        workflows: { type: integer }
        error: { type: string, description: "Why this installation was not read, or only partly." }
        unreadable:
          type: object
          additionalProperties: { type: string }
          description: Repositories whose workflows GitHub would not return, and why.

    ToolFill:
      type: object
      description: What a tool cache fill did with one requested version.
      required: [tool, request, outcome]
      properties:
        tool: { type: string, enum: [python, node, go, java, dotnet] }
        request: { type: string, description: The version as the workflows asked for it, such as 3.12 or lts/*. }
        outcome:
          type: string
          enum: [installed, present, skipped, failed]
          description: present means it was already in the cache; skipped is a request a fill cannot serve, with the reason.
        version: { type: string, description: The release the request resolved to, for installed and present. }
        reason: { type: string, description: Why, for skipped and failed. }
    ToolCacheFill:
      type: object
      description: One pool's tool cache fill on one host, the latest there has been.
      required: [host_id, host_name, state, requested, tools, queued_at]
      properties:
        host_id: { type: string }
        host_name: { type: string }
        state:
          type: string
          enum: [pending, succeeded, failed]
          description: A fill that succeeded may still have skipped or failed requests; tools says which.
        requested: { type: integer }
        tools: { type: array, items: { $ref: "#/components/schemas/ToolFill" } }
        error: { type: string }
        queued_at: { type: string, format: date-time }
        finished_at: { type: string, format: date-time }

    ToolchainScan:
      type: object
      required: [running, pools, unmatched, installations, fills]
      properties:
        running: { type: boolean }
        started_at: { type: string, format: date-time }
        finished_at: { type: string, format: date-time }
        pools:
          type: object
          description: Pool ID to what that pool's jobs ask for.
          additionalProperties:
            type: array
            items: { $ref: "#/components/schemas/ToolchainDemand" }
        unmatched:
          type: array
          description: What jobs ask for that no pool would run.
          items: { $ref: "#/components/schemas/ToolchainDemand" }
        installations:
          type: array
          items: { $ref: "#/components/schemas/ToolchainScanInstallation" }
        fills:
          type: object
          description: Pool ID to its tool cache's latest fill on each host, for the pools that keep a tool cache.
          additionalProperties:
            type: array
            items: { $ref: "#/components/schemas/ToolCacheFill" }

    PoolPrewarm:
      type: object
      properties:
        pool_id: { type: string }
        host_id: { type: string }
        host_name: { type: string }
        image: { type: string }
        state: { type: string, enum: [pending, succeeded, failed] }
        digest: { type: string }
        error: { type: string }
        updated_at: { type: string, format: date-time }

    Pool:
      type: object
      properties:
        id: { type: string }
        name: { type: string }
        installation_id: { type: string }
        installation_target: { type: string }
        labels: { type: array, items: { type: string } }
        runner_group: { type: string }
        backend: { $ref: "#/components/schemas/BackendKind" }
        platform: { $ref: "#/components/schemas/Platform" }
        image: { type: string }
        effective_image:
          type: string
          description: >-
            The image this pool's runners will actually boot: image when the pool
            names one, otherwise the variant its platform selects, otherwise the
            instance default -- and then its Docker variant when the pool gives
            its jobs a daemon.
        pull_policy: { $ref: "#/components/schemas/PullPolicy" }
        runner_version: { type: string }
        min_runners: { type: integer }
        max_runners: { type: integer }
        repository_scale_up_limit: { type: integer, minimum: 0, description: Best-effort per-repository runner creation limit; zero disables it. This cannot prevent GitHub from assigning work to compatible idle runners and is not a strict execution concurrency cap. }
        cost_per_runner_hour: { type: number, minimum: 0, nullable: true, description: Optional administrator-assigned rate used only for estimates. }
        priority: { type: integer, default: 0, description: Higher-priority pools receive creation capacity before lower-priority pools. }
        idle_timeout: { $ref: "#/components/schemas/Duration" }
        ephemeral: { type: boolean }
        docker_mode: { $ref: "#/components/schemas/DockerMode" }
        resources: { $ref: "#/components/schemas/Resources" }
        cpu_burst: { $ref: "#/components/schemas/CPUBurstPolicy" }
        sizing:
          type: string
          enum: [automatic, elastic, fixed]
          description: >-
            How this pool decides what one runner gets. `automatic` is one
            slot's share of whichever host it lands on, which is what a pool
            with no `cpus` and no `memory_mb` means; `elastic` keeps that share
            as its guarantee and may borrow unused CPU; `fixed` is the figures
            in `resources`, the same on every host.
        effective_minimum:
          type: object
          readOnly: true
          required: [cpus, memory_mb, cpus_inherited, memory_mb_inherited]
          description: >-
            The minimum this pool's runners are held to. Where the pool's own
            `resources.min_cpus` or `min_memory_mb` is zero, the fleet's
            `runners.minimum_cpus` / `minimum_memory_mb` applies instead, read
            live, unless it is at or above the pool's typed standard size.
            `resources` keeps the pool's own figures, so sending the pool back
            never makes an inherited minimum its own.
          properties:
            cpus: { type: number, description: The minimum in cores; zero is none. }
            memory_mb: { type: integer, format: int64, description: The minimum in MB; zero is none. }
            cpus_inherited: { type: boolean, description: Whether `cpus` is the fleet's figure rather than the pool's. }
            memory_mb_inherited: { type: boolean, description: Whether `memory_mb` is the fleet's figure rather than the pool's. }
        runner_settings: { $ref: "#/components/schemas/RunnerSettings" }
        cache: { $ref: "#/components/schemas/CacheConfig" }
        host_selector: { type: object, additionalProperties: { type: string } }
        env:
          type: object
          additionalProperties: { type: string }
          description: >-
            The environment injected into every runner this pool creates.
            Readable in full by operators and administrators; a viewer is sent
            the keys with empty values, because this is where a registry or
            proxy credential ends up and setting one is an operator action.
            The same applies to the pool.created and pool.updated events.
        run_as_root: { type: boolean }
        no_default_labels: { type: boolean, description: "Register runners with only the pool's own labels, without self-hosted, the operating system and the architecture (config.sh --no-default-labels). Only a non-ephemeral pool may set it: GitHub adds those labels to every just-in-time runner itself. A job asking for self-hosted no longer matches the pool unless the pool lists it." }
        enabled: { type: boolean }
        created_at: { type: string, format: date-time }
        updated_at: { type: string, format: date-time }
        counts:
          type: object
          properties:
            provisioning: { type: integer }
            registering: { type: integer }
            idle: { type: integer }
            busy: { type: integer }
            draining: { type: integer }
            failed: { type: integer }
            live: { type: integer }
        queued_jobs: { type: integer, description: "Jobs this pool has claimed and not yet started, less any an operator removed from the queue." }
        utilisation: { type: number, format: double }
        warnings:
          type: array
          items: { $ref: "#/components/schemas/Problem" }
          description: The dangerous settings this pool has in effect, if any.

    CacheConfig:
      type: object
      description: Disposable performance cache mounted at /opt/zoomies-cache; it is not persistent workflow storage and may be evicted.
      required: [enabled, scope]
      properties:
        enabled: { type: boolean, default: false }
        scope:
          type: string
          enum: [pool, repository]
          default: pool
          description: >-
            Repository scope gives each repository its own cache. Under an
            organisation-targeted installation it needs `repository` set,
            because the installation alone does not say which repository the
            pool serves.
        size_limit:
          type: integer
          format: int64
          minimum: 0
          description: >-
            Maximum bytes, enforced between one runner and the next by evicting
            whole cache entries, least recently modified first. Only a cache in
            a host directory can be measured, so a non-zero limit requires
            `source` to be an absolute host path. Zero is unlimited.
        source: { type: string, description: Optional absolute host directory or safe named-volume prefix. }
        repository:
          type: string
          description: >-
            The repository a repository-scoped cache belongs to, as owner/name.
            Required when the pool's installation targets an organisation, and
            left empty when it targets a single repository, which supplies it.
        tools:
          type: boolean
          default: false
          description: >-
            Keep the pool's tool cache -- where setup-python, setup-node,
            setup-go and setup-java unpack what they download -- between
            runners, in each host's shared folder
            (/var/lib/zoomies/shared/cache/tools), shared with the same runners
            as the cache above. Needs `enabled`, and a container backend. A job
            that can write to it can replace a tool the next job runs.

    PoolsExport:
      type: object
      required: [export_version, exported_at, version, pools]
      properties:
        export_version: { type: integer }
        exported_at: { type: string, format: date-time }
        exported_from: { type: string, description: The address the source instance answers on. }
        version: { type: string, description: The Zoomies build that wrote it. }
        pools: { type: array, items: { $ref: "#/components/schemas/PoolDocument" } }

    PoolDocument:
      type: object
      description: One pool as a pools export carries it.
      required: [name, installation, labels, backend, platform, image, pull_policy, min_runners, max_runners, idle_timeout, ephemeral, docker_mode, resources, cpu_burst, runner_settings, cache, host_selector, env_keys, run_as_root, enabled]
      properties:
        name: { type: string }
        installation: { type: string, description: The organisation or owner/repository the pool's installation covers. }
        labels: { type: array, items: { type: string } }
        runner_group: { type: string }
        backend: { type: string }
        platform: { $ref: "#/components/schemas/Platform" }
        image: { type: string }
        pull_policy: { type: string }
        runner_version: { type: string }
        min_runners: { type: integer }
        max_runners: { type: integer }
        repository_scale_up_limit: { type: integer }
        cost_per_runner_hour: { type: number, nullable: true }
        priority: { type: integer }
        idle_timeout: { type: string }
        ephemeral: { type: boolean }
        docker_mode: { type: string }
        resources: { $ref: "#/components/schemas/Resources" }
        cpu_burst: { $ref: "#/components/schemas/CPUBurstPolicy" }
        runner_settings:
          type: object
          description: Every override, with null for one the pool does not make, so importing hands it back to the fleet.
          properties:
            provision_timeout: { type: string, nullable: true }
            drain_timeout: { type: string, nullable: true }
            max_runner_lifetime: { type: string, nullable: true }
            scale_up_delay: { type: string, nullable: true }
            docker_wait: { type: string, nullable: true }
        cache: { $ref: "#/components/schemas/CacheConfig" }
        host_selector: { type: object, additionalProperties: { type: string } }
        env_keys:
          type: array
          items: { type: string }
          description: The environment variables the pool injects. Their values are never exported.
        run_as_root: { type: boolean }
        enabled: { type: boolean }
        no_default_labels: { type: boolean, description: The pool registers its runners with its own labels only. }

    PoolsImportRequest:
      type: object
      required: [document]
      properties:
        document: { type: string, description: A pools export, as text. YAML or JSON. }
        dry_run: { type: boolean, description: Plan and report; write nothing. }
        skip: { type: array, items: { type: string }, description: Names of pools in the document to leave out. }

    PoolsImportChange:
      type: object
      required: [pool, action, fields, warnings, env_keys]
      properties:
        pool: { type: string }
        action: { type: string, enum: [create, change, unchanged, refused] }
        fields:
          type: array
          description: Every setting for a create, the ones that move for a change, and none otherwise.
          items:
            type: object
            required: [field, current, incoming]
            properties:
              field: { type: string }
              current: { nullable: true, description: The pool's value here; null for a pool that does not exist yet. }
              incoming: { nullable: true, description: The document's value. }
        reason: { type: string, description: Why it is refused. }
        warnings: { type: array, items: { type: string }, description: What would not stop the import but should be known first. }
        env_keys: { type: array, items: { type: string }, description: Environment variables the source pool injected, to set by hand. }

    PoolsImport:
      type: object
      required: [applied, changes, summary]
      properties:
        applied: { type: boolean }
        changes: { type: array, items: { $ref: "#/components/schemas/PoolsImportChange" } }
        summary:
          type: object
          required: [create, change, unchanged, refused, skipped]
          properties:
            create: { type: integer }
            change: { type: integer }
            unchanged: { type: integer }
            refused: { type: integer }
            skipped: { type: integer }

    PoolCreate:
      type: object
      required: [name, installation_id, labels, backend]
      properties:
        name:
          type: string
          minLength: 1
          maxLength: 64
          description: >-
            The pool's name. Every pool name carries the brand, so a name sent
            without the `zoomies-` prefix is stored with one: `gpu` becomes
            `zoomies-gpu`. Beyond the brand, Zoomies' own convention is
            zoomies-<vcpu>vcpu[-<memory>gb]-<os>-<version>[-<arch>], so the name
            a workflow's runs-on carries says how much machine it is asking for.
            Any name is accepted.
          examples: [zoomies-4vcpu-ubuntu-2404]
        installation_id: { type: string }
        labels: { type: array, items: { type: string }, minItems: 1 }
        runner_group: { type: string }
        backend: { $ref: "#/components/schemas/BackendKind" }
        platform: { $ref: "#/components/schemas/Platform" }
        image:
          type: string
          description: >-
            Leave blank to follow the pool's platform, which selects a published
            zoomies-runner variant, or the instance default when the pool names
            no platform.
        pull_policy: { $ref: "#/components/schemas/PullPolicy" }
        runner_version: { type: string }
        min_runners: { type: integer, default: 0, minimum: 0 }
        max_runners: { type: integer, default: 4, minimum: 1 }
        repository_scale_up_limit: { type: integer, minimum: 0, description: Best-effort creation limit, not a strict execution concurrency cap. }
        cost_per_runner_hour: { type: number, minimum: 0, nullable: true }
        priority: { type: integer, default: 0 }
        idle_timeout: { allOf: [{ $ref: "#/components/schemas/Duration" }], default: "5m" }
        ephemeral: { type: boolean, default: true }
        docker_mode: { allOf: [{ $ref: "#/components/schemas/DockerMode" }], default: none }
        resources: { $ref: "#/components/schemas/Resources" }
        cpu_burst: { allOf: [{ $ref: "#/components/schemas/CPUBurstPolicy" }], default: { mode: observe, max_cpus: 0 } }
        runner_settings: { $ref: "#/components/schemas/RunnerSettings" }
        cache: { $ref: "#/components/schemas/CacheConfig" }
        host_selector: { type: object, additionalProperties: { type: string } }
        env: { type: object, additionalProperties: { type: string } }
        run_as_root: { type: boolean, default: false }
        no_default_labels: { type: boolean, default: false, description: "Register runners with only the pool's own labels, without self-hosted, the operating system and the architecture (config.sh --no-default-labels). Only a non-ephemeral pool may set it: GitHub adds those labels to every just-in-time runner itself. A job asking for self-hosted no longer matches the pool unless the pool lists it." }
        enabled: { type: boolean, default: true }

    # A PATCH body: every field is optional, and only the ones present are
    # changed. It repeats PoolCreate's properties rather than composing them,
    # because `allOf` keeps the parent's `required` list however empty the
    # child's is -- which would make a one-field change (switching a blocked
    # pool's backend, say) impossible to express in a generated client.
    PoolUpdate:
      type: object
      properties:
        name:
          type: string
          minLength: 1
          maxLength: 64
          description: >-
            The pool's name. Every pool name carries the brand, so a name sent
            without the `zoomies-` prefix is stored with one: `gpu` becomes
            `zoomies-gpu`.
          examples: [zoomies-linux-x64]
        installation_id: { type: string }
        labels: { type: array, items: { type: string }, minItems: 1 }
        runner_group: { type: string }
        backend: { $ref: "#/components/schemas/BackendKind" }
        image: { type: string }
        pull_policy: { $ref: "#/components/schemas/PullPolicy" }
        runner_version: { type: string }
        min_runners: { type: integer, minimum: 0 }
        max_runners: { type: integer, minimum: 1 }
        repository_scale_up_limit: { type: integer, minimum: 0, description: Best-effort creation limit, not a strict execution concurrency cap. }
        cost_per_runner_hour: { type: number, minimum: 0, nullable: true }
        priority: { type: integer }
        idle_timeout: { $ref: "#/components/schemas/Duration" }
        ephemeral: { type: boolean }
        docker_mode: { $ref: "#/components/schemas/DockerMode" }
        resources: { $ref: "#/components/schemas/Resources" }
        cpu_burst: { $ref: "#/components/schemas/CPUBurstPolicy" }
        runner_settings: { $ref: "#/components/schemas/RunnerSettings" }
        cache: { $ref: "#/components/schemas/CacheConfig" }
        host_selector: { type: object, additionalProperties: { type: string } }
        env: { type: object, additionalProperties: { type: string } }
        run_as_root: { type: boolean }
        no_default_labels: { type: boolean, description: "Register runners with only the pool's own labels, without self-hosted, the operating system and the architecture (config.sh --no-default-labels). Only a non-ephemeral pool may set it: GitHub adds those labels to every just-in-time runner itself. A job asking for self-hosted no longer matches the pool unless the pool lists it." }
        enabled: { type: boolean }

    # --- runners ----------------------------------------------------------
    CPUResourceState:
      type: object
      description: >-
        The live CPU state for a runner with an enforced CPU quota: lent spare CPU, held at
        its guarantee, throttled by host pressure, or -- on a pool with elastic CPU off --
        sitting exactly where it was put.
      properties:
        state: { type: string, enum: [observing, guaranteed, zoomies, maximum_zoomies, throttled, sit_and_stay] }
        label: { type: string, description: A short dog-themed operator label; clients should branch on state. }
        reason: { type: string, enum: [observe_only, base_allocation, spare_cpu_lent, host_pressure, elastic_off] }
        guaranteed_cpus: { type: number, format: double }
        current_cpus: { type: number, format: double }
        ceiling_cpus: { type: number, format: double }
        factor: { type: number, format: double }
        sized_for_cpus:
          type: integer
          description: >-
            The CPU count the runner's toolchains were told to size their workers for
            when it started (see `CPUBurstPolicy.size_for_ceiling`). Absent when they were
            told nothing.

    Runner:
      type: object
      properties:
        id: { type: string }
        name: { type: string }
        pool_id: { type: string }
        pool_name: { type: string }
        host_id: { type: string }
        host_name: { type: string }
        state: { $ref: "#/components/schemas/RunnerState" }
        github_runner_id: { type: integer, format: int64 }
        container_id: { type: string }
        ephemeral: { type: boolean }
        labels: { type: array, items: { type: string } }
        image: { type: string }
        image_digest: { type: string, description: Immutable digest resolved by the host backend. }
        runner_version: { type: string }
        current_job_id: { type: string }
        current_job: { $ref: "#/components/schemas/Job" }
        message: { type: string }
        fault_kind:
