          $ref: "#/components/schemas/FaultKind"
        fault_fix:
          type: string
          description: >-
            What to do about this runner's failure. Empty on a runner that did not fail. A
            runner that failed before ever taking a job is the case this exists for:
            nothing else in the system says why a pool's containers will not start, because
            the jobs it was meant for are still queued and none of them is marked failed.
        jobs_handled: { type: integer }
        resource_sample: { $ref: "#/components/schemas/WorkloadStats" }
        cpu_percent: { type: number, format: double }
        memory_bytes: { type: integer, format: int64 }
        allocated_cpus:
          type: number
          format: double
          description: >-
            The CPU quota this runner's workload was created with. Omitted when it has none.
            With `allocation_source` it is what tells an OOM kill or a slow job on a defaulted
            limit apart from one on a limit somebody set.
        allocated_memory_mb:
          type: integer
          format: int64
          description: The memory limit this runner's workload was created with. Omitted when it has none.
        allocation_source:
          type: string
          enum: [pool, host, reduced, history, ""]
          description: >-
            Where the allocation came from: `pool` for the pool's own limits, `host` for one
            slot's share of the host it landed on (the default when the pool sets none),
            `reduced` for a runner no host had room for at the pool's standard size, given what
            one could spare at or above the pool's minimum, and `history` for a runner sized up
            to what the jobs waiting on its pool are known to need from their recent runs
            (`scheduler.history_sizing: on`). Omitted when the runner was created with no limit
            at all.
        cpu_resource: { $ref: "#/components/schemas/CPUResourceState" }
        created_at: { type: string, format: date-time }
        container_started_at:
          type: string
          format: date-time
          description: >-
            When the runner's container (or process) started on its host. With registered_at
            it is what tells the two causes of a stuck runner apart: a container that never
            started is a backend or image problem on the host, and one that started and never
            registered is a credential, network or GitHub problem.
        registered_at:
          type: string
          format: date-time
          description: When the runner registered itself with GitHub.
        started_at: { type: [string, "null"], format: date-time }
        last_idle_at: { type: [string, "null"], format: date-time }
        finished_at: { type: [string, "null"], format: date-time }
        cleanup_error:
          type: string
          description: >-
            Why Zoomies could not finish taking this runner away: a stop or remove the
            agent could not complete, or a registration GitHub would not delete. Empty is
            the normal case. A non-empty value means something is left behind — a container
            on its host, or a registration on the organisation — and it will not go away on
            its own. Zoomies retries, and this clears when it succeeds.
        cleanup_failed_at: { type: [string, "null"], format: date-time }
        cleanup_attempts:
          type: integer
          description: >-
            How many times cleanup has been tried. It is kept after a success, because how
            many tries it took is the difference between a blip and a host worth looking at.
        create_task_issued_at: { type: [string, "null"], format: date-time, description: "First create task delivered to the host; never overwritten by redelivery or removal. Absent for older runners." }
        host_removed_at: { type: [string, "null"], format: date-time, description: "Controller receipt of positive host removal confirmation, including the workload and work directory." }
        registration_deleted_at: { type: [string, "null"], format: date-time, description: "Controller confirmation that the GitHub registration is absent." }
        cleanup_estimated_at: { type: [string, "null"], format: date-time, description: "Historical cleanup estimate from an older build; not confirmation that both sides were removed." }
        cleaned_up_at:
          type: [string, "null"]
          format: date-time
          description: >-
            The end of the runner's life: nothing of it left, on the host or on GitHub. The
            counterpart of `created_at` at the other end.

    RunnerDetail:
      allOf:
        - $ref: "#/components/schemas/Runner"
        - type: object
          properties:
            host: { $ref: "#/components/schemas/Host" }
            pool: { $ref: "#/components/schemas/Pool" }
            timeline: { type: array, items: { $ref: "#/components/schemas/TimelineEntry" } }
            logs_available: { type: boolean, description: False when the runner's host is unreachable, so the UI can say why rather than showing an empty log. }

    JobExplanation:
      type: object
      required: [job_id, state, summary, waiting, blocked, computed_at]
      properties:
        job_id: { type: string }
        state: { $ref: "#/components/schemas/JobState" }
        summary:
          type: string
          description: >-
            The sentence. Always set, including for a job that is running or finished:
            "nothing is wrong" is an answer to the question.
        detail: { type: string, description: What the summary leaves out, in the scheduler's own words where it has any. }
        fix: { type: string, description: What to do. Absent means there is nothing to do, which is different from not knowing. }
        waiting: { type: boolean, description: Whether the job is still waiting on something. }
        blocked:
          type: boolean
          description: >-
            Whether waiting will not on its own end it. A fleet that is merely busy clears;
            a pool nothing can place never will, and the two need different advice.
        pool_id: { type: string }
        runner_id: { type: string }
        host_id: { type: string }
        computed_at: { type: string, format: date-time }

    Recovery:
      type: object
      required: [fenced]
      properties:
        fenced: { type: boolean }
        reason:
          type: string
          description: Why the fence is on -- normally the backup this database was restored from.

    Backup:
      type: object
      description: One backup, as the Backups tab lists it. The manifest's facts are lifted out flat.
      required: [id, taken_at, source, location, bytes, total_bytes, schema_migrations, secrets, key_matches, key_included, restorable]
      properties:
        id: { type: string, description: The backup's directory name., examples: [zoomies-20260916-120000] }
        taken_at: { type: string, format: date-time }
        source:
          type: string
          enum: [cli, manual, scheduled, uploaded, fetched, pre-migration]
          description: >-
            Who took it. `pre-migration` is a copy the store took before applying
            migrations, and `fetched` one pulled back out of a backup remote.
            Neither an uploaded nor a fetched backup is counted or removed by
            retention.
        taken_by: { type: string }
        location:
          type: string
          enum: [backups, pre-migration]
          description: Which directory it is in.
        bytes: { type: integer, format: int64, description: The database's size. }
        total_bytes: { type: integer, format: int64, description: The whole directory, which is larger when the key is in it. }
        version: { type: string, description: The build that wrote it. }
        schema_latest: { type: string, description: The newest migration the copy had taken. }
        schema_migrations: { type: integer }
        integrity: { type: string }
        secrets: { type: integer, description: How many sealed credentials the key is needed for. }
        key_fingerprint: { type: string }
        key_matches:
          type: [boolean, "null"]
          description: Whether this host holds the key that sealed it. Null when the backup does not say.
        key_included: { type: boolean, description: The encryption key is in the backup, which makes it a credential. }
        restorable: { type: boolean, description: Every check a restore would make passes, from what the manifest says. }
        restore_problem: { type: string, description: Why not, or a caveat when it is. }
        problem: { type: string, description: Something wrong with the backup itself. }

    Backups:
      type: object
      required: [items, directory, database_bytes, disk_free_bytes, schedule, remotes, running, staged_restore, last_restore, restarting]
      properties:
        items: { type: array, items: { $ref: "#/components/schemas/Backup" } }
        directory: { type: string, description: Where backups are kept, resolved. }
        database_bytes: { type: integer, format: int64, description: The live database's size, which is roughly what a backup costs. }
        disk_free_bytes:
          type: [integer, "null"]
          format: int64
          description: Room beside the backup directory, when the platform can say.
        key_fingerprint: { type: string, description: This host's encryption key. }
        schedule: { $ref: "#/components/schemas/BackupSchedule" }
        remotes:
          type: array
          items: { $ref: "#/components/schemas/BackupRemote" }
          description: >-
            Every destination `backup.remotes` configures and what became of it.
            Empty is the default: nothing leaves the host until somebody says where
            it goes.
        running: { type: boolean, description: A backup is being taken right now. }
        staged_restore:
          oneOf:
            - $ref: "#/components/schemas/StagedRestore"
            - type: "null"
        last_restore:
          oneOf:
            - $ref: "#/components/schemas/RestoreOutcome"
            - type: "null"
        restarting: { type: boolean, description: This process has been asked to stop, so wait for the next one. }

    BackupRemote:
      type: object
      required: [name, where, endpoint, encrypted, keep, disabled, source, path_style, shadowed, uploading, copies, bytes, listed_at, last_upload_at]
      properties:
        name: { type: string, description: What this destination is called, and what the API addresses it by. }
        source:
          type: string
          enum: [file, database]
          description: >-
            Where this destination is described: `file` for zoomies.yaml and the
            environment, `database` for one added on the Backups page. Only the
            stored ones can be edited over the API.
        id: { type: string, description: The stored destination's row id; absent for one the file describes. }
        region: { type: string }
        bucket: { type: string }
        prefix: { type: string }
        access_key_id: { type: string, description: The credential's id. The secret beside it is sealed and never served. }
        path_style:
          type: [boolean, "null"]
          description: Null asks for the style to be chosen from the endpoint.
        shadowed:
          type: boolean
          description: >-
            A stored destination the file overrides by name. Nothing is sent to
            it; it is listed so that a row which quietly does nothing is visible
            rather than mysterious.
        problem:
          type: string
          description: >-
            Why this destination cannot be used at all — almost always that this
            instance's encryption key does not open its stored secrets.
        has_secret_key: { type: boolean, description: A secret key is stored for this destination. }
        where: { type: string, description: The bucket and prefix. }
        endpoint: { type: string, description: The S3-compatible service it talks to. }
        encrypted: { type: boolean, description: The archive is sealed with a passphrase before it leaves this host. }
        keep: { type: integer, description: How many copies this remote holds; 0 keeps every one. }
        disabled: { type: boolean, description: Configured and switched off, shown rather than hidden. }
        uploading: { type: boolean, description: Something is being sent right now. }
        copies: { type: integer, description: What the last listing found. }
        bytes: { type: integer, format: int64 }
        listed_at: { type: [string, "null"], format: date-time }
        last_upload_at: { type: [string, "null"], format: date-time }
        last_upload_id: { type: string }
        last_error: { type: string, description: Why the last attempt did not work, in the service's own words. }

    BackupRemoteInput:
      type: object
      description: >-
        A destination to store or change. Every field is optional on a PATCH, so
        a body carries only what somebody actually changed.
      properties:
        name: { type: string, description: Lower-case letters, digits and dashes. }
        endpoint: { type: string, description: The service's URL; its scheme decides whether the connection is encrypted. }
        region: { type: string, description: What requests are signed for. Empty is us-east-1. }
        bucket: { type: string }
        prefix: { type: string, description: The key prefix, so one bucket can hold several fleets. }
        access_key_id: { type: string }
        secret_access_key:
          type: string
          format: password
          description: Sealed with the instance key and never served back. An empty string clears it.
        passphrase:
          type: string
          format: password
          description: >-
            Seals the archive before it is uploaded. Sealed at rest and never served
            back; an empty string clears it, which sends the plain archive.
        path_style: { type: [boolean, "null"] }
        keep: { type: integer, description: How many copies this destination holds; 0 keeps every one. }
        enabled: { type: boolean }

    RemoteBackupCopy:
      type: object
      required: [remote, id, key, bytes, stored_at, taken_at, encrypted]
      properties:
        remote: { type: string }
        id: { type: string, description: The backup's own id, read back out of the object key. }
        key: { type: string, description: The object's full key, which is what finds it with any other tool. }
        bytes: { type: integer, format: int64, description: The archive's size, which is the compressed database rather than the database. }
        stored_at: { type: string, format: date-time, description: When the object was written, from the service. }
        taken_at: { type: string, format: date-time, description: When the backup was taken, from its id. }
        encrypted: { type: boolean }

    RemoteBackupCopies:
      type: object
      required: [remote, items, bytes]
      properties:
        remote: { $ref: "#/components/schemas/BackupRemote" }
        items: { type: array, items: { $ref: "#/components/schemas/RemoteBackupCopy" } }
        bytes: { type: integer, format: int64, description: What the copies add up to. }

    RemoteBackupCheck:
      type: object
      required: [name, where, ok, checked_at]
      properties:
        name: { type: string }
        where: { type: string }
        ok: { type: boolean }
        checked_at: { type: string, format: date-time }
        error: { type: string, description: The service's own refusal, worded so that a wrong secret, a missing bucket and a drifted clock read differently. }

    BackupShipment:
      type: object
      required: [sent]
      properties:
        sent: { type: array, items: { $ref: "#/components/schemas/RemoteBackupCopy" } }
        error: { type: string, description: What stopped one destination, when the others still went. }

    BackupPruning:
      type: object
      required: [keep, removed, remotes]
      description: >-
        What applying retention removed. It is reported per destination rather
        than as one total because the numbers disagree on purpose: this host keeps
        `backup.keep` copies and each bucket keeps its own.
      properties:
        keep: { type: integer, description: "`backup.keep` as the pass read it; 0 keeps every copy and removes nothing from this host." }
        removed: { type: array, items: { type: string }, description: The backups deleted from the backup directory. }
        error: { type: string, description: Why the directory could not be pruned. }
        remotes: { type: array, items: { $ref: "#/components/schemas/RemotePruning" } }

    RemotePruning:
      type: object
      required: [name, keep, removed]
      properties:
        name: { type: string }
        keep: { type: integer, description: This destination's own retention; 0 keeps every copy. }
        removed: { type: array, items: { type: string } }
        error: { type: string, description: The service's own refusal, so a bucket that would not answer reads differently from one that had nothing to remove. }

    BackupSchedule:
      type: object
      required: [enabled, interval, keep, next_due_at, last_scheduled_at]
      properties:
        enabled: { type: boolean }
        interval: { $ref: "#/components/schemas/Duration" }
        keep: { type: integer }
        next_due_at: { type: [string, "null"], format: date-time }
        last_scheduled_at: { type: [string, "null"], format: date-time }
        last_scheduled_id: { type: string }
        last_error: { type: string, description: Why the last scheduled backup failed, when it did. }

    BackupVerification:
      type: object
      required: [checked_at, ok, integrity, digest_known, digest_matches, schema_readable, migrations, problems]
      properties:
        checked_at: { type: string, format: date-time }
        ok: { type: boolean }
        integrity: { type: string, description: SQLite's own answer -- `ok`, or what it found. }
        digest_known: { type: boolean, description: The manifest recorded a digest to compare against. }
        digest_matches: { type: boolean }
        schema_readable: { type: boolean, description: This build can open it. }
        migrations: { type: integer }
        latest: { type: string }
        problems: { type: array, items: { type: string } }

    StagedRestore:
      type: object
      required: [backup_id, dir, requested_at, revoke_api_tokens, reset_agent_tokens]
      properties:
        backup_id: { type: string }
        dir: { type: string }
        taken_at: { type: string, format: date-time }
        requested_at: { type: string, format: date-time }
        requested_by: { type: string }
        revoke_api_tokens: { type: boolean }
        reset_agent_tokens: { type: boolean }

    RestoreOutcome:
      type: object
      required: [backup_id, attempted_at, ok]
      properties:
        backup_id: { type: string }
        attempted_at: { type: string, format: date-time }
        ok: { type: boolean }
        error: { type: string, description: "Why the restore did not finish. When it failed after the copy, the message says which database is in place and whether it is fenced." }
        report: { $ref: "#/components/schemas/RestoreReport" }

    RestoreReport:
      type: object
      required: [source, key_checked, invalidated, fenced]
      properties:
        source: { type: string }
        moved_aside: { type: string, description: Where the database that was there went. }
        moved_logs: { type: array, items: { type: string } }
        key_checked: { type: boolean }
        manifest_problem: { type: string }
        invalidated: { type: array, items: { type: string }, description: What the restore took away, one line each. }
        fenced: { type: string, description: The reason recorded on the fence. }

    Restarting:
      type: object
      required: [restarting, message]
      properties:
        restarting: { type: boolean }
        message: { type: string }

    SupportBundle:
      type: object
      required: [bundle_version, generated_at, instance, errors]
      properties:
        bundle_version:
          type: integer
          description: >-
            The shape's own number, so a reader given a bundle out of context knows what
            it is looking at. It moves when a section is removed or renamed, not when one
            is added.
        generated_at: { type: string, format: date-time }
        instance: { $ref: "#/components/schemas/BundleInstance" }
        config:
          type: object
          additionalProperties: true
          description: The effective configuration, the same key-by-key rendering /settings serves.
        findings:
          type: array
          description: The configuration validator's findings, the same list /settings carries.
          items: { $ref: "#/components/schemas/Problem" }
        problems:
          type: object
          description: Everything currently wrong, the same shape /problems serves.
          required: [ok, items]
          properties:
            ok: { type: boolean }
            items:
              type: array
              items: { $ref: "#/components/schemas/Problem" }
        stats: { $ref: "#/components/schemas/Stats" }
        installations:
          type: array
          items: { $ref: "#/components/schemas/Installation" }
        pools:
          type: array
          items: { $ref: "#/components/schemas/Pool" }
        hosts:
          type: array
          items: { $ref: "#/components/schemas/Host" }
        providers:
          type: array
          description: The providers this fleet rents from, the same shape /providers serves.
          items: { $ref: "#/components/schemas/Provider" }
        machines:
          type: array
          description: The machines it is renting, newest first and excluding the ones whose resource is confirmed gone.
          items: { $ref: "#/components/schemas/Machine" }
        runners:
          type: array
          items: { $ref: "#/components/schemas/Runner" }
        jobs:
          type: array
          description: >-
            The work in flight rather than the history. A bundle is taken because
            something is stuck, and finished jobs would be most of the bytes while
            answering none of it.
          items: { $ref: "#/components/schemas/Job" }
        explanations:
          type: array
          description: The controller's own answer for each unfinished job, the same one the drawer and the CLI render.
          items: { $ref: "#/components/schemas/JobExplanation" }
        scaling_events:
          type: array
          items: { $ref: "#/components/schemas/ScalingEvent" }
        logs: { $ref: "#/components/schemas/BundleLogs" }
        errors:
          type: array
          description: Why a section is missing. A bundle with nine sections and a named failure is worth more than a 500.
          items: { $ref: "#/components/schemas/BundleError" }
        truncated:
          type: array
          items: { $ref: "#/components/schemas/BundleTruncation" }

    BundleInstance:
      type: object
      description: What this process is and how it is doing -- the half of a bug report that is never in the fleet's own rows.
      properties:
        version: { type: string }
        commit: { type: string }
        build_date: { type: string }
        go: { type: string }
        os: { type: string }
        arch: { type: string }
        cpus: { type: integer }
        goroutines: { type: integer }
        heap_in_use_bytes: { type: integer, format: int64 }
        config_path: { type: string }
        database_path: { type: string }
        schema_applied: { type: integer }
        schema_latest: { type: string }
        event_subscribers: { type: integer }
        polling_only: { type: boolean }
        poller_enabled: { type: boolean }
        poller_last_poll_at: { type: string, format: date-time }
        loop_panics:
          type: array
          description: >-
            The one fact here that is always a bug in Zoomies. A loop that panicked was
            restarted and the fleet carried on, so nothing else in a bundle would show it.
          items:
            type: object
            properties:
              loop: { type: string }
              count: { type: integer }
              last: { type: string }
              at: { type: string, format: date-time }

    BundleLogs:
      type: object
      description: Where the logs are, rather than the logs.
      properties:
        note: { type: string, description: Why the bodies are not here. }
        runners:
          type: array
          items:
            type: object
            properties:
              runner_id: { type: string }
              name: { type: string }
              state: { $ref: "#/components/schemas/RunnerState" }
              pool_id: { type: string }
              download: { type: string, description: The route that fetches this runner's log. }

    BundleError:
      type: object
      required: [section, error]
      properties:
        section: { type: string }
        error: { type: string }

    BundleTruncation:
      type: object
      required: [section, reason]
      properties:
        section: { type: string }
        kept: { type: integer, description: How many rows survived, where the cap was a row count. }
        reason: { type: string }

    TimelineEntry:
      type: object
      properties:
        state: { $ref: "#/components/schemas/RunnerState" }
        stage:
          type: string
          description: >-
            A finer point within the state, when one was observed: the image was pulled,
            the container started, the runner registered with GitHub.
          enum: [image_pulling, container_started, registered]
        at: { type: string, format: date-time }
        duration_ms: { type: integer, format: int64, description: How long the runner stayed in this state. }
        message: { type: string }

    # --- jobs -------------------------------------------------------------
    Job:
      type: object
      properties:
        provisioning: { type: string, enum: ["", paused, deleted], description: "Operator demand control; empty means ready." }
        provision_now: { type: boolean, description: Expedite demand within pool priority and bypass scale-up delay. }
        cancel_requested_at:
          type: string
          format: date-time
          description: >-
            When an operator's cancellation of this job's workflow run was accepted by
            GitHub, absent when none was. GitHub's completion delivery still settles the
            conclusion and can be minutes behind, so until it arrives the job reads
            `queued` or `in_progress` while being neither: the queued half raises no
            demand and the running half has had its runner taken away. Once the job
            completes this is history and the conclusion says what happened.
        id: { type: string }
        github_job_id: { type: integer, format: int64 }
        github_run_id: { type: integer, format: int64 }
        repo: { type: string }
        workflow: { type: string }
        job_name: { type: string }
        labels: { type: array, items: { type: string } }
        state: { $ref: "#/components/schemas/JobState" }
        conclusion: { type: string, examples: [success, failure, cancelled, skipped] }
        installation_id:
          type: string
          description: >-
            The GitHub App installation covering this job's repository, resolved when the job
            was first recorded. Read-only. A pool only ever runs work in its own installation's
            target, so a pool whose labels fit is still not eligible unless this matches it.
            Empty when no installation here covers the repository.
        pool_id: { type: string }
        pool_name: { type: string }
        runner_id: { type: string }
        runner_name: { type: string }
        html_url: { type: string, description: The run on GitHub. }
        matched: { type: boolean, description: "False when no enabled pool claims this job's labels. On a job that is not queued this only says the job ran somewhere else." }
        eligible_at: { type: string, format: date-time, description: "When this fleet could first have acted on the job - an enabled pool claiming its labels. The start of the scheduling-latency interval, and deliberately not queued_at: the wait before anything could run the job is not this fleet's. Absent on a job nothing has claimed." }
        hosted: { type: boolean, description: "True when every label names GitHub's own runners or a hosted-runner vendor's, so a job no pool here claims is theirs to run rather than stuck." }
        head_branch: { type: string, description: The branch the run was for. }
        head_sha: { type: string }
        run_attempt: { type: integer, description: "1 for a first run; higher when the run was re-run." }
        run_number:
          type: integer
          format: int64
          description: >-
            GitHub's own sequential number for this workflow run - the "#1009" its Actions UI
            shows next to the workflow name, for cross-referencing the two. Zero until a
            workflow_run lookup backfills it, since the webhook that recorded the job never
            carries it.
        controller_version:
          type: string
          description: >-
            The controller version that claimed the job, stamped once and never rewritten,
            so jobs can be grouped by release. Absent on a job recorded before this field
            existed and on one no pool here claimed; neither is guessed at. Filter with
            `controller_version=unknown` to find them.
        controller_channel: { type: string, description: The install channel of that controller build. }
        agent_version: { type: string, description: The agent version the host reported when a runner on it took the job. }
        host_id: { type: string, description: The host the job's runner was on, as stamped when the runner took it. }
        peak_cpus:
          type: number
          description: >-
            The most CPU, in cores, the job's runner was measured using while the job ran on
            it -- the agent's usage samples, raised and never lowered. Absent when it was
            never measured: a job from before this was recorded, a backend that reports no
            usage, or a job too short to be sampled.
        peak_memory_mb:
          type: integer
          format: int64
          description: The most memory, in MB, the job's runner was measured using while the job ran. Absent when never measured.
        oom_killed:
          type: boolean
          description: >-
            True when the kernel killed the job's runner, or one of its steps (exit 137), for
            its memory limit. It is the fleet's failure rather than the workflow's, and the one
            `scheduler.history_sizing` corrects for: the next run of the job is placed for half
            as much memory again as this one's peak. Absent when false.
        steps:
          type: array
          description: >-
            The job's steps as GitHub last reported them. A completed job carries every
            step with its conclusion; a running one carries them mid-flight.
          items: { $ref: "#/components/schemas/JobStep" }
        failed_step:
          description: >-
            The step a completed job stopped at: the first that did not succeed, whether the
            job failed there or was cancelled there. Null when every step succeeded or while
            the job is still running. Worked out by the server so every client names the same step.
          oneOf:
            - $ref: "#/components/schemas/JobStep"
            - type: "null"
        runner_fault:
          type: string
          description: >-
            Set when the runner of this fleet that was executing the job stopped before
            GitHub reported the job over -- the fleet's own explanation of a failure GitHub
            records like any other. Empty when the runner did nothing wrong.
        fault_kind:
          $ref: "#/components/schemas/FaultKind"
        fault_domain:
          type: string
          enum: [fleet, workflow]
          description: >-
            Whose the failure is. `fleet` means this deployment is the reason the job went
            wrong; `workflow` means the job failed on its own merits and the fleet did its
            part. Empty on a job that did not fail. GitHub records both as "failure", which
            is the whole reason this field exists: the two need completely different people.
        fault_fix:
          type: string
          description: >-
            What to do about a fault of this kind, in the words of the person who has to do
            it. Empty when there is nothing to do, which is different from not knowing.
        queued_at: { type: string, format: date-time }
        started_at: { type: [string, "null"], format: date-time }
        completed_at: { type: [string, "null"], format: date-time }
        queue_wait_ms: { type: integer, format: int64 }
        duration_ms: { type: integer, format: int64 }

    WorkflowRun:
      type: object
      description: >-
        One workflow run as this fleet has seen it: the jobs GitHub reported under it,
        summed up over the latest attempt of each job. Derived from the jobs, never
        stored, so it cannot go stale on its own.
      properties:
        repo: { type: string }
        workflow: { type: string }
        github_run_id: { type: integer, format: int64 }
        run_number:
          type: integer
          format: int64
          description: >-
            GitHub's own sequential number for the run - the "#1009" its Actions UI shows.
            Zero until a job of the run has had it backfilled.
        run_attempt: { type: integer, description: The highest attempt any job of the run reported. }
        head_branch: { type: string }
        head_sha: { type: string }
        installation_id: { type: string }
        html_url: { type: string, description: The run's page on GitHub. }
        state:
          allOf:
            - $ref: "#/components/schemas/JobState"
          description: >-
            The run's own state: in_progress while any job is, queued while any job waits
            for a runner, waiting while any is held for a review, completed once every job is.
        conclusion:
          type: string
          description: >-
            The run's conclusion once it has completed, worst outcome first: a failure on
            either side, then cancelled, then action_required, then success. Empty until then.
        managed: { type: boolean, description: Whether this fleet has a hand in any job of the run. }
        hosted: { type: boolean, description: Whether every job's labels name runners somebody else operates. }
        cancelling: { type: boolean, description: Whether a cancellation of the run has been accepted by GitHub and not yet confirmed. }
        jobs: { $ref: "#/components/schemas/RunJobCounts" }
        queued_at: { type: string, format: date-time, description: When the first job was queued. }
        started_at: { type: [string, "null"], format: date-time, description: When the first job started. }
        completed_at: { type: [string, "null"], format: date-time, description: When the last job finished; null until every job has. }
        queue_wait_ms: { type: integer, format: int64 }
        duration_ms: { type: integer, format: int64, description: From the first job starting to the last finishing. }

    RunJobCounts:
      type: object
      description: >-
        How a run's jobs are getting on, counted over the latest attempt of each.
        `failed` counts failures on either side, so `faulted` -- the ones this fleet
        caused -- is always part of it.
      properties:
        total: { type: integer }
        waiting: { type: integer }
        queued: { type: integer }
        in_progress: { type: integer }
        completed: { type: integer }
        succeeded: { type: integer }
        failed: { type: integer }
        cancelled: { type: integer }
        skipped: { type: integer }
        faulted: { type: integer }
        unmatched: { type: integer, description: Queued jobs no enabled pool claims and nobody else is about to run. }
        expedited: { type: integer, description: Queued jobs an operator has asked to run now. Part of `queued`, not beside it. }
        paused: { type: integer, description: Queued jobs whose provisioning demand an operator has paused. Part of `queued`. }
        removed: { type: integer, description: Queued jobs an operator removed from the queue, which a run-level action leaves alone. Part of `queued`. }

    JobSummary:
      type: object
      description: >-
        A job without its steps, which is what `GET /jobs?include_steps=false` returns.
        `pool` is the pool's name, `host` the ID of the host that ran it and `runner` the
        runner's name.
      required: [id, repo, workflow, job_name, state, queued_at, queue_wait_ms, duration_ms]
      properties:
        id: { type: string }
        repo: { type: string }
        workflow: { type: string }
        job_name: { type: string }
        state: { $ref: "#/components/schemas/JobState" }
        conclusion: { type: string }
        fault_domain: { type: string, enum: [fleet, workflow], description: Whose the failure is; absent on a job that did not fail. }
        queued_at: { type: string, format: date-time }
        started_at: { type: [string, "null"], format: date-time }
        completed_at: { type: [string, "null"], format: date-time }
        queue_wait_ms: { type: integer, format: int64 }
        duration_ms: { type: integer, format: int64 }
        pool: { type: string }
        host: { type: string }
        runner: { type: string }
        controller_version: { type: string, description: The controller build that claimed the job. Absent when it was never stamped. }
        controller_channel: { type: string }
        agent_version: { type: string, description: The agent version the host reported when the job was assigned to it. }
        peak_memory_mb: { type: integer, format: int64, description: "The most memory, in MB, the job was measured using. Absent when never measured." }
        oom_killed: { type: boolean, description: True when the kernel killed the job's runner or one of its steps for memory. Absent when false. }

    JobPercentiles:
      type: object
      required: [samples, p50_ms, p95_ms]
      properties:
        samples: { type: integer, description: The jobs the figures were computed from. }
        p50_ms: { type: [integer, "null"], format: int64, description: Null when no job could be measured; zero would read as an answer. }
        p95_ms: { type: [integer, "null"], format: int64 }

    JobStatsGroup:
      type: object
      required: [keys, count, succeeded, failed, cancelled, fleet_failed, fleet_failed_by_kind, fleet_failure_rate, duration, queue_wait, startup, peak_cpus, peak_memory_mb, oom_killed]
      properties:
        keys:
          type: object
          additionalProperties: { type: string }
          description: Each `group_by` key and this group's value. Empty when nothing was grouped by.
        count: { type: integer, description: Completed jobs in the group. }
        succeeded: { type: integer }
        failed: { type: integer, description: Failures on either side, so `fleet_failed` is part of it. }
        cancelled: { type: integer, description: Cancelled and skipped jobs. }
        fleet_failed: { type: integer, description: Jobs lost to this fleet rather than to the workflow. }
        fleet_failed_by_kind:
          type: object
          additionalProperties: { type: integer }
          description: "`fleet_failed` split by fault category. `unclassified` is a failure recorded before categories existed."
        fleet_failure_rate: { type: number, description: "`fleet_failed` over `count`, from 0 to 1." }
        duration: { $ref: "#/components/schemas/JobPercentiles" }
        queue_wait: { $ref: "#/components/schemas/JobPercentiles" }
        startup: { $ref: "#/components/schemas/JobPercentiles" }
        peak_cpus: { type: [number, "null"], description: "The most CPU, in cores, any job in the group was measured using. Null when none was measured." }
        peak_memory_mb: { type: [integer, "null"], format: int64, description: "The most memory, in MB, any job in the group was measured using. Null when none was measured." }
        oom_killed: { type: integer, description: Jobs in the group whose runner, or one of its steps, the kernel killed for memory. }

    JobStats:
      type: object
      required: [since, until, group_by, duration_excludes, notes, truncated, groups]
      properties:
        since: { type: string, format: date-time, description: Start of the window, included. }
        until: { type: string, format: date-time, description: End of the window, not included. }
        group_by: { type: array, items: { type: string } }
        duration_excludes:
          type: array
          items: { type: string }
          description: The conclusions left out of every duration percentile.
        notes: { type: array, items: { type: string }, description: How to read the figures, in words. }
        truncated: { type: boolean, description: True when more than 500 groups matched and the rest were left out. }
        groups: { type: array, items: { $ref: "#/components/schemas/JobStatsGroup" } }

    JobStep:
      type: object
      properties:
        number: { type: integer }
        name: { type: string }
        status: { type: string, examples: [queued, in_progress, completed] }
        conclusion: { type: string, examples: [success, failure, cancelled, skipped] }
        started_at: { type: [string, "null"], format: date-time }
        completed_at: { type: [string, "null"], format: date-time }

    FaultKind:
      type: string
      description: >-
        Why the fleet, rather than the workflow, is the reason something went wrong.

        Every kind exists because something different is done about it, and the
        `fault_fix` beside it says what. `out_of_memory` is a limit to raise;
        `host_lost` is a machine or an agent to look at; `image` is a tag or a registry;
        `registration` is the GitHub App's permissions; `backend` is the container daemon
        on the host, which is the "cannot start the runner container" case; `backend_busy`
        is that daemon answering too slowly rather than not at all, which is a host carrying
        more work than it can keep up with and is fixed on the pool's limits or the host's
        capacity; `config` is a
        setting the runner itself refused, and until it is edited every runner in the pool
        will do the same thing; `out_of_disk` is a full host; `removed` is an operator who
        meant it, and needs no fixing. `runner_exited` is the unclassified case on purpose
        -- a runner that stopped for a reason nobody observed, including one reported by an
        agent newer than Zoomies. Guessing a kind would send somebody to fix
        something that is not broken.

        Empty means the fleet has nothing to confess.
      enum: [host_lost, out_of_memory, out_of_disk, removed, image, registration, backend, backend_busy, container_conflict, config, runner_exited]

    JobEventKind:
      type: string
      description: >-
        What happened. `runner_lost` is the one entry GitHub cannot produce: the runner
        stopped under the job, and GitHub will report an ordinary failure. `waiting` and
        `approved` bracket a deployment review: the time between them is GitHub's, and
        the queue wait starts at `approved`. `runner_returned` withdraws a `runner_lost`:
        the host was silent long enough to be given up on, came back with the runner
        still executing this job, and the job is being left to finish.
        `runner_start_failed` is the failure that touches no job: a runner this pool
        started died before it could take one, so the job is still queued and the next
        runner may run it -- said here because a pool that cannot start a container
        otherwise looks exactly like a pool that is merely busy. `oom_killed` is the kernel
        killing the job's runner, or one of its steps, for its memory limit -- which can be
        recorded after `completed`, because a runner whose step was killed finishes the job
        and reports the kill only when it exits.
      enum: [queued, waiting, approved, claimed, unmatched, started, completed, runner_lost, runner_returned, cancel_requested, runner_start_failed, rerun_requested, oom_killed]

    JobEvent:
      type: object
      properties:
        id: { type: string }
        job_id: { type: string }
        kind: { $ref: "#/components/schemas/JobEventKind" }
        source:
          type: string
          description: >-
            Who observed it. A timeline that is all `poller` is a controller no webhook reaches.
            `recovery` marks a re-run the fleet decided on rather than a person.
          enum: [webhook, poller, agent, controller, recovery]
        message: { type: string, description: One sentence, written for an operator. }
        runner_id: { type: string }
        runner_name: { type: string }
        at: { type: string, format: date-time }

    # --- hosts ------------------------------------------------------------
    HostUsage:
      type: object
      properties:
        cpu_percent: { type: number, minimum: 0, maximum: 100, description: Whole-host CPU occupied between samples, including I/O wait. Absent when unmeasured. }
        memory_available_mb: { type: integer, format: int64, minimum: 0, description: Whole-host available memory including reclaimable cache. Zero is a measured full host. }
        sampled_at: { type: string, format: date-time, description: Controller receipt time. Agent-provided timestamps are ignored. }
        cpu_high_since: { type: string, format: date-time, description: Beginning of sustained CPU pressure, owned by the controller. }
        cpu_held: { type: boolean, description: Admission held after sustained CPU pressure. Running jobs continue. Owned by the controller. }
        lent_cpu_percent: { type: number, minimum: 0, maximum: 100, description: The part of cpu_percent runners were using out of CPU elastic CPU lent them. The admission hold and the throttle judge CPU without it. Owned by the controller. }
        load_average_1m:
          type: number
          minimum: 0
          description: >-
            The kernel's one-minute load average for the whole machine, as the agent read it
            from /proc/loadavg. Absent when unmeasured. Judged against the host's CPU count:
            a load of at least twice the CPUs is what steps the throttle up, because a
            runnable queue that deep is a machine that has stopped keeping up even when the
            CPU figure saturates at 100.
    HostSample:
      type: object
      description: One host at one minute. Absent measurements are gaps, never zero.
      required: [host_id, at, capacity, active_runners]
      properties:
        host_id: { type: string }
        at: { type: string, format: date-time }
        capacity: { type: integer, description: The slots the host was taking that minute -- its configured capacity stepped down by any throttle. }
        active_runners: { type: integer }
        cpu_percent: { type: number, minimum: 0, maximum: 100, description: Whole-host CPU occupied, as the agent measured it. Absent when unmeasured or stale. }
        load_average_1m: { type: number, minimum: 0, description: The kernel's one-minute load average. Absent when unmeasured or stale. }
        cpus: { type: integer, description: The machine's CPUs, carried on every row so the chart can draw load against size. }
        memory_mb: { type: integer, format: int64 }
        memory_available_mb: { type: integer, format: int64, minimum: 0, description: Whole-host available memory including reclaimable cache. Absent when unmeasured or stale. }
        allocatable_cpus: { type: number, description: The machine less its reserve, with the floors applied. }
        allocatable_memory_mb: { type: integer, format: int64 }
        reserved_cpus: { type: number, description: What the live runners had promised away, from the last scheduling pass. Absent before one has run. }
        reserved_memory_mb: { type: integer, format: int64 }
        disk_total_mb: { type: integer, format: int64 }
        disk_free_mb: { type: integer, format: int64 }
    HostThrottle:
      type: object
      description: >-
        The rung the controller has stepped a host down to after sustained pressure. The
        controller owns every field: a heartbeat carries the measurements and never the
        decision, and an agent cannot set or clear one. Absent from a host on no rung.
      properties:
        level:
          type: integer
          minimum: 1
          maximum: 3
          description: >-
            The rung, 1 to 3. Each takes a quarter of the host's slots (to 75%, 50%, 25% of
            capacity, never below one slot) and lowers the CPU quota of every runner here that
            has one, down to half. Owned by the controller.
        since: { type: string, format: date-time, description: When this episode began, the first step up from none. Owned by the controller. }
        changed_at: { type: string, format: date-time, description: The last step in either direction, which the next step up is paced from. Owned by the controller. }
        calm_since: { type: string, format: date-time, description: The start of the calm streak the next step down waits on. Absent while the host is not calm. Owned by the controller. }
        reason: { type: string, description: Which measurement took the last step up, as one sentence. Owned by the controller. }
    RuntimeIncident:
      type: object
      description: >-
        A host's container-runtime cooldown as its agent last reported it: the runtime failed,
        new starts are held, and one recovery attempt is due. Kept on the host row, so it
        survives a controller restart; cleared by the first heartbeat that reports none.
      required: [failures, kind, retry_at, since, observed_at]
      properties:
        failures: { type: integer, minimum: 1, description: Runtime failures in a row. The agent counts no higher than five. }
        kind: { type: string, enum: [unavailable, timeout], description: "unavailable: the daemon could not be reached; timeout: it was reached and did not answer in time." }
        error: { type: string, description: The last failure as the backend worded it, which names the socket and how to start it. }
        retry_at: { type: string, format: date-time, description: When the agent's one recovery attempt is due, on the controller's clock. }
        since: { type: string, format: date-time, description: When the controller first heard of this episode. }
        observed_at: { type: string, format: date-time, description: When the controller last heard anything new about it. }
    ImagePullIncident:
      type: object
      description: >-
        The last runner start or prewarm on a host that failed because its pool's image could
        not be made ready. Cleared by the next start or prewarm of the same pool that succeeds
        on the host.
      required: [pool_id, pool, image, registry, source, since, observed_at]
      properties:
        pool_id: { type: string }
        pool: { type: string, description: The pool's name when the failure was recorded. }
        image: { type: string }
        registry: { type: string, description: "The registry the image is pulled from: docker.io for a bare name, otherwise the reference's host, with its port.", examples: [ghcr.io] }
        source: { type: string, enum: [start, prewarm], description: Which of the agent's results said so. }
        error: { type: string }
        since: { type: string, format: date-time, description: When this pool's image was first recorded failing here. }
        observed_at: { type: string, format: date-time, description: When the latest failure was recorded. }
    BackendInfo:
      type: object
      properties:
        kind: { $ref: "#/components/schemas/BackendKind" }
        freshness:
          type: object
          required: [state, desired_commit, published_commit, snapshot_id, checked_at]
          properties:
            state: { type: string, enum: [awaiting_merge, unavailable, stale, ready] }
            desired_commit: { type: string }
            published_commit: { type: string }
            snapshot_id: { type: string }
            checked_at: { type: string, format: date-time }
            failure: { type: string }
        setup_state: { type: string, enum: [pending, awaiting_merge] }
        setup_pr_url: { type: string }
        available: { type: boolean }
        version: { type: string }
        rootless: { type: boolean }
        endpoint: { type: string }
        detail: { type: string, description: When unavailable, what is wrong and how to fix it. }
        supports_dind: { type: boolean }
        host_socket_path: { type: string, description: Where the host daemon's socket lives, for pools that opt into host-socket mode. }
        limits:
          type: object
          description: >-
            What the daemon said it can enforce. A runner is given a default limit only on a
            field the daemon can apply, and host.limits_unenforceable names the fields it
            cannot; `known` is false from an agent too old to have asked, which defaults nothing.
          properties:
            known: { type: boolean }
            cpu: { type: boolean, description: A CPU quota. A daemon that cannot apply one refuses the container. }
            memory: { type: boolean, description: A memory limit. A daemon that cannot apply one starts the container without it. }
            pids: { type: boolean, description: A pids limit. A daemon that cannot apply one ignores it. }
        shared_folder:
          type: string
          description: >-
            What is wrong with the host's shared folder, the one runners' caches are bound from:
            a containerised agent whose container does not mount it from the host, which keeps
            no tool cache there. Empty when nothing is. See host.shared_folder_unmounted.

    Host:
      type: object
      properties:
        usage: { $ref: "#/components/schemas/HostUsage" }
        usage_fresh: { type: boolean, description: Usage is less than 90 seconds old. Unknown or stale readings retain reservation-based placement. }
        admission_reason: { type: string, description: Why current host pressure is holding new runner starts. Empty when no pressure hold applies. }
        throttle:
          allOf:
            - $ref: "#/components/schemas/HostThrottle"
          description: The throttle the controller has this host on. Absent when it is on none.
        runtime_recovering:
          allOf:
            - $ref: "#/components/schemas/RuntimeIncident"
          description: The container-runtime cooldown the agent last reported. Absent when there is none.
        runtime_reason:
          type: string
          description: >-
            The host card's sentence for the runtime cooldown, without its times: the card
            renders the retry and the report's age against the viewer's clock. Absent when
            there is none.
          examples:
            - "Runtime recovering: third failure in a row, the container runtime could not be reached. New starts here are held until one recovery attempt; running jobs continue."
        image_pull_failed:
          allOf:
            - $ref: "#/components/schemas/ImagePullIncident"
          description: The last start or prewarm here whose image could not be made ready. Absent when there is none.
        throttle_reason:
          type: string
          description: >-
            The operator sentence for the throttle: what it took, why, what it is doing to the
            jobs already running, and how it ends. Empty when the host is not throttled.
          examples:
            - "throttled to 2 of 4 slots (step 2 of 3) after sustained pressure: the 1-minute load average is 30.0, at least twice the host's 8 CPUs; running jobs continue, the 1 runner with a CPU limit at 50% of it, and the throttle lifts one step after 5m of calm"
        effective_capacity:
          type: integer
          description: >-
            The slots this host takes right now: capacity stepped down by the throttle, and
            capacity itself when there is none. `free` is measured against it, so a throttled
            host never advertises a slot the next pass would refuse.
        unlimited_runners:
          type: integer
          description: >-
            How many of the live runners here were created with no CPU quota -- a pool with
            none and default limits off, a process pool, a daemon that cannot apply one, or a
            runner from before allocations were recorded. Omitted when zero. They are the
            runners a CPU hold can mean something about, since a throttle cannot slow them.
        id: { type: string }
        name: { type: string }
        address: { type: string }
        connection: { type: string, enum: [direct, tailcat], description: Connection observed by the controller at enrolment or the latest heartbeat. }
        embedded: { type: boolean, description: True for the agent running inside the controller process. }
        capacity: { type: integer }
        active_runners: { type: integer }
        free: { type: integer }
        backends: { type: array, items: { type: string } }
        backend_info: { type: array, items: { $ref: "#/components/schemas/BackendInfo" } }
        features:
          type: array
          items: { type: string }
          description: >-
            What the agent says it can do beyond running a backend, re-read from every
            heartbeat. `elastic-cpu` means it can move a live runner's CPU quota.
        elastic_cpu:
          type: boolean
          description: >-
            Whether this host honours an elastic pool: true when its agent advertises
            `elastic-cpu`. A runner of such a pool placed where this is false is held at its
            guaranteed share, and the host's card says so.
        labels: { type: object, additionalProperties: { type: string } }
        os: { type: string, description: The kernel, as Go names it - linux, darwin, windows. }
        distro: { type: string, description: The distribution, e.g. ubuntu. Empty when the host has not said. }
        os_version: { type: string, description: The distribution's release, e.g. "24.04". }
        arch: { type: string }
        cpus: { type: integer, description: How much machine this host is. An agent in a container sees its cgroup's share, but a container runner runs beside it rather than inside that cgroup, so the daemon's larger view of the machine is the one reported. }
        memory_mb: { type: integer, format: int64 }
        disk_total_mb: { type: integer, format: int64, description: The filesystem holding the agent's work directory, where a runner's checkout and caches land. Zero means the agent did not measure it, which is not a full disk. }
        disk_free_mb: { type: integer, format: int64, description: What a runner may write to, which is less than what is unused by the reserve the filesystem keeps for root. }
        reserve_cpus: { type: integer, description: What the operator holds back from placement for the machine's own sake. Set through PATCH /hosts; a heartbeat never writes it. }
        reserve_memory_mb: { type: integer, format: int64 }
        reserve_disk_mb: { type: integer, format: int64 }
        allocatable_cpus:
          type: number
          description: >-
            The machine less its reserve: what the scheduler may place onto. The documented
            floors under the reserve -- half a core or a twentieth of the machine, whichever is
            larger, 512 MB of memory and 2 GB of disk -- are applied here, so what is shown is
            what is used. The CPU floor is what keeps the daemon, the agent and the kernel a
            core the runners' quotas can never take.
        allocatable_memory_mb: { type: integer, format: int64 }
        allocatable_disk_mb: { type: integer, format: int64 }
        reserved_cpus:
          type: number
          description: >-
            What the live runners already on this host have promised away, as of the last
            scheduling pass and from the snapshot that pass decided on. Disk is absent on
            purpose: free disk already contains what those runners have written, so charging
            their reservations too would count the same bytes twice.
        reserved_memory_mb: { type: integer, format: int64 }
        reserved_known:
          type: boolean
          description: >-
            False until a pass has run, because zero would read as an idle machine rather
            than as a question nobody has answered yet.
        resources_known:
          type: boolean
          description: >-
            Whether this host has reported what machine it is at all. An agent too old to say
            is placed by slots alone, which is what keeps an upgrade from emptying a fleet.
        platform: { $ref: "#/components/schemas/Platform" }
        platform_label: { type: string, examples: ["Ubuntu 24.04, arm64"] }
        canonical_name:
          type: string
          description: The name this machine would be given today, for a host called something that says nothing.
          examples: [zoomies-16vcpu-32gb-ubuntu-2404-build01]
        version: { type: string }
        version_channel: { type: string, examples: ["v1.0.0", "dev"], description: The published image and binary tag carrying this agent build. }
        cordoned: { type: boolean }
        protocol_version:
          type: integer
          description: >-
            The agent protocol this host reported speaking. Absent from an agent old enough
            not to send one, which is not the same as incompatible -- it is the one case the
            controller cannot judge.
        incompatible:
          type: boolean
          description: >-
            Whether this host's agent speaks a protocol the controller does not. An
            incompatible host is excluded from placement exactly as a cordoned one is, and
            nothing else: its runners keep working and are drained as normal. Refusing its
            heartbeat instead would restart every agent in the fleet at once.
        incompatible_reason: { type: string, description: What to do about it, naming both protocol versions. }
        version_skew:
          type: string
          enum: [behind, ahead, differs]
          description: >-
            How this host's release stands to the controller's, absent when they match.
            `differs` is the honest answer for a pair the controller cannot order -- a
            development build, a fork's tag -- because a wrong order would send an operator
            to upgrade the wrong side. Two builds of one tag are the same release and are
            not skew.
        upgrade_command:
          type: string
          description: >-
            Copyable install.sh --upgrade command for an older or different remote agent,
            targeting the controller's published release or dev channel. Absent for embedded,
            matching or newer agents, and for unpublished controller builds. Contains no credentials.
        upgrade_version:
          type: string
          description: Controller build the upgrade is intended to match.
        upgrade_note:
          type: string
          description: What the command does, or why no safe published command can be offered.
        healthy: { type: boolean }
        last_heartbeat: { type: string, format: date-time }
        created_at: { type: string, format: date-time }

    JoinToken:
      type: object
      properties:
        id: { type: string }
        prefix: { type: string }
        created_by: { type: string }
        capacity: { type: integer }
        labels: { type: object, additionalProperties: { type: string } }
        created_at: { type: string, format: date-time }
        expires_at: { type: string, format: date-time }
        used_at: { type: [string, "null"], format: date-time }
        used_by_id: { type: string }
        usable: { type: boolean }

    # --- providers and machines -------------------------------------------
    ProviderKindName:
      type: string
      description: Which infrastructure a provider rents from. It is CHECKed in the schema, so a kind this build cannot speak cannot be stored.
      enum: [proxmox, fake]
    MachineState:
      type: string
      description: >-
        A machine's life, from a row that names nothing to a host that runs jobs. Deleted
        is the only terminal one: failed and quarantined still need attention, and a
        failed machine may still have a resource behind it.
      enum: [planned, creating, starting, bootstrapping, enrolling, ready, draining, deleting, deleted, failed, quarantined]

    Provider:
      type: object
      required: [id, kind, name, credentials_configured, enabled, paused, machines, owned]
      properties:
        id: { type: string, examples: [prv_k3f9qz2mx7ab] }
        kind: { $ref: "#/components/schemas/ProviderKindName" }
        name: { type: string, examples: [proxmox-lab] }
        endpoint:
          type: string
          description: Where Zoomies reaches the provider. Not a secret - it is the address an operator typed - and showing it is how somebody tells two clusters apart on a page listing both.
          examples: ["https://pve.example.com:8006"]
        insecure_skip_verify: { type: boolean, description: Certificate verification is off for this provider, which the validator warns about rather than refusing. }
        connection:
          type: string
          enum: [direct, tailcat]
          description: >-
            How the controller reaches the endpoint: over the network, or through a
            `zoomies gateway` running beside the provider, for a hypervisor on a home
            network with no address the controller can route to. The gateway's address
            is sealed on the row and never returned, for the credential's reason.
        settings:
          type: object
          additionalProperties: { type: string }
          description: The non-secret answers to this driver's own settings, keyed as GET /providers/kinds describes them.
        credentials_configured:
          type: boolean
          description: >-
            Whether a credential is sealed in the row. The value itself never leaves the
            controller and has no field here: an audit row and a screenshot both outlive
            the person who took them.
        machine_labels: { type: object, additionalProperties: { type: string } }
        machine_capacity: { type: integer, description: How many runners one of this provider's machines may run at once. }
        machine_backend: { $ref: "#/components/schemas/BackendKind" }
        machine_platform: { $ref: "#/components/schemas/Platform" }
        machine_cpus: { type: number }
        machine_memory_mb: { type: integer, format: int64 }
        machine_disk_mb: { type: integer, format: int64 }
        pool_selector:
          type: object
          additionalProperties: { type: string }
          description: Which pools this provider may buy for. Empty means every pool.
        max_machines:
          type: integer
          description: >-
            The ceiling on machines this provider may own at once. Zero rents nothing,
            exactly as a pool's max_runners of zero runs nothing.
        max_creates_in_flight: { type: integer, description: How many machines may be being built at once. }
        idle_timeout_ms: { type: integer, format: int64, description: How long a machine may sit with nothing to do before it is drained. }
        cost_per_machine_hour: { type: number }
        enabled: { type: boolean }
        paused: { type: boolean, description: The operator's kill switch. It blocks new machines only. }
        paused_reason: { type: string }
        paused_until: { type: string, format: date-time, description: The breaker's own pause, which never un-presses the operator's. }
        held:
          type: string
          description: >-
            Why no new machine may be bought right now, in one sentence, or absent when one
            may. Computed rather than stored because it answers for the fence, the
            configuration and the row at once.
        consecutive_failures: { type: integer }
        last_check_at: { type: string, format: date-time }
        last_check_error: { type: string, description: The worst thing the last preflight found, in one sentence. }
        last_sweep_at: { type: string, format: date-time, description: When this provider was last asked for everything it believes it is running. }
        machines:
          type: object
          additionalProperties: { type: integer }
          description: How many machines this provider has, by state.
        owned:
          type: integer
          description: How many still believe they hold a resource, which is the number the ceiling and the bill are both counted in.
        created_at: { type: string, format: date-time }
        updated_at: { type: string, format: date-time }

    ProviderInput:
      type: object
      description: >-
        Creating and editing a provider take the same body. On a PATCH every field is
        optional and independent; what is not named is left alone.
      properties:
        kind: { $ref: "#/components/schemas/ProviderKindName" }
        name: { type: string }
        endpoint: { type: string }
        ca_pem: { type: string, description: The certificate to trust for this endpoint, instead of turning verification off. }
        insecure_skip_verify: { type: boolean }
        connection:
          type: string
          enum: [direct, tailcat]
          description: >-
            Direct, or through a `zoomies gateway` beside the provider. Choosing direct on a
            provider that had a private connection clears its stored address.
        tailcat_address:
          type: string
          description: >-
            The address `zoomies gateway` printed. Sealed with the instance key and never
            returned; an empty string on a PATCH leaves the stored one alone. Giving one
            without naming a connection means tailcat.
        settings: { type: object, additionalProperties: { type: string } }
        credential:
          type: string
          description: >-
            Sealed with the instance key and never returned. An empty string leaves the
            stored credential alone, so a form with a blank password box does not erase it.
        machine_labels: { type: object, additionalProperties: { type: string } }
        machine_capacity: { type: integer, minimum: 1, default: 2 }
        machine_backend: { $ref: "#/components/schemas/BackendKind" }
        machine_platform: { $ref: "#/components/schemas/Platform" }
        machine_cpus: { type: number, minimum: 0 }
        machine_memory_mb: { type: integer, format: int64, minimum: 0 }
        machine_disk_mb: { type: integer, format: int64, minimum: 0 }
        pool_selector: { type: object, additionalProperties: { type: string } }
        max_machines: { type: integer, minimum: 0, default: 0 }
        max_creates_in_flight: { type: integer, minimum: 0, default: 1 }
        idle_timeout: { $ref: "#/components/schemas/Duration" }
        cost_per_machine_hour: { type: number, minimum: 0 }
        enabled: { type: boolean, default: true }

    ProviderSetting:
      type: object
      required: [key, label, kind, required, advanced]
      properties:
        key: { type: string, examples: [node] }
        label: { type: string, examples: [Node] }
        kind: { type: string, enum: [text, number, bool, choice, list, secret] }
        required: { type: boolean }
        advanced: { type: boolean, description: Put behind a disclosure, because a form that asks eleven questions to do the common thing gets abandoned. }
        help: { type: string, description: One operator-facing sentence. }
        consequence: { type: string, description: What choosing it means, in the voice the pool form uses for a choice that costs something. }
        discovers:
          type: string
          description: Which discovery list fills the choices, e.g. nodes.
        default: { type: string }
        source:
          type: string
          description: >-
            Where the answer is found when discovery cannot offer it: which page of the
            provider's own console, or which command on one of its machines. `help` says
            what the setting is; this says where to look.

    ProviderGuideStep:
      type: object
      required: [title]
      description: One thing to do before a provider of this kind can rent anything.
      properties:
        title: { type: string, examples: [An API token that can clone, start and delete guests] }
        detail: { type: string, description: What to do and why, shown as written. }
        command: { type: string, description: A shell snippet to copy, when the step is done in a terminal. }

    ProviderKind:
      type: object
      required: [kind, label, bootstrap, guide, settings]
      properties:
        kind: { $ref: "#/components/schemas/ProviderKindName" }
        label: { type: string, examples: [Proxmox VE] }
        endpoint_example:
          type: string
          description: What an address for this kind looks like, scheme and port included, so the form can show one and fill the port in.
          examples: ["https://pve.example.com:8006"]
        endpoint_source: { type: string, description: Where the address is found, in the provider's own console's terms. }
        credential_source: { type: string, description: Where the credential is made, and what shape to paste it in. }
        ca_source: { type: string, description: Where the certificate to trust is found, and when to leave it empty. }
        guide:
          type: array
          description: >-
            What has to exist before this kind can rent a machine, in the order it is done.
            The wizard shows it before its first question, because each step is done
            somewhere other than the form.
          items: { $ref: "#/components/schemas/ProviderGuideStep" }
        bootstrap:
          type: string
          enum: [guest_agent, metadata, none]
          description: >-
            How the enrolment payload reaches a guest. "metadata" means it is readable by
            anyone who can read the machine's metadata, which is worth knowing before
            anything is bought.
        can_start_stop: { type: boolean }
        can_discover: { type: boolean }
        can_mark_ownership: { type: boolean, description: Whether the driver can write Zoomies' marks onto the resource itself. }
        async_operations: { type: boolean }
        cost_unit: { type: string, examples: [machine-hour] }
        settings:
          type: array
          items: { $ref: "#/components/schemas/ProviderSetting" }

    ProviderValidation:
      type: object
      required: [valid, errors, warnings]
      properties:
        valid: { type: boolean }
        errors:
          type: array
          items: { $ref: "#/components/schemas/FieldError" }
        warnings:
          type: array
          description: Answers that are legal and still cost something.
          items: { $ref: "#/components/schemas/Problem" }

    ProviderCheck:
      type: object
      required: [provider_id, ok, reachable, findings, checked_at]
      properties:
        provider_id: { type: string }
        ok:
          type: boolean
          description: Nothing found stops this provider being used. Warnings do not - they weaken the posture and say so.
        reachable:
          type: boolean
          description: >-
            Whether an answer came back at all. Separate from the findings because a
            provider that cannot be reached has one problem, not eleven.
        version: { type: string, description: The provider's own version, kept because "it worked" is worth little without "against what". }
        findings:
          type: array
          items: { $ref: "#/components/schemas/Problem" }
        checked_at: { type: string, format: date-time }

    ProviderChoice:
      type: object
      required: [value]
      properties:
        value: { type: string }
        label: { type: string }
        consequence: { type: string, description: What picking it means, because a list of identifiers with no consequences is a list somebody guesses at. }

    ProviderDiscovery:
      type: object
      required: [nodes, storages, bridges, templates]
      description: What a credential can actually see. A provider with no such concept leaves a list empty rather than inventing one.
      properties:
        nodes: { type: array, items: { $ref: "#/components/schemas/ProviderChoice" } }
        storages: { type: array, items: { $ref: "#/components/schemas/ProviderChoice" } }
        bridges: { type: array, items: { $ref: "#/components/schemas/ProviderChoice" } }
        templates: { type: array, items: { $ref: "#/components/schemas/ProviderChoice" } }
        unavailable:
          type: string
          description: >-
            Why the lists are empty, when the provider could not be asked: the address did
            not answer, the credential was refused. Only a draft's discovery sets it; the
            saved provider's route answers with an error instead.

    Orphan:
      type: object
      required: [name, note]
      properties:
        name: { type: string, examples: [zoomies-mach-k3f9q] }
        note: { type: string, description: What to do about it, which for an untracked resource is always to look at it yourself. }

    ProviderOrphans:
      type: object
      required: [provider_id, provider_name, untracked, no_resource, unverified]
      properties:
        provider_id: { type: string }
        provider_name: { type: string }
        last_sweep_at: { type: string, format: date-time, description: When the untracked list was gathered, so a stale answer says so. }
        untracked:
          type: array
          description: Resources wearing this fleet's naming that no row accounts for. Zoomies never deletes one.
          items: { $ref: "#/components/schemas/Orphan" }
        no_resource:
          type: array
          description: Rows that hold nothing, which can be released without anything being lost.
          items: { $ref: "#/components/schemas/Machine" }
        unverified:
          type: array
          description: Machines whose ownership nothing has confirmed, including every quarantined one.
          items: { $ref: "#/components/schemas/Machine" }

    MachineTimelineEntry:
      type: object
