      required: [phase, at]
      properties:
        phase: { type: string, examples: [bootstrapped] }
        at: { type: string, format: date-time }

    Machine:
      type: object
      required: [id, provider_id, name, state, labels, safe_to_delete, timeline, created_at, updated_at]
      properties:
        id: { type: string, examples: [mach_k3f9qz2mx7ab] }
        provider_id: { type: string }
        provider_name: { type: string }
        provider_kind: { $ref: "#/components/schemas/ProviderKindName" }
        name: { type: string, examples: [zoomies-mach-k3f9q] }
        state: { $ref: "#/components/schemas/MachineState" }
        message: { type: string, description: Why it is where it is, in one sentence. }
        pool_id: { type: string, description: Which pool's unmet demand asked for this machine. Not ownership - a machine serves every pool its labels match. }
        pool_name: { type: string }
        resource_zone: { type: string, examples: [pve-1] }
        resource_id: { type: string, examples: ["143"] }
        address: { type: string }
        ownership_verified_at: { type: string, format: date-time, description: The last time a fresh observation agreed this resource is ours. }
        ownership_error: { type: string, description: What disagreed. A machine with one is never deleted by anything but a person. }
        host_id: { type: string }
        host_name: { type: string }
        capacity: { type: integer }
        labels: { type: object, additionalProperties: { type: string } }
        operation: { type: string, enum: [create, start, stop, bootstrap, delete], description: The operation in flight, if any. }
        operation_id: { type: string, examples: [mop_k3f9qz2mx7ab] }
        operation_handle: { type: string, description: The provider's own handle for the call, which is what an operator pastes into its task log. }
        operation_holder: { type: string, description: The controller taking the step, so a machine stuck mid-create names the controller to go and look at. }
        operation_since: { type: string, format: date-time }
        outcome_unknown: { type: boolean, description: A call that went out and was never answered, which is the one thing a retry must not treat as a failure. }
        attempts: { type: integer }
        next_attempt_at: { type: string, format: date-time }
        provider_error: { type: string, description: What the hypervisor complained about, in its own words. }
        bootstrap_error: { type: string, description: What went wrong inside the guest, in its own words. }
        safe_to_delete: { type: boolean, description: Whether the row alone says a delete would be safe. The delete itself asks the provider again. }
        safe_to_delete_why: { type: string, description: Why not, when it is not. }
        timeline:
          type: array
          description: The phases this machine actually reached. A phase it skipped is absent rather than zero.
          items: { $ref: "#/components/schemas/MachineTimelineEntry" }
        created_at: { type: string, format: date-time }
        updated_at: { type: string, format: date-time }
        ready_at: { type: string, format: date-time }
        idle_since: { type: string, format: date-time }
        deleted_at: { type: string, format: date-time, description: When the provider confirmed the resource was gone, by an inspect that could not find it. }

    # --- audit and administration ----------------------------------------
    AuditEvent:
      type: object
      properties:
        id: { type: string }
        actor_id: { type: string }
        actor_name: { type: string }
        actor_kind: { type: string, enum: [user, token, connection, client, agent, system, webhook] }
        action: { type: string, examples: ["pool.create", "runner.drain"] }
        target_kind: { type: string }
        target_id: { type: string }
        before: { type: string, description: JSON, with secrets redacted. }
        after: { type: string }
        ip: { type: string }
        created_at: { type: string, format: date-time }

    User:
      type: object
      properties:
        id: { type: string }
        username: { type: string }
        email: { type: string }
        display_name: { type: string }
        role: { $ref: "#/components/schemas/Role" }
        oidc_subject: { type: string }
        disabled: { type: boolean }
        must_change_password: { type: boolean }
        created_at: { type: string, format: date-time }
        last_login_at: { type: [string, "null"], format: date-time }
        two_step_enabled: { type: boolean, description: Whether the account signs in with a code after its password. }

    SignInChallenge:
      type: object
      required: [two_step, username, expires_at]
      properties:
        two_step: { type: string, enum: [verify, enrol] }
        username: { type: string }
        expires_at: { type: string, format: date-time }

    TwoStepCode:
      type: object
      required: [code]
      properties:
        code:
          type: string
          description: Six digits from the authenticator app, or a recovery code. Spaces and hyphens are ignored.

    TwoStepReauth:
      type: object
      required: [password, code]
      properties:
        password: { type: string, format: password }
        code: { type: string }

    TwoStepSignIn:
      type: object
      required: [identity, recovery_code_used]
      properties:
        identity: { $ref: "#/components/schemas/Identity" }
        recovery_code_used: { type: boolean }
        recovery_codes_left: { type: integer, description: Set when a recovery code was used. }
        recovery_codes:
          type: array
          items: { type: string }
          description: Set when the sign-in enrolled an authenticator. Shown this once.

    TwoStepStatus:
      type: object
      required: [available, enabled, recovery_codes_left, required]
      properties:
        available: { type: boolean, description: False for an account that signs in through single sign-on. }
        enabled: { type: boolean }
        enabled_at: { type: string, format: date-time }
        recovery_codes_left: { type: integer }
        required: { type: boolean, description: "security.require_two_step." }

    TwoStepSetup:
      type: object
      required: [secret, otpauth_uri, qr_svg]
      properties:
        secret: { type: string, description: The key in base32, for typing into an app by hand. }
        otpauth_uri: { type: string }
        qr_svg: { type: string, description: The otpauth address as a QR code, an SVG document drawn by the controller. }

    RecoveryCodes:
      type: object
      required: [recovery_codes]
      properties:
        recovery_codes: { type: array, items: { type: string } }

    Identity:
      type: object
      properties:
        kind: { type: string, enum: [user, token, agent, system] }
        id: { type: string }
        name: { type: string }
        role: { $ref: "#/components/schemas/Role" }
        scopes: { type: array, items: { type: string } }
        must_change_password: { type: boolean }

    UserPreferences:
      type: object
      description: Private, account-scoped interface choices. Unknown tables and columns are harmless.
      properties:
        table_layouts:
          type: object
          additionalProperties:
            $ref: "#/components/schemas/TableLayoutPreference"

    TableLayoutPreference:
      type: object
      properties:
        widths:
          type: object
          additionalProperties: { type: number, minimum: 40, maximum: 1000 }
        order:
          type: array
          maxItems: 100
          items: { type: string, minLength: 1, maxLength: 100 }

    APIToken:
      type: object
      properties:
        id: { type: string }
        name: { type: string }
        role: { $ref: "#/components/schemas/Role" }
        scopes: { type: array, items: { type: string } }
        prefix: { type: string }
        revoked: { type: boolean }
        created_at: { type: string, format: date-time }
        expires_at: { type: [string, "null"], format: date-time }
        last_used_at: { type: [string, "null"], format: date-time }
        user_id: { type: string, description: The account that minted the token. }

    MCPClient:
      type: object
      required: [id, client_id, kind, name, redirect_uris, confidential, created_at, connections]
      properties:
        id: { type: string, examples: ["oac_abcdefghijklm"] }
        client_id: { type: string, description: What the client sends. The row ID, or the document URL for a metadata client. }
        kind: { type: string, enum: [dynamic, metadata, admin] }
        name: { type: string }
        client_uri: { type: string }
        redirect_uris: { type: array, items: { type: string } }
        confidential: { type: boolean }
        secret_prefix: { type: string, description: The first characters of the secret, to recognise it by. }
        secret_rotated_at: { type: [string, "null"], format: date-time }
        created_by: { type: string }
        created_at: { type: string, format: date-time }
        last_used_at: { type: [string, "null"], format: date-time }
        revoked_at: { type: [string, "null"], format: date-time }
        connections: { type: integer, description: Live connections this client holds. }
        client_secret: { type: string, description: Present once, in the response that creates or rotates it. }

    MCPConnection:
      type: object
      required: [id, client_id, client_name, client_kind, user_id, username, role, scope, created_at]
      properties:
        id: { type: string, examples: ["ocg_abcdefghijklm"] }
        client_id: { type: string }
        client_name: { type: string }
        client_kind: { type: string, enum: [dynamic, metadata, admin] }
        user_id: { type: string }
        username: { type: string }
        role: { $ref: "#/components/schemas/Role" }
        scope: { type: string, examples: ["mcp:read mcp:operate"] }
        created_at: { type: string, format: date-time }
        last_used_at: { type: [string, "null"], format: date-time }

    MCPConsent:
      type: object
      required: [id, client, redirect_uri, redirect_host, loopback_only, resource, requested_scope, roles, suggested_role, your_role, expires_at]
      properties:
        id: { type: string, examples: ["oar_abcdefghijklm"] }
        client:
          type: object
          required: [id, client_id, name, kind]
          properties:
            id: { type: string }
            client_id: { type: string }
            name: { type: string }
            kind: { type: string, enum: [dynamic, metadata, admin] }
            client_uri: { type: string }
        redirect_uri: { type: string }
        redirect_host: { type: string, description: Where approving sends you, which the consent screen shows plainly. }
        loopback_only: { type: boolean, description: Every redirect the client registered is on your own machine, where any program could listen. }
        resource: { type: string, examples: ["https://zoomies.example.com/mcp"] }
        requested_scope: { type: string }
        roles: { type: array, items: { $ref: "#/components/schemas/Role" } }
        suggested_role: { $ref: "#/components/schemas/Role" }
        your_role: { $ref: "#/components/schemas/Role" }
        expires_at: { type: string, format: date-time }

    MCPDecision:
      type: object
      required: [redirect_to]
      properties:
        redirect_to: { type: string, description: The client's redirect URI with the code or the error, for the browser to follow. }

    Setting:
      type: object
      description: >-
        One configuration key: what it is, what Zoomies is running, where
        that value came from, and whether an administrator may change it here.
      required: [key, label, section, kind, summary, secret, configured, source, env, stored, editable, scope, live, pending]
      properties:
        key: { type: string, description: The dotted key, spelled as it is in zoomies.yaml., examples: ["scheduler.interval"] }
        label: { type: string, description: The setting's name in prose, for a person reading a form., examples: ["Scheduler interval"] }
        section: { type: string, description: The part before the first dot, which the UI groups under., examples: ["scheduler"] }
        kind:
          type: string
          enum: [string, enum, bool, optional_bool, int, float, duration, strings, labels]
          description: >-
            How to parse and render the value. `duration` is carried as the text an
            operator writes (30s, 5m, 168h) rather than as a number. `optional_bool`
            has three states, because unset means the value is derived from another
            setting. `float` is the one figure that is genuinely fractional, a
            share of a CPU.
        choices:
          type: array
          items: { type: string }
          description: The permitted values, when the kind is `enum`.
        summary: { type: string, description: One line saying what the setting does. }
        value:
          nullable: true
          description: What Zoomies is running. Absent for a secret.
        default:
          nullable: true
          description: What Zoomies uses when nothing says otherwise. Absent for a secret.
        secret: { type: boolean, description: A credential. Its value is never sent; `configured` says whether one is set. }
        configured: { type: boolean, description: Whether the effective value is non-empty. }
        source:
          $ref: "#/components/schemas/SettingSource"
        env: { type: string, description: The ZOOMIES_* variable that overrides this key., examples: ["ZOOMIES_SCHEDULER_INTERVAL"] }
        stored: { type: boolean, description: Whether this fleet's database holds a value for this key. }
        editable: { type: boolean, description: Whether an administrator may change it through this API. }
        scope:
          type: string
          enum: [instance, platform, bootstrap, local]
          description: >-
            `instance` lives in the fleet's database. `platform` lives there too but
            belongs to whoever runs the controller rather than the fleet -- what the
            process binds, trusts, stores, logs or dials from its own machine -- and
            is omitted entirely for a caller below the `platform` role. `bootstrap`
            is read before that database can be opened, so it cannot. `local`
            belongs to a standalone agent's own host.
        reason: { type: string, description: Why it is not editable, written for the person reading it. }
        live: { type: boolean, description: Whether a change is in force by the time the response is written. }
        restart_reason: { type: string, description: Why a change waits for a restart. }
        pending: { type: boolean, description: A stored value is waiting for that restart. }
        updated_at: { type: string, format: date-time }
        updated_by: { type: string }

    Settings:
      type: object
      properties:
        config:
          type: object
          additionalProperties: true
          description: >-
            The effective configuration as a nested object, shaped like the file.
            A secret never appears; each one contributes a `<key>_configured`
            boolean instead.
        settings:
          type: array
          items: { $ref: "#/components/schemas/Setting" }
          description: Every configuration key, in the order the documentation lists them.
        findings:
          type: array
          items: { $ref: "#/components/schemas/Problem" }
        pending_restart:
          type: array
          items: { type: string }
          description: Settings stored since this process started that it cannot apply to itself.
        pinned_by_environment:
          type: array
          items: { type: string }
          description: >-
            Settings an environment variable is holding. A change to one of these
            would be stored and then overridden at the next restart, so it is refused.
        config_path: { type: string }
        restart_required_keys:
          type: array
          items: { type: string }
          description: Every key whose change waits for a restart, whether or not one is waiting now.
        version: { type: string }
        database_path: { type: string }
        event_subscribers: { type: integer }

    SettingsExport:
      type: object
      required: [export_version, exported_at, version, settings, secrets_configured]
      properties:
        export_version: { type: integer }
        exported_at: { type: string, format: date-time }
        exported_from: { type: string, description: The address the source instance answers on. }
        version: { type: string, description: The Zoomies build that wrote it. }
        settings:
          type: object
          additionalProperties: true
          description: The nested tree, shaped like zoomies.yaml.
        secrets_configured:
          type: array
          items: { type: string }
          description: Credentials that were set on the source and are not in this document.

    SettingsImportRequest:
      type: object
      required: [document]
      properties:
        document: { type: string, description: An export, or a zoomies.yaml, as text. YAML or JSON. }
        dry_run: { type: boolean, description: Plan and report; write nothing. }
        skip: { type: array, items: { type: string }, description: Keys in the document to leave out. }

    SettingsImportChange:
      type: object
      required: [key, current, incoming, action, live, secret]
      properties:
        key: { type: string }
        label: { type: string }
        section: { type: string }
        current: { nullable: true, description: The running value, as the settings page renders it. Never a secret's. }
        incoming: { nullable: true, description: The document's value, parsed. Never a secret's. }
        action: { type: string, enum: [change, unchanged, unset, refused] }
        live: { type: boolean, description: A change is in force at once; false waits for a restart. }
        secret: { type: boolean }
        reason: { type: string, description: Why it is refused. }

    SettingsImport:
      type: object
      required: [applied, changes, summary, secrets_configured]
      properties:
        applied: { type: boolean }
        changes: { type: array, items: { $ref: "#/components/schemas/SettingsImportChange" } }
        summary:
          type: object
          required: [change, unchanged, unset, refused, skipped]
          properties:
            change: { type: integer }
            unchanged: { type: integer }
            unset: { type: integer }
            refused: { type: integer }
            skipped: { type: integer }
        secrets_configured: { type: array, items: { type: string } }
        settings: { $ref: "#/components/schemas/Settings" }

    # --- agent protocol (internal) ------------------------------------------
    # The wire types of the agent routes. internal/agent/protocol.go owns them;
    # these describe what it sends so the document is whole.
    AgentJoinRequest:
      type: object
      required: [protocol_version, join_token, name, capacity, os, arch, version, backends]
      properties:
        protocol_version: { type: integer }
        join_token: { type: string, format: password }
        name: { type: string }
        address: { type: string, description: How the host reports itself. The controller never dials it. }
        capacity: { type: integer, description: Concurrent runners the host accepts. 0 lets the join token or the CPU count decide. }
        os: { type: string }
        arch: { type: string }
        version: { type: string, description: The agent's build version, for skew warnings. }
        labels: { type: object, additionalProperties: { type: string } }
        backends: { type: array, items: { $ref: "#/components/schemas/BackendInfo" } }
    AgentJoinResponse:
      type: object
      properties:
        host_id: { type: string }
        agent_token: { type: string, description: Shown once. The controller keeps only its hash. }
        controller_version: { type: string }
        heartbeat_interval: { $ref: "#/components/schemas/Duration" }
    AgentHeartbeatRequest:
      type: object
      properties:
        usage: { $ref: "#/components/schemas/HostUsage" }
        protocol_version: { type: integer }
        capacity: { type: integer, description: The agent's configured value, sent for the log. The controller does not write it. }
        version: { type: string }
        features: { type: array, items: { type: string }, description: Additive runtime capabilities understood by this agent. }
        backends: { type: array, items: { $ref: "#/components/schemas/BackendInfo" } }
        runners: { type: array, items: { $ref: "#/components/schemas/RunnerReport" } }
    AgentHeartbeatResponse:
      type: object
      properties:
        mutations_paused: { type: boolean, description: Preserve workloads and quotas while controller authority is paused. }
        ok: { type: boolean }
        cordoned: { type: boolean, description: Mirrors the host's cordon flag so the agent stops asking for work at once. }
        controller_version: { type: string }
        resync_requested: { type: boolean, description: Send a full runner report next time. Set after the controller restarts. }
        throttle: { $ref: "#/components/schemas/ThrottleDirective" }
        elastic_cpu: { type: array, items: { $ref: "#/components/schemas/ElasticCPUDirective" }, description: Complete boosted-runner set; omission restores a previous boost to its guarantee. }
    ThrottleDirective:
      type: object
      properties:
        level: { type: integer, minimum: 0, maximum: 3 }
        cpu_factor: { type: number, format: double, description: Below one reduces every limited runner on this host; pressure always overrides elastic CPU. }
    ElasticCPUDirective:
      type: object
      required: [runner_id, cpu_factor, base_cpus, target_cpus]
      properties:
        runner_id: { type: string }
        cpu_factor: { type: number, format: double, minimum: 1 }
        base_cpus: { type: number, format: double }
        target_cpus: { type: number, format: double }
        reason: { type: string, enum: [squirrel_spotted] }
    RunnerReport:
      type: object
      required: [runner_id, observed_at]
      properties:
        host_removed: { type: boolean, description: "Positive confirmation that backend removal completed, including its work directory; process exit alone is insufficient." }
        cleanup_error: { type: string, description: "Failure of autonomous host cleanup; retained until its retry succeeds." }
        runner_id: { type: string }
        state:
          description: >-
            The state the agent asserts, or empty once the workload is up: whether GitHub has
            handed the runner a job is not the agent's call.
          oneOf:
            - $ref: "#/components/schemas/RunnerState"
            - { type: string, const: "" }
        handle: { type: string, description: The backend's own name for the workload, such as a container ID. }
        phase: { type: string, enum: [starting, running, exited, exit_unknown, failed, gone] }
        exit_code: { type: integer }
        message: { type: string }
        stats: { $ref: "#/components/schemas/WorkloadStats" }
        github_runner_id: { type: integer, format: int64, description: Filled in once the runner has registered. }
        observed_at: { type: string, format: date-time }
    WorkloadStats:
      type: object
      properties:
        sampled_at: { type: string, format: date-time, description: Time of the last successful sample. Absence means freshness is unknown. Retained samples keep their original timestamp. }
        cpu_throttling:
          type: object
          description: Cumulative cgroup CPU quota counters. Absent when unsupported; resets on workload recreation.
          properties:
            periods: { type: integer, format: int64 }
            throttled_periods: { type: integer, format: int64 }
            throttled_nanoseconds: { type: integer, format: int64 }
        cpu_percent: { type: number, format: double }
        memory_bytes: { type: integer, format: int64 }
        memory_limit: { type: integer, format: int64 }
        cpu_allocation_factor: { type: number, format: double, description: One is the guaranteed creation quota; above one is elastic CPU and below one is host-pressure throttling. }
        busiest_half_percent: { type: number, format: double, description: For a docker-in-docker pair, how much of its own creation quota the busier container is using, in percent. Absent for a single container. }
    AgentTaskKind:
      type: string
      enum: [create_runner, stop_runner, remove_runner, stream_logs, cancel_logs, prewarm_image, fill_tool_cache]
    AgentTask:
      type: object
      description: One unit of work for an agent. Tasks are idempotent; the controller may redeliver one after a restart.
      required: [id, kind, issued_at]
      properties:
        id: { type: string }
        kind: { $ref: "#/components/schemas/AgentTaskKind" }
        runner_id: { type: string }
        spec: { $ref: "#/components/schemas/RunnerSpec" }
        backend: { $ref: "#/components/schemas/BackendKind" }
        pool_id: { type: string }
        image: { type: string }
        pull_policy: { $ref: "#/components/schemas/PullPolicy" }
        stop_timeout: { type: integer, format: int64, description: Nanoseconds. Bounds a graceful stop. }
        stream_id: { type: string, description: The log relay a stream_logs or cancel_logs task concerns. }
        log_options: { $ref: "#/components/schemas/LogOptions" }
        tools:
          type: array
          description: What a fill_tool_cache task puts in the tool cache of the pool its spec names.
          items:
            type: object
            required: [tool, version]
            properties:
              tool: { type: string }
              version: { type: string }
              distribution: { type: string }
        issued_at: { type: string, format: date-time }
        attempt: { type: integer, description: "Deliveries of this task so far, from 1. A create that cannot tell whether its runner already exists fails a first delivery promptly and leaves a redelivery for the lease. Absent from older controllers." }
    RunnerSpec:
      type: object
      description: >-
        Everything a backend needs to create one runner. The one place a JIT config crosses
        the wire, which is why the agent transport requires TLS off loopback.
      properties:
        name: { type: string, description: The runner name GitHub will know it by. It doubles as the container name. }
        runner_id: { type: string }
        pool_id: { type: string }
        pool_name: { type: string }
        image: { type: string }
        pull_policy: { $ref: "#/components/schemas/PullPolicy" }
        start_before: { type: string, format: date-time, description: Do not create a new workload at or after this provisioning deadline; existing workloads are still adopted. }
        credentials:
          type: object
          description: The runner's registration credentials. Never logged, never shown.
          properties:
            jit_config: { type: string, format: password }
            registration_token: { type: string, format: password }
            expires_at: { type: string, format: date-time, description: GitHub token expiry when known. }
            url: { type: string, description: The organisation or repository URL the runner registers against. }
            runner_group: { type: string }
            labels: { type: array, items: { type: string } }
            no_default_labels: { type: boolean, description: Pass --no-default-labels to config.sh on the registration-token path. }
        env: { type: object, additionalProperties: { type: string } }
        ephemeral: { type: boolean }
        resources: { $ref: "#/components/schemas/Resources" }
        cache: { $ref: "#/components/schemas/CacheConfig" }
        repository: { type: string }
        docker_mode: { $ref: "#/components/schemas/DockerMode" }
        run_as_root: { type: boolean }
        network: { type: string }
        work_dir: { type: string }
        runner_version: { type: string, description: The actions/runner release the process backend downloads. }
    LogOptions:
      type: object
      description: How a log relay reads the workload's output. The names are capitalised on the wire, as the Go type carries no JSON tags.
      properties:
        Follow: { type: boolean }
        Tail: { type: integer, description: Lines of backlog to send first. 0 means everything. }
        Since: { type: string, format: date-time }
        Timestamps: { type: boolean }
    AgentTaskResult:
      type: object
      required: [task_id, ok, completed_at]
      properties:
        task_id: { type: string }
        kind: { $ref: "#/components/schemas/AgentTaskKind" }
        runner_id: { type: string }
        ok: { type: boolean }
        error: { type: string }
        handle: { type: string }
        startup_wait: { type: integer, format: int64, description: Nanoseconds waiting for host startup admission. }
        dind_ready_duration: { type: integer, format: int64, description: Nanoseconds creating and awaiting a healthy sidecar after its image is available. }
        image_pull_duration: { type: integer, format: int64, description: Nanoseconds. Absent when the backend cannot tell pulling from creation. }
        create_duration: { type: integer, format: int64, description: Nanoseconds. }
        container_started_at: { type: string, format: date-time }
        digest: { type: string }
        state: { $ref: "#/components/schemas/RunnerState" }
        tool_fills: { type: array, items: { $ref: "#/components/schemas/ToolFill" }, description: What a fill_tool_cache task did with each request. }
        completed_at: { type: string, format: date-time }
    AgentTaskBatch:
      type: object
      required: [tasks]
      properties:
        tasks: { type: array, items: { $ref: "#/components/schemas/AgentTask" } }
        backoff: { type: integer, format: int64, description: Nanoseconds to wait before polling again, when the controller sheds load. }

// The shapes below are the parts of api/openapi.yaml the tables read. They are
// deliberately partial: a field this CLI does not render is a field it does not
// declare, and `--output json` passes the server's bytes through untouched, so
// nothing is lost by leaving one out.

// listResponse is the envelope every list route returns.
type listResponse[T any] struct {
	Items  []T `json:"items"`
	Total  int `json:"total"`
	Limit  int `json:"limit"`
	Offset int `json:"offset"`
	// Next is the cursor for the following page, where the listing has one.
	Next string `json:"next"`
}

type poolCounts struct {
	Provisioning int `json:"provisioning"`
	Registering  int `json:"registering"`
	Idle         int `json:"idle"`
	Busy         int `json:"busy"`
	Draining     int `json:"draining"`
	Failed       int `json:"failed"`
	Live         int `json:"live"`
}

type poolItem struct {
	ID                 string            `json:"id"`
	Name               string            `json:"name"`
	InstallationID     string            `json:"installation_id"`
	InstallationTarget string            `json:"installation_target"`
	Labels             []string          `json:"labels"`
	RunnerGroup        string            `json:"runner_group"`
	Backend            string            `json:"backend"`
	Platform           platformItem      `json:"platform"`
	Image              string            `json:"image"`
	EffectiveImage     string            `json:"effective_image"`
	PullPolicy         string            `json:"pull_policy"`
	RunnerVersion      string            `json:"runner_version"`
	MinRunners         int               `json:"min_runners"`
	MaxRunners         int               `json:"max_runners"`
	Priority           int               `json:"priority"`
	IdleTimeout        string            `json:"idle_timeout"`
	Ephemeral          bool              `json:"ephemeral"`
	DockerMode         string            `json:"docker_mode"`
	HostSelector       map[string]string `json:"host_selector"`
	Env                map[string]string `json:"env"`
	RunAsRoot          bool              `json:"run_as_root"`
	NoDefaultLabels    bool              `json:"no_default_labels"`
	Enabled            bool              `json:"enabled"`
	CreatedAt          time.Time         `json:"created_at"`
	UpdatedAt          time.Time         `json:"updated_at"`
	Counts             poolCounts        `json:"counts"`
	QueuedJobs         int               `json:"queued_jobs"`
	Utilisation        float64           `json:"utilisation"`
	Warnings           []problemItem     `json:"warnings"`
	// Resources is the size this pool asks for on every host, and Sizing says
	// whether it asks for one at all: "automatic" is a pool whose runners are
	// each given one slot's share of the machine they land on.
	Resources poolResources `json:"resources"`
	Sizing    string        `json:"sizing"`
	// CPUBurst is the pool's elastic CPU policy: whether a busy runner may be
	// lent the host's spare CPU above its guaranteed share.
	CPUBurst poolCPUBurst `json:"cpu_burst"`
}

// poolCPUBurst mirrors the API's CPUBurstPolicy. An empty mode is off, which
// is what every pool created before the policy existed has.
type poolCPUBurst struct {
	Mode    string  `json:"mode"`
	MaxCPUs float64 `json:"max_cpus"`
	// SizeForCeiling is absent on a pool that has never said, which is on.
	SizeForCeiling *bool `json:"size_for_ceiling,omitempty"`
}

// poolResources is the size a pool asks for per runner. Every field is zero on
// a pool that leaves the answer to its host.
type poolResources struct {
	CPUs      float64 `json:"cpus"`
	MemoryMB  int64   `json:"memory_mb"`
	DiskGB    int64   `json:"disk_gb"`
	PidsLimit int64   `json:"pids_limit"`
}

// platformItem is the machine a pool needs, or the machine a host is.
type platformItem struct {
	OS        string `json:"os"`
	OSVersion string `json:"os_version"`
	Arch      string `json:"arch"`
}

// String renders the platform the way the UI does: "ubuntu 24.04, arm64", or
// "any" when the pool promises nothing.
func (p platformItem) String() string {
	var parts []string
	if p.OS != "" {
		os := p.OS
		if p.OSVersion != "" {
			os += " " + p.OSVersion
		}
		parts = append(parts, os)
	}
	if p.Arch != "" {
		parts = append(parts, p.Arch)
	}
	if len(parts) == 0 {
		return "any"
	}
	return strings.Join(parts, ", ")
}

	DurationMS     int64      `json:"duration_ms"`

	NoResource   []machineItem `json:"no_resource"`

}

// bundleResponse is GET /diagnostics/bundle, decoded only as far as the
