# Zoomies controller and agent.
#
# One binary, two subcommands. Built static (CGO_ENABLED=0 -- the SQLite driver
# is pure Go) so the runtime image can be distroless.

# ---- UI ---------------------------------------------------------------------
# UI assets are architecture-independent; build them once on the builder's CPU.
FROM --platform=$BUILDPLATFORM node:26-alpine@sha256:0b36e8c136b94cd4fcf02188228e76c31ad5872eef3fec8cbd2eee500cfd9e80 AS ui
WORKDIR /src/web
COPY web/package.json web/package-lock.json* ./
# No `|| npm install` fallback: that turns a lockfile CI would reject into an
# image built from whatever npm resolved today.
RUN npm ci --no-audit --no-fund
COPY web/ ./
RUN npm run build

# ---- Go ---------------------------------------------------------------------
# Go cross-compiles on the builder's CPU instead of running the compiler in QEMU.
FROM --platform=$BUILDPLATFORM golang:1.27-alpine@sha256:8a5910f31396cd4d89662f56c68b3ae31d374308270a1c3bd96672ee5ed43414 AS build
WORKDIR /src
RUN apk add --no-cache git ca-certificates
COPY go.mod go.sum ./
RUN go mod download
COPY . .
# The UI build output is embedded by internal/api; it must be present before the
# Go build so that //go:embed finds it.
COPY --from=ui /src/internal/api/webdist ./internal/api/webdist
# VERSION is the release without its leading v, the same string `make dist`
# stamps into the binaries: one release must not report two versions depending
# on how it was installed. DATE is passed because -trimpath and a build context
# with no .git leave Go nothing to infer one from.
ARG VERSION=dev
ARG COMMIT=""
ARG DATE=""
# Runner tags are separate from VERSION (main-sha-* is not a runner tag).
# Keep this a binary default, not ENV ZOOMIES_RUNNER_IMAGE: a baked environment
# override would incorrectly take precedence over the operator's YAML setting.
ARG RUNNER_IMAGE_TAG=dev
# Redeclare BuildKit's automatic target arguments without overriding their values.
ARG TARGETOS
ARG TARGETARCH
RUN CGO_ENABLED=0 GOOS=$TARGETOS GOARCH=$TARGETARCH \
    go build -trimpath \
      -ldflags "-s -w \
        -X github.com/eyupio/zoomies/internal/version.Version=${VERSION} \
        -X github.com/eyupio/zoomies/internal/version.Commit=${COMMIT} \
        -X github.com/eyupio/zoomies/internal/version.Date=${DATE} \
        -X github.com/eyupio/zoomies/internal/naming.RunnerImageTag=${RUNNER_IMAGE_TAG}" \
      -o /out/zoomies ./cmd/zoomies

# An empty state directory to copy into the runtime stages. distroless has no
# shell, so this is the only way to get /var/lib/zoomies into the image owned by
# the user that runs there.
RUN install -d -m 0750 /out/state

# ---- Runtime ----------------------------------------------------------------
FROM gcr.io/distroless/static-debian12:nonroot@sha256:afa5c872c891853ca7fcf1f12c3edb23f7eeef36189728842dd51042ff57f7ab AS controller
# Re-declared after FROM: the ones set above are out of scope here, and a label
# written from an ARG that is not in scope is silently empty.
ARG VERSION=dev
ARG COMMIT=""
ARG DATE=""
# The image had no labels at all, so a registry listing said nothing about what
# it was or where it came from, and `docker inspect` could not answer which
# release a running container was. The binary inside has always known; this is
# the same fact where a person can reach it without starting anything.
LABEL org.opencontainers.image.title="zoomies" \
      org.opencontainers.image.description="Self-hosted GitHub Actions runner fleet controller" \
      org.opencontainers.image.source="https://github.com/eyupio/zoomies" \
      org.opencontainers.image.url="https://zoomies.sh" \
      org.opencontainers.image.documentation="https://zoomies.sh/quickstart/" \
      org.opencontainers.image.vendor="EyUp.io" \
      org.opencontainers.image.licenses="AGPL-3.0-only" \
      org.opencontainers.image.version="${VERSION}" \
      org.opencontainers.image.revision="${COMMIT}" \
      org.opencontainers.image.created="${DATE}"
COPY --from=build /out/zoomies /usr/local/bin/zoomies
# The state directory must exist in the image, owned by the user that runs. A
# VOLUME on a path the image does not have gets created by the container runtime
# as root, and then uid 65532 cannot create the database in it -- SQLite reports
# only "unable to open database file (14)". Docker seeds a fresh named volume
# from the image, so baking the ownership in here is what makes that volume
# writable.
COPY --from=build --chown=65532:65532 /out/state /var/lib/zoomies
# 65532 is distroless' "nonroot" user. The controller never needs root.
USER 65532:65532
VOLUME ["/var/lib/zoomies"]
EXPOSE 8080
ENV ZOOMIES_STATE_DIR=/var/lib/zoomies \
    ZOOMIES_CONFIG_DIR=/etc/zoomies \
    ZOOMIES_DB_PATH=/var/lib/zoomies/zoomies.db
# The check the compose files already spell out, declared here so that a plain
# `docker run` gets it too -- an unhealthy controller that still has a running
# container is exactly the state an operator finds out about by accident.
#
# Exec form: distroless has no shell, so the string form docker would otherwise
# wrap in /bin/sh could never run. The port is the one EXPOSE names and the
# installer's ContainerPort constant uses; a controller told to listen
# elsewhere overrides this with its own --health-cmd.
HEALTHCHECK --interval=30s --timeout=5s --start-period=20s --retries=3 \
    CMD ["/usr/local/bin/zoomies", "healthcheck", "--url", "http://127.0.0.1:8080"]
ENTRYPOINT ["/usr/local/bin/zoomies"]
CMD ["controller"]

# The agent needs a shell only when it uses the process backend; for the
# container backends distroless is enough. It talks to the Docker or Podman
# socket, which is bind-mounted in.
FROM gcr.io/distroless/static-debian12:nonroot@sha256:afa5c872c891853ca7fcf1f12c3edb23f7eeef36189728842dd51042ff57f7ab AS agent
# Re-declared after FROM for the same reason the controller's are: the ARGs set
# in the build stage are out of scope here, and a label written from one that is
# not in scope is silently empty.
ARG VERSION=dev
ARG COMMIT=""
ARG DATE=""
# This target went unpublished for as long as it has existed, so nothing ever
# noticed it had no labels. Now that it is published it makes the same promise
# every other image here makes -- say what you are without being started.
LABEL org.opencontainers.image.title="zoomies-agent" \
      org.opencontainers.image.description="Zoomies agent: runs a runner fleet on one host for a controller" \
      org.opencontainers.image.source="https://github.com/eyupio/zoomies" \
      org.opencontainers.image.url="https://zoomies.sh" \
      org.opencontainers.image.documentation="https://zoomies.sh/hosts/" \
      org.opencontainers.image.vendor="EyUp.io" \
      org.opencontainers.image.licenses="AGPL-3.0-only" \
      org.opencontainers.image.version="${VERSION}" \
      org.opencontainers.image.revision="${COMMIT}" \
      org.opencontainers.image.created="${DATE}"
COPY --from=build /out/zoomies /usr/local/bin/zoomies
COPY --from=build --chown=65532:65532 /out/state /var/lib/zoomies
USER 65532:65532
ENV ZOOMIES_STATE_DIR=/var/lib/zoomies
VOLUME ["/var/lib/zoomies"]
ENTRYPOINT ["/usr/local/bin/zoomies"]
CMD ["agent"]

# The Zoomies runner image.
#
# It carries the actions/runner release and its .NET dependencies, and an
# entrypoint that understands the environment contract Zoomies' backends use.
# Built for linux/amd64 and linux/arm64.
#
# One file builds every variant in internal/naming's catalogue -- Ubuntu 24.04
# and 22.04, Debian 12, Fedora and Rocky Linux -- published as
# ghcr.io/eyupio/zoomies-runner:<os>-<version>. That <os>-<version> is the same
# string a Zoomies pool name carries, so an operator can read a pool name and
# know which image its runners boot. The variant is chosen with build
# arguments:
#
#   docker build -f deploy/Dockerfile.runner \
#     --build-arg BASE=debian:12-slim@sha256:88200866dfff7ea7f5cbcb6ec7c8a701889efe6fe859fe64d6990e4b07ea4171 --build-arg OS_FAMILY=apt \
#     --build-arg OS_ID=debian --build-arg OS_VERSION=12 \
#     -t ghcr.io/eyupio/zoomies-runner:debian-12 .
#
# Everything a distribution names differently lives in deploy/runner-*.sh, one
# script per concern, each branching on the package family. That is deliberate:
# the alternative is a chain of shell conditionals inside a RUN, where nobody
# can read one distribution's list without reading all of them.
#
# Alpine is absent on purpose. actions/runner ships glibc binaries and .NET
# dependencies that musl does not satisfy, so an Alpine image would build and
# then fail at the first job.
#
# It also carries the toolchain a build typically reaches for -- a compiler, the
# headers native extensions link against, python3 and node. That is a reversal:
# this file used to argue that a runner should stay small because a smaller
# image means a faster cold start, and that what a job needs beyond the runner
# belongs in its own setup steps.
#
# The argument was sound while an image was pulled in front of the job that
# needed it. It is not any more. A pool's image is prewarmed on every host that
# can run the pool, and images.refresh_interval re-runs that prewarm, so the
# pull happens on a timer in the background and the job finds the image already
# there. What is left of "large image" is disk on the host, not queue wait.
#
# Against that, a runner missing cc is a workflow that fails in the middle, on
# somebody else's afternoon, with an error about a missing compiler rather than
# about this image. Parity with what actions/runner-images ships is the less
# surprising default, and a pool that wants something leaner can name its own.
#
# Three targets come out of this file:
#
#   runner         the image above, published as ghcr.io/eyupio/zoomies-runner
#   runner-docker  that plus the Docker CLI, published as
#                  ghcr.io/eyupio/zoomies-runner-docker
#   runner-full    runner-docker plus the language toolchains, published as
#                  ghcr.io/eyupio/zoomies-runner-full for the Ubuntu variants
#
# The second exists because a pool's docker_mode gives a job a *daemon* and
# nothing else. Without a client on PATH, `docker/setup-qemu-action` and every
# other step that shells out to docker dies with "Unable to locate executable
# file: docker", which says nothing about the daemon being right there. The
# split keeps that cost off the pools that never build an image.
#
# `runner` is the last stage on purpose, so that a plain `docker build -f
# deploy/Dockerfile.runner .` still produces the plain runner; the variant is
# built with --target runner-docker.

ARG RUNNER_VERSION=2.337.0
# The SHA-256 GitHub publishes for each release archive, from the release
# notes; internal/backend/runner_digests.go carries the same values for the
# process backend, and the runner-version workflow moves all of them together.
ARG RUNNER_SHA256_X64=70920811a4f8ad4328818682bca5c6469c1c942fab52448868071d0063816613
ARG RUNNER_SHA256_ARM64=9b1dc70626422526e3c94767cf024896beb15da5342a3f4819bf2feac13e0393
ARG BASE=ubuntu:24.04@sha256:224a1869083a311ef3f13648a154ba79832fbef6364d31493642ca03082da254

FROM ${BASE} AS runner-base
# Re-declared after FROM: an ARG from before it is out of scope in the build
# stage, and the labels below would otherwise record empty strings.
ARG BASE
ARG RUNNER_VERSION
ARG RUNNER_SHA256_X64
ARG RUNNER_SHA256_ARM64
ARG TARGETARCH

# OS_FAMILY selects the package manager: "apt" for Ubuntu and Debian, "dnf" for
# Fedora and Rocky. It is a build argument rather than something detected at
# build time so that a typo fails the build rather than quietly producing an
# image missing half its dependencies.
ARG OS_FAMILY=apt
# OS_ID and OS_VERSION are what this variant claims to be. They become image
# labels and environment, which is what `docker inspect` and the entrypoint's
# first log line read to confirm a running container is the platform its pool
# asked for.
ARG OS_ID=ubuntu
ARG OS_VERSION=24.04
# Only stable metadata belongs on the shared base. Release arguments are
# declared on the final targets, after every package installation, because
# all RUN instructions implicitly consume the arguments already in scope.
LABEL org.opencontainers.image.title="zoomies-runner" \
      org.opencontainers.image.description="GitHub Actions runner image for Zoomies" \
      org.opencontainers.image.source="https://github.com/eyupio/zoomies" \
      org.opencontainers.image.url="https://zoomies.sh" \
      org.opencontainers.image.documentation="https://zoomies.sh/hosts-and-pools/" \
      org.opencontainers.image.vendor="EyUp.io" \
      org.opencontainers.image.licenses="AGPL-3.0-only" \
      org.opencontainers.image.base.name="${BASE}" \
      io.zoomies.runner-version="${RUNNER_VERSION}" \
      io.zoomies.os="${OS_ID}" \
      io.zoomies.os-version="${OS_VERSION}" \
      io.zoomies.os-family="${OS_FAMILY}"

ENV DEBIAN_FRONTEND=noninteractive \
    RUNNER_MANUALLY_TRAP_SIG=1 \
    ACTIONS_RUNNER_PRINT_LOG_TO_STDOUT=1

# git, curl, ca-certificates and jq are what essentially every workflow assumes
# exists. actions/runner's own .NET dependencies are installed further down by
# the tarball's installdependencies.sh, which knows each distribution's names
# for them -- naming them here is what made this file Ubuntu-24.04-only.
#
# The apt and dnf helpers accompany every script that installs packages,
# here and below: they recover from stale indexes and repository metadata
# skew. Each step removes its helpers after installation.
COPY --chmod=0755 deploy/runner-dnf.sh /tmp/
COPY --chmod=0755 deploy/runner-apt.sh deploy/runner-packages.sh /tmp/
RUN /tmp/runner-packages.sh "${OS_FAMILY}" && rm /tmp/runner-packages.sh /tmp/runner-apt.sh /tmp/runner-dnf.sh
ENV LANG=en_US.UTF-8

# The runner must not be root. It gets passwordless sudo because a great many
# real workflows expect it; a pool that does not want that can override the
# entrypoint's user.
#
# uid 1001 rather than 1000: Fedora and Rocky leave 1000 free but Ubuntu's
# cloud images take it, and a fixed uid is what lets a host bind-mount a work
# directory the runner can actually write to.
#
# sudo resets the environment by default, and the proxy variables the agent
# hands every runner on a host behind a proxy went with it: `curl` in a step
# reached the internet and `sudo apt-get install` in the next one timed out,
# which reads as a broken mirror rather than a dropped proxy. env_keep carries
# exactly the six names internal/backend/proxy.go passes on, and a test there
# holds the two lists together. visudo checks the file, because sudo refuses
# to run at all over a sudoers.d entry it cannot parse.
#
# RPM bases ship shadow with mode 0000. PAM's setuid helper cannot read it on
# every container runtime; give its root owner read access without exposing
# it to the runner or bypassing PAM's account checks.
RUN set -eux; \
    groupadd -g 1001 runner 2>/dev/null || true; \
    useradd -m -s /bin/bash -u 1001 -g 1001 runner; \
    if [ "${OS_FAMILY}" = dnf ]; then chmod 0400 /etc/shadow; fi; \
    mkdir -p /etc/sudoers.d; \
    { \
      echo 'Defaults:runner env_keep += "HTTP_PROXY HTTPS_PROXY NO_PROXY http_proxy https_proxy no_proxy"'; \
      echo "runner ALL=(ALL) NOPASSWD: ALL"; \
    } > /etc/sudoers.d/runner; \
    chmod 0440 /etc/sudoers.d/runner; \
    if ! grep -Eq '^[[:space:]]*(@|#)includedir[[:space:]]+/etc/sudoers.d([[:space:]]|$)' /etc/sudoers; then \
      printf '\n#includedir /etc/sudoers.d\n' >> /etc/sudoers; \
    fi; \
    visudo -c; \
    su -s /bin/sh runner -c 'sudo -n true'; \
    su -s /bin/sh runner -c 'HTTPS_PROXY=http://proxy.invalid:3128 no_proxy=.invalid sudo -n env' > /tmp/runner-sudo-env; \
    grep -qx 'HTTPS_PROXY=http://proxy.invalid:3128' /tmp/runner-sudo-env; \
    grep -qx 'no_proxy=.invalid' /tmp/runner-sudo-env; \
    rm /tmp/runner-sudo-env

# Two directories the runner must own before anything is mounted over them.
#
# /opt/hostedtoolcache is the tool cache: where setup-python, setup-node,
# setup-go and the rest unpack what they download, named for the path GitHub's
# own runners use. Left to its default, the runner puts it under _work/_tool,
# which an ephemeral runner throws away with every job; here it is a fixed
# place that an image built FROM this one can fill ahead of time, so those
# steps find the version already there rather than downloading it again.
#
# /opt/zoomies-cache is where a pool's cache is mounted. A fresh named volume
# takes its ownership from the directory it is mounted over, and with no such
# directory in the image it came up owned by root: the pool cache existed, and
# the runner could not write a byte to it without sudo. Owned by the runner
# here, a new volume is the runner's too.
RUN set -eux; \
    install -d -o runner -g runner -m 0755 /opt/hostedtoolcache /opt/zoomies-cache
ENV AGENT_TOOLSDIRECTORY=/opt/hostedtoolcache

# The archive is checked against the digest GitHub published before it is
# unpacked: this image runs whatever is inside it, on every job, and a mirror
# or a proxy between the build and github.com is a place to substitute it.
# The dependency script is allowed to fail the build, too. It used to be
# silenced, which shipped an image that was missing a library the runner dies
# without on the first job rather than failing here, where the log says why.
#
# It is GitHub's script and installs the runner's .NET dependencies with the
# distribution's package manager, so it is exposed to the same archive mirror
# that is briefly out of step with its own index as everything
# deploy/runner-apt.sh covers. It cannot use that helper -- it is not ours to
# edit -- so the attempts are here instead, and the last one still fails the
# build.
WORKDIR /home/runner
RUN set -eux; \
    case "${TARGETARCH}" in \
      amd64) RUNNER_ARCH=x64; RUNNER_SHA256="${RUNNER_SHA256_X64}" ;; \
      arm64) RUNNER_ARCH=arm64; RUNNER_SHA256="${RUNNER_SHA256_ARM64}" ;; \
      *) echo "unsupported architecture: ${TARGETARCH}" >&2; exit 1 ;; \
    esac; \
    curl -fsSL -o runner.tar.gz \
      "https://github.com/actions/runner/releases/download/v${RUNNER_VERSION}/actions-runner-linux-${RUNNER_ARCH}-${RUNNER_VERSION}.tar.gz"; \
    echo "${RUNNER_SHA256}  runner.tar.gz" | sha256sum -c -; \
    tar xzf runner.tar.gz; \
    rm runner.tar.gz; \
    for attempt in 1 2 3; do \
      if ./bin/installdependencies.sh; then break; fi; \
      [ "$attempt" -lt 3 ] || exit 1; \
      echo "installdependencies.sh failed; trying again in $((attempt * 10))s" >&2; \
      sleep $((attempt * 10)); \
    done; \
    rm -rf /var/lib/apt/lists/*; \
    mkdir -p /home/runner/_work; \
    chown -R runner:runner /home/runner

# The build toolchain, after the runner download on purpose: this list is the
# part of the image most likely to be edited, and putting it last means editing
# it does not re-fetch the ~200 MB archive above. What is in it, and what is
# deliberately not, is in deploy/runner-toolchain.sh.
COPY --chmod=0755 deploy/runner-dnf.sh /tmp/
COPY --chmod=0755 deploy/runner-apt.sh deploy/runner-toolchain.sh /tmp/
RUN /tmp/runner-toolchain.sh "${OS_FAMILY}" && rm /tmp/runner-toolchain.sh /tmp/runner-apt.sh /tmp/runner-dnf.sh

# The GitHub CLI, from GitHub's own repository because no distribution here
# carries it.
COPY --chmod=0755 deploy/runner-dnf.sh /tmp/
COPY --chmod=0755 deploy/runner-apt.sh deploy/runner-gh.sh /tmp/
RUN /tmp/runner-gh.sh "${OS_FAMILY}" && rm /tmp/runner-gh.sh /tmp/runner-apt.sh /tmp/runner-dnf.sh

# ShellCheck, which GitHub's hosted runners carry and shell-linting workflows
# assume; deploy/runner-shellcheck.sh says why it is a pinned download.
COPY --chmod=0755 deploy/runner-shellcheck.sh /tmp/
RUN /tmp/runner-shellcheck.sh "${TARGETARCH}" && rm /tmp/runner-shellcheck.sh

# Prove the toolchain is actually reachable, for the same reason the Docker
# variant checks its client: a package that installed but left nothing on PATH
# is the failure this exists to prevent, and it is far cheaper to catch in the
# build than in somebody's workflow. It is also what keeps the two families'
# package lists honest -- they are not translations of each other, and this is
# what says whether each one is complete.
RUN set -eux; \
    cc --version; \
    make --version; \
    cmake --version; \
    python3 --version; \
    node --version; \
    npm --version; \
    git lfs version; \
    gh --version; \
    shellcheck --version

# The fleet's own packages, last, so that editing the list costs one package
# install rather than the whole toolchain above -- and so that a build with
# EXTRA_PACKAGES set is cheap enough for CI to run one on every variant, which
# is what keeps this build argument from quietly ceasing to work.
COPY --chmod=0755 deploy/runner-dnf.sh /tmp/
COPY --chmod=0755 deploy/runner-apt.sh deploy/runner-extra.sh /tmp/
# Declare this only at its installation step so changing the package list
# reuses the runner download and toolchain layers above.
ARG EXTRA_PACKAGES=""
RUN /tmp/runner-extra.sh "${OS_FAMILY}" ${EXTRA_PACKAGES} && rm /tmp/runner-extra.sh /tmp/runner-apt.sh /tmp/runner-dnf.sh

COPY --chmod=0755 deploy/runner-entrypoint.sh /usr/local/bin/entrypoint.sh
COPY --chmod=0755 deploy/runner-inventory.sh /usr/local/lib/zoomies/runner-inventory.sh

# What this image is, for the entrypoint's first log line and for a job that
# wants to branch on it. A pool pointed at the wrong variant otherwise shows up
# as a missing package several minutes into a workflow.
ENV ZOOMIES_RUNNER_OS="${OS_ID}" \
    ZOOMIES_RUNNER_OS_VERSION="${OS_VERSION}" \
    ZOOMIES_RUNNER_VERSION="${RUNNER_VERSION}"

RUN mkdir -p /usr/local/share/zoomies && /usr/local/lib/zoomies/runner-inventory.sh > /usr/local/share/zoomies/installed-software.json
USER runner
ENV RUNNER_ALLOW_RUNASROOT=0
ENTRYPOINT ["/usr/local/bin/entrypoint.sh"]


# --- runner-docker ------------------------------------------------------------
#
# The Docker CLI, buildx and compose, for pools whose docker_mode is dind or
# host-socket. Only the client: the daemon is the pool's business, and this
# image never starts one.
#
# From Docker's own apt repository rather than Ubuntu's docker.io package,
# because that one drags in the daemon, containerd and runc -- a few hundred MB
# of software this image must never run.
FROM runner-base AS runner-docker
ARG OS_FAMILY
ARG OS_ID
USER root

COPY --chmod=0755 deploy/runner-dnf.sh /tmp/
COPY --chmod=0755 deploy/runner-apt.sh deploy/runner-docker-cli.sh /tmp/
RUN /tmp/runner-docker-cli.sh "${OS_FAMILY}" "${OS_ID}" && rm /tmp/runner-docker-cli.sh /tmp/runner-apt.sh /tmp/runner-dnf.sh
# Prove the client landed somewhere the runner will actually find it: a plugin
# installed but unreachable is the same failure as no client at all, and it is
# far cheaper to catch here than in somebody's workflow.
RUN set -eux; \
    docker --version; \
    docker buildx version
RUN mkdir -p /usr/local/share/zoomies && /usr/local/lib/zoomies/runner-inventory.sh > /usr/local/share/zoomies/installed-software.json
USER runner

# Stamp the finished image without invalidating its Docker CLI installation.
ARG VERSION=dev
ARG COMMIT=""
ARG DATE=""
LABEL org.opencontainers.image.title="zoomies-runner-docker" \
      org.opencontainers.image.description="GitHub Actions runner image for Zoomies, with the Docker CLI" \
      org.opencontainers.image.version="${VERSION}" \
      org.opencontainers.image.revision="${COMMIT}" \
      org.opencontainers.image.created="${DATE}"


# --- runner-full --------------------------------------------------------------
#
# runner-docker plus the language toolchains the setup-* actions would
# otherwise download at the start of every job: Python, Node.js, Go and Java in
# the tool cache, laid out exactly as setup-python, setup-node, setup-go and
# setup-java look for them, and .NET, Maven, Gradle and Rust where a workflow
# finds them without a setup action. Which releases is deploy/toolcache.lock,
# every archive pinned by digest; deploy/runner-toolcache.sh is how each one
# lands.
#
# Published as ghcr.io/eyupio/zoomies-runner-full, for the Ubuntu variants
# only: the Python builds setup-python installs are made for Ubuntu and nothing
# else, and a full image without them would be the one toolchain most jobs ask
# for first. It is built on runner-docker because a pool that wants a build
# environment wants to build images in it too, and the client is a rounding
# error beside the rest.
#
# One layer per toolchain, so a lock change that moves one Node patch rebuilds
# that layer and not the other several gigabytes.
FROM runner-docker AS runner-full
ARG OS_VERSION
ARG TARGETARCH
USER root

# Rust's homes are fixed paths rather than the runner's ~/.cargo, so that the
# image can put them on PATH; the runner owns them, so rustup can still add a
# toolchain a workflow asks for.
ENV RUSTUP_HOME=/usr/local/rustup \
    CARGO_HOME=/usr/local/cargo

COPY --chmod=0755 deploy/runner-toolcache.sh /usr/local/lib/zoomies/runner-toolcache.sh
COPY deploy/toolcache.lock /usr/local/lib/zoomies/toolcache.lock
RUN /usr/local/lib/zoomies/runner-toolcache.sh /usr/local/lib/zoomies/toolcache.lock "${OS_VERSION}" "${TARGETARCH}" python \
    && chown -R runner:runner "${AGENT_TOOLSDIRECTORY}/Python"
RUN /usr/local/lib/zoomies/runner-toolcache.sh /usr/local/lib/zoomies/toolcache.lock "${OS_VERSION}" "${TARGETARCH}" node \
    && chown -R runner:runner "${AGENT_TOOLSDIRECTORY}/node"
RUN /usr/local/lib/zoomies/runner-toolcache.sh /usr/local/lib/zoomies/toolcache.lock "${OS_VERSION}" "${TARGETARCH}" go \
    && chown -R runner:runner "${AGENT_TOOLSDIRECTORY}/go"
RUN /usr/local/lib/zoomies/runner-toolcache.sh /usr/local/lib/zoomies/toolcache.lock "${OS_VERSION}" "${TARGETARCH}" java \
    && chown -R runner:runner "${AGENT_TOOLSDIRECTORY}/Java_Temurin-Hotspot_jdk"
# setup-dotnet installs into /usr/share/dotnet as the runner, so the runner
# owns it; otherwise asking for an SDK the image lacks fails on permissions.
RUN /usr/local/lib/zoomies/runner-toolcache.sh /usr/local/lib/zoomies/toolcache.lock "${OS_VERSION}" "${TARGETARCH}" dotnet \
    && chown -R runner:runner /usr/share/dotnet
RUN /usr/local/lib/zoomies/runner-toolcache.sh /usr/local/lib/zoomies/toolcache.lock "${OS_VERSION}" "${TARGETARCH}" maven \
    && /usr/local/lib/zoomies/runner-toolcache.sh /usr/local/lib/zoomies/toolcache.lock "${OS_VERSION}" "${TARGETARCH}" gradle
RUN /usr/local/lib/zoomies/runner-toolcache.sh /usr/local/lib/zoomies/toolcache.lock "${OS_VERSION}" "${TARGETARCH}" rustup \
    && chown -R runner:runner "${RUSTUP_HOME}" "${CARGO_HOME}"

# JDK 17 is the default GitHub's Ubuntu runners give a job that does not ask,
# and the same here; setup-java replaces it for one that does. Maven and Gradle
# need a JAVA_HOME before either will start.
ENV JAVA_HOME=/usr/lib/jvm/temurin-17 \
    PATH=/usr/local/cargo/bin:/usr/lib/jvm/temurin-17/bin:${PATH} \
    DOTNET_ROOT=/usr/share/dotnet \
    DOTNET_NOLOGO=1 \
    DOTNET_CLI_TELEMETRY_OPTOUT=1 \
    DOTNET_SKIP_FIRST_TIME_EXPERIENCE=1

# Prove each toolchain answers from where a job will look for it, as the
# other targets do for theirs.
RUN set -eux; \
    java -version; \
    mvn --version; \
    gradle --version --no-daemon; \
    dotnet --list-sdks; \
    rustc --version; \
    cargo --version; \
    cargo clippy --version; \
    rustfmt --version
RUN mkdir -p /usr/local/share/zoomies && /usr/local/lib/zoomies/runner-inventory.sh > /usr/local/share/zoomies/installed-software.json
USER runner

ARG VERSION=dev
ARG COMMIT=""
ARG DATE=""
LABEL org.opencontainers.image.title="zoomies-runner-full" \
      org.opencontainers.image.description="GitHub Actions runner image for Zoomies, with the Docker CLI and the language toolchains setup-* actions install" \
      org.opencontainers.image.version="${VERSION}" \
      org.opencontainers.image.revision="${COMMIT}" \
      org.opencontainers.image.created="${DATE}"


# --- runner -------------------------------------------------------------------
#
# The default target: the runner and the build toolchain, without the Docker
# client. Last in the file so that a bare build with no --target produces it.
FROM runner-base AS runner
ARG VERSION=dev
ARG COMMIT=""
ARG DATE=""
LABEL org.opencontainers.image.version="${VERSION}" \
      org.opencontainers.image.revision="${COMMIT}" \
      org.opencontainers.image.created="${DATE}"

# The reverse proxy in front of the controller, when this deployment gets its
# certificate automatically.
#
# Zoomies terminates TLS itself when it is handed a certificate, so this exists
# for the one case it cannot cover: no certificate to hand, and no Cloudflare.
# Caddy asks Let's Encrypt for one, renews it, and redirects port 80 to 443 on
# its own -- which is the whole of what is needed and the reason the file is
# this short.
#
# It proxies to the controller on loopback, so the controller is never
# published to the internet itself.
{
	__ZOOMIES_ACME_GLOBAL__
}

__ZOOMIES_HOSTNAME__ {
	# X-Forwarded-For is set by Caddy, and the controller believes it because
	# the answer file names this proxy in trusted_proxies. Without that pair,
	# every audit row would record the proxy and the login rate limiter would
	# throttle the whole internet as one caller.
	reverse_proxy __ZOOMIES_PUBLISH_ADDR__:8080
}

# The marketplace deployment package

What a VPS provider needs to offer Zoomies as a one-click deployment, and what
an operator can run by hand to get the same result.

It deploys **a controller**. Zoomies is self-hosted and
bring-your-own-infrastructure: this puts the always-on half on one instance, and
the runner capacity stays yours. The default install also runs an agent on that
instance, so it can execute jobs from the first minute; set `ZOOMIES_MODE` to
`controller` when the runners live elsewhere.

## The files

| File | What it is |
| --- | --- |
| `release.env` | The release this package installs: the controller image by tag and digest, the installer and its checksum, and the version a joining agent is given. Hand-edited when a new release becomes the baseline. |
| `images.lock` | Every image that release publishes, and the digest each tag resolved to. Generated by `make marketplace-lock`. |
| `inputs.env.example` | The settings that differ between one customer and the next. Copy it, fill it in. |
| `answers.yaml.tmpl` | The answers `zoomies init` is given, with the instance's own values still to substitute. |
| `bootstrap.sh` | First boot: install a container runtime, render the answers, run the pinned installer, wait for health, put a certificate holder in front if one is wanted, leave a note. |
| `Caddyfile.tmpl`, `proxy-compose.yml.tmpl` | The certificate holder, for `ZOOMIES_TLS=acme`. |
| `tunnel-compose.yml.tmpl` | The Cloudflare Tunnel daemon, for `ZOOMIES_TLS=tunnel`. |
| `cloud-init.yaml.tmpl` | The cloud-config the three files above are rendered into. |
| `render.sh` | Does the rendering. |

## Using it

```sh
cp inputs.env.example inputs.env
$EDITOR inputs.env                 # at minimum, the hostname
./render.sh inputs.env > cloud-init.yaml
```

Boot an Ubuntu 24.04 LTS instance with `cloud-init.yaml` as its user data. When
it comes up, `/etc/zoomies/first-login.txt` says how to finish: read the setup
token from the controller's log, create the first administrator in the browser,
connect GitHub, make a pool.

## What it will not do

**It carries no secret you have an alternative to.** Not the GitHub App's
private key, not the webhook secret, not an administrator password, not a join
token. A Cloudflare Tunnel token is the single exception, and it is optional:
leave it out and the instance still boots ready for you to paste it over SSH. Everything a provider's
form collects becomes instance metadata, which is readable by anything on the
instance that can reach the metadata service, kept in the provider's own
database, and printed in cloud-init's log — and a credential that has been
copied to all three places cannot be rotated out of them. `render.sh` refuses an
inputs file that sets one.

So the parts that need a credential happen afterwards, in the browser, over the
connection the operator already trusts. The first administrator is created with
the setup token the controller prints while no account exists; GitHub is
connected from the UI by an administrator who is already signed in.

**It offers no plain-HTTP public endpoint.** The origin often speaks HTTP —
that is what three of the five arrangements do — but something in front always
holds a certificate for the public name: a Cloudflare Tunnel dialling out from
this instance, Cloudflare in front of a published origin, a proxy here with a
certificate from Let's Encrypt, Zoomies itself with one you supply, or a load
balancer of yours. An unrecognised `ZOOMIES_TLS` is refused by name rather than
defaulted. [docs/marketplace.md](../../docs/marketplace.md) has all five, and
the table of which proxy each one believes.

**It has not been tested on a provider yet.** The implementation is complete and
its rendering is checked by tests in `internal/docs`; a pristine-VPS run, the
first-workflow journey and a pilot review are separate work and are not claimed
here.

# The answers `zoomies init` is given on this instance's first boot.
#
# Rendered by bootstrap.sh into /etc/zoomies/answers.yaml. Every key is one
# question the interactive installer would have asked, so this file is also the
# record of what setup decided -- worth reading before wondering why the
# controller came up the way it did.
#
# What is deliberately absent matters as much as what is here: no GitHub App
# credentials, no webhook secret and no administrator password. A containerised
# deployment creates its first administrator in the browser, and GitHub is
# connected there too, so nothing secret has to survive in instance metadata or
# on this disk to get from a booted image to a working fleet.

# single runs an agent inside the controller; controller runs none.
mode: __ZOOMIES_MODE__

# compose, because upgrading is then pulling one pinned image, and because the
# database lives in a volume the installer never opens -- which is what makes
# the browser-side administrator bootstrap the supported path.
deployment: compose
deployment_dir: /etc/zoomies
image: __ZOOMIES_CONTROLLER_IMAGE__
config_dir: /etc/zoomies

backend: docker

# For a containerised deployment this is the address the container is published
# on, not the listener: inside the container Zoomies always binds :8080, and
# what is chosen here is what the host exposes. Loopback means only this
# instance and whatever proxies from it can connect, which is what every
# arrangement except a certificate of your own wants.
bind: __ZOOMIES_BIND__

tls:
  # Quoted: an unquoted off is a boolean in YAML, not a word.
  #
  # "files" means Zoomies terminates TLS itself with the certificate below and
  # is published straight on 443. Anything else means something in front holds
  # the certificate -- the bundled proxy, or a load balancer of the provider's.
  mode: "__ZOOMIES_TLS_MODE__"
  # Empty unless the mode is files. The paths are the host's, and the
  # deployment mounts them into the container unchanged.
  cert_file: __ZOOMIES_TLS_CERT_FILE__
  key_file: __ZOOMIES_TLS_KEY_FILE__

trusted_proxies: [__ZOOMIES_TRUSTED_PROXIES__]

# How GitHub and the browser reach this controller.
external_url: __ZOOMIES_EXTERNAL_URL__

github:
  # Connected in the UI, by an administrator who is already signed in. The
  # unattended path would need an App's private key and webhook secret in this
  # file, which is exactly what a marketplace form must not collect.
  skip: true

#!/bin/sh
# First boot of a Zoomies instance deployed from a provider's marketplace.
#
# It is deliberately dull: install a container runtime, write an answer file,
# run the pinned installer, and leave a note saying how to finish. Everything
# that needs a secret -- the first administrator, the GitHub App -- happens
# afterwards in the browser, because a marketplace form's answers live in
# instance metadata and a boot log, and neither is a place for a credential.
#
# It is rendered into a cloud-config by render.sh and runs as root, once. A
# second run is safe: each step checks what is already there, so a boot that
# failed halfway can be resumed by running this again.
#
# Failure is loud and final. A half-built controller that answers on :8080 is
# worse than one that never started, because the first thing an operator does
# with a reachable Zoomies is point GitHub at it.
set -eu

# The paths are overridable so that the test suite can run the rendering half
# of this script against a temporary directory and check that a real boot would
# write an answer file `zoomies init` accepts. Proving that without a VM is
# worth a seam: the alternative is a test that reimplements the substitution
# below and then agrees with itself while the boot fails.
ENV_FILE=${ZOOMIES_ENV_FILE:-/etc/zoomies/marketplace.env}
ANSWERS_TMPL=${ZOOMIES_ANSWERS_TEMPLATE:-/etc/zoomies/answers.yaml.tmpl}
ANSWERS=${ZOOMIES_ANSWERS_FILE:-/etc/zoomies/answers.yaml}
CADDY_TMPL=${ZOOMIES_CADDY_TEMPLATE:-/etc/zoomies/Caddyfile.tmpl}
PROXY_TMPL=${ZOOMIES_PROXY_TEMPLATE:-/etc/zoomies/proxy-compose.yml.tmpl}
PROXY_DIR=${ZOOMIES_PROXY_DIR:-/etc/zoomies/proxy}
TUNNEL_TMPL=${ZOOMIES_TUNNEL_TEMPLATE:-/etc/zoomies/tunnel-compose.yml.tmpl}
TUNNEL_DIR=${ZOOMIES_TUNNEL_DIR:-/etc/zoomies/tunnel}
NOTES=${ZOOMIES_NOTES_FILE:-/etc/zoomies/first-login.txt}
LOG_TAG=zoomies-bootstrap

say() { echo "[$LOG_TAG] $*"; }
die() { echo "[$LOG_TAG] $*" >&2; exit 1; }

# ---------------------------------------------------------------- the inputs

[ -r "$ENV_FILE" ] || die "$ENV_FILE is missing; the image was rendered without its inputs"
# shellcheck disable=SC1090
. "$ENV_FILE"

: "${ZOOMIES_RELEASE:?the rendered inputs name no release}"
: "${ZOOMIES_INSTALLER_URL:?the rendered inputs name no installer}"
: "${ZOOMIES_INSTALLER_SHA256:?the rendered inputs name no installer checksum}"
ZOOMIES_PROXY_IMAGE=${ZOOMIES_PROXY_IMAGE:-}
ZOOMIES_TUNNEL_IMAGE=${ZOOMIES_TUNNEL_IMAGE:-}
ZOOMIES_TUNNEL_TOKEN=${ZOOMIES_TUNNEL_TOKEN:-}

ZOOMIES_HOSTNAME=${ZOOMIES_HOSTNAME:-}
[ -n "$ZOOMIES_HOSTNAME" ] || die "no hostname was given: set ZOOMIES_HOSTNAME to the DNS name that points at this instance"

ZOOMIES_MODE=${ZOOMIES_MODE:-single}
case "$ZOOMIES_MODE" in
  single|controller) ;;
  *) die "mode $ZOOMIES_MODE is not one this package installs: use single or controller" ;;
esac

# Who holds the certificate for the public name. Refusing an unknown value by
# name beats publishing an origin to the internet in the clear because an input
# was spelled in a way nothing here reads.
#
# Three of the four leave the controller speaking plain HTTP, which is correct:
# the origin is not the public endpoint, and something in front of it is.
ZOOMIES_TLS=${ZOOMIES_TLS:-acme}
case "$ZOOMIES_TLS" in
  acme|files|tunnel|cloudflare|off) ;;
  *) die "TLS mode $ZOOMIES_TLS is not one this package installs: use acme, files, tunnel, cloudflare or off" ;;
esac

ZOOMIES_ACME_EMAIL=${ZOOMIES_ACME_EMAIL:-}
ZOOMIES_TLS_CERT_FILE=${ZOOMIES_TLS_CERT_FILE:-}
ZOOMIES_TLS_KEY_FILE=${ZOOMIES_TLS_KEY_FILE:-}
if [ "$ZOOMIES_TLS" = "files" ]; then
  [ -n "$ZOOMIES_TLS_CERT_FILE" ] && [ -n "$ZOOMIES_TLS_KEY_FILE" ] || \
    die "TLS mode files needs ZOOMIES_TLS_CERT_FILE and ZOOMIES_TLS_KEY_FILE: the certificate this instance serves, and its key"
fi

# The listener, what the instance exposes, and which proxies it believes.
#
# The last of those is the one that goes wrong silently. X-Forwarded-For is
# read only from a peer in trusted_proxies, and CF-Connecting-IP only from a
# peer that is Cloudflare's own edge -- so the right answer differs between
# Cloudflare in front of a published origin and a tunnel, even though both are
# Cloudflare. Getting it wrong costs every audit row the real client's address
# and throttles the whole internet as one caller, and nothing reports it.
case "$ZOOMIES_TLS" in
  files)
    # The only arrangement where Zoomies itself is the public endpoint.
    ZOOMIES_PUBLISH_ADDR=${ZOOMIES_PUBLISH_ADDR:-0.0.0.0}
    ZOOMIES_TRUSTED_PROXIES=${ZOOMIES_TRUSTED_PROXIES:-127.0.0.1/32,::1/128}
    ZOOMIES_BIND=0.0.0.0:443
    ZOOMIES_TLS_MODE=files
    # -k, because the question is whether the controller is answering, not
    # whether a certificate issued for the public name matches 127.0.0.1.
    HEALTH_URL=https://127.0.0.1/healthz
    HEALTH_CURL_OPTS=-k
    ;;
  cloudflare)
    # Cloudflare's edge connects to a published origin over plain HTTP on 80,
    # so the peer is Cloudflare and the word expands to its ranges -- which is
    # what makes CF-Connecting-IP, the one header a client cannot forge, count.
    ZOOMIES_PUBLISH_ADDR=${ZOOMIES_PUBLISH_ADDR:-0.0.0.0}
    ZOOMIES_BIND=$ZOOMIES_PUBLISH_ADDR:80
    ZOOMIES_TLS_MODE=off
    ZOOMIES_TRUSTED_PROXIES=${ZOOMIES_TRUSTED_PROXIES:-cloudflare}
    HEALTH_URL=http://127.0.0.1:80/healthz
    HEALTH_CURL_OPTS=
    ;;
  *)
    # acme, tunnel and off all reach the controller on loopback. For a tunnel
    # the peer is cloudflared on this machine rather than Cloudflare's edge, so
    # trusting Cloudflare's ranges would trust nothing that ever connects: the
    # address to believe is the local daemon's, and the header that survives is
    # X-Forwarded-For.
    ZOOMIES_PUBLISH_ADDR=${ZOOMIES_PUBLISH_ADDR:-127.0.0.1}
    ZOOMIES_TRUSTED_PROXIES=${ZOOMIES_TRUSTED_PROXIES:-127.0.0.1/32,::1/128}
    ZOOMIES_BIND=$ZOOMIES_PUBLISH_ADDR:8080
    ZOOMIES_TLS_MODE=off
    HEALTH_URL=http://$ZOOMIES_PUBLISH_ADDR:8080/healthz
    HEALTH_CURL_OPTS=
    ;;
esac

ZOOMIES_EXTERNAL_URL=${ZOOMIES_EXTERNAL_URL:-https://$ZOOMIES_HOSTNAME}
ZOOMIES_DATA_DIR=${ZOOMIES_DATA_DIR:-/var/lib/zoomies}
ZOOMIES_CONTROLLER_IMAGE=${ZOOMIES_CONTROLLER_IMAGE:-}
[ -n "$ZOOMIES_CONTROLLER_IMAGE" ] || die "the rendered inputs name no controller image"

ZOOMIES_ADMIN_BOOTSTRAP=${ZOOMIES_ADMIN_BOOTSTRAP:-setup-token}
[ "$ZOOMIES_ADMIN_BOOTSTRAP" = "setup-token" ] || \
  die "administrator bootstrap $ZOOMIES_ADMIN_BOOTSTRAP is not supported: setup-token is the only one that needs no secret in instance metadata"

say "deploying Zoomies $ZOOMIES_RELEASE for $ZOOMIES_EXTERNAL_URL"

# ------------------------------------------------------------ the dependency

install_runtime() {
  if command -v docker >/dev/null 2>&1 && docker compose version >/dev/null 2>&1; then
    say "a container runtime with compose is already here"
    return 0
  fi
  command -v apt-get >/dev/null 2>&1 || \
    die "no container runtime, and this bootstrap only knows how to install one with apt: install Docker and compose, then run this again"

  say "installing the distribution's Docker and compose packages"
  export DEBIAN_FRONTEND=noninteractive
  # The distribution's own packages rather than a script piped from the
  # internet: this runs unattended on first boot, and a pipeline to a shell is
  # one more thing that can change between the day this was tested and the day
  # somebody deploys it.
  apt-get update -qq
  apt-get install -y -qq docker.io docker-compose-v2 ca-certificates curl
  systemctl enable --now docker
}

# ------------------------------------------------------------------ the data

prepare_data_dir() {
  # A compose deployment keeps the database in a named volume. Backing that
  # volume with a directory chosen here is what lets a provider's attached disk
  # hold it -- and what makes "where is my data" answerable without knowing how
  # Docker lays out its own storage.
  mkdir -p "$ZOOMIES_DATA_DIR"
  # The published image runs as an unprivileged uid that does not exist on this
  # host. A directory owned by anyone else gives "unable to open database file
  # (14)" at the first start, which reads like corruption and is not.
  chown 65532:65532 "$ZOOMIES_DATA_DIR"
  chmod 0750 "$ZOOMIES_DATA_DIR"

  if docker volume inspect zoomies-data >/dev/null 2>&1; then
    say "the zoomies-data volume already exists; leaving it alone"
    return 0
  fi
  say "backing the zoomies-data volume with $ZOOMIES_DATA_DIR"
  docker volume create \
    --driver local \
    --opt type=none \
    --opt "device=$ZOOMIES_DATA_DIR" \
    --opt o=bind \
    zoomies-data >/dev/null
}

# --------------------------------------------------------------- the answers

render_answers() {
  [ -r "$ANSWERS_TMPL" ] || die "$ANSWERS_TMPL is missing; the image was rendered without its answer template"
  umask 077

  # Each CIDR is quoted on the way into the YAML flow sequence. An IPv6 one has
  # to be: ::1/128 unquoted starts a plain scalar with a colon, which is not a
  # scalar at all, and the parser stops on the whole answer file rather than on
  # the setting -- so the loopback default alone would have failed at boot.
  trusted=$(printf '%s' "$ZOOMIES_TRUSTED_PROXIES" | awk -F, '{
    out = ""
    for (i = 1; i <= NF; i++) {
      gsub(/^[ \t]+|[ \t]+$/, "", $i)
      if ($i == "") continue
      out = out (out == "" ? "" : ", ") "\"" $i "\""
    }
    printf "%s", out
  }')

  sed \
    -e "s|__ZOOMIES_MODE__|$ZOOMIES_MODE|g" \
    -e "s|__ZOOMIES_CONTROLLER_IMAGE__|$ZOOMIES_CONTROLLER_IMAGE|g" \
    -e "s|__ZOOMIES_BIND__|$ZOOMIES_BIND|g" \
    -e "s|__ZOOMIES_TLS_MODE__|$ZOOMIES_TLS_MODE|g" \
    -e "s|__ZOOMIES_TLS_CERT_FILE__|$ZOOMIES_TLS_CERT_FILE|g" \
    -e "s|__ZOOMIES_TLS_KEY_FILE__|$ZOOMIES_TLS_KEY_FILE|g" \
    -e "s|__ZOOMIES_TRUSTED_PROXIES__|$trusted|g" \
    -e "s|__ZOOMIES_EXTERNAL_URL__|$ZOOMIES_EXTERNAL_URL|g" \
    "$ANSWERS_TMPL" > "$ANSWERS"

  # A placeholder nobody wired up would otherwise reach `zoomies init` as a
  # literal, and the failure would be a YAML value that looks like a mistake
  # rather than an omission.
  if grep -q '__ZOOMIES_[A-Z_]*__' "$ANSWERS"; then
    die "the answer file still has unfilled placeholders: $(grep -o '__ZOOMIES_[A-Z_]*__' "$ANSWERS" | sort -u | tr '\n' ' ')"
  fi
}

# ------------------------------------------------------------- the installer

run_installer() {
  script=$(mktemp)
  say "fetching the pinned installer"
  curl -fsSL --retry 3 --retry-delay 2 -o "$script" "$ZOOMIES_INSTALLER_URL"

  actual=$(sha256sum "$script" | cut -d' ' -f1)
  if [ "$actual" != "$ZOOMIES_INSTALLER_SHA256" ]; then
    rm -f "$script"
    die "the installer's checksum is $actual and this release pins $ZOOMIES_INSTALLER_SHA256; refusing to run it"
  fi

  say "installing Zoomies $ZOOMIES_RELEASE"
  sh "$script" --answers "$ANSWERS" --version "$ZOOMIES_RELEASE"
  rm -f "$script"
}

# ----------------------------------------------------------------- the proxy

render_proxy() {
  [ "$ZOOMIES_TLS" = "acme" ] || return 0
  [ -r "$CADDY_TMPL" ] && [ -r "$PROXY_TMPL" ] || \
    die "the ACME path needs $CADDY_TMPL and $PROXY_TMPL, and the image was rendered without them"
  [ -n "$ZOOMIES_PROXY_IMAGE" ] || die "the rendered inputs name no proxy image, so the ACME path has nothing to run"

  say "writing the configuration for a certificate holder in front of the controller"
  mkdir -p "$PROXY_DIR" "$ZOOMIES_DATA_DIR/caddy"

  # An empty email is not the same as no email: "email" alone is not a
  # directive, so the whole line goes rather than its value.
  acme_global=""
  [ -n "$ZOOMIES_ACME_EMAIL" ] && acme_global="email $ZOOMIES_ACME_EMAIL"

  sed \
    -e "s|__ZOOMIES_ACME_GLOBAL__|$acme_global|g" \
    -e "s|__ZOOMIES_HOSTNAME__|$ZOOMIES_HOSTNAME|g" \
    -e "s|__ZOOMIES_PUBLISH_ADDR__|$ZOOMIES_PUBLISH_ADDR|g" \
    "$CADDY_TMPL" > "$PROXY_DIR/Caddyfile"

  sed \
    -e "s|__ZOOMIES_PROXY_IMAGE__|$ZOOMIES_PROXY_IMAGE|g" \
    -e "s|__ZOOMIES_DATA_DIR__|$ZOOMIES_DATA_DIR|g" \
    "$PROXY_TMPL" > "$PROXY_DIR/docker-compose.yml"
}

render_tunnel() {
  [ "$ZOOMIES_TLS" = "tunnel" ] || return 0
  [ -r "$TUNNEL_TMPL" ] || die "the tunnel path needs $TUNNEL_TMPL, and the image was rendered without it"
  [ -n "$ZOOMIES_TUNNEL_IMAGE" ] || die "the rendered inputs name no tunnel image, so the tunnel path has nothing to run"

  say "writing the tunnel daemon's configuration"
  mkdir -p "$TUNNEL_DIR"
  sed -e "s|__ZOOMIES_TUNNEL_IMAGE__|$ZOOMIES_TUNNEL_IMAGE|g" "$TUNNEL_TMPL" > "$TUNNEL_DIR/docker-compose.yml"

  # The token is written beside the compose file rather than into it, and only
  # if there is one. A deployment rendered without a token is the better shape:
  # the operator pastes it here over SSH and it never passes through instance
  # metadata, the provider's database or cloud-init's log.
  if [ -n "$ZOOMIES_TUNNEL_TOKEN" ]; then
    (umask 077; printf 'TUNNEL_TOKEN=%s\n' "$ZOOMIES_TUNNEL_TOKEN" > "$TUNNEL_DIR/.env")
  elif [ ! -f "$TUNNEL_DIR/.env" ]; then
    (umask 077; printf '# Paste the tunnel token from the Cloudflare dashboard, then:\n#   docker compose -f %s/docker-compose.yml up -d\nTUNNEL_TOKEN=\n' "$TUNNEL_DIR" > "$TUNNEL_DIR/.env")
  fi
}

start_tunnel() {
  [ "$ZOOMIES_TLS" = "tunnel" ] || return 0
  if ! grep -q '^TUNNEL_TOKEN=.' "$TUNNEL_DIR/.env" 2>/dev/null; then
    say "no tunnel token yet, so the tunnel is not started; $NOTES says where to paste one"
    return 0
  fi
  docker compose -f "$TUNNEL_DIR/docker-compose.yml" up -d
}

start_proxy() {
  [ "$ZOOMIES_TLS" = "acme" ] || return 0
  docker compose -f "$PROXY_DIR/docker-compose.yml" up -d

  if [ "${ZOOMIES_DNS:-pending}" != "ready" ]; then
    # Not a failure. Caddy retries, so an instance booted before its DNS record
    # existed becomes healthy on its own once the record does -- which is the
    # usual order when the provider assigns the address at boot.
    say "the certificate cannot be issued until $ZOOMIES_HOSTNAME resolves to this instance; the proxy will keep trying"
  fi
}

# ----------------------------------------------------------------- the notes

write_notes() {
  umask 022
  cat > "$NOTES" <<NOTE
Zoomies $ZOOMIES_RELEASE is installed on this instance.

  Address   $ZOOMIES_EXTERNAL_URL
  Published $ZOOMIES_PUBLISH_ADDR:8080
  Data      $ZOOMIES_DATA_DIR (the zoomies-data volume)
  Answers   $ANSWERS

Finish setup in three steps.

1. Read this instance's setup token:

     docker compose -f /etc/zoomies/docker-compose.yml logs zoomies | grep 'setup token'

   It is printed only while no account exists, and a restart mints a new one.
   Holding it is the proof of ownership that an empty database is not: without
   it, whoever loads the page first would become the administrator.

2. Open $ZOOMIES_EXTERNAL_URL, paste the token, and create the first
   administrator.

3. Connect GitHub from the UI. Nothing runs until a pool exists, so make one
   after that.
NOTE

  # What each arrangement still needs from a person, which is the part a
  # generic note would leave them to work out on their own.
  case "$ZOOMIES_TLS" in
    tunnel)
      cat >> "$NOTES" <<NOTE

This deployment publishes no port. Cloudflare serves HTTPS on
$ZOOMIES_HOSTNAME and a tunnel daemon on this instance dials out to it, so
there is no inbound rule, no DNS record of this machine's own and no
certificate here.
NOTE
      if grep -q '^TUNNEL_TOKEN=.' "$TUNNEL_DIR/.env" 2>/dev/null; then
        cat >> "$NOTES" <<NOTE
The tunnel is running with the token this instance was rendered with.
NOTE
      else
        cat >> "$NOTES" <<NOTE
The tunnel is not running yet, because it has no token. Create the tunnel in
the Cloudflare dashboard, point its public hostname at
http://127.0.0.1:8080, then:

  \$EDITOR $TUNNEL_DIR/.env          # paste the token
  docker compose -f $TUNNEL_DIR/docker-compose.yml up -d

Pasting it here rather than into the provider's form is deliberate: a token in
instance metadata is also in the provider's database and in cloud-init's log.
NOTE
      fi
      ;;
    cloudflare)
      cat >> "$NOTES" <<NOTE

This instance serves plain HTTP on port 80 for Cloudflare to proxy, and
believes X-Forwarded-For and CF-Connecting-IP from Cloudflare's own ranges.

Firewall port 80 to those ranges. Left open to everything, the origin is
reachable directly and Cloudflare is merely in front of it rather than in the
way -- so a caller who finds this address bypasses every rule set at the edge.
NOTE
      ;;
  esac
  chmod 0644 "$NOTES"

  if [ -d /etc/update-motd.d ]; then
    cat > /etc/update-motd.d/99-zoomies <<'MOTD'
#!/bin/sh
[ -r /etc/zoomies/first-login.txt ] && cat /etc/zoomies/first-login.txt
MOTD
    chmod 0755 /etc/update-motd.d/99-zoomies
  fi
}

# ----------------------------------------------------------------- the check

wait_for_health() {
  # The question is whether the controller answers, not whether compose
  # reported success: an image that starts and then exits on a bad setting
  # leaves a healthy-looking `up -d` behind it.
  i=0
  while [ "$i" -lt 60 ]; do
    # shellcheck disable=SC2086
    if curl -fsS $HEALTH_CURL_OPTS -o /dev/null "$HEALTH_URL"; then
      say "the controller is answering on $HEALTH_URL"
      return 0
    fi
    i=$((i + 1))
    sleep 2
  done
  die "the controller did not answer /healthz within two minutes; its log is: docker compose -f /etc/zoomies/docker-compose.yml logs zoomies"
}

# Rendering is everything this script decides; the rest is installing what it
# decided. Stopping here is how the tests read those decisions.
if [ "${ZOOMIES_RENDER_ONLY:-}" = "1" ]; then
  render_answers
  render_proxy
  render_tunnel
  say "rendered $ANSWERS and stopped, because ZOOMIES_RENDER_ONLY is set"
  exit 0
fi

install_runtime
prepare_data_dir
render_answers
run_installer
wait_for_health
render_proxy
start_proxy
render_tunnel
start_tunnel
write_notes

say "done. $NOTES says how to finish setup."

#cloud-config
# Zoomies, deployed from a provider's marketplace.
#
# This is a template. render.sh fills in the three blocks below from
# release.env and an inputs file, and what it prints is the user-data a
# provider boots. Rendering rather than templating in the provider's own
# console is the point: the rendered file is a fixed artefact that can be
# diffed, reviewed and archived beside the release it installs.
#
# Nothing secret belongs in here. Instance metadata is readable by anything on
# the instance that can reach the metadata service, it is kept in the
# provider's database, and it is printed in cloud-init's own log -- so the
# first administrator and the GitHub App are set up in the browser afterwards,
# and this file carries only settings.

write_files:
  # What the bootstrap was told, and what the release pins. Mode 0600 because
  # it is configuration for root, not because any of it is a credential.
  - path: /etc/zoomies/marketplace.env
    owner: root:root
    permissions: '0600'
    content: |
      __ZOOMIES_ENV__

  # The answers `zoomies init` is given, with the instance's own values still
  # to be substituted at boot.
  - path: /etc/zoomies/answers.yaml.tmpl
    owner: root:root
    permissions: '0600'
    content: |
      __ZOOMIES_ANSWERS_TMPL__

  # The certificate holder, used only when ZOOMIES_TLS is acme. Written either
  # way: an instance that is later moved onto its own certificate, or off one,
  # should not need a different image to do it.
  - path: /etc/zoomies/Caddyfile.tmpl
    owner: root:root
    permissions: '0644'
    content: |
      __ZOOMIES_CADDYFILE__

  - path: /etc/zoomies/proxy-compose.yml.tmpl
    owner: root:root
    permissions: '0644'
    content: |
      __ZOOMIES_PROXY_COMPOSE__

  # The tunnel daemon, used only when ZOOMIES_TLS is tunnel. Written either
  # way, for the same reason as the proxy above.
  - path: /etc/zoomies/tunnel-compose.yml.tmpl
    owner: root:root
    permissions: '0644'
    content: |
      __ZOOMIES_TUNNEL_COMPOSE__

  - path: /usr/local/sbin/zoomies-bootstrap
    owner: root:root
    permissions: '0700'
    content: |
      __ZOOMIES_BOOTSTRAP__

runcmd:
  # One command, so that a failure is one exit status and cloud-init's own
  # status reports it. The script is idempotent: a boot that failed halfway can
  # be resumed by running it again over SSH.
  - [/usr/local/sbin/zoomies-bootstrap]

# A controller-only instance, answered in full: `zoomies init --answers
# controller-answers.yaml`.
#
# This is the shape a Terraform module or a configuration-management run
# writes: nobody is at the console, so every question the installer would ask
# is answered here, and nothing has to be read back out of a log afterwards.
# Replace the example values; the keys are the whole contract.
#
# It runs no agent. Runners live on the hosts that join it, each with
# `zoomies agent join` and a join token minted through the API by the account
# below -- so the settings page leaves out the agent settings this process has
# no use for.

# controller runs no embedded agent; the answer the file exists to give.
mode: controller

# native: a systemd service, and the installer creates the first account below
# on the console. A containerised controller creates it from the environment
# instead -- see ZOOMIES_BOOTSTRAP_* in docs/configuration.md.
deployment: native

# Zoomies terminates TLS itself with a certificate the provisioner put on disk,
# so the controller is reachable by agents on other hosts with nothing in front.
bind: 0.0.0.0:8443
tls:
  mode: files
  cert_file: /etc/zoomies/tls/fullchain.pem
  key_file: /etc/zoomies/tls/privkey.pem

# How agents, GitHub and the browser reach this controller.
external_url: https://zoomies.example.com:8443

# The first account, which holds the platform role. The password is read from
# a file the provisioner wrote with mode 0600 and is never written here.
# The installer records it in the audit log as auth.bootstrap, method
# answer_file.
admin:
  username: platform
  password_file: /etc/zoomies/bootstrap-password

github:
  # Connected later, in the UI or through the API, by the account above.
  skip: true

pool:
  # A controller with no agent has no runners of its own for a pool to
  # describe; pools are created once hosts have joined.
  skip: true

# Every image v1.3.0 deploys, and the digest its tag resolved to.
#
# Generated by `make marketplace-lock`; do not edit. Each line is one image
# reference and the digest it pointed at when this release was locked, so a

# whatever the tag means today.
#
# The runner images are here for that audit, not because the bootstrap picks
# one: a controller resolves its runners from its own build tag, so pinning
